```go
// dtTable parses save text and returns the named table.
func dtTable(t *testing.T, save, name string) *netfilter.Table {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.Parse(strings.NewReader(save))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse: %v", err)
	}
	tb := rs.Table(name)
	if tb == nil {
		t.Fatalf("no table %s in %q", name, save)
	}
	return tb
}

func TestDtUnsupported(t *testing.T) {
	supported := Detection{Version: "29.9.1", Driver: "iptables", DockerVariant: "nft", UFWVariant: "nft", RawProtection: true}
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		edit func(d *Detection)
		want []string
	}{
		{"every condition holds", func(*Detection) {}, nil},
		{"28.0 is the floor", func(d *Detection) { d.Version = "28.0.0" }, nil},
		{"a pre-release of 28.0", func(d *Detection) { d.Version = "28.0.0-rc.1" }, nil},
		{"legacy on both sides", func(d *Detection) { d.DockerVariant, d.UFWVariant = "legacy", "legacy" }, nil},
		{"Docker 27", func(d *Detection) { d.Version = "27.5.1" }, []string{"Docker 27.5.1 is older than 28.0"}},
		{"Docker 9", func(d *Detection) { d.Version = "9.9.9" }, []string{"Docker 9.9.9 is older than 28.0"}},
		{"no version", func(d *Detection) { d.Version = "" }, []string{`Docker version "" is not recognised`}},
		{"a version that is not numbers", func(d *Detection) { d.Version = "dev" }, []string{`Docker version "dev" is not recognised`}},
		{"nftables backend", func(d *Detection) { d.Driver = "nftables" },
			[]string{`Docker's firewall backend is "nftables"; only "iptables" is supported`}},
		{"no driver", func(d *Detection) { d.Driver = "" },
			[]string{`Docker's firewall backend is ""; only "iptables" is supported`}},
		{"Docker's chains are nowhere", func(d *Detection) { d.DockerVariant = "" },
			[]string{"Docker's chains DOCKER-USER and DOCKER-FORWARD are in neither iptables variant"}},
		{"Docker's chains are in both variants", func(d *Detection) { d.DockerVariant = "both" },
			[]string{"Docker's chains are in both iptables variants"}},
		{"Docker and UFW use different variants", func(d *Detection) { d.DockerVariant, d.UFWVariant = "nft", "legacy" },
			[]string{"Docker's chains are in iptables-nft but UFW uses iptables-legacy"}},
		{"UFW's variant is unknown", func(d *Detection) { d.UFWVariant = "" },
			[]string{"UFW's iptables variant is not known"}},
		{"raw protection is not loaded", func(d *Detection) { d.RawProtection = false },
			[]string{"Docker's raw-table protection of published ports is not loaded"}},
		{"every reason, in order", func(d *Detection) {
			d.Version, d.Driver, d.DockerVariant, d.UFWVariant, d.RawProtection = "27.5.1", "nftables", "both", "legacy", false
		}, []string{
			"Docker 27.5.1 is older than 28.0",
			`Docker's firewall backend is "nftables"; only "iptables" is supported`,
			"Docker's chains are in both iptables variants",
			"Docker's raw-table protection of published ports is not loaded",
		}},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			d := supported
			tt.edit(&d)
			if got := Unsupported(d); !slices.Equal(got, tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("Unsupported(%+v) = %q, want %q", d, got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestDtDockerChains(t *testing.T) {
	const head = "*filter\n:INPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n"
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		save string
		want bool
	}{
		{"both chains with rules", head + ":DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:DOCKER-FORWARD - [0:0]\n-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER\n-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-FORWARD\nCOMMIT\n", true},
		{"both chains empty", head + ":DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:DOCKER-FORWARD - [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n", true},
		{"only DOCKER-USER", head + ":DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n", false},
		{"only DOCKER-FORWARD", head + ":DOCKER-FORWARD - [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n", false},
		{"neither", head + ":ufw-user-input - [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n", false},
		{"a table nft cannot show", "# Table `filter' is incompatible, use 'nft' tool.\n", false},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := DockerChains(dtTable(t, tt.save, "filter")); got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("DockerChains = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
	if DockerChains(nil) {
		t.Error("DockerChains(nil) = true")
	}
}

const dtRaw = `*raw
:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]
:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]
-A PREROUTING -d 172.17.0.2/32 ! -i docker0 -j DROP
-A PREROUTING -d 172.21.0.2/32 ! -i br-a2871ddf38b3 -j DROP
-A PREROUTING -d 127.0.0.1/32 ! -i lo -p tcp -m tcp --dport 5432 -j DROP
-A PREROUTING -d 172.21.0.3/32 ! -i br-a2871ddf38b3 -j DROP
COMMIT
`

// dtFacts is the running containers behind dtRaw: a cache on the default
// bridge, a database published on 127.0.0.1 and a web server published on
// every address.
func dtFacts() Facts {
	a := netip.MustParseAddr
	app := []Endpoint{{Network: "app", Bridge: "br-a2871ddf38b3", Addr4: a("172.21.0.2")}}
	web := []Endpoint{{Network: "app", Bridge: "br-a2871ddf38b3", Addr4: a("172.21.0.3")}}
	return Facts{
		Containers: []Container{
			{ID: "c1", Name: "cache", Endpoints: []Endpoint{{Network: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0", Addr4: a("172.17.0.2")}}},
			{ID: "c2", Name: "db", Endpoints: app,
				Ports: []Published{{HostAddr: a("127.0.0.1"), HostPort: 5432, ContainerPort: 5432, Proto: "tcp"}}},
			{ID: "c3", Name: "web", Endpoints: web,
				Ports: []Published{{HostAddr: a("0.0.0.0"), HostPort: 8000, ContainerPort: 8000, Proto: "tcp"}}},
		},
		Networks: []Network{
			{ID: "0123456789abcdef", Name: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.17.0.0/16")}},
			{ID: "a2871ddf38b3aaaa", Name: "app", Bridge: "br-a2871ddf38b3", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.21.0.0/16")}},
		},
	}
}

func TestDtRawProtected(t *testing.T) {
	a := netip.MustParseAddr
	without := func(line string) string { return strings.Replace(dtRaw, line+"\n", "", 1) }
	routedNet := func(f *Facts, mode string) {
		f.Containers = append(f.Containers, Container{ID: "c9", Name: "direct",
			Endpoints: []Endpoint{{Network: "direct", Bridge: "br-direct", Addr4: a("198.51.100.2")}}})
		f.Networks = append(f.Networks, Network{ID: "dddddddddddd", Name: "direct", Bridge: "br-direct", GatewayModeV4: mode})
	}
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		raw  string
		edit func(f *Facts)
		want bool
	}{
		{"Docker 29's own rules", dtRaw, func(*Facts) {}, true},
		{"the loopback port rule is missing", without("-A PREROUTING -d 127.0.0.1/32 ! -i lo -p tcp -m tcp --dport 5432 -j DROP"), func(*Facts) {}, false},
		{"a container address has no drop rule", without("-A PREROUTING -d 172.21.0.3/32 ! -i br-a2871ddf38b3 -j DROP"), func(*Facts) {}, false},
		{"the drop rule names another bridge", strings.Replace(dtRaw, "172.21.0.3/32 ! -i br-a2871ddf38b3", "172.21.0.3/32 ! -i docker0", 1), func(*Facts) {}, false},
		{"the rule is not negated", strings.Replace(dtRaw, "172.17.0.2/32 ! -i docker0", "172.17.0.2/32 -i docker0", 1), func(*Facts) {}, false},
		{"a loopback UDP port needs a udp rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) {
			f.Containers[1].Ports = []Published{{HostAddr: a("127.0.0.1"), HostPort: 5432, ContainerPort: 5432, Proto: "udp"}}
		}, false},
		{"a loopback UDP port with its udp rule", strings.Replace(dtRaw, "-p tcp -m tcp --dport 5432", "-p udp -m udp --dport 5432", 1), func(f *Facts) {
			f.Containers[1].Ports = []Published{{HostAddr: a("127.0.0.1"), HostPort: 5432, ContainerPort: 5432, Proto: "udp"}}
		}, true},
		{"another loopback port is not covered by the 5432 rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) {
			f.Containers[1].Ports[0].HostPort = 5433
		}, false},
		{"a port on a specific public address needs no raw rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) {
			f.Containers[2].Ports = append(f.Containers[2].Ports, Published{HostAddr: a("192.0.2.10"), HostPort: 9000, ContainerPort: 9000, Proto: "tcp"})
		}, true},
		{"a port on the IPv6 loopback is not an IPv4 rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) {
			f.Containers[2].Ports = append(f.Containers[2].Ports, Published{HostAddr: a("::1"), HostPort: 9001, ContainerPort: 9001, Proto: "tcp"})
		}, true},
		{"an endpoint with no IPv4 address", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) {
			f.Containers = append(f.Containers, Container{ID: "c8", Name: "six",
				Endpoints: []Endpoint{{Network: "app", Bridge: "br-a2871ddf38b3", Addr6: a("fd00:dead::2")}}})
		}, true},
		{"a NAT network's container without its rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) { routedNet(f, "") }, false},
		{"a routed network needs no rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) { routedNet(f, "routed") }, true},
		{"a nat-unprotected network needs no rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) { routedNet(f, "nat-unprotected") }, true},
		{"an endpoint of an unknown network is held to the rule", dtRaw, func(f *Facts) {
			f.Containers = append(f.Containers, Container{ID: "c7", Name: "lost",
				Endpoints: []Endpoint{{Network: "gone", Bridge: "br-gone", Addr4: a("172.25.0.2")}}})
		}, false},
		{"nothing to protect", "*raw\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n", func(f *Facts) { *f = Facts{} }, true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := dtFacts()
			tt.edit(&f)
			if got := RawProtected(dtTable(t, tt.raw, "raw"), f); got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("RawProtected = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
	t.Run("no raw table", func(t *testing.T) {
		if RawProtected(nil, Facts{}) {
			t.Error("RawProtected(nil, no containers) = true")
		}
	})
	t.Run("a raw table nft cannot show", func(t *testing.T) {
		tb := dtTable(t, "# Table `raw' is incompatible, use 'nft' tool.\n", "raw")
		if RawProtected(tb, Facts{}) {
			t.Error("RawProtected(incompatible table, no containers) = true")
		}
	})
}

// dtInspect and dtNet are the fields of the captured Docker inspect output
// that the facts need.
type dtInspect struct {
	ID              string
	Name            string
	State           struct{ Running bool }
	NetworkSettings struct {
		Ports    map[string][]struct{ HostIP, HostPort string }
		Networks map[string]struct{ IPAddress, GlobalIPv6Address string }
	}
}

type dtNet struct {
	Name, ID, Driver string
	EnableIPv6       bool
	Options          map[string]string
	IPAM             struct{ Config []struct{ Subnet string } }
}

// dtDecode reads a capture file holding a JSON array or a stream of objects.
func dtDecode[T any](t *testing.T, data []byte) []T {
	t.Helper()
	var list []T
	if err := json.Unmarshal(data, &list); err == nil {
		return list
	}
	list = nil
	dec := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
	for dec.More() {
		var v T
		if err := dec.Decode(&v); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("decode capture JSON: %v", err)
		}
		list = append(list, v)
	}
	return list
}

// dtCaptureFacts is the facts the capture's running containers and networks
// give.
func dtCaptureFacts(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) Facts {
	t.Helper()
	var f Facts
	bridge := map[string]string{}
	mode := map[string]string{}
	for _, n := range dtDecode[dtNet](t, capFile(t, image, scenario, "networks.json")) {
		b := n.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.name"]
		switch {
		case b != "":
		case n.Name == "bridge":
			b = "docker0"
		default:
			b = "br-" + n.ID[:12]
		}
		bridge[n.Name], mode[n.Name] = b, n.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv4"]
		nw := Network{ID: n.ID, Name: n.Name, Driver: n.Driver, Bridge: b, IPv6: n.EnableIPv6, GatewayModeV4: mode[n.Name]}
		for _, c := range n.IPAM.Config {
			nw.Subnets = append(nw.Subnets, netip.MustParsePrefix(c.Subnet))
		}
		f.Networks = append(f.Networks, nw)
	}
	for _, c := range dtDecode[dtInspect](t, capFile(t, image, scenario, "containers.json")) {
		if !c.State.Running {
			continue
		}
		ct := Container{ID: c.ID, Name: strings.TrimPrefix(c.Name, "/")}
		for key, bindings := range c.NetworkSettings.Ports {
			port, proto, _ := strings.Cut(key, "/")
			for _, b := range bindings {
				host := netip.IPv4Unspecified()
				if b.HostIP != "" {
					host = netip.MustParseAddr(b.HostIP)
				}
				cp, err := strconv.ParseUint(port, 10, 16)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				hp, err := strconv.ParseUint(b.HostPort, 10, 16)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				ct.Ports = append(ct.Ports, Published{HostAddr: host, HostPort: uint16(hp), ContainerPort: uint16(cp), Proto: proto})
			}
		}
		for name, ep := range c.NetworkSettings.Networks {
			e := Endpoint{Network: name, Bridge: bridge[name]}
			if ep.IPAddress != "" {
				e.Addr4 = netip.MustParseAddr(ep.IPAddress)
			}
			if ep.GlobalIPv6Address != "" {
				e.Addr6 = netip.MustParseAddr(ep.GlobalIPv6Address)
			}
			ct.Endpoints = append(ct.Endpoints, e)
		}
		f.Containers = append(f.Containers, ct)
	}
	return f
}

// TestDtCaptures holds this file's functions to what Docker 29.9.1 and UFW
// left on the four images.
func TestDtCaptures(t *testing.T) {
	for _, image := range capImages {
		for _, scenario := range capScenarios {
			t.Run(image+"/"+scenario, func(t *testing.T) {
				v4 := capLoad(t, image, scenario)[fwstate.V4]
				if v4 == nil {
					t.Fatal("the capture has no IPv4 tables")
				}
				if !DockerChains(v4.Table("filter")) {
					t.Error("DockerChains = false on the variant UFW uses")
				}
				facts := dtCaptureFacts(t, image, scenario)
				protected := RawProtected(v4.Table("raw"), facts)
				if !protected {
					t.Errorf("RawProtected = false for facts %+v", facts.Containers)
				}
				var info struct {
					ServerVersion   string
					FirewallBackend *struct{ Driver string }
				}
				if err := json.Unmarshal(capFile(t, image, scenario, "info.json"), &info); err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				driver := "iptables"
				if info.FirewallBackend != nil {
					driver = info.FirewallBackend.Driver
				}
				// capLoad reads only the variant UFW uses, so the variant fields
				// stand in for each other here.
				d := Detection{Version: info.ServerVersion, Driver: driver, DockerVariant: "nft", UFWVariant: "nft", RawProtection: protected}
				if got := Unsupported(d); len(got) != 0 {
					t.Errorf("Unsupported(%+v) = %q", d, got)
				}
				if scenario != "base" {
					return
				}
				// The control: the captured containers do need raw rules.
				if len(facts.Containers) == 0 {
					t.Fatal("the base capture has no running container")
				}
				if RawProtected(&netfilter.Table{Name: "raw"}, facts) {
					t.Error("RawProtected(empty raw table, the base capture's containers) = true")
				}
			})
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `detect.go` in package `dockerfw`. It imports only the standard library and `internal/platform/netfilter`, and reads no host state. Every exported identifier has a doc comment. Every other top-level identifier in it starts with `det`, so it cannot collide with another dockerfw task's unexported names.

1. `Detection` exactly as Contracts "dockerfw detection" declares it.
2. `Unsupported(d Detection) []string` appends these reasons in this order, each when its condition holds, and returns nil when none does. Strings are exact; `%q` means Go's quoted form:
   1. Version. Read the leading `<major>.<minor>` of `d.Version`: digits, a dot, digits, whatever follows the minor (`.1`, `-rc.1`) is ignored. Not readable (including empty): `Docker version %q is not recognised`. Major below 28: `Docker <d.Version> is older than 28.0` with the version as given. A major of 28 or more passes whatever the minor.
   2. `d.Driver` is not exactly `iptables`: `Docker's firewall backend is %q; only "iptables" is supported`.
   3. `d.UFWVariant` is neither `nft` nor `legacy`: `UFW's iptables variant is not known`.
   4. `d.DockerVariant`: `nft` or `legacy` and UFW's variant is known and different: `Docker's chains are in iptables-<docker variant> but UFW uses iptables-<ufw variant>`; `both`: `Docker's chains are in both iptables variants`; any other value, the empty string included: `Docker's chains DOCKER-USER and DOCKER-FORWARD are in neither iptables variant`.
   5. `!d.RawProtection`: `Docker's raw-table protection of published ports is not loaded`.
3. `DockerChains(filter *netfilter.Table) bool` is true when the table is not nil and declares both `DOCKER-USER` and `DOCKER-FORWARD`, with or without rules. A nil table, a table nft cannot show (`Incompatible` set) and a table with only one of the two are false.
4. `RawProtected(raw *netfilter.Table, facts Facts) bool` reports whether the IPv4 raw table holds the protection Docker 28 and later loads for the running containers in `facts`. A nil table or one with `Incompatible` set is false. Otherwise it is true when every expectation below is met, so a host with no container to protect is true. A short comment on the function says why: an idle Docker loads no raw rule, so absence of rules proves nothing until a container exists. Every rule it looks for is in the `PREROUTING` chain, has target `DROP` and is not a jump.
   - For every endpoint of every container that has an `Addr4`, unless the endpoint's network (looked up by name in `facts.Networks`) has `GatewayModeV4` `routed` or `nat-unprotected`: a rule with destination exactly `<Addr4>/32` (not negated), a negated in-interface equal to the endpoint's `Bridge`, no `-p` and no `-m` match. An endpoint of a network that `facts.Networks` does not list is held to this rule too. An endpoint with only `Addr6` expects nothing, because only the IPv4 table is read.
   - For every published port whose `HostAddr` is an IPv4 loopback address: a rule with destination exactly `<HostAddr>/32` (not negated), negated in-interface `lo`, `-p <Proto>`, and the `-m <Proto>` match with a single non-negated `--dport <HostPort>`. A port on any other address, including `::1`, expects nothing.

If `TestDtCaptures` fails for a capture, the capture is the oracle: report the image, scenario and the rule text it contradicts instead of loosening a check. If it fails only because `dtCaptureFacts` cannot decode Task 1's `containers.json` or `networks.json`, fix that helper in the test file (it reads only the fields it declares), not the capture.

```go
// dtfTable parses save text and returns the named table.
func dtfTable(t *testing.T, save, name string) *netfilter.Table {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.Parse(strings.NewReader(save))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse: %v", err)
	}
	tb := rs.Table(name)
	if tb == nil {
		t.Fatalf("no table %s in %q", name, save)
	}
	return tb
}

func TestDtfForeignDNAT(t *testing.T) {
	got := ForeignDNAT(dtfTable(t, dtfNat, "nat"))
	var texts []string
	for _, r := range got {
		texts = append(texts, r.Text)
	}
	want := []string{
		"-A PREROUTING -d 192.0.2.10/32 -i eth0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:8080",
		"-A PREROUTING -p tcp -m tcp --dport 8000:8100 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.6",
		"-A PREROUTING -d 192.0.2.11/32 -p udp -m udp --dport 53 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.7:5353 --persistent",
		`-A lan-fwd -d 192.0.2.13/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 25 -m comment --comment "mail" -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.9:25`,
		"-A PREROUTING ! -i eth1 -d 192.0.2.12/32 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.8",
	}
	if !slices.Equal(texts, want) {
		t.Errorf("ForeignDNAT =\n%s\nwant\n%s", strings.Join(texts, "\n"), strings.Join(want, "\n"))
	}
	t.Run("no nat table", func(t *testing.T) {
		if got := ForeignDNAT(nil); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("ForeignDNAT(nil) = %v", got)
		}
	})
	t.Run("no PREROUTING chain", func(t *testing.T) {
		tb := dtfTable(t, "*nat\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n-A OUTPUT -p tcp -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.1\nCOMMIT\n", "nat")
		if got := ForeignDNAT(tb); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("ForeignDNAT = %v", got)
		}
	})
	t.Run("Docker's prefixed chains are Docker's", func(t *testing.T) {
		tb := dtfTable(t, "*nat\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:DOCKER-INGRESS - [0:0]\n-A PREROUTING -j DOCKER-INGRESS\n"+
			"-A DOCKER-INGRESS -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.18.0.2:80\nCOMMIT\n", "nat")
		if got := ForeignDNAT(tb); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("ForeignDNAT = %v", got)
		}
	})
}

// dtfRule parses one rule line of nat PREROUTING.
func dtfRule(t *testing.T, line string) netfilter.Rule {
	t.Helper()
	tb := dtfTable(t, "*nat\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n-A PREROUTING "+line+"\nCOMMIT\n", "nat")
	return tb.Chain("PREROUTING").Rules[0]
}

func dtfExemption(inIface, origDst string, origPort uint16, dst, proto string, port uint16) Exemption {
	return Exemption{InInterface: inIface, OrigDestination: netip.MustParseAddr(origDst), OrigPort: origPort,
		Destination: netip.MustParseAddr(dst), Proto: proto, Port: port}
}

func TestDtfPropose(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		fam  fwstate.Family
		rule string
		want Exemption
		ok   bool
	}{
		{"a port forward", fwstate.V4,
			"-d 192.0.2.10/32 -i eth0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:8080",
			dtfExemption("eth0", "192.0.2.10", 80, "10.9.0.5", "tcp", 8080), true},
		{"the translated port is the original one when the target names none", fwstate.V4,
			`-d 192.0.2.13/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 25 -m comment --comment "mail" -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.9`,
			dtfExemption("", "192.0.2.13", 25, "10.9.0.9", "tcp", 25), true},
		{"a UDP forward of every port to one port", fwstate.V4,
			"-d 192.0.2.11/32 -p udp -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.7:5353",
			dtfExemption("", "192.0.2.11", 0, "10.9.0.7", "udp", 5353), true},
		{"a forward of every port to every port", fwstate.V4,
			"-d 192.0.2.11/32 -p tcp -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.7",
			dtfExemption("", "192.0.2.11", 0, "10.9.0.7", "tcp", 0), true},
		{"a source restriction does not change what the rule translates", fwstate.V4,
			"-s 203.0.113.0/24 -d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:80",
			dtfExemption("", "192.0.2.10", 80, "10.9.0.5", "tcp", 80), true},
		{"an interface wildcard is kept as written", fwstate.V4,
			"-d 192.0.2.10/32 -i eth+ -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5",
			dtfExemption("eth+", "192.0.2.10", 80, "10.9.0.5", "tcp", 80), true},
		{"an IPv6 forward", fwstate.V6,
			"-d 2001:db8::10/128 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination [fd00::5]:8443",
			dtfExemption("", "2001:db8::10", 443, "fd00::5", "tcp", 8443), true},
		{"an IPv6 forward without a target port", fwstate.V6,
			"-d 2001:db8::10/128 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination fd00::5",
			dtfExemption("", "2001:db8::10", 443, "fd00::5", "tcp", 443), true},
		{"no destination address", fwstate.V4, "-p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:80", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a destination network", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.0/24 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:80", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a negated destination", fwstate.V4, "! -d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:80", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a negated in-interface", fwstate.V4, "! -i eth1 -d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:80", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a port range", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 8000:8100 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a port list", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m multiport --dports 80,443 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a source port", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --sport 1024 --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"an address type match", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -m addrtype --src-type LOCAL -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a rule the parser keeps opaque", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5 --persistent", Exemption{}, false},
		{"no protocol", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a protocol that has no ports", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p icmp -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a translated address range", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5-10.9.0.9", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a target of the other family", fwstate.V6, "-d 2001:db8::10/128 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"a rule of the other family", fwstate.V6, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5", Exemption{}, false},
		{"not a DNAT rule", fwstate.V4, "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j ACCEPT", Exemption{}, false},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, ok := Propose(dtfRule(t, tt.rule), tt.fam)
			if ok != tt.ok || got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("Propose = %+v, %v; want %+v, %v", got, ok, tt.want, tt.ok)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestDtfCovered(t *testing.T) {
	const line = "-d 192.0.2.10/32 -i eth0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:8080"
	exact := dtfExemption("eth0", "192.0.2.10", 80, "10.9.0.5", "tcp", 8080)
	with := func(edit func(e *Exemption)) Exemption {
		e := exact
		edit(&e)
		return e
	}
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		rule string
		ex   []Exemption
		want bool
	}{
		{"an exemption equal to the proposal", line, []Exemption{exact}, true},
		{"one matching exemption among others", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.Proto = "udp" }), exact}, true},
		{"an exemption for any interface", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.InInterface = "" })}, true},
		{"an exemption for any original port", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.OrigPort = 0 })}, true},
		{"an exemption for any translated port", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.Port = 0 })}, true},
		{"an exemption for another interface", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.InInterface = "eth1" })}, false},
		{"an exemption for another original port", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.OrigPort = 81 })}, false},
		{"an exemption for another translated port", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.Port = 8081 })}, false},
		{"an exemption for another original address", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.OrigDestination = netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.11") })}, false},
		{"an exemption for another destination", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.Destination = netip.MustParseAddr("10.9.0.6") })}, false},
		{"an exemption for another protocol", line, []Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.Proto = "udp" })}, false},
		{"no exemptions", line, nil, false},
		{"a rule with no destination address is never covered", "-p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:8080",
			[]Exemption{with(func(e *Exemption) { e.InInterface = "" })}, false},
		{"an IPv6 rule", "-d 2001:db8::10/128 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination [fd00::5]:8443",
			[]Exemption{dtfExemption("", "2001:db8::10", 443, "fd00::5", "tcp", 8443)}, true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := Covered(dtfRule(t, tt.rule), tt.ex); got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("Covered = %v, want %v", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestDtfExemptionConflicts(t *testing.T) {
	p := netip.MustParsePrefix
	nets := []Network{
		{Name: "bridge", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{p("172.17.0.0/16")}},
		{Name: "app", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{p("172.21.0.0/16"), p("fd00:dead::/64")}},
		{Name: "narrow", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{p("172.21.0.0/24")}},
	}
	ex := []Exemption{
		dtfExemption("", "192.0.2.10", 80, "10.9.0.5", "tcp", 80),
		dtfExemption("", "192.0.2.11", 80, "172.21.0.9", "tcp", 80),
		dtfExemption("", "2001:db8::10", 80, "fd00:dead::7", "tcp", 80),
		dtfExemption("", "192.0.2.12", 80, "172.17.0.3", "udp", 53),
	}
	want := []string{
		"exemption 1: destination 172.21.0.9 lies in Docker network app (172.21.0.0/16)",
		"exemption 1: destination 172.21.0.9 lies in Docker network narrow (172.21.0.0/24)",
		"exemption 2: destination fd00:dead::7 lies in Docker network app (fd00:dead::/64)",
		"exemption 3: destination 172.17.0.3 lies in Docker network bridge (172.17.0.0/16)",
	}
	if got := ExemptionConflicts(ex, nets); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("ExemptionConflicts =\n%q\nwant\n%q", got, want)
	}
	if got := ExemptionConflicts(ex[:1], nets); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ExemptionConflicts(no conflict) = %q", got)
	}
	if got := ExemptionConflicts(ex, nil); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ExemptionConflicts(no networks) = %q", got)
	}
}

// TestDtfCaptures holds ForeignDNAT to what Docker 29.9.1 left in the nat table
// of the four images.
func TestDtfCaptures(t *testing.T) {
	for _, image := range capImages {
		for _, scenario := range capScenarios {
			t.Run(image+"/"+scenario, func(t *testing.T) {
				v4 := capLoad(t, image, scenario)[fwstate.V4]
				if v4 == nil {
					t.Fatal("the capture has no IPv4 tables")
				}
				nat := v4.Table("nat")
				if nat == nil {
					t.Fatal("no nat table in the capture")
				}
				if got := ForeignDNAT(nat); len(got) != 0 {
					t.Errorf("ForeignDNAT = %d rules on a host with only Docker's forwards: %q", len(got), got[0].Text)
				}
				if scenario != "base" {
					return
				}
				// The control: the captured nat table does hold Docker's DNAT
				// rules, so the check above proves something.
				dnat := 0
				for _, c := range nat.Chains {
					for _, r := range c.Rules {
						if r.Target.Name == "DNAT" {
							dnat++
						}
					}
				}
				if dnat == 0 {
					t.Error("the base capture's nat table holds no DNAT rule, so the ForeignDNAT check proves nothing")
				}
			})
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `forward.go` in package `dockerfw`. It imports only the standard library, `internal/modules/firewall/fwstate` and `internal/platform/netfilter`, and reads no host state. Every exported identifier has a doc comment. Every other top-level identifier in it starts with `dtf`, so it cannot collide with another dockerfw task's unexported names.

1. `ForeignDNAT(nat *netfilter.Table) []netfilter.Rule` returns every rule with target `DNAT` that is reachable from the `PREROUTING` chain and is not in one of Docker's chains, in walk order. Walk `PREROUTING`'s rules in order; at a jump rule, walk the target chain at that point unless the chain is Docker's (named `DOCKER` or starting `DOCKER-`) or was already walked (each chain is walked once, `PREROUTING` itself included, so a loop or a second jump to the same chain cannot repeat or hang). A rule with target `DNAT` is returned even when the parser keeps it opaque. Rules in chains no jump reaches, other targets such as `REDIRECT`, and the `OUTPUT` chain are not returned. A nil table or one without `PREROUTING` returns nil.
2. `Propose(r netfilter.Rule, f fwstate.Family) (Exemption, bool)` turns a foreign DNAT rule into the exemption that names it exactly (spec 2.6), or reports false with the zero `Exemption`, whatever it had read so far. It is false unless all of these hold:
   - the target is `DNAT`, the rule is not opaque (`Rule.Opaque()`) and has no goto;
   - the rule's `-d` is present, not negated, a single address (a /32 or /128 prefix) of family `f`, and becomes `OrigDestination` (a rule with no destination address, or a network, has no `origDestination` to name, so it can never be covered and enabling the integration keeps refusing until the operator adds `-d`);
   - `-p` is present, not negated, and is `tcp` or `udp`, which becomes `Proto`;
   - `-i`, when present, is not negated and becomes `InInterface` as written (a wildcard such as `eth+` stays);
   - every `-m` module is `tcp`, `udp` (matching `-p`) or `comment`; the tcp or udp module carries at most `--dport`, not negated, one port with no range or list, which becomes `OrigPort`; a source restriction (`-s`) is ignored, since the exemption matches only connections this rule itself translated;
   - `--to-destination` is one address of family `f` (IPv4 `addr` or `addr:port`; IPv6 `addr` or `[addr]:port`), no range; it becomes `Destination`, and its port becomes `Port`; when it names no port, `Port` is the rule's `--dport` (0 when there is none), since DNAT keeps the original port.
3. `Covered(r netfilter.Rule, ex []Exemption) bool` is false when `r.Dest` has no valid prefix (nothing to derive the family from) or `Propose` is false for it, using family IPv4 when the destination is IPv4 and IPv6 otherwise. Otherwise it is true when some exemption `e` matches the proposal `p` as follows: `e.OrigDestination`, `e.Destination` and `e.Proto` equal `p`'s, and each of `InInterface`, `OrigPort` and `Port` is either unset in `e` (empty, 0) or equal to `p`'s. An exemption that is broader than the rule covers it; a narrower one does not.
4. `ExemptionConflicts(ex []Exemption, nets []Network) []string` returns, in exemption order, then network order, one string per (exemption, network) pair where some subnet of the network contains the exemption's `Destination`: `exemption <i>: destination <addr> lies in Docker network <name> (<subnet>)`, with `<i>` the exemption's zero-based index and `<subnet>` the first containing subnet of that network. Nil when nothing conflicts.

If `TestDtfCaptures` fails for a capture, the capture is the oracle: report the image, scenario and the rule text it contradicts instead of loosening a check.

```go
// TestFdFakeDockerDefaults: a new fake is Docker 29.9.1 with the iptables
// driver, no containers and the default bridge network, and it records
// each call by its method name.
func TestFdFakeDockerDefaults(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := t.Context()
	d := newFakeDocker()
	info, err := d.Info(ctx)
	if err != nil || info.ServerVersion != "29.9.1" || info.FirewallBackend == nil || info.FirewallBackend.Driver != "iptables" {
		t.Errorf("Info = %+v, %v; want Docker 29.9.1 with the iptables driver", info, err)
	}
	if v, err := d.Version(ctx); err != nil || v.Version != "29.9.1" {
		t.Errorf("Version = %+v, %v; want 29.9.1", v, err)
	}
	if cs, err := d.ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{All: true}); err != nil || len(cs) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ListContainers = %v, %v; want none", cs, err)
	}
	nets, err := d.ListNetworks(ctx, nil)
	if err != nil || len(nets) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("ListNetworks = %v, %v; want the bridge network only", nets, err)
	}
	n := nets[0]
	if n.Name != "bridge" || n.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.name"] != "docker0" ||
		len(n.IPAM.Config) != 1 || n.IPAM.Config[0].Subnet != netip.MustParsePrefix("172.17.0.0/16") {
		t.Errorf("network %+v, want bridge on docker0 with 172.17.0.0/16", n)
	}
	want := []string{"Info", "Version", "ListContainers", "ListNetworks"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(d.calls, want) {
		t.Errorf("calls %q, want %q", d.calls, want)
	}
}

// TestFdFakeDockerContainers: the list holds the running containers unless
// All is set, an inspect finds a container by id, name or /name and answers
// the daemon's 404 otherwise, and err fails every call.
func TestFdFakeDockerContainers(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := t.Context()
	d := newFakeDocker()
	web := fdContainer("web", func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) { c.Config.Labels["com.docker.compose.project"] = "shop" })
	gone := fdContainer("gone", func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) { c.State = dockerapi.ContainerState{Status: "exited"} })
	d.containers = []dockerapi.ContainerJSON{web, gone}

	running, err := d.ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{})
	if err != nil || len(running) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("running containers = %v, %v; want web only", running, err)
	}
	if s := running[0]; s.ID != web.ID || !reflect.DeepEqual(s.Names, []string{"/web"}) || s.State != "running" || s.Labels["com.docker.compose.project"] != "shop" {
		t.Errorf("summary %+v, want web, running, with its labels", s)
	}
	all, err := d.ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{All: true})
	if err != nil || len(all) != 2 || all[1].State != "exited" {
		t.Errorf("all containers = %v, %v; want web and the exited gone", all, err)
	}

	d.calls = nil
	for _, id := range []string{web.ID, "web", "/web"} {
		got, err := d.InspectContainer(ctx, id)
		if err != nil || got.ID != web.ID {
			t.Errorf("InspectContainer(%q) = %q, %v; want web", id, got.ID, err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := d.InspectContainer(ctx, "nope"); !dockerapi.IsNotFound(err) {
		t.Errorf("InspectContainer(nope) = %v, want the daemon's 404", err)
	}
	if want := []string{"InspectContainer " + web.ID, "InspectContainer web", "InspectContainer /web", "InspectContainer nope"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(d.calls, want) {
		t.Errorf("calls %q, want %q", d.calls, want)
	}

	boom := errors.New("fdtest: the daemon is down")
	d.err = boom
	if _, err := d.Info(ctx); !errors.Is(err, boom) {
		t.Errorf("Info = %v, want %v", err, boom)
	}
	if _, err := d.Version(ctx); !errors.Is(err, boom) {
		t.Errorf("Version = %v, want %v", err, boom)
	}
	if _, err := d.ListContainers(ctx, dockerapi.ListContainersOptions{}); !errors.Is(err, boom) {
		t.Errorf("ListContainers = %v, want %v", err, boom)
	}
	if _, err := d.InspectContainer(ctx, "web"); !errors.Is(err, boom) {
		t.Errorf("InspectContainer = %v, want %v", err, boom)
	}
	if _, err := d.ListNetworks(ctx, nil); !errors.Is(err, boom) {
		t.Errorf("ListNetworks = %v, want %v", err, boom)
	}
	if s, err := d.Events(ctx, dockerapi.EventsOptions{}); !errors.Is(err, boom) || s != nil {
		t.Errorf("Events = %v, %v; want no stream and %v", s, err, boom)
	}
}

// TestFdFakeDockerEvents: a stream delivers what the test sends on events,
// ends with io.EOF once it is closed or events is closed, and with the
// context's error once the context ends.
func TestFdFakeDockerEvents(t *testing.T) {
	d := newFakeDocker()
	s, err := d.Events(t.Context(), dockerapi.EventsOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	d.events <- dockerapi.Event{Type: "container", Action: "start"}
	ev, err := s.Next()
	if err != nil || ev.Type != "container" || ev.Action != "start" {
		t.Errorf("Next = %+v, %v; want the container start", ev, err)
	}
	if err := s.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("Close = %v", err)
	}
	if err := s.Close(); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("second Close = %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Next(); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Errorf("Next after Close = %v, want io.EOF", err)
	}

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(t.Context())
	s2, err := d.Events(ctx, dockerapi.EventsOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	cancel()
	if _, err := s2.Next(); !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		t.Errorf("Next after cancel = %v, want context.Canceled", err)
	}

	close(d.events)
	s3, err := d.Events(t.Context(), dockerapi.EventsOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := s3.Next(); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Errorf("Next on a closed events channel = %v, want io.EOF", err)
	}
	if want := []string{"Events", "Events", "Events"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(d.calls, want) {
		t.Errorf("calls %q, want %q", d.calls, want)
	}
}

// TestFdNetwork: fdNetwork names the bridge through Docker's option only
// when one is given, marks IPv6 from the subnets and gives a name its own
// stable 64-digit id.
func TestFdNetwork(t *testing.T) {
	n := fdNetwork("custom", "dpcustom", "172.30.0.0/24", "fd00:dead::/64")
	if n.Name != "custom" || n.Driver != "bridge" || n.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.name"] != "dpcustom" || !n.EnableIPv6 {
		t.Errorf("network %+v, want bridge-driver custom on dpcustom with IPv6", n)
	}
	var subnets []netip.Prefix
	for _, c := range n.IPAM.Config {
		subnets = append(subnets, c.Subnet)
	}
	if want := []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.30.0.0/24"), netip.MustParsePrefix("fd00:dead::/64")}; !reflect.DeepEqual(subnets, want) {
		t.Errorf("subnets %v, want %v", subnets, want)
	}
	if len(n.ID) != 64 || n.ID != fdNetwork("custom", "").ID || n.ID == fdNetwork("other", "").ID {
		t.Errorf("id %q, want 64 digits, stable per name and distinct between names", n.ID)
	}
	plain := fdNetwork("plain", "", "10.9.0.0/24")
	if _, ok := plain.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.name"]; ok || plain.EnableIPv6 {
		t.Errorf("network %+v, want no bridge option and no IPv6", plain)
	}
}

// TestFdContainer: a container is running and has empty label, port and
// network maps for options to fill, and an option may change anything.
func TestFdContainer(t *testing.T) {
	c := fdContainer("web")
	if c.Name != "/web" || len(c.ID) != 64 || !c.State.Running || c.State.Status != "running" {
		t.Errorf("container %+v, want /web, a 64-digit id, running", c)
	}
	if c.Config.Labels == nil || c.NetworkSettings.Ports == nil || c.NetworkSettings.Networks == nil {
		t.Errorf("container %+v, want empty non-nil maps", c)
	}
	c2 := fdContainer("web", func(c *dockerapi.ContainerJSON) {
		c.NetworkSettings.Networks["bridge"] = &dockerapi.EndpointSettings{IPAddress: netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.2")}
	})
	if c2.ID != c.ID || c2.NetworkSettings.Networks["bridge"].IPAddress != netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.2") {
		t.Errorf("container %+v, want the same id and the option's endpoint", c2)
	}
}

// TestFdDeps: fdDeps extends the host's deps with the Docker fake and
// answers every other Docker-facing read as an empty host, or from the
// fake host's hooks, which it reads when called.
func TestFdDeps(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := t.Context()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	d := newFakeDocker()
	dd := fdDeps(h, d)
	if dd.docker != dockerAPI(d) || dd.root != h.root {
		t.Errorf("docker %v root %q, want the fake and the host's root", dd.docker, dd.root)
	}
	if cfg, err := dd.readConfig(dd.root); err != nil || !cfg.Enabled {
		t.Errorf("readConfig = %v, %v; want the host's configuration", cfg.Enabled, err)
	}
	if fdDeps(h, nil).docker != nil {
		t.Error("fdDeps(h, nil) set docker")
	}

	rs, err := dd.readVariant(ctx, h.env(), fwstate.V4, "legacy", []string{"filter"})
	if rs != nil || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("readVariant = %v, %v; want nil, nil", rs, err)
	}
	if socks, err := dd.sockets(); socks != nil || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("sockets = %v, %v; want none", socks, err)
	}
	if ifs, err := dd.interfaces(); ifs != nil || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("interfaces = %v, %v; want none", ifs, err)
	}
	if _, err := dd.routeGet(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1")}); !errors.Is(err, netstat.ErrNoRoute) {
		t.Errorf("routeGet = %v, want netstat.ErrNoRoute", err)
	}
	if on, known, err := dd.shieldsUp(ctx); on || known || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("shieldsUp = %v, %v, %v; want false, false, nil", on, known, err)
	}

	want := fhParse(t, fhSave)
	var gotFamily fwstate.Family
	var gotVariant string
	var gotTables []string
	h.onReadVariant = func(f fwstate.Family, variant string, tables []string) (*netfilter.Ruleset, error) {
		gotFamily, gotVariant, gotTables = f, variant, tables
		return want, nil
	}
	if rs, err := dd.readVariant(ctx, h.env(), fwstate.V6, "nft", []string{"filter", "raw"}); rs != want || err != nil ||
		gotFamily != fwstate.V6 || gotVariant != "nft" || !reflect.DeepEqual(gotTables, []string{"filter", "raw"}) {
		t.Errorf("readVariant = %v, %v for %v %q %q; want the hook's ruleset for the arguments", rs, err, gotFamily, gotVariant, gotTables)
	}
	h.onSockets = func() ([]netstat.Socket, error) { return []netstat.Socket{{Proto: netstat.ProtoTCP}}, nil }
	if socks, err := dd.sockets(); err != nil || len(socks) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("sockets = %v, %v; want the hook's socket", socks, err)
	}
	h.onInterfaces = func() ([]netstat.Interface, error) { return []netstat.Interface{{Name: "docker0"}}, nil }
	if ifs, err := dd.interfaces(); err != nil || len(ifs) != 1 || ifs[0].Name != "docker0" {
		t.Errorf("interfaces = %v, %v; want the hook's interface", ifs, err)
	}
	h.onRouteGet = func(q netstat.RouteQuery) (netstat.Route, error) {
		return netstat.Route{OutIface: "eth0", PrefSrc: q.Dst}, nil
	}
	if rt, err := dd.routeGet(netstat.RouteQuery{Dst: netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1")}); err != nil || rt.OutIface != "eth0" {
		t.Errorf("routeGet = %+v, %v; want the hook's route", rt, err)
	}
	h.onShieldsUp = func() (bool, bool, error) { return true, true, nil }
	if on, known, err := dd.shieldsUp(ctx); !on || !known || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("shieldsUp = %v, %v, %v; want true, true, nil", on, known, err)
	}
}

// TestFdShieldsUpVia: shields-up is tailscaled's preference, and a
// tailscaled that cannot be reached is not known to have it on.
func TestFdShieldsUpVia(t *testing.T) {
	boom := errors.New("fdtest: tailscaled failed")
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		prefs     func(context.Context) (*tslocal.Prefs, error)
		on, known bool
		err       error
	}{
		{"on", func(context.Context) (*tslocal.Prefs, error) { return &tslocal.Prefs{ShieldsUp: true}, nil }, true, true, nil},
		{"off", func(context.Context) (*tslocal.Prefs, error) { return &tslocal.Prefs{}, nil }, false, true, nil},
		{"unavailable", func(context.Context) (*tslocal.Prefs, error) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("tslocal: GET prefs: %w", tslocal.ErrUnavailable)
		}, false, false, nil},
		{"failed", func(context.Context) (*tslocal.Prefs, error) { return nil, boom }, false, false, boom},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			on, known, err := shieldsUpVia(tc.prefs)(t.Context())
			if on != tc.on || known != tc.known || !errors.Is(err, tc.err) {
				t.Errorf("shieldsUp = %v, %v, %v; want %v, %v, %v", on, known, err, tc.on, tc.known, tc.err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// fdDaemon serves the Docker API on a Unix socket in a short temporary
// directory and returns the socket's path.
func fdDaemon(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dir, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "dp")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = os.RemoveAll(dir) })
	mux := http.NewServeMux()
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /version", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"Version":"29.9.1","ApiVersion":"1.49","MinAPIVersion":"1.44"}`)
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1.49/info", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"ServerVersion":"29.9.1","FirewallBackend":{"Driver":"iptables"}}`)
	})
	mux.HandleFunc("GET /v1.49/events", func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"Type":"container","Action":"start","Actor":{"ID":"c1","Attributes":{"name":"web"}}}`+"\n")
	})
	l, err := net.Listen("unix", filepath.Join(dir, "d.sock"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	srv := httptest.NewUnstartedServer(mux)
	_ = srv.Listener.Close()
	srv.Listener = l
	srv.Start()
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	return filepath.Join(dir, "d.sock")
}

// TestFdDockerClient: the adapter passes the client's answers through,
// hands back the events stream, and returns no stream, not a nil pointer
// inside the interface, when the stream cannot be opened.
func TestFdDockerClient(t *testing.T) {
	c := newDockerClient(fdDaemon(t))
	info, err := c.Info(t.Context())
	if err != nil || info.ServerVersion != "29.9.1" || info.FirewallBackend == nil || info.FirewallBackend.Driver != "iptables" {
		t.Errorf("Info = %+v, %v; want Docker 29.9.1 with the iptables driver", info, err)
	}
	s, err := c.Events(t.Context(), dockerapi.EventsOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer func() { _ = s.Close() }()
	ev, err := s.Next()
	if err != nil || ev.Type != "container" || ev.Action != "start" || ev.Actor.Attributes["name"] != "web" {
		t.Errorf("Next = %+v, %v; want the container start of web", ev, err)
	}
	if _, err := s.Next(); !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
		t.Errorf("Next at the end of the stream = %v, want io.EOF", err)
	}

	down := newDockerClient(filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "none.sock"))
	if _, err := down.Info(t.Context()); !errors.Is(err, dockerapi.ErrUnavailable) {
		t.Errorf("Info without a daemon = %v, want dockerapi.ErrUnavailable", err)
	}
	if s, err := down.Events(t.Context(), dockerapi.EventsOptions{}); !errors.Is(err, dockerapi.ErrUnavailable) || s != nil {
		t.Errorf("Events without a daemon = %v, %v; want no stream and dockerapi.ErrUnavailable", s, err)
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

`docker-sources.tsx` exports `DockerSources`, with a doc comment saying each edit plans `firewall.docker.set-sources` with the one list it changes. It uses `darkraise-ui` components (`Button`, `Card` family, `Input`, `Label`, `RadioGroup`, `Table` family, `Textarea`) and `FirewallChange` as the neighbouring firewall components do, and follows their style (no semicolons, double quotes). All copy below is exact; the tests read it.

1. State: the draft of the private-sources textarea as `{base, text} | null`, the add form's draft (interface, original destination, original port, destination, port, protocol with default `tcp`), a problem message (empty when none) and the pending change (`{title, input}` or null). `docker.settings.privateSources`, `.forwardExemptions` and `docker.foreignForwards` may each be missing or null in the JSON (Go encodes a nil slice as `null`), so each is read as an empty list then. The textarea shows the current ranges joined by `\n`, unless the draft's `base` still equals that current text, in which case it shows the draft's `text`: a status that changes under an open edit therefore replaces the draft. The submitted ranges are the textarea's lines, each trimmed, blanks dropped. No client-side CIDR check: the action validates and the dialog shows its refusal.
2. Card "Private sources" (description: "Traffic from these ranges reaches every published port, whatever the container rules allow."): a `<form aria-label="Private sources">` with a `Label` "Private source ranges" tied by `htmlFor` to a `Textarea` (6 rows, monospace), the hint "One CIDR per line.", and a submit button "Set private sources" that is disabled while the submitted ranges equal the current ones. Submitting plans title `Set the private sources` with input `{privateSources: <the ranges>}` and nothing else.
3. Card "Forward exemptions" (description: "Port forwards that are not Docker's, which the block would otherwise deny."):
   - With no exemptions it shows the paragraph "No forward exemptions."; otherwise a `Table` with `aria-label="Forward exemptions"` and the columns Interface, Original destination, Original port, Destination, Port, Protocol and a last column whose header is screen-reader-only "Actions". A row shows `inInterface`, `origPort` and `port` as "any" when absent, the addresses in monospace, and a button "Remove" with `aria-label` `Remove exemption <n>` (1-based). It plans title `Remove a forward exemption` with input `{forwardExemptions: <the list without that row>}`; removing the last one sends `[]`.
   - When `foreignForwards` is not empty, a second table with the same columns and `aria-label="Proposed forward exemptions"`, each row with a button "Add" whose `aria-label` is `Add proposed exemption <n>`. It plans title `Add a forward exemption` with input `{forwardExemptions: <the current list followed by that proposal>}`. With none, no such table exists. Both tables are one component taking the label, the rows and a render function for the actions cell.
   - A `<form aria-label="Add forward exemption">` with text fields labelled exactly `In interface (optional)`, `Original destination`, `Original port (optional)`, `Destination` and `Destination port (optional)`, a protocol radio group (legend and group label "Protocol", options `tcp` and `udp`, default `tcp`, each option's `Label` tied to its radio) and a submit button "Add exemption". On submit: when the trimmed original destination or destination is empty, show `Enter the original destination and the destination.` and plan nothing; otherwise a port field that is not empty and is not a whole number from 1 to 65535 (digits only, so `80a` and `0` and `70000` all fail) shows `Ports are whole numbers from 1 to 65535.` and plans nothing. The message is a `<p role="alert">` inside the form, shown only while it is set and cleared by a valid submit. A valid submit plans title `Add a forward exemption` with input `{forwardExemptions: <the current list followed by the new exemption>}`; the new exemption has the trimmed `origDestination` and `destination` and `proto`, and `inInterface` (trimmed), `origPort` and `port` (numbers) only when their fields are not empty. No address-format check: the action validates.
4. One `FirewallChange` at the end with `action="firewall.docker.set-sources"`, the pending title (empty when none) and the pending input (`null` when none). Its `onClose` clears the pending change, the private-sources draft and the add form's draft.
5. Do not edit `types.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, `firewall-page.tsx` or any other file: Task 29 places the component.

Create `web/src/modules/firewall/exposure-page.test.tsx` with exactly this content. The test renders the whole `FirewallRoutes` at `/hosts/h1/firewall/exposure`, so it also proves that the route exists and that the page reads `hostId` from the route params (an unstubbed request answers 404 and fails the test).

```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { Route, Routes } from "react-router"
import { expect, test } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { fwExposure, fwStatus } from "./fixtures"
import FirewallRoutes from "./routes"
import type { ExposureRow, ExposureVerdict } from "./types"

const EXPOSURE = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/firewall/exposure"
const STATUS = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/firewall/status"

function epVerdict(cls: string, verdict: ExposureVerdict["verdict"], over: Partial<ExposureVerdict> = {}): ExposureVerdict {
  return { class: cls, verdict, ...over }
}

function epRows(): ExposureRow[] {
  return [
    {
      proto: "tcp", addr: "0.0.0.0", port: 22, family: "v4", process: "sshd",
      classes: [
        epVerdict("internet", "open", { decidedBy: "ufw-user-input#2 allow 22/tcp" }),
        epVerdict("private", "open", { range: "10.0.0.0/8", decidedBy: "ufw-user-input#2 allow 22/tcp" }),
        epVerdict("tailnet", "open", { note: "host firewall; tailnet policy not evaluated" }),
        epVerdict("localhost", "open"),
      ],
    },
    {
      proto: "tcp", addr: "0.0.0.0", port: 8080, family: "v4",
      container: { name: "web", binding: { selector: "web", hostPort: 8080, proto: "tcp" }, containerPort: 80, proxied: false },
      classes: [
        epVerdict("internet", "partial", {
          allowed: [
            { sources: ["203.0.113.0/24"], ifaces: ["eth0"], decidedBy: "dp-b-0123456789ab line 2" },
            { sources: ["198.51.100.0/24", "192.0.2.0/24"], srcPorts: ["53"], decidedBy: "dp-b-0123456789ab line 3" },
          ],
        }),
        epVerdict("private", "open", { range: "10.0.0.0/8", decidedBy: "DOCKER-USER line 5" }),
        epVerdict("tailnet", "closed", { decidedBy: "Tailscale shields-up" }),
      ],
    },
    {
      proto: "udp", addr: "::", port: 5353, family: "v6",
      container: { name: "dns", binding: { selector: "dns", hostPort: 5353, proto: "udp" }, containerPort: 53, proxied: true },
      classes: [epVerdict("internet", "closed", { decidedBy: "ufw6-user-input policy" })],
    },
    {
      proto: "tcp", addr: "127.0.0.1", port: 5432, family: "v4", process: "postgres",
      classes: [epVerdict("internet", "closed", { decidedBy: "bound to loopback" }), epVerdict("localhost", "open")],
    },
    {
      proto: "tcp", addr: "0.0.0.0", port: 3000, family: "v4", process: "node",
      classes: [epVerdict("internet", "unknown", { note: "mark set outside netfilter" })],
    },
  ]
}

function epRender(routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const calls = stubFetch({ [EXPOSURE]: { body: fwExposure({ rows: epRows() }) }, [STATUS]: { body: fwStatus() }, ...routes })
  const result = renderWithProviders(
    <Routes>
      <Route path="/hosts/:hostId/firewall/*" element={<FirewallRoutes hostId="h1" />} />
    </Routes>,
    { path: "/hosts/h1/firewall/exposure" },
  )
  return { calls, ...result }
}

async function epTable() {
  return screen.findByRole("table", { name: "Exposure" })
}

// epPorts lists the rows shown as protocol/port, in table order.
function epPorts(table: HTMLElement): string[] {
  return within(table)
    .getAllByRole("row")
    .slice(1)
    .map((r) => {
      const cells = within(r).getAllByRole("cell")
      return `${cells[0]?.textContent ?? ""}/${cells[2]?.textContent ?? ""}`
    })
}

function epItems(table: HTMLElement, label: string): string[] {
  return within(within(table).getByRole("list", { name: label })).getAllByRole("listitem").map((li) => li.textContent ?? "")
}

test("lists every listening port with its listener, in the server's order", async () => {
  epRender()
  const table = await epTable()
  const rows = within(table).getAllByRole("row").slice(1).map((r) => within(r).getAllByRole("cell").slice(0, 5).map((c) => c.textContent))
  expect(rows).toEqual([
    ["tcp", "0.0.0.0", "22", "v4", "sshd"],
    ["tcp", "0.0.0.0", "8080", "v4", "container web, port 80"],
    ["udp", "::", "5353", "v6", "container dns, port 53 (docker-proxy)"],
    ["tcp", "127.0.0.1", "5432", "v4", "postgres"],
    ["tcp", "0.0.0.0", "3000", "v4", "node"],
  ])
})

test("shows each source class's verdict with what decides it", async () => {
  epRender()
  const table = await epTable()
  expect(epItems(table, "Reachability of tcp 0.0.0.0 port 22")).toEqual([
    "internet: open — decided by ufw-user-input#2 allow 22/tcp",
    "private 10.0.0.0/8: open — decided by ufw-user-input#2 allow 22/tcp",
    "tailnet: open — host firewall; tailnet policy not evaluated",
    "localhost: open",
  ])
  expect(epItems(table, "Reachability of tcp 0.0.0.0 port 8080")).toEqual([
    "internet: partial — allowed from 203.0.113.0/24 on eth0 (dp-b-0123456789ab line 2); allowed from 198.51.100.0/24, 192.0.2.0/24 from source ports 53 (dp-b-0123456789ab line 3)",
    "private 10.0.0.0/8: open — decided by DOCKER-USER line 5",
    "tailnet: closed — decided by Tailscale shields-up",
  ])
  expect(epItems(table, "Reachability of tcp 127.0.0.1 port 5432")).toEqual(["internet: closed — decided by bound to loopback", "localhost: open"])
  expect(epItems(table, "Reachability of tcp 0.0.0.0 port 3000")).toEqual(["internet: unknown — mark set outside netfilter"])
})

test("the protocol and family filters narrow the rows", async () => {
  epRender()
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await epTable()
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("radio", { name: "udp" }))

  await user.click(screen.getByRole("radio", { name: "All protocols" }))

  await user.click(screen.getByRole("radio", { name: "All families" }))
  expect(epPorts(await epTable())).toHaveLength(5)
})

test("the internet filter keeps the ports that are open, partly open or undecided for the internet", async () => {
  epRender()
  const user = userEvent.setup()
  await epTable()
  await user.click(screen.getByRole("checkbox", { name: "Only ports the internet can reach" }))

test("the notes are listed above the table", async () => {

  expect((await screen.findByText("No listening ports")).textContent).toBe("No listening ports")
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. Create `exposure-page.tsx` exporting `ExposurePage()` with a doc comment. It reads `hostId` with `useParams()` (default `""`, as `pages/host.tsx` does) and fetches with `useQuery`: `queryKey: exposureQueryKey(hostId)`, `queryFn: () => readResource<ExposureView>(hostId, FIREWALL_MODULE, "exposure")`. Layout, on the pattern of `SnapshotsPage` in `firewall-page.tsx`: a `flex flex-col gap-4` div holding a `Link to=".." relative="path"` with the text `Back to the firewall` (same classes as `SnapshotsPage`'s) and a `Card` titled `Exposure` whose content is the state below.
2. States. Pending: `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the exposure" />`. Error: a destructive `Alert` with `role="alert"` whose description is `errorMessage(error)` and nothing else. Data: an `ExposureTable` component.
3. `ExposureTable` keeps its filter state in `useState` (no URL state). Notes first: when `notes` is non-empty, a `warning` `Alert` with `role="status"` holding `<ul aria-label="Exposure notes">` with one `<li>` per note; the notes show in every data state. When `rows` is empty, show the notes and an `EmptyState` titled `No listening ports` with the description `Nothing on this host is listening for connections.`; render no filters then.
4. Filters, above the table: two radio fieldsets built as `Choice` in `rule-form.tsx` is (a `fieldset` with a `legend`, a `RadioGroup` with `aria-label` equal to the legend, and a `RadioGroupItem` with its `Label` per option, ids `exp-<name>-<value>`). `Protocol` has the options `All protocols` (value `all`), `tcp` and `udp`; `Family` has `All families` (value `all`), `v4` and `v6`. Third, a `Checkbox` (id `exp-internet`) labelled `Only ports the internet can reach`, which keeps a row only when one of its classes has `class` `internet` and a verdict of `open`, `partial` or `unknown`. A row is shown when it passes all three filters; the server's order is kept. When no row passes, show an `EmptyState` titled `No rows match the filters` with the description `Change the filters to see the other listening ports.` in place of the table and keep the filters on screen.
5. The table has `aria-label="Exposure"` and the headers `Protocol`, `Address`, `Port`, `Family`, `Listener`, `Reachable from`, one row per shown `ExposureRow` keyed by `proto/addr/port/family`. The first four cells are `proto`, `addr` (monospace), `port` and `family`. `Listener` is `container <name>, port <containerPort>` for a row with a `container`, followed by ` (docker-proxy)` when `proxied` is true; otherwise `process`, or `—` when it is absent or empty.
6. `Reachable from` is `<ul aria-label="Reachability of <proto> <addr> port <port>">` with one `<li>` per class verdict, in the given order. The `<li>` is a `<span>` with `<label>: `, then a small `Badge` whose text is the verdict, then, when the detail below is not empty, a small muted `<span>` with ` — <detail>`. The label is `private <range>` when `class` is `private` and `range` is set, otherwise the `class`. The detail joins these parts with `; ` in this order: `decided by <decidedBy>` when `decidedBy` is set; for each `allowed` entry in order, `allowed from <sources joined by ", ">`, then ` on <ifaces joined by ", ">` when it has ifaces, then ` from source ports <srcPorts joined by ", ">` when it has source ports, then ` (<the entry's decidedBy>)`; and the `note` last when set. Badge variants: `open` destructive, `partial` default, `unknown` secondary, `closed` and `filtered` outline; the verdict word always appears as text, never colour alone.

```go
package dockerfw

import (
	"bytes"
	"net/netip"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

func bkA(s string) netip.Addr   { return netip.MustParseAddr(s) }
func bkP(s string) netip.Prefix { return netip.MustParsePrefix(s) }
func bkPs(s ...string) []netip.Prefix {
	var out []netip.Prefix
	for _, p := range s {
		out = append(out, bkP(p))
	}
	return out
}

// bkRuleset parses restore text into the ruleset iptables-restore would load.
func bkRuleset(t *testing.T, text []byte) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(bytes.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse restore input: %v\n%s", err, text)
	}
	return rs
}

// bkInput holds three bindings: aaaaaaaaaaaa is published on both families,
// bbbbbbbbbbbb on IPv4 only and cccccccccccc on IPv6 only.
func bkInput() BlockInput {
	s := DefaultSettings()
	s.ForwardExemptions = []Exemption{
		{InInterface: "eth1", OrigDestination: bkA("203.0.113.9"), OrigPort: 8080, Destination: bkA("10.9.0.5"), Proto: "tcp", Port: 80},
		{OrigDestination: bkA("2001:db8::9"), Destination: bkA("2001:db8:1::5"), Proto: "udp"},
	}
	return BlockInput{
		CustomBridges: []string{"dpcustom"},
		Settings:      s,
		Lines: []BindingLine{
			{Proto: "tcp", ContainerAddr: bkA("172.17.0.2"), ContainerPort: 80, HostPort: 8080, Chain: "dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa"},
			{Proto: "tcp", ContainerAddr: bkA("172.30.0.2"), ContainerPort: 80, HostAddr: bkA("203.0.113.7"), HostPort: 9090, Chain: "dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb"},
			{Proto: "udp", ContainerAddr: bkA("fd00:dead::2"), ContainerPort: 53, HostAddr: bkA("2001:db8::7"), HostPort: 5353, Chain: "dp-b-cccccccccccc"},
			{Proto: "tcp", ContainerAddr: bkA("fd00:dead::3"), ContainerPort: 80, HostPort: 8080, Chain: "dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa"},
		},
		Chains: []BindingChain{
			{Name: "dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa", Deny: bkPs("203.0.113.0/24", "2001:db8:bad::/48")},
			{Name: "dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb", Allow: bkPs("198.51.100.0/24")},
			{Name: "dp-b-cccccccccccc", Allow: bkPs("2001:db8:aa::/48")},
		},
	}
}

func TestBkRender(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		in     BlockInput
		family fwstate.Family
		want   string
	}{
		{"IPv4 with bridges, exemptions, bindings and chains", bkInput(), fwstate.V4, bkWantV4},
		{"IPv6 keeps only its own entries", bkInput(), fwstate.V6, bkWantV6},
		{"no settings, bindings or bridges still gates private destinations", BlockInput{}, fwstate.V6, bkWantV6Empty},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := string(Render(tt.in, tt.family)); got != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("Render =\n%s\nwant\n%s", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBkRenderChainFamilies(t *testing.T) {
	in := BlockInput{
		Settings: DefaultSettings(),
		Lines: []BindingLine{
			{Proto: "tcp", ContainerAddr: bkA("172.30.0.2"), ContainerPort: 80, HostPort: 9090, Chain: "dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb"},
			{Proto: "tcp", ContainerAddr: bkA("fd00:dead::2"), ContainerPort: 80, HostPort: 9090, Chain: "dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb"},
		},
		Chains: []BindingChain{{Name: "dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb", Deny: bkPs("203.0.113.0/24"), Allow: bkPs("198.51.100.0/24")}},
	}
	chain := func(f fwstate.Family) []string {
		var out []string
		for _, l := range strings.Split(string(Render(in, f)), "\n") {
			if strings.HasPrefix(l, "-A dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb ") {
				out = append(out, l)
			}
		}
		return out
	}
	wantV4 := []string{
		"-A dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb -s 203.0.113.0/24 -j darkpanel-docker-deny",
		"-A dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j ufw-user-forward",
		"-A dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb -j darkpanel-docker-deny",
	}
	// An allow list with no source of the family lets nothing of it through.
	wantV6 := []string{"-A dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb -j darkpanel-docker-deny"}
	if got := chain(fwstate.V4); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, wantV4) {
		t.Errorf("IPv4 chain = %q, want %q", got, wantV4)
	}
	if got := chain(fwstate.V6); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, wantV6) {
		t.Errorf("IPv6 chain = %q, want %q", got, wantV6)
	}
}

func TestBkRenderParses(t *testing.T) {
	wantRules := map[fwstate.Family]map[string]int{
		fwstate.V4: {"ufw-user-forward": 0, "DOCKER-USER": 17, "darkpanel-docker-bindings": 3, "darkpanel-docker-deny": 2, "dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa": 3, "dp-b-bbbbbbbbbbbb": 2},
		fwstate.V6: {"ufw6-user-forward": 0, "DOCKER-USER": 13, "darkpanel-docker-bindings": 3, "darkpanel-docker-deny": 2, "dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa": 3, "dp-b-cccccccccccc": 2},
	}
	for f, want := range wantRules {
		filter := bkRuleset(t, Render(bkInput(), f)).Table("filter")
		if filter == nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s: no filter table", f)
		}
		got := map[string]int{}
		for _, c := range filter.Chains {
			got[c.Name] = len(c.Rules)
			for _, r := range c.Rules {
				if r.Opaque() {
					t.Errorf("%s: rule %q is opaque: %v", f, r.Text, r.Unsupported)
				}
				if r.Target.Name != "" && r.Target.Name != "RETURN" && r.Target.Name != "DROP" && r.Target.Name != "LOG" && !r.Target.Chain {
					t.Errorf("%s: rule %q does not jump to a declared chain", f, r.Text)
				}
			}
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: rules per chain = %v, want %v", f, got, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestBkBlockRules(t *testing.T) {
	text := Render(bkInput(), fwstate.V4)
	got, err := BlockRules(text)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("BlockRules: %v", err)
	}
	if want := bkRuleset(t, text); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("BlockRules differs from the restore parser's ruleset")
	}
	if _, err := BlockRules([]byte("-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n")); err == nil {
		t.Error("BlockRules accepted input with no table")
	}
}

const (
	bkAfter = "# rules.input-after\n*filter\n:ufw-after-input - [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n"
	bkBody  = "*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\nCOMMIT\n"
	bkBegin = "# BEGIN DARKPANEL docker\n"
	bkEnd   = "# END DARKPANEL docker\n"
	bkOther = "# BEGIN DARKPANEL firewall/other\n-A x\n# END DARKPANEL firewall/other\n"
)

func TestBkWithBlock(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name, file, block, want string
		wantErr                 bool
	}{
		{name: "appends to a file", file: bkAfter, block: bkBody, want: bkAfter + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd},
		{name: "appends after a last line without a newline", file: "a\nCOMMIT", block: bkBody, want: "a\nCOMMIT\n" + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd},
		{name: "appends to an empty file", file: "", block: bkBody, want: bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd},
		{name: "ends an unterminated block text with a newline", file: bkAfter, block: "COMMIT", want: bkAfter + bkBegin + "COMMIT\n" + bkEnd},
		{name: "replaces the block in place", file: "before\n" + bkBegin + "*filter\nold\nCOMMIT\n" + bkEnd + "after\n", block: bkBody, want: "before\n" + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd + "after\n"},
		{name: "leaves another module's block alone", file: bkOther + bkAfter, block: bkBody, want: bkOther + bkAfter + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd},
		{name: "refuses a duplicated block", file: bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd, block: bkBody, wantErr: true},
		{name: "refuses a nested block", file: bkBegin + bkOther + bkEnd, block: bkBody, wantErr: true},
		{name: "refuses an unterminated block", file: bkAfter + bkBegin + bkBody, block: bkBody, wantErr: true},
		{name: "refuses an end marker without its beginning", file: bkAfter + bkEnd, block: bkBody, wantErr: true},
		{name: "refuses a marker line ending in whitespace", file: "# BEGIN DARKPANEL docker \n" + bkBody + bkEnd, block: bkBody, wantErr: true},
		{name: "refuses a block that holds a marker line", file: bkAfter, block: "# END DARKPANEL docker\n", wantErr: true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := WithBlock([]byte(tt.file), []byte(tt.block))
			if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
			}
			if err == nil && string(got) != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("WithBlock =\n%q\nwant\n%q", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBkWithBlockIsIdempotent(t *testing.T) {
	once, err := WithBlock([]byte(bkAfter), []byte(bkBody))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	twice, err := WithBlock(once, []byte(bkBody))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(once, twice) {
		t.Errorf("a second WithBlock changed the file:\n%q\n%q", once, twice)
	}
}

func TestBkWithoutBlock(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name, file, want string
		wantErr          bool
	}{
		{name: "removes the block and its markers", file: bkAfter + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd, want: bkAfter},
		{name: "keeps the text on both sides", file: "before\n" + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd + "after\n", want: "before\nafter\n"},
		{name: "keeps another module's block", file: bkOther + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd, want: bkOther},
		{name: "returns a file without the block as it is", file: "a\nCOMMIT", want: "a\nCOMMIT"},
		{name: "refuses an unterminated block", file: bkBegin + bkBody, wantErr: true},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := WithoutBlock([]byte(tt.file))
			if (err != nil) != tt.wantErr {
				t.Fatalf("err = %v, wantErr %v", err, tt.wantErr)
			}
			if err == nil && string(got) != tt.want {
				t.Errorf("WithoutBlock = %q, want %q", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestBkBlockOf(t *testing.T) {
	file := []byte(bkAfter + bkBegin + bkBody + bkEnd + "tail\n")
	block, ok, err := BlockOf(file)
	if err != nil || !ok || string(block) != bkBody {
		t.Errorf("BlockOf = %q, %v, %v; want the block's body", block, ok, err)
	}
	if block, ok, err := BlockOf([]byte(bkAfter)); err != nil || ok || block != nil {
		t.Errorf("BlockOf without a block = %q, %v, %v; want nil, false, nil", block, ok, err)
	}
	for name, bad := range map[string]string{
		"duplicated":   bkBegin + bkEnd + bkBegin + bkEnd,
		"nested":       bkBegin + bkOther + bkEnd,
		"unterminated": bkBegin + bkBody,
	} {
		if _, _, err := BlockOf([]byte(bad)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("BlockOf accepted a %s block", name)
		}
	}
	// What WithBlock writes is what BlockOf reads back.
	rendered := Render(bkInput(), fwstate.V4)
	written, err := WithBlock([]byte(bkAfter), rendered)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if back, ok, err := BlockOf(written); err != nil || !ok || !bytes.Equal(back, rendered) {
		t.Errorf("BlockOf(WithBlock(f, b)) = %q, %v, %v; want b", back, ok, err)
	}
}

func TestBkWithoutBlockUndoesWithBlock(t *testing.T) {
	for _, file := range []string{"", bkAfter, bkOther + bkAfter, "before\n" + bkBegin + "old\n" + bkEnd + "after\n"} {
		with, err := WithBlock([]byte(file), []byte(bkBody))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		without, err := WithoutBlock(with)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		want := file
		if i := strings.Index(file, bkBegin); i >= 0 {
			want = "before\nafter\n"
		}
		if string(without) != want {
			t.Errorf("WithoutBlock(WithBlock(%q)) = %q, want %q", file, without, want)
		}
	}
}

func TestBkOwned(t *testing.T) {
	for chain, want := range map[string]bool{
		"DOCKER-USER":               true,
		"darkpanel-docker-bindings": true,
		"darkpanel-docker-deny":     true,
		"darkpanel-anything":        true,
		"dp-b-0123456789ab":         true,
		"DOCKER":                    false,
		"DOCKER-FORWARD":            false,
		"ufw-user-forward":          false,
		"docker-user":               false,
		"dp-c-0123456789ab":         false,
		"FORWARD":                   false,
	} {
		if got := Owned(chain); got != want {
			t.Errorf("Owned(%q) = %v, want %v", chain, got, want)
		}
	}
}

// bkChain reads one chain from iptables-save style text, as the loaded state
// holds it; declared are the other chains its rules jump to.
func bkChain(t *testing.T, name, rules string, declared ...string) *netfilter.Chain {
	t.Helper()
	text := "*filter\n:" + name + " - [0:0]\n"
	for _, d := range declared {
		text += ":" + d + " - [0:0]\n"
	}
	text += rules + "COMMIT\n"
	rs, err := netfilter.Parse(strings.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse save text: %v", err)
	}
	return rs.Table("filter").Chain(name)
}

func bkTexts(rules []netfilter.Rule) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, r := range rules {
		out = append(out, r.Text)
	}
	return out
}

func TestBkForeign(t *testing.T) {
	known := func(f fwstate.Family, chain string) []netfilter.Rule {
		return bkRuleset(t, Render(bkInput(), f)).Table("filter").Chain(chain).Rules
	}
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		family fwstate.Family
		chain  *netfilter.Chain
		known  []netfilter.Rule
		want   []string
	}{
		{
			name:   "a rule among the block's lines and a conditional return are foreign, in chain order",
			family: fwstate.V4,
			chain: bkChain(t, "DOCKER-USER", `-A DOCKER-USER -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j RETURN
-A DOCKER-USER -i docker0 -j RETURN
-A DOCKER-USER -s 192.0.2.0/24 -j DROP
-A DOCKER-USER -i br-+ -j RETURN
-A DOCKER-USER -s 10.0.0.0/8 -j RETURN
-A DOCKER-USER -i eth0 -j RETURN
-A DOCKER-USER -m conntrack --ctstate DNAT -j darkpanel-docker-bindings
-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN
`, "darkpanel-docker-bindings"),
			known: known(fwstate.V4, "DOCKER-USER"),
			want:  []string{"-A DOCKER-USER -s 192.0.2.0/24 -j DROP", "-A DOCKER-USER -i eth0 -j RETURN"},
		},
		{
			name:   "Docker's default chain holds no foreign rule",
			family: fwstate.V4,
			chain:  bkChain(t, "DOCKER-USER", "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n"),
			want:   nil,
		},
		{
			name:   "a second copy of a known rule is not foreign",
			family: fwstate.V4,
			chain:  bkChain(t, "DOCKER-USER", "-A DOCKER-USER -i docker0 -j RETURN\n-A DOCKER-USER -i docker0 -j RETURN\n"),
			known:  known(fwstate.V4, "DOCKER-USER"),
			want:   nil,
		},
		{
			name:   "rules compare by key, not by text",
			family: fwstate.V4,
			chain: bkChain(t, "darkpanel-docker-bindings", `-A darkpanel-docker-bindings -d 172.17.0.2/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 -j dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa
-A darkpanel-docker-bindings -d 172.17.0.9/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 -j dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa
`, "dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa"),
			known: known(fwstate.V4, "darkpanel-docker-bindings"),
			want:  []string{"-A darkpanel-docker-bindings -d 172.17.0.9/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -m conntrack --ctorigdstport 8080 -j dp-b-aaaaaaaaaaaa"},
		},
		{
			name:   "the family selects the defaults a key fills in",
			family: fwstate.V6,
			chain:  bkChain(t, "DOCKER-USER", "-A DOCKER-USER -s 2001:db8::1/128 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp6-port-unreachable\n"),
			known:  bkRuleset(t, []byte("*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -s 2001:db8::1 -j REJECT\nCOMMIT\n")).Table("filter").Chain("DOCKER-USER").Rules,
			want:   nil,
		},
		{name: "no chain has no foreign rule", family: fwstate.V4, chain: nil, want: nil},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := bkTexts(Foreign(tt.chain, tt.known, tt.family)); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("Foreign = %q, want %q", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
	t.Run("the same rule under the other family is foreign", func(t *testing.T) {
		chain := bkChain(t, "DOCKER-USER", "-A DOCKER-USER -s 2001:db8::1/128 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp6-port-unreachable\n")
		k := bkRuleset(t, []byte("*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -s 2001:db8::1 -j REJECT\nCOMMIT\n")).Table("filter").Chain("DOCKER-USER").Rules
		if got := Foreign(chain, k, fwstate.V4); len(got) != 1 {
			t.Errorf("Foreign under V4 = %q, want the one rule", bkTexts(got))
		}
	})
}
```
