- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `block.go` with the constants and types of Contracts "dockerfw block" (a doc comment on each exported identifier), then:

1. `Render(in BlockInput, f fwstate.Family) []byte` writes spec 2.6's filter section for one family, every line ending in `\n`, from `*filter` to `COMMIT`, and reads no state. An entry belongs to the family of its address: a `BindingLine` by `ContainerAddr`, a `privateSources` prefix by its address, a forward exemption by `Exemption.Family()`, a deny or allow prefix by its address. A `BindingChain` belongs to the family when at least one `BindingLine` of that family names it. Everything of the other family is left out. The lines, in this order (`<user>` is `ufw-user-forward` for V4 and `ufw6-user-forward` for V6; `<br>` is each `CustomBridges` entry in order; a prefix prints as `netip.Prefix.String()` and an address as `netip.Addr.String()` with no mask):
   - declarations `:<user> - [0:0]`, `:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]`, `:darkpanel-docker-bindings - [0:0]`, `:darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]`, then `:<chain> - [0:0]` for each chain of the family in `Chains` order;
   - `-A DOCKER-USER -m conntrack --ctstate RELATED,ESTABLISHED -j RETURN`, `-A DOCKER-USER -i docker0 -j RETURN`, `-A DOCKER-USER -i br-+ -j RETURN`, `-A DOCKER-USER -i <br> -j RETURN` per bridge, `-A DOCKER-USER -s <prefix> -j RETURN` per private source of the family in `Settings` order;
   - one line per exemption of the family in `Settings` order: `-A DOCKER-USER`, then ` -i <InInterface>` when set, then ` -m conntrack --ctstate DNAT --ctorigdst <OrigDestination>`, then ` --ctorigdstport <OrigPort>` when non-zero, then ` -p <Proto> -d <Destination>`, then ` --dport <Port>` when non-zero, then ` -j RETURN`;
   - `-A DOCKER-USER -m conntrack --ctstate DNAT -j darkpanel-docker-bindings`, `-A DOCKER-USER -o docker0 -j darkpanel-docker-deny`, `-A DOCKER-USER -o br-+ -j darkpanel-docker-deny`, `-A DOCKER-USER -o <br> -j darkpanel-docker-deny` per bridge;
   - the private destinations, which come from no setting: V4 prints `-A DOCKER-USER -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j darkpanel-docker-deny`, then the same for `172.16.0.0/12` and `192.168.0.0/16`; V6 prints one line with `fc00::/7`; then `-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN`;
   - per `BindingLine` of the family in `Lines` order: `-A darkpanel-docker-bindings -p <Proto> -d <ContainerAddr> --dport <ContainerPort> -m conntrack`, then ` --ctorigdst <HostAddr>` only when `HostAddr` is valid, then ` --ctorigdstport <HostPort> -j <Chain>`; then `-A darkpanel-docker-bindings -j darkpanel-docker-deny`;
   - per chain of the family in `Chains` order: `-A <name> -s <prefix> -j darkpanel-docker-deny` for each `Deny` prefix of the family in order; then the allow lines `-A <name> -s <prefix> -j <user>`: one per `Allow` prefix of the family in order, or, when `Allow` is empty, one with `0.0.0.0/0` (V4) or `::/0` (V6); an `Allow` that is not empty but holds no prefix of the family gives no allow line, so nothing of that family gets through; then `-A <name> -j darkpanel-docker-deny`;
   - `-A darkpanel-docker-deny -m limit --limit 3/min -j LOG --log-prefix "[DARKPANEL DOCKER DENY] "` built from `LogPrefix` (the prefix keeps its trailing space inside the quotes), `-A darkpanel-docker-deny -j DROP`, `COMMIT`.
2. Markers. A marker line is `# BEGIN DARKPANEL <id>` or `# END DARKPANEL <id>`; `BlockID` is `docker`, so this block's lines are `# BEGIN DARKPANEL docker` and `# END DARKPANEL docker`. Write one unexported scan that reads every marker line of any id in a file the way `scanMarkers` in `internal/platform/blocks.go` does with the prefix `#` and returns each block's begin and end line index. It refuses, with an error starting `dockerfw:`, a block that begins inside another, a block id that appears twice, an end marker whose id is not the open block's, a block with no end marker, and a marker line that ends in a space, tab or carriage return.
3. `BlockOf(file)` runs the scan and returns the lines strictly between this block's markers (newlines kept), `true`, or `nil, false, nil` when the file has no block; a scan error is returned as it is. `WithBlock(file, block)` wraps `block` in the two marker lines (adding a final newline to `block` when it lacks one), replaces the existing block's lines from its begin marker to its end marker, or, when the file has no block, appends the wrapped block after the file (adding a newline first when the file is not empty and lacks one); it scans the result and returns the scan's error when `block` held a marker line. Text before and after the block, and other modules' blocks, stay byte for byte. `WithoutBlock(file)` removes the lines from the begin marker to the end marker inclusive and returns a file with no block unchanged, the same bytes.
4. `Owned(chain)` is true for `DOCKER-USER` and any name starting `darkpanel-` or `dp-b-`. `BlockRules(block)` is `netfilter.ParseRestore` over the bytes.
5. `Foreign(chain, known, f)` returns, in chain order, every rule of `chain` whose `netfilter.Key(rule, f == fwstate.V6)` equals the key of no rule in `known` and is not an unconditional `-j RETURN` (the key `-j RETURN`: no address, interface, protocol or match). Keys are compared as a set, so a second copy of a known rule is not foreign. A nil `chain` returns nil.

```go
// TestDtgFilesOverlay: the files a change writes replace the configured
// after files in the configuration the predictor reads and in the target's
// configurations, keeping each file's mode and owner; the caller's
// configuration is left alone.
func TestDtgFilesOverlay(t *testing.T) {
	h := newTGHost(t, tgRunning, true)
	var seen map[string][]byte
	h.f.d.predict = func(cfg fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, _ fwstate.Transition) (fwstate.Loaded, error) {
		seen = map[string][]byte{}
		for p, e := range cfg.Files {
			seen[p] = e.Data
		}
		return cur, nil
	}
	cfg0 := h.config()
	before4, before6, beforeRules := cfg0.Files[dtgAfter4], cfg0.Files[dtgAfter6], cfg0.Files["/etc/ufw/before.rules"]
	files := map[string][]byte{dtgAfter4: dtgAfterWith(), dtgAfter6: []byte("*filter\n# after6 with block\nCOMMIT\n")}

	tg, err := h.f.predictTarget(cfg0, h.cur(), change{files: files, reload: true})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, p := range []string{dtgAfter4, dtgAfter6} {
		if string(seen[p]) != string(files[p]) {
			t.Errorf("predictor read %s as %q, want the written file %q", p, seen[p], files[p])
		}
		for name, cfg := range map[string]fwstate.Config{"cfgN": tg.cfgN, "final": tg.final} {
			got := cfg.Files[p]
			if !got.Present || string(got.Data) != string(files[p]) || got.Mode != cfg0.Files[p].Mode || got.UID != cfg0.Files[p].UID {
				t.Errorf("%s holds %s as %+v, want the written data with mode and owner of %+v", name, p, got, cfg0.Files[p])
			}
		}
	}
	if string(seen["/etc/ufw/before.rules"]) != string(beforeRules.Data) {
		t.Errorf("the predictor read before.rules as %q, want it unchanged", seen["/etc/ufw/before.rules"])
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(cfg0.Files[dtgAfter4], before4) || !reflect.DeepEqual(cfg0.Files[dtgAfter6], before6) {
		t.Error("predictTarget changed the caller's configuration")
	}
}

// TestDtgFilesRefused: only the two after files can be written, and a file
// UFW cannot start without is a plain error.
func TestDtgFilesRefused(t *testing.T) {
	for _, path := range []string{"/etc/ufw/before.rules", "/etc/ufw/user.rules", "/etc/passwd", "etc/ufw/after.rules"} {
		h := newTGHost(t, tgRunning, true)
		_, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{files: map[string][]byte{path: []byte("x\n")}, reload: true})
		var coded *errcode.Error
		if err == nil || errors.As(err, &coded) || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "firewall:") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), path) {
			t.Errorf("file %q: %v, want a plain firewall error naming the path", path, err)
		}
	}
	h := newTGHost(t, tgRunning, true)
	if err := os.Remove(filepath.Join(h.root, dtgAfter6)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	_, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{files: map[string][]byte{dtgAfter6: []byte("x\n")}, reload: true})
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), dtgAfter6+" is missing") {
		t.Errorf("a missing after6.rules: %v, want an error saying it is missing", err)
	}
}

// TestDtgReload: reload makes an action on an active UFW a reload, which no
// other field does; with UFW stopped or being stopped it adds nothing.
func TestDtgReload(t *testing.T) {
	files := map[string][]byte{dtgAfter4: dtgAfterWith()}
	cases := []struct {
		name    string
		save    string
		enabled bool
		change  change
		tr      fwstate.Transition
		cmds    []string
	}{
		{"reload on an active UFW", tgRunning, true, change{files: files, reload: true}, fwstate.TransReload, []string{"reload"}},
		{"reload alone on an active UFW", tgRunning, true, change{reload: true}, fwstate.TransReload, []string{"reload"}},
		{"reload with enable on an active UFW", tgRunning, true, change{enable: &yes, reload: true}, fwstate.TransReload, []string{"reload"}},
		{"files without reload", tgRunning, true, change{files: files}, fwstate.TransNone, nil},
		{"the flag and the rows are not predicted", tgRunning, true, change{flag: &yes, rowsDel: []string{"01J00000000000000000000009"}}, fwstate.TransNone, nil},
		{"reload on a stopped UFW", tgStopped, false, change{files: files, reload: true}, fwstate.TransNone, nil},
		{"reload with enable starts UFW once", tgStopped, false, change{enable: &yes, files: files, reload: true}, fwstate.TransEnable, []string{"--force enable"}},
		{"reload with disable stops UFW", tgRunning, true, change{enable: &no, files: files, reload: true}, fwstate.TransDisable, []string{"disable"}},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newTGHost(t, c.save, c.enabled)
			tg, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), c.change)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if tg.tr != c.tr || !reflect.DeepEqual(tgCmds(tg.cmds), c.cmds) {
				t.Errorf("transition %s with %q, want %s with %q", tg.tr, tgCmds(tg.cmds), c.tr, c.cmds)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDtgPredictsTheBlock: with the real predictor, a block written to
// after.rules replaces what DOCKER-USER holds after a reload, and an
// unchanged after.rules leaves Docker's chain alone.
func TestDtgPredictsTheBlock(t *testing.T) {
	h := newTGHost(t, dtgDocker, true)
	h.f.d.predict = predict.Predict
	tg, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{files: map[string][]byte{dtgAfter4: dtgAfterWith(), dtgAfter6: dtgAfterWith()}, reload: true})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for name, rs := range map[string]*netfilter.Ruleset{"v4": tg.pred.V4, "v6": tg.pred.V6} {
		du := dtgChain(rs, "DOCKER-USER")
		if du == nil || len(du.Rules) != 4 || du.Rules[1].Text != "-A DOCKER-USER -i docker0 -j RETURN" {
			t.Errorf("%s DOCKER-USER after the reload = %v, want the block's four rules", name, du)
		}
		if dtgChain(rs, "darkpanel-docker-deny") == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s predicted state lacks darkpanel-docker-deny", name)
		}
	}
	tg, err = h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{reload: true})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if du := dtgChain(tg.pred.V4, "DOCKER-USER"); du == nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(dtgTexts(du), []string{"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN"}) {
		t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER after a reload with no block = %v, want Docker's own rule", du)
	}
}

// TestDtgCleanup: the cleanup runs before the transition, so the prediction
// starts from a loaded state without Darkpanel's chains, and DOCKER-USER
// holds only -j RETURN in both families; every other chain and table is
// kept, and the caller's loaded state is not modified.
func TestDtgCleanup(t *testing.T) {
	assertClean := func(t *testing.T, name string, rs *netfilter.Ruleset, inputRules int) {
		t.Helper()
		du := dtgChain(rs, "DOCKER-USER")
		if du == nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(dtgTexts(du), []string{"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN"}) {
			t.Errorf("%s DOCKER-USER = %v, want only -j RETURN", name, du)
		}
		for _, c := range rs.Table("filter").Chains {
			if strings.HasPrefix(c.Name, "darkpanel-") || strings.HasPrefix(c.Name, "dp-b-") {
				t.Errorf("%s still holds chain %s", name, c.Name)
			}
		}
		for _, keep := range []string{"INPUT", "FORWARD", "DOCKER-FORWARD", "foreign-chain", "ufw-user-input"} {
			if dtgChain(rs, keep) == nil {
				t.Errorf("%s lost chain %s", name, keep)
			}
		}
		if got := dtgChain(rs, "INPUT"); got.Policy != "DROP" || len(got.Rules) < inputRules {
			t.Errorf("%s INPUT policy %q with %d rules, want DROP with at least %d", name, got.Policy, len(got.Rules), inputRules)
		}
		if nat := rs.Table("nat"); nat == nil || nat.Chain("DOCKER") == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s lost the nat table's DOCKER chain", name)
		}
	}

	t.Run("no transition", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newTGHost(t, tgStopped, false)
		h.loaded = fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(t, dtgLoadedBlock), V6: fhParse(t, dtgLoadedBlock)}
		cur := h.cur()
		tg, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), cur, change{cleanup: true})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if tg.tr != fwstate.TransNone {
			t.Errorf("transition %s, want none", tg.tr)
		}
		assertClean(t, "v4", tg.pred.V4, 1)
		assertClean(t, "v6", tg.pred.V6, 1)
		for name, rs := range map[string]*netfilter.Ruleset{"v4": cur.V4, "v6": cur.V6} {
			if dtgChain(rs, "dp-b-0123456789ab") == nil || len(dtgChain(rs, "DOCKER-USER").Rules) != 3 {
				t.Errorf("the caller's %s loaded state was modified", name)
			}
		}
	})

	t.Run("the predictor starts from the cleaned state", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newTGHost(t, tgRunning, true)
		h.loaded = fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(t, dtgLoadedBlock), V6: fhParse(t, dtgLoadedBlock)}
		var from fwstate.Loaded
		h.f.d.predict = func(_ fwstate.Config, cur fwstate.Loaded, _ fwstate.Transition) (fwstate.Loaded, error) {
			from = cur
			return cur, nil
		}
		tg, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{cleanup: true, reload: true})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if tg.tr != fwstate.TransReload {
			t.Errorf("transition %s, want reload", tg.tr)
		}
		assertClean(t, "predictor input v4", from.V4, 1)
		assertClean(t, "predictor input v6", from.V6, 1)
		assertClean(t, "prediction v4", tg.pred.V4, 1)
	})

	t.Run("with the real predictor and the block gone from the files", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newTGHost(t, tgRunning, true)
		h.loaded = fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(t, dtgLoadedBlock), V6: fhParse(t, dtgLoadedBlock)}
		h.f.d.predict = predict.Predict
		plain := map[string][]byte{dtgAfter4: []byte("*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n"), dtgAfter6: []byte("*filter\n# after6\nCOMMIT\n")}
		tg, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{files: plain, reload: true, cleanup: true})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		assertClean(t, "v4", tg.pred.V4, 1)
		assertClean(t, "v6", tg.pred.V6, 1)
		tg, err = h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{files: plain, reload: true})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if dtgChain(tg.pred.V4, "darkpanel-docker-deny") == nil {
			t.Error("without cleanup a reload keeps the loaded darkpanel chains, as UFW does")
		}
	})

	t.Run("a host without DOCKER-USER or IPv6", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newTGHost(t, tgStopped, false)
		h.loaded = fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(t, tgStopped), V6: nil}
		tg, err := h.f.predictTarget(h.config(), h.cur(), change{cleanup: true})
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if du := dtgChain(tg.pred.V4, "DOCKER-USER"); du == nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(dtgTexts(du), []string{"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN"}) {
			t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER = %v, want it declared with -j RETURN, as the cleanup input declares it", du)
		}
		if tg.pred.V6 != nil {
			t.Error("a family the host does not have gained a ruleset")
		}
	})
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

All changes are in `internal/modules/firewall/target.go`.

1. Add to the `change` struct, below its existing fields, the seven fields of Contracts "change and target" with their types and the comments given there: `files map[string][]byte`, `flag *bool`, `sources *dockerfw.Settings`, `rowsAdd []dockerfw.ContainerRule`, `rowsDel []string`, `cleanup bool`, `reload bool`. Import `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw` and `internal/platform/netfilter`. Only `files`, `cleanup` and `reload` are read here; `flag`, `sources`, `rowsAdd` and `rowsDel` change no loaded state and `predictTarget` ignores them (they are applied by Task 38's `fw.run`).
2. `overlayBlockFiles(cfg fwstate.Config, files map[string][]byte) (fwstate.Config, error)` returns a copy of `cfg` whose `Files` map is a clone with each given path's `core.RestoreEntry.Data` replaced; `Present`, `Mode`, `UID` and `GID` stay as they were, as `predict.Edit`'s own writes keep them. It never changes the map or entries of `cfg` it was given. Walk the paths in sorted order so an error is deterministic. A path other than `/etc/ufw/after.rules` and `/etc/ufw/after6.rules` is a plain error `firewall: <path> is not a file a Docker change writes`; a path whose entry is absent or has `Present` false is a plain error `firewall: <path> is missing`. Neither is an `*errcode.Error`.
3. `predictChainCleanup(cur fwstate.Loaded) fwstate.Loaded` returns a copy of `cur` (all other fields as they are) whose `V4` and `V6` are cleaned independently; a nil family stays nil, and a ruleset with no `filter` table is returned unchanged. In the `filter` table it drops every chain whose name starts with `darkpanel-` or `dp-b-`, gives `DOCKER-USER` exactly one rule, a bare `-j RETURN`, and appends `DOCKER-USER` holding that rule when the chain is not loaded, as the cleanup's restore input declares it (Contracts "dockerfw restore inputs"). Build the rule by parsing the fixed text `*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\nCOMMIT\n` with `netfilter.ParseRestore` and taking that chain's rule, so its `Text` and fields are what a real parse gives. Other tables, other chains and every built-in chain's policy and rules stay as they are. The copy must not share a modified slice with `cur`: clone the table list, the filter table's chain list and the replaced chain's rule list; leave untouched tables shared.
4. In `predictTarget`:
   - After the `c.restore` block (so the overlay lands on a restore's configuration too) and before the transition switch, when `len(c.files) > 0` set `tg.cfgN` to `overlayBlockFiles(tg.cfgN, c.files)`, returning its error unchanged. The transition commands' edits copy `Files`, so the overlay reaches `tg.final` and the predictor's `cfg`.
   - Before `ufwRunning(cur)` is first evaluated, when `c.cleanup` set `cur = predictChainCleanup(cur)`, so the cleanup (which runs before the transition commands) is what every `d.predict` call starts from and what a no-transition prediction returns. `cur.Sysctl` is untouched.
   - In the switch's third case (`want && (len(c.ops) > 0 || c.restore != nil || c.repair)`) add `|| c.reload`. That case is reached only for a configuration that is enabled before the change and stays wanted, so a reload on an inactive UFW or a change that stops UFW adds no transition. `files` alone never forces a reload.
5. Extend `predictTarget`'s doc comment: the files overlay, that `reload` forces a reload of an active UFW, and that the cleanup is applied to the loaded state before the transition. Comments only for the non-obvious why, in full sentences.

```tsx
import { screen, waitFor, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test, vi } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import type { ContainerRef } from "@/modules/types"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type FetchCall, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { AllowAction, DenyAction } from "./container-actions"
import { fwBinding, fwDocker } from "./fixtures"
import type { DockerStatus } from "./types"

const CA_DOCKER = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/firewall/docker"

// caDocker is a healthy, supported integration whatever fwDocker's defaults are.
function caDocker(over: Partial<DockerStatus> = {}): DockerStatus {
  return fwDocker({ available: true, supported: true, unsupported: [], enabled: true, bindings: [], ...over })
}

function caContainer(over: Partial<ContainerRef> = {}): ContainerRef {
  return {
    hostId: "h1",
    containerId: "c1",
    name: "web",
    ports: [{ privatePort: 80, protocol: "tcp", bindings: [{ hostIp: "0.0.0.0", hostPort: 8080 }, { hostIp: "::", hostPort: 8080 }] }],
    ...over,
  }
}

function caRender(kind: "allow" | "deny", docker: DockerStatus, container: ContainerRef = caContainer(), routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}) {
  const plan = (call: FetchCall) => {
    const action = call.path.split("/")[6] ?? ""
    return { body: { planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "+", text: action }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-24T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null } }
  }
  const calls = stubFetch({
    [CA_DOCKER]: { body: docker },
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/firewall/availability": { body: { module: "firewall", available: true, reason: null, actions: [] } },
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.container.allow/v1/plan": plan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.container.deny/v1/plan": plan,
    ...routes,
  })
  const onDone = vi.fn()
  const view = kind === "allow" ? <AllowAction container={container} onDone={onDone} /> : <DenyAction container={container} onDone={onDone} />
  const result = renderWithProviders(view)
  return { calls, onDone, ...result }
}

function caPlanCall(calls: FetchCall[]): { path: string; body: unknown } {
  const call = calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/plan"))
  return { path: call?.path ?? "", body: call?.body }
}

  all: fwBinding({ binding: { selector: "web", hostPort: 8080, proto: "tcp" }, containers: ["web"], allowed: [], denied: [] }),

  await waitFor(() => expect(onDone).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1))
})
```

Replace the body of `web/src/modules/firewall/container-actions.tsx`. Keep the exported names `AllowAction` and `DenyAction` and give both the props `{container: ContainerRef; onDone: () => void}`. Both render one shared unexported component that takes `kind: "allow" | "deny"`. Match `state-controls.tsx` and `rule-form.tsx` for markup (a `RadioGroup` of `RadioGroupItem` and `Label` pairs, `Input`, `Button`, `Alert`, `Spinner` from `darkraise-ui`), and give the component no state beyond what follows.

1. Read `DockerStatus` with `useQuery`, key `dockerQueryKey(container.hostId)`, function `readResource<DockerStatus>(container.hostId, FIREWALL_MODULE, "docker")`. While pending render `<Spinner aria-label="Loading the Docker integration" />`. On error render `<Alert variant="destructive" role="alert">` holding `errorMessage(error)` and nothing else.
2. Candidate bindings, in this order, de-duplicated by the key `hostAddr|hostPort|proto` (an absent `hostAddr` is the empty string):
   - every `docker.bindings` entry whose `containers` includes `container.name`: its `binding` is used exactly as received (so a stored Compose selector `project/service` is kept), and it counts as allowed when its `allowed` list is not empty;
   - then, for every published binding of `container.ports` whose key is not yet present: a binding `{selector: container.name, hostAddr, hostPort, proto: <the port's protocol>}`, never allowed. `hostAddr` is left out when Docker's `hostIp` is `""`, `0.0.0.0` or `::`, so Docker's pair of IPv4 and IPv6 entries for one published port is one candidate on every address, and is the `hostIp` otherwise. A port with no published binding adds nothing.
   - Allow offers every candidate. Deny offers only the candidates that are allowed (an explicit deny applies to an allowed binding).
3. A candidate's label, used for its radio and in titles, is `<addr>:<hostPort>/<proto>`, where `<addr>` is `all` for no `hostAddr`, the address, or the address in square brackets when it contains a colon: `all:8080/tcp`, `127.0.0.1:8081/tcp`, `[::1]:5353/udp`. The first candidate is selected until the operator picks another; keep the picked key in state and fall back to the first candidate when it is no longer offered.
4. A reason disables the form and is shown in `<Alert variant="warning" role="status">`, the first that applies: Docker not `available` shows `docker.reason`, or `Docker is unavailable on this host.` when it has none; not `supported` shows `The Docker integration is not supported: ` followed by `docker.unsupported` joined with `; `; no candidate shows `<container name> publishes no ports.` for Allow and `<container name> has no allowed binding. Allow one first.` for Deny. Read `reason` and `unsupported` as `types.ts` declares them (they are optional in the JSON).
5. The form is `<form aria-label="Allow">` or `<form aria-label="Deny">` and holds: a `fieldset` with legend `Binding` and the radio group (`aria-label="Binding"`); an `Input` labelled `From`, with a placeholder naming a CIDR such as `203.0.113.0/24` and, for Allow, that an empty value means any source; and a submit button `Plan`. The button is disabled while a reason shows, while nothing is selected, and, for Deny only, while the trimmed `From` is empty. Give ids that are unique per kind so Allow and Deny can mount together.
6. Submit does not post anything itself. It sets the pending change that `FirewallChange` (props `hostId: container.hostId`, `action`, `title`, `input`, `onClose`) opens: action `firewall.container.allow` or `firewall.container.deny`; input `{binding: <the selected binding>}` plus `from: <trimmed From>` only when it is not empty (always present for Deny); title `Allow <any source|the From> to <container name> on <label>` for Allow and `Deny <From> to <container name> on <label>` for Deny. `onClose` clears the pending change and calls `onDone()`, so the slot's host learns the dialog ended whether or not the change applied; `FirewallChange` already refreshes the host's resources.
7. No `any`, no new dependency, no change to `FirewallChange`, `types.ts`, `fixtures.ts` or `registry.ts`.

Create `internal/modules/firewall/docker_store_test.go`. `dsDB` is the shared helper of Contracts "Docker store": wave 1's `fwTestDB` (which applies every migration `agentMigrations()` embeds, so it includes 0003 once the file exists) plus a check that the four Docker tables exist.

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"errors"
	"io/fs"
	"net/netip"
	"path/filepath"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"testing/fstest"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/store"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw"
)

var dsTables = []string{"firewall_settings", "firewall_container_rules", "firewall_docker_cleanups", "firewall_docker_foreign"}

// dsDB opens a temporary agent database with the core's and every
// firewall migration applied, and fails unless the Docker tables exist.
func dsDB(t *testing.T) *store.DB {
	t.Helper()
	db := fwTestDB(t)
	for _, table := range dsTables {
		var name string
		err := db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' AND name = ?", table).Scan(&name)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("table %s is missing after the firewall migrations: %v", table, err)
		}
	}
	return db
}

var dsT0 = time.Date(2026, 10, 28, 9, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)

func dsWrite(t *testing.T, db *store.DB, fn func(tx *sql.Tx) error) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := db.Write(context.Background(), fn); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

func dsExec(t *testing.T, db *store.DB, query string, args ...any) error {
	t.Helper()
	return db.Write(context.Background(), func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		_, err := tx.Exec(query, args...)
		return err
	})
}

func dsRule(id, selector, host string, port uint16, proto string, kind dockerfw.Kind, from string) dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	r := dockerfw.ContainerRule{
		ID:      id,
		Binding: dockerfw.Binding{Selector: selector, HostPort: port, Proto: proto},
		Kind:    kind,
	}
	if host != "" {
		r.Binding.HostAddr = netip.MustParseAddr(host)
	}
	if from != "" {
		r.From = netip.MustParsePrefix(from)
	}
	return r
}

func dsAllRules(t *testing.T, db *store.DB) []dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	t.Helper()
	got, err := listContainerRules(context.Background(), db)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return got
}

func dsOwners(t *testing.T, db *store.DB) []string {
	t.Helper()
	got, err := pendingCleanups(context.Background(), db)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return got
}

func TestDsMigrationOnlyAddsTables(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db, err := store.Open(ctx, filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "agent.db"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = db.Close() })
	coreSet, err := store.CoreMigrations(store.SideAgent)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	old := fstest.MapFS{}
	for _, name := range []string{"0001_firewall.sql", "0002_firewall_restore_kind.sql"} {
		b, err := fs.ReadFile(agentMigrations(), name)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		old[name] = &fstest.MapFile{Data: b}
	}
	opts := store.MigrateOptions{Side: store.SideAgent, BinaryVersion: "test", BackupRoot: filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "backups"), Keep: 5, Now: time.Now()}
	if res, err := store.Migrate(ctx, db, opts, coreSet, []store.MigrationSet{{Module: ID, FS: old}}); err != nil || len(res.Failed) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("migrate 0001-0002: %v %v", err, res.Failed)
	}
	if err := dsExec(t, db, `INSERT INTO firewall_snapshots (id, created_at, actor, entries, state, hashes) VALUES ('s1', 't', 'a', '[]', '{}', '{}')`); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	opts.BinaryVersion = "test2"
	if res, err := store.Migrate(ctx, db, opts, coreSet, []store.MigrationSet{{Module: ID, FS: agentMigrations()}}); err != nil || len(res.Failed) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("migrate 0003: %v %v", err, res.Failed)
	}
	var snapshots int
	if err := db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT count(*) FROM firewall_snapshots WHERE id = 's1'").Scan(&snapshots); err != nil || snapshots != 1 {
		t.Errorf("the snapshot written before 0003: count %d, err %v, want 1", snapshots, err)
	}
	for _, table := range dsTables {
		var strict int
		err := db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT strict FROM pragma_table_list WHERE name = ?", table).Scan(&strict)
		if err != nil || strict != 1 {
			t.Errorf("table %s: strict %d, err %v, want a STRICT table", table, strict, err)
		}
	}
}

func TestDsMigrationConstraints(t *testing.T) {
	db := dsDB(t)
	const insert = "INSERT INTO firewall_container_rules (id, selector, host_addr, host_port, proto, kind, source, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 't')"
	if err := dsExec(t, db, insert, "r0", "web", "", 8080, "tcp", "allow", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a valid row: %v", err)
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name  string
		query string
		args  []any
	}{
		{"settings row other than 1", "INSERT INTO firewall_settings (id, docker, settings) VALUES (2, 0, '{}')", nil},
		{"docker flag 2", "INSERT INTO firewall_settings (id, docker, settings) VALUES (1, 2, '{}')", nil},
		{"port 0", insert, []any{"r1", "web", "", 0, "tcp", "allow", ""}},
		{"port 65536", insert, []any{"r1", "web", "", 65536, "tcp", "allow", ""}},
		{"proto icmp", insert, []any{"r1", "web", "", 8080, "icmp", "allow", ""}},
		{"kind maybe", insert, []any{"r1", "web", "", 8080, "tcp", "maybe", ""}},
		{"same tuple under another id", insert, []any{"r1", "web", "", 8080, "tcp", "allow", ""}},
		{"same id", insert, []any{"r0", "other", "", 8080, "tcp", "allow", ""}},
	} {
		if err := dsExec(t, db, c.query, c.args...); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s: the insert succeeded, want a constraint error", c.name)
		}
	}
	if err := dsExec(t, db, insert, "r2", "web", "", 8080, "tcp", "deny", "203.0.113.0/24"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("the same binding with another kind and source: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestDsDockerConfig(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := dsDB(t)
	got, err := readDockerConfig(ctx, db)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := (dockerConfig{Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("no row: %+v, want the integration off with the default settings %+v", got, want)
	}

	boom := errors.New("boom")
	err = db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := writeDockerConfig(ctx, tx, dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()}); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return boom
	})
	if !errors.Is(err, boom) {
		t.Fatalf("Write = %v, want the rollback error", err)
	}
	if got, _ := readDockerConfig(ctx, db); got.Enabled {
		t.Error("a write in a rolled-back transaction was stored")
	}

	first := dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dockerfw.Settings{
		PrivateSources: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("10.0.0.0/8"), netip.MustParsePrefix("fc00::/7")},
		ForwardExemptions: []dockerfw.Exemption{{
			InInterface: "eth0", OrigDestination: netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.10"), OrigPort: 2222,
			Destination: netip.MustParseAddr("10.9.0.5"), Proto: "tcp", Port: 22,
		}},
	}}
	second := dockerConfig{Enabled: false, Settings: dockerfw.Settings{
		PrivateSources:    []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("192.168.0.0/16")},
		ForwardExemptions: []dockerfw.Exemption{},
	}}
	for _, want := range []dockerConfig{first, second} {
		dsWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return writeDockerConfig(ctx, tx, want) })
		got, err := readDockerConfig(ctx, db)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("read back %+v, want %+v", got, want)
		}
	}
	var rows int
	if err := db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT count(*) FROM firewall_settings").Scan(&rows); err != nil || rows != 1 {
		t.Errorf("firewall_settings holds %d rows (err %v), want the one row rewritten", rows, err)
	}

	if err := dsExec(t, db, "UPDATE firewall_settings SET settings = 'not json'"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := readDockerConfig(ctx, db); err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "firewall:") {
		t.Errorf("a corrupt settings column: %v, want a firewall: error", err)
	}
}

func TestDsContainerRulesRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := dsDB(t)
	rules := []dockerfw.ContainerRule{
		dsRule("01J00000000000000000000003", "shop/web", "192.0.2.10", 443, "tcp", dockerfw.Deny, "203.0.113.0/24"),
		dsRule("01J00000000000000000000001", "web", "", 8080, "tcp", dockerfw.Allow, ""),
		dsRule("01J00000000000000000000002", "dns", "2001:db8::1", 53, "udp", dockerfw.Allow, "198.51.100.0/24"),
	}
	for i, r := range rules {
		at := dsT0.Add(time.Duration(i) * time.Minute)
		dsWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertContainerRule(ctx, tx, r, at) })
	}
	want := []dockerfw.ContainerRule{rules[1], rules[2], rules[0]}
	if got := dsAllRules(t, db); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("listContainerRules =\n%+v\nwant, ordered by id,\n%+v", got, want)
	}
	for _, r := range rules {
		got, ok, err := containerRule(ctx, db, r.ID)
		if err != nil || !ok || !reflect.DeepEqual(got, r) {
			t.Errorf("containerRule(%s) = %+v, %v, %v, want %+v", r.ID, got, ok, err, r)
		}
	}
	if _, ok, err := containerRule(ctx, db, "missing"); ok || err != nil {
		t.Errorf("containerRule(missing) = %v, %v, want not found without an error", ok, err)
	}

	var host, source, created string
	err := db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT host_addr, source, created_at FROM firewall_container_rules WHERE id = ?", rules[1].ID).Scan(&host, &source, &created)
	if err != nil || host != "" || source != "" || created != formatSnapshotTime(dsT0.Add(time.Minute)) {
		t.Errorf("stored columns of an any rule = %q %q %q (err %v), want empty, empty and the creation time", host, source, created, err)
	}
	err = db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT host_addr, source FROM firewall_container_rules WHERE id = ?", rules[0].ID).Scan(&host, &source)
	if err != nil || host != "192.0.2.10" || source != "203.0.113.0/24" {
		t.Errorf("stored columns of a deny rule = %q %q (err %v), want 192.0.2.10 and 203.0.113.0/24", host, source, err)
	}
}

func TestDsContainerRuleRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	db := dsDB(t)
	base := dsRule("01J00000000000000000000001", "web", "", 8080, "tcp", dockerfw.Allow, "")
	dsWrite(t, db, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertContainerRule(ctx, tx, base, dsT0) })
	sameTuple := base
	sameTuple.ID = "01J00000000000000000000002"
	sameID := dsRule(base.ID, "other", "", 9090, "tcp", dockerfw.Allow, "")
	for name, r := range map[string]dockerfw.ContainerRule{"the same binding, kind and source": sameTuple, "the same id": sameID} {
		err := db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return insertContainerRule(ctx, tx, r, dsT0) })
		if err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "firewall:") {
			t.Errorf("insert of %s: %v, want a firewall: error", name, err)
		}
	}
	if got := dsAllRules(t, db); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, []dockerfw.ContainerRule{base}) {
		t.Errorf("after the refused inserts: %+v, want only the first rule", got)
	}

	if err := dsExec(t, db, "UPDATE firewall_container_rules SET host_addr = 'nonsense'"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := listContainerRules(ctx, db); err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "firewall:") {
		t.Errorf("list with a corrupt host address: %v, want a firewall: error", err)
	}
	if _, _, err := containerRule(ctx, db, base.ID); err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "firewall:") {
		t.Errorf("containerRule with a corrupt host address: %v, want a firewall: error", err)
	}
}

	}
	if err := beginCleanup(ctx, db, "01J00000000000000000000001", dsT0.Add(time.Second)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := dsOwners(t, db), []string{"uninstall", "01J00000000000000000000001"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("pendingCleanups = %v, want %v, oldest intent first", got, want)
	}

	if err := beginCleanup(ctx, db, "uninstall", dsT0.Add(time.Hour)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	var started string
	if err := db.Read().QueryRow("SELECT started_at FROM firewall_docker_cleanups WHERE owner = 'uninstall'").Scan(&started); err != nil || started != formatSnapshotTime(dsT0) {
		t.Errorf("started_at after recording an owner twice = %q (err %v), want the first time", started, err)
	}
	if got := dsOwners(t, db); len(got) != 2 {
		t.Errorf("recording an owner twice left %v, want two intents", got)
	}

	if err := endCleanup(ctx, db, "uninstall"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := endCleanup(ctx, db, "uninstall"); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("endCleanup of an absent owner: %v", err)
	}
	if got, want := dsOwners(t, db), []string{"01J00000000000000000000001"}; !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("pendingCleanups after ending one = %v, want %v", got, want)
	}
	if err := endCleanup(ctx, db, "01J00000000000000000000001"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := dsOwners(t, db); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("pendingCleanups after ending both = %v, want none", got)
	}
}
```

1. Create `migrations/agent/0003_firewall_docker.sql` with exactly the four `CREATE TABLE` statements of Contracts "Docker store" (same columns, `CHECK` constraints, `UNIQUE` and `STRICT`), after a header comment in the style of `0001_firewall.sql` that says: the tables hold the Docker integration's logical state (spec 2.6); `host_addr` and `source` are the empty string for "every address" and "any source"; a cleanup intent exists from the cleanup's first step until it verified; a foreign-rule record exists from before a transition until `DOCKER-USER` was reloaded after it. The migration is expand-only: it creates tables and touches no existing one. `docker_store.go` already embeds it, because `store.go`'s `//go:embed migrations/agent/*.sql` matches by glob; do not edit `store.go`.
2. Create `docker_store.go`, package `firewall`, with a doc comment on every function, wrapping every database error as `firewall: <what failed>: %w`:
   - `type dockerConfig struct { Enabled bool; Settings dockerfw.Settings }` with the JSON tags of the Contract.
   - `readDockerConfig(ctx, db *store.DB)` reads `firewall_settings` where `id = 1` through `db.Read()`. No row returns `dockerConfig{Enabled: false, Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()}` and no error. The `settings` column is the JSON of `dockerfw.Settings`; a column that does not decode is an error (`firewall: decode the Docker settings: …`).
   - `writeDockerConfig(ctx, tx *sql.Tx, c dockerConfig)` upserts the single row `id = 1` (`INSERT … ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE`) with `docker` = `c.Enabled` and `settings` = `json.Marshal(c.Settings)`. It runs on the transaction it is given and never opens its own.
   - `listContainerRules(ctx, db)` selects `id, selector, host_addr, host_port, proto, kind, source` ordered by `id` through `db.Read()`; no rows returns a nil slice. `containerRule(ctx, db, id)` reads one row and returns `(rule, true, nil)`, or `(zero, false, nil)` when there is none. Both share one scan function (a `rowScanner` parameter) that turns `host_addr` `""` into the zero `netip.Addr` and a non-empty one into `netip.ParseAddr`'s result, `source` `""` into the zero `netip.Prefix` and a non-empty one into `netip.ParsePrefix`'s result, and `kind` into `dockerfw.Kind`. A value that does not parse is an error naming the rule id (`firewall: container rule <id>: host address "…": …`).
   - `insertContainerRule(ctx, tx, r, at)` inserts one row on `tx`: `host_addr` is `r.Binding.HostAddr.String()` when valid else `""`, `source` is `r.From.String()` when valid else `""`, `created_at` is `formatSnapshotTime(at)`. A constraint failure (duplicate id, or the same selector, host address, port, protocol, kind and source under another id) is returned wrapped (`firewall: insert container rule <id>: …`), never translated to a sentinel and never ignored. The function does not validate the rule: `dockerfw.ContainerRule.Validate` is the actions' job.
   - `deleteContainerRule(ctx, tx, id)` deletes by id on `tx`; an id with no row is not an error, so a replayed inverse effect is harmless.
   - `replaceContainerRules(ctx, tx, rows, at)` deletes every row, then inserts `rows` in the given order through `insertContainerRule` with the same `at`, all on `tx`; the first insert error is returned and the caller's transaction rolls everything back.
   - `beginCleanup(ctx, db, owner, at)` inserts `(owner, formatSnapshotTime(at))` through `db.Write` with `ON CONFLICT (owner) DO NOTHING`, so an owner recorded twice keeps its first `started_at`. `db.Write` commits with `synchronous=FULL`, which is the fsync spec 2.6 step 1 asks for.
   - `endCleanup(ctx, db, owner)` deletes the owner's row; an absent owner is not an error.
   - `pendingCleanups(ctx, db)` returns the owners ordered by `started_at`, then `owner`; none returns a nil slice.
3. Do not add functions for `firewall_docker_foreign` (Task 36), do not call any of these functions from existing code (later tasks do), and change no existing file.

```go
package dockerfw

import (
	"net/netip"
	"reflect"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

const (
	rzID1 = "01J00000000000000000000001"
	rzID2 = "01J00000000000000000000002"
	rzID3 = "01J00000000000000000000003"
	rzID4 = "01J00000000000000000000004"
)

// rzPub is a published port: host address (empty for 0.0.0.0), host port,
// container port, protocol.
func rzPub(host string, hostPort, containerPort uint16, proto string) Published {
	if host == "" {
		host = "0.0.0.0"
	}
	return Published{HostAddr: netip.MustParseAddr(host), HostPort: hostPort, ContainerPort: containerPort, Proto: proto}
}

// rzEp is a container's endpoint on a network; an empty address is absent.
func rzEp(network, bridge, v4, v6 string) Endpoint {
	e := Endpoint{Network: network, Bridge: bridge}
	if v4 != "" {
		e.Addr4 = netip.MustParseAddr(v4)
	}
	if v6 != "" {
		e.Addr6 = netip.MustParseAddr(v6)
	}
	return e
}

func rzContainer(name string, ports []Published, eps ...Endpoint) Container {
	return Container{ID: "id-" + name, Name: name, Ports: ports, Endpoints: eps}
}

func rzNetwork(name, bridge string, subnets ...string) Network {
	n := Network{ID: "id-" + name, Name: name, Driver: "bridge", Bridge: bridge}
	for _, s := range subnets {
		n.Subnets = append(n.Subnets, netip.MustParsePrefix(s))
	}
	return n
}

func rzFacts(containers []Container, networks ...Network) Facts {
	return Facts{Containers: containers, Networks: networks}
}

// rzRow is a container rule: an empty host is every address, an empty from
// is any source.
func rzRow(id, selector, host string, port uint16, kind Kind, from string) ContainerRule {
	r := ContainerRule{ID: id, Binding: Binding{Selector: selector, HostPort: port, Proto: "tcp"}, Kind: kind}
	if host != "" {
		r.Binding.HostAddr = netip.MustParseAddr(host)
	}
	if from != "" {
		r.From = netip.MustParsePrefix(from)
	}
	return r
}

func rzRoute(action model.Action, id, from, bridge, to, port string, fam model.Family) model.Rule {
	return model.Rule{Action: action, Direction: model.DirRoute, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: from, To: to, ToPort: port,
		OutIface: bridge, Family: fam, Log: model.LogOff, Comment: LabelPrefix + id, Origin: model.OriginDarkpanel}
}

func rzIn(action model.Action, id, from, to, port string, fam model.Family) model.Rule {
	return model.Rule{Action: action, Direction: model.DirIn, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: from, To: to, ToPort: port,
		Family: fam, Log: model.LogOff, Comment: LabelPrefix + id, Origin: model.OriginDarkpanel}
}

func rzLine(b Binding, addr string, containerPort uint16) BindingLine {
	return BindingLine{Proto: b.Proto, ContainerAddr: netip.MustParseAddr(addr), ContainerPort: containerPort,
		HostAddr: b.HostAddr, HostPort: b.HostPort, Chain: b.Chain()}
}

func rzPrefixes(s ...string) []netip.Prefix {
	var out []netip.Prefix
	for _, p := range s {
		out = append(out, netip.MustParsePrefix(p))
	}
	return out
}

// rzCheck compares the parts of a Realized separately for readable output.
func rzCheck(t *testing.T, got Realized, lines []BindingLine, chains []BindingChain, rules []model.Rule) {
	t.Helper()
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Block.Lines, lines) {
		t.Errorf("Block.Lines =\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got.Block.Lines, lines)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Block.Chains, chains) {
		t.Errorf("Block.Chains =\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got.Block.Chains, chains)
	}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Rules, rules) {
		t.Errorf("Rules =\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got.Rules, rules)
	}
}

func TestRzRealizeRouteAllow(t *testing.T) {
	facts := rzFacts(
		[]Container{rzContainer("web", []Published{rzPub("", 8080, 80, "tcp")}, rzEp("bridge", "docker0", "172.17.0.2", ""))},
		rzNetwork("bridge", "docker0", "172.17.0.0/16"))
	row := rzRow(rzID1, "web", "", 8080, Allow, "")
	got := Realize([]ContainerRule{row}, facts, DefaultSettings())
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Block.Settings, DefaultSettings()) || got.Block.CustomBridges != nil {
		t.Errorf("Block settings %+v and custom bridges %v, want the settings passed in and no custom bridge", got.Block.Settings, got.Block.CustomBridges)
	}
	rzCheck(t, got,
		[]BindingLine{rzLine(row.Binding, "172.17.0.2", 80)},
		[]BindingChain{{Name: row.Binding.Chain()}},
		[]model.Rule{rzRoute(model.ActionAllow, rzID1, "any", "docker0", "172.17.0.2", "80", model.FamilyV4)})

	dns := rzRow(rzID2, "dns", "", 53, Allow, "")
	dns.Binding.Proto = "udp"
	facts = rzFacts([]Container{rzContainer("dns", []Published{rzPub("", 53, 5353, "udp")}, rzEp("bridge", "docker0", "172.17.0.3", ""))})
	udpRule := rzRoute(model.ActionAllow, rzID2, "any", "docker0", "172.17.0.3", "5353", model.FamilyV4)
	udpRule.Proto = model.ProtoUDP
	got = Realize([]ContainerRule{dns}, facts, DefaultSettings())
	rzCheck(t, got,
		[]BindingLine{rzLine(dns.Binding, "172.17.0.3", 5353)},
		[]BindingChain{{Name: dns.Binding.Chain()}},
		[]model.Rule{udpRule})
}

			[]BindingLine{rzLine(row.Binding, c.wantAddr, 80)},
			[]BindingChain{{Name: row.Binding.Chain()}},
			[]model.Rule{rzRoute(model.ActionAllow, rzID1, "any", "docker0", c.wantAddr, "80", fam)})
		if t.Failed() {
			t.Fatalf("case %q failed", c.name)
		}
	}
}

	web.Project, web.Service = "shop", "web"

func TestRzRealizeNothingToRealize(t *testing.T) {
	running := rzContainer("web", []Published{rzPub("", 8080, 80, "tcp")}, rzEp("bridge", "docker0", "172.17.0.2", ""))
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name  string
		facts Facts
		row   ContainerRule
	}{
		{"the container is not running", rzFacts(nil), rzRow(rzID1, "web", "", 8080, Allow, "")},
		{"another container's name", rzFacts([]Container{running}), rzRow(rzID1, "api", "", 8080, Allow, "")},
		{"another host port", rzFacts([]Container{running}), rzRow(rzID1, "web", "", 9090, Allow, "")},
		{"another protocol", rzFacts([]Container{running}), func() ContainerRule {
			r := rzRow(rzID1, "web", "", 8080, Allow, "")
			r.Binding.Proto = "udp"
			return r
		}()},
	} {
		settings := Settings{PrivateSources: rzPrefixes("10.0.0.0/8")}
		got := Realize([]ContainerRule{c.row}, c.facts, settings)
		if len(got.Block.Lines) != 0 || len(got.Block.Chains) != 0 || len(got.Rules) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s: realized %+v, want no line, chain or rule", c.name, got)
		}
		if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.Block.Settings, settings) {
			t.Errorf("%s: Block.Settings = %+v, want the settings passed in", c.name, got.Block.Settings)
		}
	}
	if got := Realize(nil, rzFacts([]Container{running}), DefaultSettings()); len(got.Rules) != 0 || len(got.Block.Lines) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("no rows realized %+v", got)
	}
}

func TestRzRealizeIsIndependentOfRowOrder(t *testing.T) {
	facts := rzFacts([]Container{rzContainer("web",
		[]Published{rzPub("", 8080, 80, "tcp"), rzPub("::", 8080, 80, "tcp"), rzPub("", 8081, 80, "tcp")},
		rzEp("bridge", "docker0", "172.17.0.2", ""))})
	rows := []ContainerRule{
		rzRow(rzID1, "web", "", 8080, Deny, "203.0.113.0/24"),
		rzRow(rzID2, "web", "", 8080, Allow, "198.51.100.0/24"),
		rzRow(rzID3, "web", "", 8080, Allow, ""),
		rzRow(rzID4, "web", "", 8081, Allow, ""),
	}
	want := Realize(rows, facts, DefaultSettings())
	if len(want.Rules) == 0 || len(want.Block.Lines) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the fixture realized nothing: %+v", want)
	}
	for name, order := range map[string][]int{"reversed": {3, 2, 1, 0}, "shuffled": {2, 0, 3, 1}} {
		var shuffled []ContainerRule
		for _, i := range order {
			shuffled = append(shuffled, rows[i])
		}
		if got := Realize(shuffled, facts, DefaultSettings()); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("%s rows: %+v, want the result of the sorted rows %+v", name, got, want)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `realize.go` in package `dockerfw`. It is pure: it reads no host state and imports only the standard library, `fwstate` and `model` besides the package's own types. Give `Realized` and `Realize` doc comments. `Realize` follows these rules; every ordering below is part of its contract, because the block, the UFW rule operations (Task 24) and reconcile compare its output byte for byte between passes.

1. **Rows.** Work on a copy of `rows` sorted by `ID` (the caller's slice is not reordered). Group the rows by `Binding.ID()`; the groups are taken in the order of each group's smallest row `ID`. A group with no allow row realizes nothing, so a deny row alone has no effect. Ignore a row of any other kind.
2. **Custom bridges.** `Block.CustomBridges` holds the `Bridge` of every `facts.Networks` entry whose `Driver` is `bridge`, whose `Bridge` is not empty, is not `docker0` and does not start with `br-` (the block's `br-+` wildcard already covers those), without duplicates, sorted; it is `nil` when there is none. `Block.Settings` is `s`, whatever the rows are.
3. **Family and address of a family.** An address belongs to IPv4 when `Unmap` makes it IPv4, otherwise to IPv6. An allow row applies to a family when its `From` is the zero prefix (any source) or an address of that family; a deny row applies to a family only when `From` is an address of that family.
4. **What a binding is published on.** For each container of `facts.Containers`, in the facts' order, that the group's binding selects (`Binding.Selects(c.Name, c.Project, c.Service)`), look at the `Ports` entries with the binding's `HostPort` and `Proto`. With the binding's `HostAddr` unset, every such entry matches and its host address gives the family. With `HostAddr` set, an entry matches when its host address equals `HostAddr` or is the unspecified address of `HostAddr`'s family, and the family is `HostAddr`'s. For each family the first matching entry gives the container port. A container with no matching entry realizes nothing for the binding.
5. **Per container and family** (IPv4 then IPv6), for a family the binding is published on and for which at least one allow row applies (otherwise the family realizes nothing: the binding stays closed there, which is also why a binding whose only source is an IPv6 range gets no IPv4 line):
   - The container's *targets* in that family are its `Endpoints`, in order, that have a valid address in the family (`Addr4` or `Addr6`) and a non-empty `Bridge`.
   - With targets, for each target: one `BindingLine` appended to `Block.Lines` (`Proto` the binding's, `ContainerAddr` the target's address, `ContainerPort` the published container port, `HostAddr` the binding's `HostAddr` as set, zero when unset, `HostPort` the binding's, `Chain` `Binding.Chain()`); one route allow rule per applicable allow row: direction `route`, action `allow`, `OutIface` the target's `Bridge`, `Proto` the binding's, `From` the row's `From` as text (`any` when unset), `To` the target's address, `ToPort` the container port as a decimal string, `Family` `v4` or `v6`, `Comment` `LabelPrefix + row.ID`; and one route deny rule per applicable deny row, the same but action `deny` and the deny row's `From`.
   - Without targets (the container has no address in the family, so `docker-proxy` serves it on the host): per applicable allow row one rule with direction `in`, action `allow`, `Proto` the binding's, `From` as above, `To` the binding's `HostAddr` text or `any`, `ToPort` the host port, `Family` the family, `Comment` as above; per applicable deny row the same with action `deny`. No line is added.
6. **Binding chains.** A group that produced at least one line adds one `BindingChain` to `Block.Chains`, in group order: `Name` is `Binding.Chain()`, `Deny` is every deny row's `From` in row order (nil when none), `Allow` is every allow row's `From` in row order, except that it is nil when any allow row has no `From` (an allow from any source makes the others redundant, and an empty `Allow` renders as `0.0.0.0/0` or `::/0`). Both lists carry prefixes of both families; Task 17's `Render` selects the family's.
7. **Rule form.** Pass every rule through `model.Rule.Normalize()`, so that `Log` is `off`, `Origin` is `darkpanel`, a `/32` or `/128` source is written as the plain address and the text equals what UFW's files read back as. `ID` stays empty.
8. **Duplicates.** Two rules equal in every field but `Comment` (two bindings of one container port, or one deny of two bindings) are one rule: keep the first generated, which carries the smaller row id.
9. **Merging the families.** UFW stores an allow-in rule from any to any as one rule for both families, and wave 1's rule list reads it back as `Family` `both`. An allow-in rule for `v4` and one for `v6` that are equal in every field but `Family` (including `Comment`) and whose `From` and `To` are both `any` are therefore returned as one rule with `Family` `both`, at the position of the `v4` rule.
10. **Order of `Rules`.** All deny-in rules, then all allow-in rules, then all route allow rules, then all route deny rules; inside each group, in the order generated (group order, container order, family order, target order, row order). This puts every route deny after every route allow for the same container address and port, and every deny-in before the allow-in of its family.
11. `Block.Lines` and `Block.Chains` are nil when empty; so is `Rules`.

Do not validate rows (the actions do), do not read the clock, and do not call `Render`.

Create `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw/health_test.go` with exactly this content. The test builds a healthy host from `Render` (the block in both `after` files, the same text loaded, Docker's `FORWARD` jumps, UFW's incoming policy `DROP`) and breaks one thing per row.

```go
package dockerfw

import (
	"net/netip"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

const (
	hlChainName   = "dp-b-0123456789ab"
	hlForeignDNAT = "-A PREROUTING -d 198.51.100.7/32 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 2222 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.168.1.5:22\n"
	hlForeignRule = "-A DOCKER-USER -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j DROP"
)

func hlNetworks() []Network {
	return []Network{
		{ID: "aaaaaaaaaaaa1111", Name: "bridge", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.17.0.0/16")}},
		{ID: "bbbbbbbbbbbb2222", Name: "app", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "br-bbbbbbbbbbbb", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.18.0.0/16")}},
		{ID: "cccccccccccc3333", Name: "custom", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "dpcustom", Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.30.0.0/24")}},
	}
}

func hlV6Network() Network {
	return Network{ID: "dddddddddddd4444", Name: "v6net", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "br-dddddddddddd", IPv6: true, Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("fd00:dead::/64")}}
}

func hlBlockInput(s Settings) BlockInput {
	return BlockInput{
		CustomBridges: []string{"dpcustom"},
		Settings:      s,
		Lines: []BindingLine{
			{Proto: "tcp", ContainerAddr: netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.2"), ContainerPort: 80, HostPort: 8080, Chain: hlChainName},
			{Proto: "tcp", ContainerAddr: netip.MustParseAddr("fd00:dead::2"), ContainerPort: 80, HostPort: 8080, Chain: hlChainName},
		},
		Chains: []BindingChain{{Name: hlChainName, Deny: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("203.0.113.0/24"), netip.MustParsePrefix("2001:db8::/32")}}},
	}
}

// hlLoaded parses what the kernel holds for one family: Docker's FORWARD
// jumps, the block's chains and a nat table with Docker's PREROUTING jump
// followed by nat.
func hlLoaded(t *testing.T, block []byte, nat string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	t.Helper()
	text := "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:DOCKER-FORWARD - [0:0]\n" +
		"-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER\n-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-FORWARD\nCOMMIT\n" + string(block) +
		"*nat\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:DOCKER - [0:0]\n-A PREROUTING -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -j DOCKER\n" + nat + "COMMIT\n"
	rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse loaded rules: %v", err)
	}
	return rs
}

// hlDockerDefault is Docker's own DOCKER-USER before the integration is on.
var hlDockerDefault = []byte("*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\nCOMMIT\n")

// hlInput is a healthy host with the integration on: the block in both
// after files, loaded as rendered, UFW's incoming policy DROP, and nat4 as
// the IPv4 nat rules after Docker's.
func hlInput(t *testing.T, s Settings, nat4 string) HealthInput {
	t.Helper()
	in := HealthInput{
		Want:         true,
		Files:        map[fwstate.Family][]byte{},
		Expected:     map[fwstate.Family][]byte{},
		Loaded:       map[fwstate.Family]*netfilter.Ruleset{},
		IPv6:         true,
		DefaultInput: "DROP",
		Facts:        Facts{Networks: hlNetworks()},
		Settings:     s,
		Interfaces:   []string{"lo", "eth0", "docker0", "br-bbbbbbbbbbbb", "dpcustom"},
	}
	for _, f := range []fwstate.Family{fwstate.V4, fwstate.V6} {
		block := Render(hlBlockInput(s), f)
		file, err := WithBlock([]byte("# after.rules\n"), block)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("write the block: %v", err)
		}
		nat := ""
		if f == fwstate.V4 {
			nat = nat4
		}
		in.Files[f], in.Expected[f], in.Loaded[f] = file, block, hlLoaded(t, block, nat)
	}
	return in
}

func hlChain(t *testing.T, in HealthInput, f fwstate.Family, name string) *netfilter.Chain {
	t.Helper()
	c := in.Loaded[f].Table("filter").Chain(name)
	if c == nil {
		t.Fatalf("loaded %s rules have no chain %s", f, name)
	}
	return c
}

func hlRule(t *testing.T, line string) netfilter.Rule {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader("*filter\n" + line + "\nCOMMIT\n"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse %q: %v", line, err)
	}
	return rs.Table("filter").Chains[0].Rules[0]
}

func hlExemption(t *testing.T) Exemption {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader("*nat\n" + hlForeignDNAT + "COMMIT\n"))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	ex, ok := Propose(rs.Table("nat").Chain("PREROUTING").Rules[0], fwstate.V4)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("Propose refused the foreign DNAT rule")
	}
	return ex
}

type hlWant struct {
	level  Level
	reason string
}

func TestHlHealth(t *testing.T) {
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		mutate func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput)
		want   []hlWant
	}{
		{name: "a healthy host", mutate: func(*testing.T, *HealthInput) {}},
		{name: "REJECT is a valid incoming policy", mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) { in.DefaultInput = "REJECT" }},
		{
			name: "block missing from after.rules",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Files[fwstate.V4] = []byte("# after.rules\n")
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "after.rules holds no Darkpanel Docker block"}},
		},
		{
			name: "block missing from after6.rules",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				delete(in.Files, fwstate.V6)
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "after6.rules holds no Darkpanel Docker block"}},
		},
		{
			name: "duplicated block markers",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Files[fwstate.V4] = slices.Concat(in.Files[fwstate.V4], in.Files[fwstate.V4])
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "after.rules: "}},
		},
		{
			name: "IPV6=no leaves after6.rules and the IPv6 chains alone",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.IPv6 = false
				delete(in.Files, fwstate.V6)
				delete(in.Loaded, fwstate.V6)
			},
		},
		{
			name: "a loaded rule is missing",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V4, "DOCKER-USER")
				c.Rules = slices.Delete(c.Rules, 0, 1)
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "loaded DOCKER-USER (IPv4) does not match the Docker block"}},
		},
		{
			name: "a loaded rule is duplicated",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V6, ChainDeny)
				c.Rules = slices.Insert(c.Rules, 0, c.Rules[0])
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "loaded " + ChainDeny + " (IPv6) does not match the Docker block"}},
		},
		{
			name: "loaded rules are out of order",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V4, hlChainName)
				c.Rules[0], c.Rules[1] = c.Rules[1], c.Rules[0]
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "loaded " + hlChainName + " (IPv4) does not match the Docker block"}},
		},
		{
			name: "a binding chain is not loaded",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				tbl := in.Loaded[fwstate.V4].Table("filter")
				tbl.Chains = slices.DeleteFunc(tbl.Chains, func(c netfilter.Chain) bool { return c.Name == hlChainName })
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "loaded " + hlChainName + " (IPv4) does not match the Docker block: chain is not loaded"}},
		},
		{
			name: "a stale binding chain is loaded",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				tbl := in.Loaded[fwstate.V4].Table("filter")
				tbl.Chains = append(tbl.Chains, netfilter.Chain{Name: "dp-b-ffffffffffff", Rules: []netfilter.Rule{hlRule(t, "-A dp-b-ffffffffffff -j RETURN")}})
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "loaded dp-b-ffffffffffff (IPv4) does not match the Docker block: chain is not in the block"}},
		},
		{
			name: "a foreign DOCKER-USER rule is reported once and not as a mismatch",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V4, "DOCKER-USER")
				c.Rules = slices.Insert(c.Rules, 0, hlRule(t, hlForeignRule))
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "DOCKER-USER (IPv4) holds a foreign rule: " + hlForeignRule}},
		},
		{
			name: "a rule of a stale block on disk is Darkpanel's, not foreign",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				stale := DefaultSettings()
				stale.PrivateSources = append(stale.PrivateSources, netip.MustParsePrefix("192.0.2.0/24"))
				block := Render(hlBlockInput(stale), fwstate.V4)
				file, err := WithBlock([]byte("# after.rules\n"), block)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatal(err)
				}
				in.Files[fwstate.V4], in.Loaded[fwstate.V4] = file, hlLoaded(t, block, "")
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "loaded DOCKER-USER (IPv4) does not match the Docker block"}},
		},
		{
			name: "FORWARD does not jump to DOCKER-USER",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V4, "FORWARD")
				c.Rules = slices.Delete(c.Rules, 0, 1)
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "FORWARD (IPv4) does not jump to DOCKER-USER"}},
		},
		{
			name: "Docker's rule comes before the jump to DOCKER-USER",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V4, "FORWARD")
				c.Rules[0], c.Rules[1] = c.Rules[1], c.Rules[0]
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "FORWARD (IPv4) reaches Docker's rule -A FORWARD -j DOCKER-FORWARD before DOCKER-USER"}},
		},
		{
			name: "no IPv6 network, so ip6tables FORWARD need not jump",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V6, "FORWARD")
				c.Rules = slices.Delete(c.Rules, 0, 1)
			},
		},
		{
			name: "an IPv6 network needs the ip6tables FORWARD jump",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Facts.Networks = append(in.Facts.Networks, hlV6Network())
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V6, "FORWARD")
				c.Rules = slices.Delete(c.Rules, 0, 1)
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "FORWARD (IPv6) does not jump to DOCKER-USER"}},
		},
		{
			name: "an incoming policy of ACCEPT in the configuration",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.DefaultInput = "ACCEPT"
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY is ACCEPT, not DROP or REJECT"}},
		},
		{
			name: "an incoming policy of ACCEPT loaded",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Loaded[fwstate.V4].Table("filter").Chain("INPUT").Policy = "ACCEPT"
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "loaded INPUT policy (IPv4) is ACCEPT, not DROP"}},
		},
		{
			name: "a non-Docker br-* interface",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Interfaces = append(in.Interfaces, "br-lan")
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Degraded, "interface br-lan is a br-* bridge that is not a Docker network's bridge"}},
		},
		{
			name: "a network in routed gateway mode",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Facts.Networks[1].GatewayModeV4 = "routed"
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Degraded, "network app is unprotected: gateway mode routed bypasses the DNAT gate"}},
		},
		{
			name: "a custom bridge name with a public subnet",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Facts.Networks[2].Subnets = []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("203.0.113.0/24")}
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Degraded, "network custom is unprotected: custom bridge name dpcustom with non-private subnet 203.0.113.0/24"}},
		},
		{
			name: "IPV6=no with an IPv6 Docker network",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.IPv6 = false
				delete(in.Files, fwstate.V6)
				delete(in.Loaded, fwstate.V6)
				in.Facts.Networks = append(in.Facts.Networks, hlV6Network())
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Degraded, "IPV6=no in /etc/default/ufw while Docker network v6net has IPv6 enabled"}},
		},
		{
			name: "issues come in the order of the specification",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				in.Files[fwstate.V4] = []byte("# after.rules\n")
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V4, "DOCKER-USER")
				c.Rules = slices.Insert(c.Rules, 0, hlRule(t, hlForeignRule))
				in.DefaultInput = "ACCEPT"
				in.Interfaces = append(in.Interfaces, "br-lan")
			},
			want: []hlWant{
				{Broken, "after.rules holds no Darkpanel Docker block"},
				{Broken, "DOCKER-USER (IPv4) holds a foreign rule"},
				{Broken, "DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY is ACCEPT"},
				{Degraded, "interface br-lan"},
			},
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			in := hlInput(t, DefaultSettings(), "")
			tc.mutate(t, &in)
			hlCheck(t, Health(in), tc.want)
		})
	}
}

func hlCheck(t *testing.T, got []Issue, want []hlWant) {
	t.Helper()
	if len(got) != len(want) {
		t.Fatalf("issues = %+v, want %d", got, len(want))
	}
	for i, w := range want {
		if got[i].Level != w.level || !strings.Contains(got[i].Reason, w.reason) {
			t.Errorf("issue %d = %+v, want level %s containing %q", i, got[i], w.level, w.reason)
		}
	}
}

func TestHlHealthForeignForwards(t *testing.T) {
	covered := DefaultSettings()
	covered.ForwardExemptions = []Exemption{hlExemption(t)}
	inDocker := DefaultSettings()
	inDocker.ForwardExemptions = []Exemption{{
		OrigDestination: netip.MustParseAddr("198.51.100.7"),
		Destination:     netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.9"),
		Proto:           "tcp",
	}}
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		s    Settings
		nat  string
		want []hlWant
	}{
		{name: "no foreign DNAT rule", s: DefaultSettings()},
		{
			name: "a foreign DNAT rule without an exemption",
			s:    DefaultSettings(),
			nat:  hlForeignDNAT,
			want: []hlWant{{Degraded, "foreign DNAT forward has no exemption (IPv4): " + strings.TrimSuffix(hlForeignDNAT, "\n")}},
		},
		{name: "a foreign DNAT rule its exemption covers", s: covered, nat: hlForeignDNAT},
		{
			name: "an exemption whose destination lies in a Docker subnet",
			s:    inDocker,
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "exemption 0: destination 172.17.0.9 lies in Docker network bridge (172.17.0.0/16)"}},
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			hlCheck(t, Health(hlInput(t, tc.s, tc.nat)), tc.want)
		})
	}
}

func TestHlHealthWithoutTheBlock(t *testing.T) {
	// flag on while UFW is disabled: Want is false and Docker's own
	// DOCKER-USER is loaded.
	base := func(t *testing.T) HealthInput {
		in := hlInput(t, DefaultSettings(), hlForeignDNAT)
		in.Want = false
		in.Files, in.Expected = nil, nil
		for _, f := range []fwstate.Family{fwstate.V4, fwstate.V6} {
			in.Loaded[f] = hlLoaded(t, hlDockerDefault, hlForeignDNAT)
			in.Loaded[f].Table("filter").Chain("INPUT").Policy = "ACCEPT"
		}
		return in
	}
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		mutate func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput)
		want   []hlWant
	}{
		{name: "block, chains, FORWARD, DNAT and loaded policy are not checked", mutate: func(*testing.T, *HealthInput) {}},
		{
			name: "a foreign DOCKER-USER rule still counts",
			mutate: func(t *testing.T, in *HealthInput) {
				c := hlChain(t, *in, fwstate.V4, "DOCKER-USER")
				c.Rules = slices.Insert(c.Rules, 0, hlRule(t, hlForeignRule))
			},
			want: []hlWant{{Broken, "DOCKER-USER (IPv4) holds a foreign rule: " + hlForeignRule}},
		},
		{
			name:   "the configured incoming policy still counts",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) { in.DefaultInput = "ACCEPT" },
			want:   []hlWant{{Broken, "DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY is ACCEPT, not DROP or REJECT"}},
		},
		{
			name:   "a non-Docker br-* interface still counts",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) { in.Interfaces = append(in.Interfaces, "br-lan") },
			want:   []hlWant{{Degraded, "interface br-lan"}},
		},
		{
			name:   "an unprotected network still counts",
			mutate: func(_ *testing.T, in *HealthInput) { in.Facts.Networks[1].GatewayModeV4 = "nat-unprotected" },
			want:   []hlWant{{Degraded, "network app is unprotected: gateway mode nat-unprotected bypasses the DNAT gate"}},
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			in := base(t)
			tc.mutate(t, &in)
			hlCheck(t, Health(in), tc.want)
		})
	}
}

func TestHlUnprotected(t *testing.T) {
	pfx := func(ps ...string) []netip.Prefix {
		var out []netip.Prefix
		for _, p := range ps {
			out = append(out, netip.MustParsePrefix(p))
		}
		return out
	}
	br := func(over func(*Network)) Network {
		n := Network{ID: "eeeeeeeeeeee5555", Name: "n", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "br-eeeeeeeeeeee", Subnets: pfx("172.20.0.0/16")}
		over(&n)
		return n
	}
	only := Settings{PrivateSources: pfx("203.0.113.0/24")}
	tests := []struct {
		name   string
		n      Network
		s      Settings
		reason string
	}{
		{name: "the default bridge", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.Name, n.Bridge = "bridge", "docker0" }), s: DefaultSettings()},
		{name: "nat mode", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.GatewayModeV4 = "nat" }), s: DefaultSettings()},
		{name: "routed IPv4 mode", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.GatewayModeV4 = "routed" }), s: DefaultSettings(), reason: "gateway mode routed bypasses the DNAT gate"},
		{name: "nat-unprotected IPv4 mode", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.GatewayModeV4 = "nat-unprotected" }), s: DefaultSettings(), reason: "gateway mode nat-unprotected bypasses the DNAT gate"},
		{name: "routed IPv6 mode", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.GatewayModeV6 = "routed" }), s: DefaultSettings(), reason: "gateway mode routed bypasses the DNAT gate"},
		{name: "a network that is not a bridge", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.Driver, n.Bridge, n.GatewayModeV4 = "macvlan", "", "routed" }), s: DefaultSettings()},
		{name: "a custom bridge name with a private subnet", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.Bridge = "dpcustom" }), s: DefaultSettings()},
		{
			name:   "a custom bridge name with a public subnet",
			n:      br(func(n *Network) { n.Bridge, n.Subnets = "dpcustom", pfx("172.20.0.0/16", "203.0.113.0/24") }),
			s:      DefaultSettings(),
			reason: "custom bridge name dpcustom with non-private subnet 203.0.113.0/24",
		},
		{name: "a default bridge name with a public subnet", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.Subnets = pfx("203.0.113.0/24") }), s: DefaultSettings()},
		{name: "a custom bridge name whose subnet is a private source", n: br(func(n *Network) { n.Bridge, n.Subnets = "dpcustom", pfx("203.0.113.0/24") }), s: only},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			reason, got := Unprotected(tc.n, tc.s)
			if got != (tc.reason != "") || reason != tc.reason {
				t.Errorf("Unprotected = %q, %v, want %q", reason, got, tc.reason)
			}
		})
	}
}
```
