- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `health.go`, declare the Contracts "dockerfw health" types and functions with doc comments. `Level` values are `degraded` and `broken`; `Issue` has the JSON tags Contracts gives. Do not add a package comment (`settings.go` has it).

`Health(in HealthInput) []Issue` returns nil for a healthy host and otherwise the issues in the order of the checks below. The order is check by check, and within a check IPv4 before IPv6; it is never grouped by family. Rule text in a reason is `netfilter.Rule.Text`. Family names in reasons are `IPv4` and `IPv6`; the files are `after.rules` (V4) and `after6.rules` (V6).

Setup, before the checks:

1. The families examined are V4, plus V6 when `in.IPv6` is true. With `IPv6` false, `after6.rules` and the IPv6 chains are never examined, because UFW never reads them. Every per-family check below runs over these families only. A family whose `Loaded` entry is nil skips the checks that read loaded rules; a nil entry of `Files` or `Expected` is a family with no file or no expected block.
2. The expected rules of a family are `BlockRules(in.Expected[f])`; an `Expected` entry that is nil or does not parse is skipped by the chain comparison (check 2).
3. The known Darkpanel rules of a family are the rules of the `DOCKER-USER` chain in the filter table of the expected block, plus those of the block `BlockOf(in.Files[f])` finds in the file on disk (a missing, malformed or unparsable block adds none). Counting the block on disk keeps a stale block's own rules from being called foreign.

The checks, in order. "W" marks a check that runs only when `in.Want` is true:

1. W, block presence, per family: `BlockOf(in.Files[f])` returning an error is a `Broken` issue `<file>: <the error text>`; no block is a `Broken` issue `<file> holds no Darkpanel Docker block`.
2. W, loaded chains, per family: compare, with `netfilter.Key(rule, f == fwstate.V6)`, the filter-table chains the expected block declares and that `Owned` accepts (in the block's order), then any other `Owned` chain loaded in the filter table (in loaded order). For a `DOCKER-USER` chain, first drop the foreign rules (the rules `Foreign(chain, known, f)` returns, matched in chain order by `Line` and `Text`), because check 4 reports them. A chain that differs is one `Broken` issue `loaded <chain> (<family>) does not match the Docker block: <detail>` where the detail is `chain is not loaded` (expected, not loaded), `chain is not in the block` (loaded, not expected), `it holds <n> rules, the block has <m>` (different counts, after the foreign rules are dropped) or `rule <i> differs from the block` (same counts; `i` is the 1-based index of the first rule whose key differs). A duplicated, missing, extra or reordered rule is therefore always reported.
3. W, `FORWARD`, per family (IPv6 only when some network in `Facts.Networks` has `IPv6` true, because Docker loads no IPv6 rules otherwise): `Broken` `FORWARD (<family>) does not jump to DOCKER-USER` when the filter table has no `FORWARD` chain or no rule of it has target `DOCKER-USER`; otherwise, when a rule before the first jump to `DOCKER-USER` is one of Docker's own, `Broken` `FORWARD (<family>) reaches Docker's rule <text> before DOCKER-USER`. A rule is Docker's own when its target is the chain `DOCKER-FORWARD`, `DOCKER` or `DOCKER-ISOLATION-STAGE-1`, or its target is `ACCEPT` and its in or out interface is `br-+` or the `Bridge` of a network in `Facts.Networks`. The missing-jump test comes first, so a `FORWARD` with Docker's rules and no jump reports the missing jump.
4. Foreign `DOCKER-USER` rules, per family, whatever `Want` says: one `Broken` issue per rule `Foreign(chain, known, f)` returns, `DOCKER-USER (<family>) holds a foreign rule: <text>`.
5. W, foreign forwards, per family: for each rule of `ForeignDNAT(<the loaded nat table>)` that `Covered(rule, in.Settings.ForwardExemptions)` does not cover, `Degraded` `foreign DNAT forward has no exemption (<family>): <text>`.
6. Exemption conflicts, whatever `Want` says: one `Broken` issue per string `ExemptionConflicts(in.Settings.ForwardExemptions, in.Facts.Networks)` returns, the string being the reason.
7. Incoming policy: when `in.DefaultInput` is not `DROP` or `REJECT` (the empty string included), `Broken` `DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY is <value>, not DROP or REJECT`, whatever `Want` says. Then, W only, per family, when the filter table's `INPUT` chain exists and its policy is not `DROP` (UFW's `REJECT` default is realized in rules, so the loaded policy is `DROP` either way), `Broken` `loaded INPUT policy (<family>) is <policy>, not DROP`. The loaded policy is not checked while `Want` is false, because UFW disabled leaves it `ACCEPT`.
8. Non-Docker bridges, whatever `Want` says: for each name of `in.Interfaces` that starts with `br-` and is not the `Bridge` of a network in `Facts.Networks`, `Degraded` `interface <name> is a br-* bridge that is not a Docker network's bridge`.
9. Unprotected networks, whatever `Want` says: for each network of `Facts.Networks` in order for which `Unprotected(n, in.Settings)` reports true, `Degraded` `network <name> is unprotected: <reason>`.
10. `IPV6=no`, whatever `Want` says: when `in.IPv6` is false, for each network with `IPv6` true, `Degraded` `IPV6=no in /etc/default/ufw while Docker network <name> has IPv6 enabled`.

With `Want` false (the flag is on and UFW is disabled) checks 1, 2, 3, 5 and the loaded half of 7 are skipped, and checks 4, 6, the configured half of 7, 8, 9 and 10 run.

`Unprotected(n Network, s Settings) (reason string, unprotected bool)`, first match wins:

1. A network whose `Driver` is not `bridge` is `"", false`.
2. For `GatewayModeV4` then `GatewayModeV6`: a value of `routed` or `nat-unprotected` gives `gateway mode <value> bypasses the DNAT gate`, true.
3. A default bridge name (`docker0`, or `br-` plus the first 12 characters of `ID` when `ID` has at least 12) is `"", false`.
4. For the first subnet in `n.Subnets` that no `s.PrivateSources` range holds (the range contains the subnet's address and its prefix length is no longer than the subnet's): `custom bridge name <n.Bridge> with non-private subnet <subnet>`, true.
5. Otherwise `"", false`.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw/restore_input_test.go` with exactly this content. Rule lines are written in save syntax, as `netfilter.Rule.Text` holds them; the block is three hand-written `DOCKER-USER` lines whose last is the block's own `-j RETURN`.

```go
package dockerfw

import (
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

const (
	chForeignA = "-A DOCKER-USER -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j DROP"
	chForeignB = "-A DOCKER-USER -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT"
	chForeignC = "-A DOCKER-USER -i eth9 -j REJECT --reject-with icmp-port-unreachable"
)

var chBlock = []string{
	"-A DOCKER-USER -i docker0 -j RETURN",
	"-A DOCKER-USER -m conntrack --ctstate DNAT -j darkpanel-docker-bindings",
	"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN",
}

func chRules(t *testing.T, lines ...string) []netfilter.Rule {
	t.Helper()
	c := chChain(t, lines...)
	return c.Rules
}

func chChain(t *testing.T, lines ...string) *netfilter.Chain {
	t.Helper()
	text := "*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n" + strings.Join(lines, "\n") + "\nCOMMIT\n"
	rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(text))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("parse %q: %v", lines, err)
	}
	return rs.Table("filter").Chain("DOCKER-USER")
}

func chJoin(parts ...[]string) []string { return slices.Concat(parts...) }

func TestChLayoutOf(t *testing.T) {
	a, b, c := []string{chForeignA}, []string{chForeignB}, []string{chForeignC}
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		chain []string // nil: no chain at all
		known []string
		want  Layout
	}{
		{name: "no chain", want: Layout{}},
		{name: "only the block", chain: chBlock, known: chBlock, want: Layout{}},
		{name: "foreign before the block", chain: chJoin(a, chBlock), known: chBlock, want: Layout{Before: a}},
		{name: "foreign after the block", chain: chJoin(chBlock, a), known: chBlock, want: Layout{After: a}},
		{
			name:  "foreign on both sides",
			chain: chJoin(a, c, chBlock, b),
			known: chBlock,
			want:  Layout{Before: chJoin(a, c), After: b},
		},
		{name: "only foreign rules", chain: chJoin(a, b), known: chBlock, want: Layout{Before: chJoin(a, b)}},
		{
			name:  "Docker's default RETURN counts as the block",
			chain: chJoin(a, []string{"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN"}, b),
			want:  Layout{Before: a, After: b},
		},
		{
			name:  "foreign between block lines",
			chain: chJoin(a, chBlock[:1], b, chBlock[1:]),
			known: chBlock,
			want: Layout{
				Before:      chJoin(a, b),
				Interleaved: true,
				Order:       chJoin(a, chBlock[:1], b, chBlock[1:]),
			},
		},
		{
			name:  "interleaved moves the rule after the block too",
			chain: chJoin(chBlock[:1], a, chBlock[1:], b),
			known: chBlock,
			want: Layout{
				Before:      chJoin(a, b),
				Interleaved: true,
				Order:       chJoin(chBlock[:1], a, chBlock[1:], b),
			},
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			var chain *netfilter.Chain
			if tc.chain != nil {
				chain = chChain(t, tc.chain...)
			}
			var known []netfilter.Rule
			if tc.known != nil {
				known = chRules(t, tc.known...)
			}
			if got := LayoutOf(chain, known, fwstate.V4); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("LayoutOf = %#v, want %#v", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestChLayoutOfIPv6(t *testing.T) {
	block := []string{"-A DOCKER-USER -d fc00::/7 -j darkpanel-docker-deny", "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN"}
	foreign := "-A DOCKER-USER -s 2001:db8::/32 -j DROP"
	got := LayoutOf(chChain(t, chJoin([]string{foreign}, block)...), chRules(t, block...), fwstate.V6)
	if want := (Layout{Before: []string{foreign}}); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("LayoutOf = %#v, want %#v", got, want)
	}
}

func TestChDockerUserInput(t *testing.T) {
	a, b := []string{chForeignA}, []string{chForeignB}
	const head = "*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n"
	tests := []struct {
		name  string
		block []string
		l     Layout
		want  string
	}{
		{name: "no block, no foreign rules", want: head + "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\nCOMMIT\n"},
		{
			name:  "the block alone",
			block: chBlock,
			want:  head + strings.Join(chBlock, "\n") + "\nCOMMIT\n",
		},
		{
			name:  "foreign rules around the block",
			block: chBlock,
			l:     Layout{Before: a, After: b},
			want:  head + chForeignA + "\n" + strings.Join(chBlock, "\n") + "\n" + chForeignB + "\nCOMMIT\n",
		},
		{
			name: "foreign rules around Docker's default RETURN",
			l:    Layout{Before: a, After: b},
			want: head + chForeignA + "\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n" + chForeignB + "\nCOMMIT\n",
		},
		{
			name:  "an empty block slice is -j RETURN",
			block: []string{},
			want:  head + "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\nCOMMIT\n",
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := string(DockerUserInput(tc.block, tc.l)); got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("DockerUserInput =\n%s\nwant\n%s", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// A layout that is not interleaved survives a reload: the chain the input
// builds gives the same layout back.
func TestChLayoutRoundTrip(t *testing.T) {
	l := Layout{Before: []string{chForeignA, chForeignC}, After: []string{chForeignB}}
	rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(string(DockerUserInput(chBlock, l))))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("the input does not parse: %v", err)
	}
	chain := rs.Table("filter").Chain("DOCKER-USER")
	if got := LayoutOf(chain, chRules(t, chBlock...), fwstate.V4); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, l) {
		t.Errorf("LayoutOf(reloaded) = %#v, want %#v", got, l)
	}
}

func TestChCleanupInput(t *testing.T) {
	const head = "*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n"
	loaded := func(t *testing.T, text string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
		t.Helper()
		rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(text))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return rs
	}
	full := loaded(t, "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:ufw-user-forward - [0:0]\n"+
		":darkpanel-docker-bindings - [0:0]\n:darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]\n:dp-b-0123456789ab - [0:0]\n:dp-b-fedcba987654 - [0:0]\n"+
		strings.Join(chBlock, "\n")+"\n-A dp-b-0123456789ab -j darkpanel-docker-deny\nCOMMIT\n"+
		"*nat\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:darkpanel-nat - [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n")
	bare := loaded(t, "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:ufw-user-forward - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\nCOMMIT\n")
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		rs   *netfilter.Ruleset
		want string
	}{
		{
			name: "every darkpanel and binding chain is flushed, then deleted",
			rs:   full,
			want: head +
				"-F darkpanel-docker-bindings\n-F darkpanel-docker-deny\n-F dp-b-0123456789ab\n-F dp-b-fedcba987654\n" +
				"-X darkpanel-docker-bindings\n-X darkpanel-docker-deny\n-X dp-b-0123456789ab\n-X dp-b-fedcba987654\nCOMMIT\n",
		},
		{name: "no owned chain besides DOCKER-USER", rs: bare, want: head + "COMMIT\n"},
		{name: "no ruleset", rs: nil, want: head + "COMMIT\n"},
	}
	for _, tc := range tests {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := string(CleanupInput(tc.rs)); got != tc.want {
				t.Errorf("CleanupInput =\n%s\nwant\n%s", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

In `restore_input.go`, declare the Contracts "dockerfw restore inputs" `Layout` (with its JSON tags) and the three functions, each with a doc comment. No package comment.

`LayoutOf(chain *netfilter.Chain, known []netfilter.Rule, f fwstate.Family) Layout`:

1. A nil `chain` gives the zero `Layout` (every field nil or false).
2. Call `Foreign(chain, known, f)` once. Mark a rule of `chain.Rules` foreign by walking the returned slice as a subsequence of the chain: the rule equals the next foreign rule in both `Line` and `Text`. Do not call `Foreign` per rule.
3. Every rule that is not foreign is a block line. That includes an unconditional `-j RETURN`, whether it is Docker's default (no block loaded) or the block's last line. Find the first and last block line in chain order.
4. A foreign rule before the first block line, or any foreign rule when the chain holds no block line, goes into `Before`; one after the last block line goes into `After`; one between the first and last block line makes `Interleaved` true. Rule text is `Rule.Text` verbatim, in chain order.
5. When `Interleaved` is true: `Before` holds every foreign rule in chain order (the ones that were after the block too), `After` is nil, and `Order` holds the `Text` of every rule of the chain, foreign and block, in chain order. When it is false, `Order` is nil.
6. An empty `Before` or `After` is nil, not an empty slice (the tests compare with `reflect.DeepEqual`, and the record is stored as JSON).

`DockerUserInput(block []string, l Layout) []byte`: `block` holds the `DOCKER-USER` lines to load (save syntax, each already starting `-A DOCKER-USER`). The output is these lines, each ended by `\n`, in this order: `*filter`; `:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]`; every `l.Before` line; every `block` line, or the single line `-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN` when `block` is nil or empty; every `l.After` line; `COMMIT`. Lines are copied verbatim and nothing else is added or reordered. The declaration flushes the chain under `-n`, so the chain ends up exactly as the lines say. `Interleaved` and `Order` play no part: a caller that sees `Interleaved` has put every foreign rule into `Before` already.

`CleanupInput(loaded *netfilter.Ruleset) []byte`: the output is, each line ended by `\n`: `*filter`; `:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]`; `-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN`; then `-F <chain>` for every owned chain; then `-X <chain>` for every owned chain, in the same order; then `COMMIT`. An owned chain is a chain of the filter table of `loaded`, in the order that table lists them, for which `Owned(name)` is true and the name is not `DOCKER-USER`. Every `-F` comes before every `-X` so that no chain is deleted while another still jumps to it. Only the filter table is read. A nil `loaded`, or one without a filter table, gives the three-line header and `COMMIT`.

### Task 24: dockerfw: UFW rule operations

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw/ruleops.go`
- Test: `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw/ruleops_test.go`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Contracts "dockerfw bindings and rules" (`LabelPrefix`, `RuleOf`: a realized rule's label is `ctr <ContainerRule.ID>`), Contracts "dockerfw realization" (the rules `Realize` returns: ID empty, Comment `ctr <rule id>`, one family each), and wave 1's `model.Rule` with `Normalize`, `Validate`, `AddArgs`, `InsertArgs`, `DeleteArgs` and `Merge`. The test also calls wave 1's `predict.Edit`, which numbers, inserts and replaces rules as UFW 0.36 does.
- Produces: Contracts "dockerfw rule operations": `RuleOp` and `RuleOps`, exactly as stated there. `RuleOps` is pure: it reads no host state and runs nothing.

**Items:** 9

**Depends on:** Task 21
**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 2 - coupling 2 - risk 0 = 5

`RuleOps` turns the rules `Realize` wants into the UFW commands that bring the host there. The module root (Task 43) runs each operation as a journaled effect: a `Delete` through `model.DeleteArgs` of the current rule with that id, an `Add` through `model.InsertArgs(Insert, *Add)` or, when `Insert` is 0, `model.AddArgs(*Add)`. Three facts of UFW 0.36 shape the rules below: `ufw delete` matches a rule by its specification and ignores the comment; `ufw route allow ...` for a tuple that UFW already holds with another comment does not add a rule but replaces the comment of the existing one (`predict.Edit` reproduces this); and UFW numbers the rules of `user.rules` first and those of `user6.rules` after them, `ufw insert N` placing the new rule before the rule now numbered N.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw/ruleops_test.go`. Every case runs `RuleOps`, compares the operations exactly, then replays current and the operations through `predict.Edit` and checks what UFW would hold: the container rules of each family in the order of `desired`, and every other rule untouched and in its order. A wrong position therefore fails twice, once on the number and once on the replay.

```go
package dockerfw

import (
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/predict"
)

// roULID is the n-th 26-character ULID of these tests.
func roULID(n int) string { return fmt.Sprintf("01J%023d", n) }

// roRule is a route rule to 172.17.0.2 port 80 out on docker0 as Realize
// makes it: no id, labelled for container rule ctr.
func roRule(action model.Action, from string, ctr int) model.Rule {
	return model.Rule{
		Action: action, Direction: model.DirRoute, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: from,
		To: "172.17.0.2", ToPort: "80", OutIface: "docker0", Family: model.FamilyV4,
		Comment: LabelPrefix + roULID(ctr),
	}
}

// roRule6 is roRule for the IPv6 address of the container on br-0123456789ab.
func roRule6(action model.Action, from string, ctr int) model.Rule {
	r := roRule(action, from, ctr)
	r.To, r.OutIface, r.Family = "fd00:dead::2", "br-0123456789ab", model.FamilyV6
	return r
}

// roHave is r as UFW holds it once written with the tag id: the shape
// wave 1's status lists.
func roHave(r model.Rule, id int) model.Rule {
	r.ID, r.Origin, r.Log = roULID(id), model.OriginDarkpanel, model.LogOff
	return r
}

// roManual is a manual incoming allow of one TCP port, IPv4 only.
func roManual(port string) model.Rule {
	return model.Rule{
		ID: "manual-" + strings.Repeat("0", 16-len(port)) + port, Action: model.ActionAllow, Direction: model.DirIn,
		Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: model.Any, To: model.Any, ToPort: port, Family: model.FamilyV4,
		Origin: model.OriginManual, Log: model.LogOff, Comment: "manual " + port,
	}
}

// roOther is a Darkpanel rule that is not a container rule.
func roOther() model.Rule {
	return roHave(model.Rule{
		Action: model.ActionAllow, Direction: model.DirIn, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: model.Any,
		To: model.Any, ToPort: "2222", Family: model.FamilyV4, Comment: "ssh",
	}, 900)
}

func roDel(id int) RuleOp { return RuleOp{Delete: roULID(id)} }

// roAdd is the operation that adds r with the new id n at position insert.
func roAdd(r model.Rule, n, insert int) RuleOp {
	r = r.Normalize()
	r.ID = roULID(n)
	return RuleOp{Add: &r, Insert: insert}
}

// roShow prints operations with their rules dereferenced.
func roShow(ops []RuleOp) string {
	var parts []string
	for _, op := range ops {
		if op.Add != nil {
			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("add@%d %+v", op.Insert, *op.Add))
		} else {
			parts = append(parts, "delete "+op.Delete)
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
}

// roSeq returns a newID function that hands out roULID(first), then the
// next numbers, and counts its calls in *calls.
func roSeq(first int, calls *int) func() string {
	return func() string {
		*calls++
		return roULID(first + *calls - 1)
	}
}

// roReplay runs the rules of current, then ops, through predict.Edit, which
// numbers and orders rules as UFW 0.36 does, and returns the rules UFW
// would then hold.
func roReplay(t *testing.T, current []model.Rule, ops []RuleOp) []model.Rule {
	t.Helper()
	empty := []byte("*filter\nCOMMIT\n")
	cfg := fwstate.Config{
		IPv6: true, LogLevel: "low", DefaultInput: "DROP", DefaultOutput: "ACCEPT", DefaultForward: "DROP",
		Files: map[string]core.RestoreEntry{
			"/etc/ufw/user.rules":  {Path: "/etc/ufw/user.rules", Present: true, Data: empty},
			"/etc/ufw/user6.rules": {Path: "/etc/ufw/user6.rules", Present: true, Data: empty},
		},
	}
	run := func(args []string) {
		t.Helper()
		next, err := predict.Edit(cfg, args)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("ufw %s: %v", strings.Join(args, " "), err)
		}
		cfg = next
	}
	byID := map[string]model.Rule{}
	for _, r := range current {
		byID[r.ID] = r
		run(model.AddArgs(r))
	}
	for _, op := range ops {
		switch {
		case op.Delete != "":
			r, ok := byID[op.Delete]
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("delete of %s, which current does not hold", op.Delete)
			}
			run(model.DeleteArgs(r))
		case op.Add != nil && op.Insert > 0:
			run(model.InsertArgs(op.Insert, *op.Add))
		case op.Add != nil:
			run(model.AddArgs(*op.Add))
		default:
			t.Fatal("an operation that neither deletes nor adds")
		}
	}
	return model.Merge(cfg.Rules4, cfg.Rules6)
}

// roLabels lists the labels of the container rules of one family, in order.
func roLabels(rules []model.Rule, fam model.Family) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, r := range rules {
		if _, ok := RuleOf(r.Comment); ok && r.Origin == model.OriginDarkpanel && r.Family == fam {
			out = append(out, r.Comment)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// roOthers lists the comments of the rules that are not container rules.
func roOthers(rules []model.Rule) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, r := range rules {
		if _, ok := RuleOf(r.Comment); !ok || r.Origin != model.OriginDarkpanel {
			out = append(out, r.Comment)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func TestRoRuleOps(t *testing.T) {
	allow := roRule(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 1)
	deny := roRule(model.ActionDeny, "203.0.113.0/24", 3)
	other := roRule(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 5)
	other.To = "172.17.0.3"
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		current []model.Rule
		desired []model.Rule
		want    []RuleOp
		// labels lists the container rules of each family UFW must hold after
		// the operations, in order; nil derives them from desired.
		labels map[model.Family][]string
	}{
		{
			name:    "adds append when UFW holds no container rule",
			current: []model.Rule{roManual("22")},
			desired: []model.Rule{allow, deny},
			want:    []RuleOp{roAdd(allow, 500, 0), roAdd(deny, 501, 0)},
		},
		{
			name:    "a rule equal but for its id is kept",
			current: []model.Rule{roHave(allow, 101), roHave(deny, 103)},
			desired: []model.Rule{allow, deny},
		},
		{
			name:    "a changed rule is deleted and added again",
			current: []model.Rule{roHave(allow, 101)},
			desired: []model.Rule{other},
			want:    []RuleOp{roDel(101), roAdd(other, 500, 0)},
		},
		{
			name:    "a rule no desired rule equals is deleted",
			current: []model.Rule{roHave(allow, 101), roHave(deny, 103)},
			desired: []model.Rule{allow},
			want:    []RuleOp{roDel(103)},
		},
		{
			name:    "nothing desired deletes every container rule and nothing else",
			current: []model.Rule{roOther(), roHave(allow, 101), roManual("22"), roHave(deny, 103)},
			desired: nil,
			want:    []RuleOp{roDel(101), roDel(103)},
		},
		{
			name:    "a new rule goes right after the desired rule before it",
			current: []model.Rule{roManual("22"), roHave(allow, 101), roManual("80"), roHave(deny, 103)},
			desired: []model.Rule{allow, other, deny},
			want:    []RuleOp{roAdd(other, 500, 3)},
		},
		{
			name:    "a new first rule goes before the first kept rule",
			current: []model.Rule{roManual("22"), roHave(allow, 101)},
			desired: []model.Rule{other, allow},
			want:    []RuleOp{roAdd(other, 500, 2)},
		},
		{
			name:    "a kept rule that is out of order is deleted and added after its predecessor",
			current: []model.Rule{roHave(deny, 103), roHave(allow, 101)},
			desired: []model.Rule{allow, deny},
			want:    []RuleOp{roDel(103), roAdd(deny, 500, 0)},
		},
		{
			name: "an IPv6 rule is numbered after every IPv4 rule",
			current: []model.Rule{
				roManual("22"), roHave(allow, 101),
				roHave(roRule6(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 7), 107),
			},
			desired: []model.Rule{
				allow, roRule6(model.ActionDeny, "2001:db8::/32", 9), roRule6(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 7),
			},
			want: []RuleOp{roAdd(roRule6(model.ActionDeny, "2001:db8::/32", 9), 500, 3)},
		},
		{
			name:    "an IPv4 rule inserted ahead of IPv6 rules keeps its IPv4 number",
			current: []model.Rule{roManual("22"), roHave(roRule6(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 7), 107)},
			desired: []model.Rule{allow, roRule6(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 7)},
			want:    []RuleOp{roAdd(allow, 500, 0)},
		},
		{
			name:    "two desired rules that differ only in label collapse to the first",
			current: nil,
			desired: []model.Rule{allow, roRule(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 2)},
			want:    []RuleOp{roAdd(allow, 500, 0)},
			labels:  map[model.Family][]string{model.FamilyV4: {allow.Comment}},
		},
		{
			name:    "a manual rule and a manual-looking label are never touched",
			current: []model.Rule{roManual("22"), {ID: "manual-00000000000000aa", Action: model.ActionAllow, Direction: model.DirIn, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: model.Any, To: model.Any, ToPort: "81", Family: model.FamilyV4, Origin: model.OriginManual, Log: model.LogOff, Comment: allow.Comment}},
			desired: []model.Rule{deny},
			want:    []RuleOp{roAdd(deny, 500, 0)},
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			calls := 0
			got, err := RuleOps(tt.current, tt.desired, roSeq(500, &calls))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tt.want) && (len(got) != 0 || len(tt.want) != 0) {
				t.Fatalf("operations:\n%s\nwant:\n%s", roShow(got), roShow(tt.want))
			}
			adds := 0
			for _, op := range got {
				if op.Add != nil {
					adds++
				}
			}
			if calls != adds {
				t.Errorf("newID called %d times for %d adds", calls, adds)
			}
			rules := roReplay(t, tt.current, got)
			for _, fam := range []model.Family{model.FamilyV4, model.FamilyV6} {
				want := tt.labels[fam]
				if tt.labels == nil {
					for _, d := range tt.desired {
						if d.Family == fam {
							want = append(want, d.Comment)
						}
					}
				}
				if have := roLabels(rules, fam); !slices.Equal(have, want) {
					t.Errorf("UFW holds %s container rules %q after the operations, want %q", fam, have, want)
				}
			}
			if have, want := roOthers(rules), roOthers(tt.current); !slices.Equal(have, want) {
				t.Errorf("rules that are not container rules are %q after the operations, want %q", have, want)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestRoRuleOpsRefuses(t *testing.T) {
	allow := roRule(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, 1)
	noLabel := allow
	noLabel.Comment = "web"
	both := model.Rule{Action: model.ActionAllow, Direction: model.DirIn, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: model.Any, To: model.Any, ToPort: "80", Family: model.FamilyBoth, Comment: LabelPrefix + roULID(1)}
	manualTwin := roManual("80")
	manualTwin.Direction, manualTwin.Proto = model.DirRoute, model.ProtoTCP
	manualTwin.To, manualTwin.ToPort, manualTwin.OutIface = "172.17.0.2", "80", "docker0"
	manualTwin.Comment = "by hand"
	raw := roHave(allow, 101)
	raw.Raw = "### tuple ### route:allow tcp 80 172.17.0.2 any 0.0.0.0/0 out_docker0"
	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		current []model.Rule
		desired []model.Rule
		newID   func() string
		want    string
	}{
		{
			name: "a desired rule without a container label", desired: []model.Rule{noLabel},
			newID: func() string { return roULID(500) }, want: "dockerfw: desired rule",
		},
		{
			name: "a desired rule for both families", desired: []model.Rule{both},
			newID: func() string { return roULID(500) }, want: "dockerfw: desired rule",
		},
		{
			name: "an id that is not a ULID", desired: []model.Rule{allow},
			newID: func() string { return "not-a-ulid" }, want: "dockerfw: ",
		},
		{
			name: "a desired rule that would take over a manual rule", current: []model.Rule{manualTwin},
			desired: []model.Rule{allow}, newID: func() string { return roULID(500) },
			want: manualTwin.ID,
		},
		{
			name: "a container rule outside the model", current: []model.Rule{raw},
			desired: nil, newID: func() string { return roULID(500) }, want: roULID(101),
		},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			ops, err := RuleOps(tt.current, tt.desired, tt.newID)
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("no error, operations:\n%s", roShow(ops))
			}
			if !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "dockerfw: ") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("error %q, want the prefix \"dockerfw: \" and %q", err, tt.want)
			}
			if len(ops) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("an error came with operations:\n%s", roShow(ops))
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw/ruleops.go` in package `dockerfw`, importing only `fmt`, `slices` and `internal/modules/firewall/model`. Every exported identifier has a doc comment; every error is a plain error from `fmt.Errorf` whose text starts with `dockerfw: ` (not an `*errcode.Error`); the text of a `Validate` error is included with `%v`, never `%w`, so that it cannot reach a client as a field error.

1. Declare `RuleOp` as Contracts "dockerfw rule operations" gives it.
2. Helpers. A **container rule** is a rule whose `Origin` is empty or `model.OriginDarkpanel` and whose `Comment` `RuleOf` reads. The **tuple** of a rule is `r.Normalize()` with `ID`, `Comment`, `Raw` and `Origin` cleared: what UFW matches on. Two tuples are the **same** when they are equal as structs, except that `Family` `both` is compatible with `v4` and with `v6` (UFW writes a rule of both families to both files).
3. `RuleOps(current, desired, newID)` works in six passes.
   1. *Desired rules.* Take each rule of `desired` in order and `Normalize` it. Refuse (`dockerfw: desired rule %q has no container label`) one whose `Origin` is not `darkpanel` or whose `Comment` `RuleOf` does not read, and (`dockerfw: desired rule %q is for family %q, not one family`) one whose `Family` is not `v4` or `v6`. Skip, without error, a rule that has the same `Family` and the same tuple as an earlier desired rule: UFW holds one rule per tuple, so the later rule's label is not realized and the first one's is. Refuse every other rule for which a rule of `current` that is not a container rule has the same tuple (`dockerfw: container rule %q would take over the rule %s: ufw keeps one rule per tuple`, naming that rule's id): adding it would rewrite the comment of a manual or other Darkpanel rule. The survivors, in order, are `des`.
   2. *Rules outside the model.* A container rule of `current` whose `Raw` is not empty cannot be deleted by specification: refuse with `dockerfw: container rule %s is outside the model and cannot be changed`, naming its id.
   3. *Keeps.* Walk `des` in order with `last[family]` starting at 0. For each rule, find the first container rule of `current`, not yet matched, at index `j` whose `Normalize`d form with `ID` and `Raw` cleared equals the desired rule as a struct (so `Comment`, `Family` and `Log` count). When there is one and `j+1 > last[family]`, it is kept: mark it matched and set `last[family] = j+1`. When there is none, or it lies before a rule already kept for that family, the desired rule is to be added and the found rule stays unmatched. The order test is what puts a deny back behind its allow when an earlier state held them the other way round.
   4. *Deletes.* Every container rule of `current` that is not matched yields `RuleOp{Delete: its id}`, in `current`'s order. A rule of family `both` equals no desired rule, so it is deleted. No other rule of `current` is ever deleted or moved.
   5. *Numbering lists.* Build two lists of what UFW will hold once the deletes have run: `v4` holds the surviving rules of `current` whose family is `v4` or `both`, `v6` those whose family is `v6` or `both`, each in `current`'s order. An entry remembers which `des` index it keeps, or none.
   6. *Adds.* Walk `des` in order; for each rule not kept, call `newID()` once, set it as the rule's `ID` and refuse with `dockerfw: rule for %q: %v` when `Validate` fails. Let `L` be the list of the rule's family as it is now (after the deletes and the adds before this one). Choose the 0-based index `p` at which the rule enters `L`: right after the entry for the nearest earlier `des` rule of the same family that `L` holds (kept, or added before); when there is none, at the index of the entry for the nearest later `des` rule of the same family that `L` holds (only kept rules can be there yet); when there is none either, `len(L)`. `Insert` is 0 when `p == len(L)` (UFW appends within the family), and otherwise `p+1` for `v4` and `len(v4)+p+1` for `v6`, where `len(v4)` is the length of the IPv4 list at this moment. Then insert the new entry into `L` at `p`. The operation is `RuleOp{Add: &rule, Insert: insert}`, where `rule` is the normalized desired rule with its new `ID`.
4. Return the deletes followed by the adds. With nothing to do the result is a nil slice and nil error; on any error the result is nil.

The three tests are `TestDcRealize`, `TestDcPrediction` and `TestDcDecisions`, each over the four images.

**Items:** 8, 9, 10

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-sonnet-medium

This task adds a test file and no production code. Task 1's captures are the only data: its `block` scenario holds the block written by hand into both `after` files, the two route rules UFW stored for the `web` binding, and the loaded state after `ufw reload`; its `base` and `cleanup` scenarios hold the same host without the block. Each test compares one stage of the pipeline with that data:

- `TestDcRealize`: `Realize` on the capture's facts and the two rows of Task 1's `block` scenario (allow `web` 8080/tcp from any, id `...0001`; deny 203.0.113.0/24 on it, id `...0003`) makes the route rules UFW stored, the route deny after the route allow, and, if Docker reported the binding on `::` for the IPv4-only default bridge, nothing else but IPv6 `in` rules for that proxied family; `Render` of its block gives, chain by chain and key by key, what the capture's hand-written block holds, for `DOCKER-USER`, `darkpanel-docker-bindings` and `darkpanel-docker-deny` in both families and for the binding chain in IPv4. (The binding chain's declaration in `after6.rules` is not compared: spec 2.6 does not say whether IPv6 declares it.)
- `TestDcPrediction`: `predict.Predict` of a reload with the `block` files, starting from the `base` loaded state, equals the `block` capture on every Darkpanel chain and on `ufw-user-forward` and `ufw6-user-forward`. This is the check Assumptions names: a non-UFW chain the block declares is flushed and refilled, and a Docker chain it does not declare is kept. The chains it ignores depend on `before.rules`, which the capture does not hold; the test gives `conf.Read` a minimal one.
- `TestDcDecisions`: `eval.Evaluate` on the capture decides sixteen packets as spec 2.6 says, each also evaluated on `base` and `cleanup` so that a verdict the block changed is shown to be the block's doing.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the test**

Create `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw/decisions_test.go`.

```go
package dockerfw

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"slices"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/conf"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/eval"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/loaded"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/predict"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

// The container rules of Task 1's block scenario: the ids its two UFW rules
// carry after "ctr ".
const (
	dcRowAllow = "01J00000000000000000000001"
	dcRowDeny  = "01J00000000000000000000003"
)

// dcDenied is the part of a reason that names a drop by the block's deny
// chain.
const dcDenied = "filter/darkpanel-docker-deny#"

// dcInspect is the part of a container's inspect output that Facts needs.
type dcInspect struct {
	ID     string `json:"Id"`
	Name   string
	State  struct{ Running bool }
	Config struct{ Labels map[string]string }

	NetworkSettings struct {
		Ports map[string][]struct {
			HostIP   string `json:"HostIp"`
			HostPort string
		}
		Networks map[string]struct{ IPAddress, GlobalIPv6Address string }
	}
}

// dcNet is the part of a network's inspect output that Facts needs.
type dcNet struct {
	ID         string `json:"Id"`
	Name       string
	Driver     string
	EnableIPv6 bool
	IPAM       struct{ Config []struct{ Subnet string } }
	Options    map[string]string
}

func dcAddr(s string) netip.Addr {
	if s == "" {
		return netip.IPv4Unspecified()
	}
	a, err := netip.ParseAddr(s)
	if err != nil {
		return netip.Addr{}
	}
	return a
}

// dcFacts reads what the module root would read from Docker for one capture
// scenario: its bridge networks and running containers.
func dcFacts(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) Facts {
	t.Helper()
	var nets []dcNet
	if err := json.Unmarshal(capFile(t, image, scenario, "networks.json"), &nets); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s/%s networks.json: %v", image, scenario, err)
	}
	var cts []dcInspect
	if err := json.Unmarshal(capFile(t, image, scenario, "containers.json"), &cts); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s/%s containers.json: %v", image, scenario, err)
	}
	var f Facts
	bridges := map[string]string{}
	for _, n := range nets {
		if n.Driver != "bridge" {
			continue
		}
		bridge := n.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.name"]
		switch {
		case bridge != "":
		case n.Name == "bridge":
			bridge = "docker0"
		default:
			bridge = "br-" + n.ID[:12]
		}
		net := Network{
			ID: n.ID, Name: n.Name, Driver: n.Driver, Bridge: bridge, IPv6: n.EnableIPv6,
			GatewayModeV4: n.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv4"],
			GatewayModeV6: n.Options["com.docker.network.bridge.gateway_mode_ipv6"],
		}
		for _, c := range n.IPAM.Config {
			if p, err := netip.ParsePrefix(c.Subnet); err == nil {
				net.Subnets = append(net.Subnets, p)
			}
		}
		f.Networks = append(f.Networks, net)
		bridges[n.Name] = bridge
	}
	sort.Slice(f.Networks, func(i, j int) bool { return f.Networks[i].Name < f.Networks[j].Name })
	for _, c := range cts {
		if !c.State.Running {
			continue
		}
		ct := Container{
			ID: c.ID, Name: strings.TrimPrefix(c.Name, "/"),
			Project: c.Config.Labels["com.docker.compose.project"], Service: c.Config.Labels["com.docker.compose.service"],
		}
		for key, bs := range c.NetworkSettings.Ports {
			port, proto, _ := strings.Cut(key, "/")
			cport, err := strconv.ParseUint(port, 10, 16)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s: published port key %q", ct.Name, key)
			}
			for _, b := range bs {
				hport, err := strconv.ParseUint(b.HostPort, 10, 16)
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("%s: host port %q", ct.Name, b.HostPort)
				}
				ct.Ports = append(ct.Ports, Published{HostAddr: dcAddr(b.HostIP), HostPort: uint16(hport), ContainerPort: uint16(cport), Proto: proto})
			}
		}
		sort.Slice(ct.Ports, func(i, j int) bool {
			a, b := ct.Ports[i], ct.Ports[j]
			if a.HostPort != b.HostPort {
				return a.HostPort < b.HostPort
			}
			return a.HostAddr.Less(b.HostAddr)
		})
		for name, e := range c.NetworkSettings.Networks {
			if bridge, ok := bridges[name]; ok {
				ct.Endpoints = append(ct.Endpoints, Endpoint{Network: name, Bridge: bridge, Addr4: dcAddr(e.IPAddress), Addr6: dcAddr(e.GlobalIPv6Address)})
			}
		}
		sort.Slice(ct.Endpoints, func(i, j int) bool { return ct.Endpoints[i].Network < ct.Endpoints[j].Network })
		f.Containers = append(f.Containers, ct)
	}
	sort.Slice(f.Containers, func(i, j int) bool { return f.Containers[i].Name < f.Containers[j].Name })
	return f
}

// dcWorld is one capture scenario: its facts, the name of the interface
// that faces the internet and the loaded rules of each family.
type dcWorld struct {
	facts  Facts
	uplink string
	rs     map[fwstate.Family]*netfilter.Ruleset
}

func dcLoad(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) dcWorld {
	t.Helper()
	w := dcWorld{facts: dcFacts(t, image, scenario), rs: capLoad(t, image, scenario)}
	have := map[string]bool{}
	var names []string
	for _, line := range strings.Fields(string(capFile(t, image, scenario, "interfaces.txt"))) {
		name, _, _ := strings.Cut(line, "@")
		have[name] = true
		names = append(names, name)
	}
	for _, n := range w.facts.Networks {
		if !have[n.Bridge] {
			t.Errorf("%s/%s: network %s has bridge %s, which interfaces.txt does not list", image, scenario, n.Name, n.Bridge)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(names)
	for _, name := range names {
		isBridge := slices.ContainsFunc(w.facts.Networks, func(n Network) bool { return n.Bridge == name })
		if name != "lo" && !isBridge && !strings.HasPrefix(name, "veth") && !strings.HasPrefix(name, "br-") {
			w.uplink = name
			break
		}
	}
	if w.uplink == "" {
		t.Fatalf("%s/%s: interfaces.txt lists no uplink interface: %q", image, scenario, names)
	}
	return w
}

// endpoint returns the container's address in the family and its bridge.
func (w dcWorld) endpoint(t *testing.T, name string, fam fwstate.Family) (netip.Addr, string) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, c := range w.facts.Containers {
		if c.Name != name {
			continue
		}
		for _, e := range c.Endpoints {
			if a := map[fwstate.Family]netip.Addr{fwstate.V4: e.Addr4, fwstate.V6: e.Addr6}[fam]; a.IsValid() {
				return a, e.Bridge
			}
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no running container %s with a %s address", name, fam)
	return netip.Addr{}, ""
}

// route is the router the evaluator asks once DNAT has rewritten a
// destination: a container's address is forwarded out of its bridge.
func (w dcWorld) route(p fwstate.Packet) (string, string, error) {
	for _, c := range w.facts.Containers {
		for _, e := range c.Endpoints {
			if p.Dst == e.Addr4 || p.Dst == e.Addr6 {
				return "forward", e.Bridge, nil
			}
		}
	}
	return "", "", fmt.Errorf("no route to %s", p.Dst)
}

// arrive is the first packet of a connection from src to a port of this
// host, arriving on the uplink.
func (w dcWorld) arrive(fam fwstate.Family, src string, port uint16) fwstate.Packet {
	host := map[fwstate.Family]string{fwstate.V4: "192.0.2.10", fwstate.V6: "2001:db8::10"}[fam]
	return fwstate.Packet{
		Family: fam, Path: "input", InIface: w.uplink, Src: netip.MustParseAddr(src), Dst: netip.MustParseAddr(host),
		SrcPort: 40000, DstPort: port, Proto: "tcp", CtState: "NEW",
	}
}

// leave is the first packet of a connection from a container to the
// internet.
func (w dcWorld) leave(t *testing.T, name string, fam fwstate.Family, dst string) fwstate.Packet {
	t.Helper()
	a, bridge := w.endpoint(t, name, fam)
	return fwstate.Packet{
		Family: fam, Path: "forward", InIface: bridge, OutIface: w.uplink, Src: a, Dst: netip.MustParseAddr(dst),
		SrcPort: 50000, DstPort: 443, Proto: "tcp", CtState: "NEW",
	}
}

// between is the first packet of a connection from a container to another
// address of its own bridge.
func (w dcWorld) between(t *testing.T, name string, fam fwstate.Family) fwstate.Packet {
	t.Helper()
	a, bridge := w.endpoint(t, name, fam)
	dst := a
	for range 40 {
		dst = dst.Next()
	}
	return fwstate.Packet{
		Family: fam, Path: "forward", InIface: bridge, OutIface: bridge, Src: a, Dst: dst,
		SrcPort: 50000, DstPort: 80, Proto: "tcp", CtState: "NEW",
	}
}

// into is a packet forwarded from the uplink straight to a container's port
// 80, with no DNAT.
func (w dcWorld) into(t *testing.T, name string, fam fwstate.Family, src, state string) fwstate.Packet {
	t.Helper()
	a, bridge := w.endpoint(t, name, fam)
	return fwstate.Packet{
		Family: fam, Path: "forward", InIface: w.uplink, OutIface: bridge, Src: netip.MustParseAddr(src), Dst: a,
		SrcPort: 40000, DstPort: 80, Proto: "tcp", CtState: state,
	}
}

// dcWithout returns the ruleset without one table.
func dcWithout(rs *netfilter.Ruleset, table string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
	out := &netfilter.Ruleset{LegacyPresent: rs.LegacyPresent}
	for _, tb := range rs.Tables {
		if tb.Name != table {
			out.Tables = append(out.Tables, tb)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// dcCase is one packet and what the capture decides for it with the block
// loaded and without it.
type dcCase struct {
	name string
	pkt  func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet
	// noRaw evaluates without the raw table, whose protection of container
	// addresses would drop the packet before the block is reached. The
	// kernel reaches the container address of a reply only after raw has
	// run, so a reply is evaluated this way too.
	noRaw bool
	block fwstate.Verdict
	// base is the verdict in the base and cleanup captures, which hold no
	// block; "" skips them.
	base fwstate.Verdict
}

func (c dcCase) decide(t *testing.T, w dcWorld, want fwstate.Verdict, reason string) {
	t.Helper()
	p := c.pkt(t, w)
	rs := w.rs[p.Family]
	if c.noRaw {
		rs = dcWithout(rs, "raw")
	}
	got := eval.Evaluate(rs, p, w.route)
	if got.Verdict != want {
		t.Errorf("verdict %q (reason %q, trace %q), want %q", got.Verdict, got.Reason, got.Trace, want)
	}
	if want == fwstate.Drop && !strings.Contains(got.Reason, reason) {
		t.Errorf("reason %q does not contain %q", got.Reason, reason)
	}
}

// dcRequireBlock fails unless the capture holds the block's chains loaded.
func dcRequireBlock(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) {
	t.Helper()
	for _, fam := range []fwstate.Family{fwstate.V4, fwstate.V6} {
		f := w.rs[fam].Table("filter")
		if f == nil || f.Chain("darkpanel-docker-deny") == nil || f.Chain("DOCKER-USER") == nil || len(f.Chain("DOCKER-USER").Rules) < 2 {
			t.Fatalf("the %s filter table of the block capture does not hold the block", fam)
		}
	}
}

func TestDcDecisions(t *testing.T) {
	v4, v6 := fwstate.V4, fwstate.V6
	cases := []dcCase{
		{
			name:  "a published port is open to a source its binding allows",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v4, "198.51.100.7", 8080) },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "the binding's explicit deny closes it to its range",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v4, "203.0.113.9", 8080) },
			block: fwstate.Drop, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a published port without a binding is closed to the internet",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v4, "198.51.100.7", 9090) },
			block: fwstate.Drop, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a private source reaches a published port without a binding, 10/8",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v4, "10.9.9.9", 9090) },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a private source reaches a published port without a binding, 192.168/16",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v4, "192.168.7.7", 9090) },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a tailnet source reaches a published port without a binding",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v4, "100.64.5.5", 9090) },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a container reaches the internet from the default bridge",
			pkt:   func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.leave(t, "web", v4, "198.51.100.2") },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a container reaches the internet from a custom-named bridge",
			pkt:   func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.leave(t, "app", v4, "198.51.100.2") },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "two containers talk on the default bridge",
			pkt:   func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.between(t, "web", v4) },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "two containers talk on a custom-named bridge",
			pkt:   func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.between(t, "app", v4) },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name: "replies to a container's connection return first",
			pkt: func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet {
				return w.into(t, "web", v4, "198.51.100.7", "ESTABLISHED")
			},
			noRaw: true, block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a new connection forwarded without DNAT to the default bridge is denied",
			pkt:   func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.into(t, "web", v4, "198.51.100.7", "NEW") },
			noRaw: true, block: fwstate.Drop, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a new connection forwarded without DNAT to a custom-named bridge is denied",
			pkt:   func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.into(t, "app", v4, "198.51.100.7", "NEW") },
			noRaw: true, block: fwstate.Drop, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "an IPv6 published port without a binding is closed to the internet",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v6, "2001:db8:1::7", 8443) },
			block: fwstate.Drop, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a private IPv6 source reaches a published port without a binding",
			pkt:   func(_ *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.arrive(v6, "fc00::5", 8443) },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
		{
			name:  "a container reaches the internet over IPv6",
			pkt:   func(t *testing.T, w dcWorld) fwstate.Packet { return w.leave(t, "six", v6, "2001:db8:2::2") },
			block: fwstate.Accept, base: fwstate.Accept,
		},
	}
	for _, image := range capImages {
		block := dcLoad(t, image, "block")
		dcRequireBlock(t, block)
		bases := map[string]dcWorld{"base": dcLoad(t, image, "base"), "cleanup": dcLoad(t, image, "cleanup")}
		for _, c := range cases {
			t.Run(image+"/"+c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
				c.decide(t, block, c.block, dcDenied)
				for name, w := range bases {
					if c.base != "" {
						t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) { c.decide(t, w, c.base, "") })
					}
				}
			})
		}
	}
}

// dcConfig reads the configured state of a capture scenario's UFW: its
// rule files and defaults, with a minimal before.rules and ufw.conf, which
// the chains compared below do not depend on.
func dcConfig(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) fwstate.Config {
	t.Helper()
	root := t.TempDir()
	put := func(path string, data []byte) {
		full := filepath.Join(root, path)
		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(full), 0o750); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(full, data, 0o600); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	for _, p := range []string{"etc/ufw/user.rules", "etc/ufw/user6.rules", "etc/ufw/after.rules", "etc/ufw/after6.rules", "etc/default/ufw"} {
		put(p, capFile(t, image, scenario, "files/"+p))
	}
	for _, p := range []string{"etc/ufw/before.rules", "etc/ufw/before6.rules"} {
		put(p, []byte("*filter\nCOMMIT\n"))
	}
	put("etc/ufw/ufw.conf", []byte("ENABLED=yes\nLOGLEVEL=low\n"))
	cfg, err := conf.Read(root)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(cfg.Unsupported) > 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%s/%s: the configuration is unsupported: %q", image, scenario, cfg.Unsupported)
	}
	return cfg
}

func TestDcPrediction(t *testing.T) {
	keep := func(_ fwstate.Family, table, chain string) bool {
		return table == "filter" && (Owned(chain) || chain == "ufw-user-forward" || chain == "ufw6-user-forward")
	}
	for _, image := range capImages {
		t.Run(image, func(t *testing.T) {
			block := dcLoad(t, image, "block")
			dcRequireBlock(t, block)
			base := dcLoad(t, image, "base")
			cur := fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "capture", V4: base.rs[fwstate.V4], V6: base.rs[fwstate.V6]}
			got, err := predict.Predict(dcConfig(t, image, "block"), cur, fwstate.TransReload)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			want := fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "capture", V4: block.rs[fwstate.V4], V6: block.rs[fwstate.V6]}
			for _, d := range loaded.Compare(got, want, keep) {
				t.Errorf("predicted and captured %s %s/%s differ: only predicted %q, only captured %q, order differs %v, policy %q/%q",
					d.Family, d.Table, d.Chain, d.OnlyA, d.OnlyB, d.OrderDiffers, d.PolicyA, d.PolicyB)
			}
		})
	}
}

// dcConfigured returns the rules of the capture's user.rules and
// user6.rules, merged as wave 1's status lists them.
func dcConfigured(t *testing.T, image, scenario string) []model.Rule {
	t.Helper()
	var v4, v6 []model.Tuple
	for _, f := range []struct {
		path string
		v6   bool
		dst  *[]model.Tuple
	}{{"files/etc/ufw/user.rules", false, &v4}, {"files/etc/ufw/user6.rules", true, &v6}} {
		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(capFile(t, image, scenario, f.path)), "\n") {
			if !strings.HasPrefix(line, model.TuplePrefix) {
				continue
			}
			tp, err := model.ParseTuple(line, f.v6)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("%s: %v", f.path, err)
			}
			*f.dst = append(*f.dst, tp)
		}
	}
	return model.Merge(v4, v6)
}

// dcTuple is a rule without what UFW and the caller assign: its id and raw
// text.
func dcTuple(r model.Rule) model.Rule {
	r = r.Normalize()
	r.ID, r.Raw = "", ""
	return r
}

// dcChains returns the rule keys of every chain of a block's filter table.
func dcChains(t *testing.T, block []byte, fam fwstate.Family) map[string][]string {
	t.Helper()
	rs, err := BlockRules(block)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f := rs.Table("filter")
	if f == nil {
		t.Fatal("the block has no filter table")
	}
	out := map[string][]string{}
	for _, c := range f.Chains {
		keys := []string{}
		for _, r := range c.Rules {
			keys = append(keys, netfilter.Key(r, fam == fwstate.V6))
		}
		out[c.Name] = keys
	}
	return out
}

func TestDcRealize(t *testing.T) {
	web := Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}
	rows := []ContainerRule{
		{ID: dcRowAllow, Binding: web, Kind: Allow},
		{ID: dcRowDeny, Binding: web, Kind: Deny, From: netip.MustParsePrefix("203.0.113.0/24")},
	}
	for _, image := range capImages {
		t.Run(image, func(t *testing.T) {
			got := Realize(rows, dcFacts(t, image, "block"), DefaultSettings())

			var captured []model.Rule
			for _, r := range dcConfigured(t, image, "block") {
				if _, ok := RuleOf(r.Comment); ok && r.Origin == model.OriginDarkpanel {
					captured = append(captured, r)
				}
			}
			if len(captured) != 2 {
				t.Fatalf("the capture's user rules hold %d container rules, want 2", len(captured))
			}
			index := func(c model.Rule) int {
				return slices.IndexFunc(got.Rules, func(r model.Rule) bool { return dcTuple(r) == dcTuple(c) })
			}
			for _, c := range captured {
				if index(c) < 0 {
					t.Errorf("Realize does not make the rule UFW stored in the capture: %+v\nit makes %+v", dcTuple(c), got.Rules)
				}
			}
			if a, d := index(captured[0]), index(captured[1]); a >= 0 && d >= 0 && (captured[0].Action != model.ActionAllow || captured[1].Action != model.ActionDeny || a > d) {
				t.Errorf("the route deny must follow the route allow: captured %s then %s, Realize puts them at %d and %d",
					captured[0].Action, captured[1].Action, a, d)
			}
			for _, r := range got.Rules {
				if !slices.ContainsFunc(captured, func(c model.Rule) bool { return dcTuple(c) == dcTuple(r) }) && (r.Direction != model.DirIn || r.Family != model.FamilyV6) {
					t.Errorf("Realize makes %+v, which is neither in the capture nor an IPv6 rule for a proxied family", r)
				}
			}

			for _, fam := range []fwstate.Family{fwstate.V4, fwstate.V6} {
				file := map[fwstate.Family]string{fwstate.V4: "after.rules", fwstate.V6: "after6.rules"}[fam]
				text, ok, err := BlockOf(capFile(t, image, "block", "files/etc/ufw/"+file))
				if err != nil || !ok {
					t.Fatalf("%s holds no block: %v", file, err)
				}
				want, have := dcChains(t, text, fam), dcChains(t, Render(got.Block, fam), fam)
				names := []string{ChainDockerUser, ChainBindings, ChainDeny}
				if fam == fwstate.V4 {
					names = append(names, web.Chain())
				}
				for _, name := range names {
					if len(want[name]) == 0 {
						t.Errorf("%s: the captured block has no rules in %s", fam, name)
					}
					if !slices.Equal(have[name], want[name]) {
						t.Errorf("%s %s: Render gives\n%s\nthe captured block holds\n%s", fam, name, strings.Join(have[name], "\n"), strings.Join(want[name], "\n"))
					}
				}
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
// deTestHold sets the chains the fake host has loaded: the IPv4 and IPv6

func deTestRun(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, op dockerOp) core.Effect {

func TestDeRunDockerEffectOutcomes(t *testing.T) {
	boom := errors.New("boom")
	// chains runs a chains op that leaves the host as set by leave, which
	// may also fail.
	chains := func(h *fakeHost, ran *bool, leave string, fail error) dockerOp {
		return chainsOp("absent", func(context.Context, core.Env) error {
			*ran = true
			deTestHold(h.t, h, leave, leave)
			return fail
		})
	}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name      string
		op        func(h *fakeHost, ran *bool) dockerOp
		failOn    string
		wantErr   bool
		wantState core.EffectState
		wantNone  bool
	}{
		{name: "fails, nothing changed", wantErr: true, wantState: core.EffectSkipped,
			op: func(h *fakeHost, ran *bool) dockerOp { return chains(h, ran, deTestSaveDeny, boom) }},
		{name: "succeeds, nothing changed", wantState: core.EffectSkipped,
			op: func(h *fakeHost, ran *bool) dockerOp { return chains(h, ran, deTestSaveDeny, nil) }},
		{name: "fails after the change", wantErr: true, wantState: core.EffectIntended,
			op: func(h *fakeHost, ran *bool) dockerOp { return chains(h, ran, deTestSavePlain, boom) }},
		{name: "ends in neither state", wantErr: true, wantState: core.EffectIntended,
			op: func(_ *fakeHost, ran *bool) dockerOp {
				op := sourcesOp(dockerfw.Settings{PrivateSources: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("10.0.0.0/8")}})
				write := sourcesOp(dockerfw.Settings{PrivateSources: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("192.168.0.0/16")}}).apply
				op.apply = func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) error { *ran = true; return write(ctx, env) }
				return op
			}},
		{name: "journal refuses the intent", failOn: "intend", wantErr: true, wantNone: true,
			op: func(h *fakeHost, ran *bool) dockerOp { return chains(h, ran, deTestSavePlain, nil) }},
		{name: "journal refuses made", failOn: "made", wantErr: true, wantState: core.EffectIntended,
			op: func(h *fakeHost, ran *bool) dockerOp { return chains(h, ran, deTestSavePlain, nil) }},
		{name: "op without apply", wantErr: true, wantNone: true,
			op: func(*fakeHost, *bool) dockerOp {
				return dockerOp{Kind: core.EffectModify, Resource: "firewall.chains:docker", After: "absent"}
			}},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h := newFakeHost(t)
			deTestHold(t, h, deTestSaveDeny, deTestSaveDeny)
			h.journal.failOn = c.failOn
			ran := false
			err := runDockerEffect(context.Background(), h.env(), h.deps(), c.op(h, &ran))
			if (err != nil) != c.wantErr {
				t.Errorf("runDockerEffect = %v, want error %v", err, c.wantErr)
			}
			if c.wantNone {
				if len(h.journal.effects) != 0 || ran {
					t.Errorf("%d effects journaled and apply run %v, want neither", len(h.journal.effects), ran)
				}
				return
			}
			if e := efTestOnly(t, h); e.State != c.wantState {
				t.Errorf("effect state = %s, want %s", e.State, c.wantState)
			}
		})
	}
}

}

func TestDeObserveDockerResources(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	deTestHold(t, h, deTestSavePlain, "")
	for _, c := range []struct {
		kind     core.EffectKind
		resource string
		want     string
		matches  int
		found    string
	}{
		{core.EffectModify, "firewall.setting:docker", `false`, 1, ""},
		{core.EffectModify, "firewall.setting:sources", deTestDefaultSources, 1, ""},
		{core.EffectDelete, "firewall.container:" + deTestID1, `null`, 1, ""},
		{core.EffectCreate, "firewall.container:?" + deTestID1, `null`, 0, ""},
		{core.EffectModify, "firewall.chains:docker", `"absent"`, 1, ""},
	} {
		obs := obTestObserve(t, h, c.kind, c.resource)
		if !jsonEqual(obs.Current.State, json.RawMessage(c.want)) || obs.Current.Version != nil || obs.Matches != c.matches ||
			!obs.Exclusive || obs.Resource != c.found {
			t.Errorf("%s = %+v, want state %s, %d matches", c.resource, obs, c.want, c.matches)
		}
		doc, err := dockerDoc(ctx, h.env(), h.deps(), c.resource)
		if err != nil || !jsonEqual(doc, json.RawMessage(c.want)) {
			t.Errorf("dockerDoc(%s) = %s, %v, want %s", c.resource, doc, err, c.want)
		}
	}

	deTestRun(t, h, flagOp(true))
	deTestRun(t, h, rowCreateOp(deTestDeny()))
	for _, c := range []struct {
		kind     core.EffectKind
		resource string
		want     string
		matches  int
		found    string
	}{
		{core.EffectModify, "firewall.setting:docker", `true`, 1, ""},
		{core.EffectDelete, "firewall.container:" + deTestID2, deTestDenyJSON, 1, ""},
		{core.EffectCreate, "firewall.container:?" + deTestID2, deTestDenyJSON, 1, "firewall.container:" + deTestID2},
	} {
		obs := obTestObserve(t, h, c.kind, c.resource)
		if !jsonEqual(obs.Current.State, json.RawMessage(c.want)) || obs.Matches != c.matches || !obs.Exclusive || obs.Resource != c.found {
			t.Errorf("%s = %+v, want state %s, %d matches, resource %q", c.resource, obs, c.want, c.matches, c.found)
		}
	}

	for name, c := range map[string]struct{ v4, v6, want string }{
		"no chain":                     {deTestSavePlain, deTestSavePlain, `"absent"`},
		"IPv6 not present":             {deTestSavePlain, "", `"absent"`},
		"a darkpanel chain in IPv4":    {deTestSaveDeny, deTestSavePlain, `"loaded"`},
		"a binding chain in IPv6 only": {deTestSavePlain, deTestSaveBinding, `"loaded"`},
		"a darkpanel chain, no IPv6":   {deTestSaveDeny, "", `"loaded"`},
	} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			deTestHold(t, h, c.v4, c.v6)
			if obs := obTestObserve(t, h, core.EffectModify, "firewall.chains:docker"); !jsonEqual(obs.Current.State, json.RawMessage(c.want)) {
				t.Errorf("chains = %s, want %s", obs.Current.State, c.want)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `docker_effects.go`: declare `nounSetting`, `nounContainer` and `nounChains` (the strings above) and `type dockerOp struct { Kind core.EffectKind; Resource string; After any; apply func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env) error }` as Contracts "Docker effects" gives it. `Resource` is `firewall.setting:docker`, `firewall.setting:sources`, `firewall.container:<rule id>` or `firewall.chains:docker`; `After` is JSON-marshalled into the effect's `After.State`, and `nil` marshals to the JSON `null`.
2. The five builders, each returning a `dockerOp` and doing no I/O until its `apply` runs:
   - `flagOp(on)`: kind Modify, resource `firewall.setting:docker`, `After` is `on`. `apply` reads the stored config with `readDockerConfig(ctx, env.DB)`, sets only `Enabled` and writes the whole config with `writeDockerConfig` inside one `env.DB.Write` transaction, so the stored settings are kept.
   - `sourcesOp(s)`: kind Modify, resource `firewall.setting:sources`, `After` is `s` with a nil `PrivateSources` or `ForwardExemptions` replaced by an empty slice, so that a value written as `null` and one written as `[]` never differ as state. `apply` reads the config, replaces only `Settings` with `s` and writes it in one transaction, so the stored flag is kept.
   - `rowCreateOp(r)`: kind Create, resource `firewall.container:<r.ID>`, `After` is `r`. `apply` runs `insertContainerRule(ctx, tx, r, env.Clock.Now())` in one transaction.
   - `rowDeleteOp(r)`: kind Delete, resource `firewall.container:<r.ID>`, `After` is nil. `apply` runs `deleteContainerRule(ctx, tx, r.ID)` in one transaction.
   - `chainsOp(state, apply)`: kind Modify, resource `firewall.chains:docker`, `After` is `state` (`"loaded"` or `"absent"`), `apply` is the argument.
3. `dockerDoc(ctx, env, d, resource)` returns the resource's `State` as JSON, and never a `Version`:
   - `firewall.setting:docker` is `true` or `false` from `readDockerConfig`;
   - `firewall.setting:sources` is the stored `dockerfw.Settings`, normalised as in `sourcesOp`;
   - `firewall.container:<id>` is the JSON of the `dockerfw.ContainerRule` that `containerRule` finds, or `null` when the row is absent (the identity may carry the `?` of a pending creation; `splitResource` removes it);
   - `firewall.chains:docker` is `"loaded"` when any chain whose name starts with `darkpanel-` or `dp-b-` is declared in any table of `d.readLoaded(ctx, env)`'s `V4` or `V6` (a nil `V6` is skipped), else `"absent"`. `DOCKER-USER` does not count;
   - any other noun or identity (`firewall.setting:other`, `firewall.chains:other`, an empty identity) is an error that names the resource.
4. `observe` in `observe.go`: right after `splitResource`, for the three new nouns, return `core.Observation{Current: StateDoc{State: dockerDoc(…)}, Matches: 1, Exclusive: true}`; for a `firewall.container` effect of kind Create, `Matches` is 0 when the row is absent, and when it is present `Matches` is 1 and `Resource` is `firewall.container:<id>` (without the `?`). Nothing changes for the existing nouns, and the new branch runs before wave 1's `d.readConfig` call, which the Docker nouns do not need.
5. `runDockerEffect(ctx, env, d, op)`, journaled like `runUfw`:
   1. An op whose `apply` is nil is refused with an error before anything is journaled.
   2. `Before` is `dockerDoc` of the resource now. A Create whose `Before` is not `null` (the row exists) and a Delete whose `Before` is `null` are refused with an error before anything is journaled.
   3. The effect is `core.Effect{Kind, Resource, Local: true, InverseLocal: true, Before, After}` with no `Version`. A Create's `Resource` is `firewall.container:?<id>` with `Recovery` `&core.RecoveryID{Kind: "marker", Value: <id>}`, as `runUfw` does for a rule.
   4. Call `runJournaled(ctx, env, d, e, op.Resource, …)` with a call that runs `op.apply(ctx, env)` and returns an empty `core.CmdResult`. It records Made (State-equal to `After`; for a creation, exactly one match), Skipped (equal to `Before`, whatever the call returned) or leaves the effect intended with an error. Any error is returned wrapped with `firewall: <resource>: %w`.

   Do not change wave 1's other effect functions; the inverse side is Task 27.

```go
// diTestForward runs op forward and returns its made effect.
func diTestForward(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, d deps, op dockerOp) core.Effect {
	t.Helper()
	h.journal.effects = nil
	if err := runDockerEffect(context.Background(), h.env(), d, op); err != nil {

	}
	e := efTestOnly(t, h)

}

func diTestUndo(h *fakeHost, d deps, e core.Effect) error {
	return inverse(context.Background(), h.env(), d, snapshot{}, e)
}

func TestDiInverseChains(t *testing.T) {
	boom := errors.New("boom")
	// loadsChains is the forward call that loads the chains, as a ufw
	// reload with the block does; cleansChains is the one that removes them.
	loadsChains := func(h *fakeHost) func(context.Context, core.Env) error {
		return func(context.Context, core.Env) error { deTestHold(h.t, h, deTestSaveDeny, deTestSavePlain); return nil }
	}
	cleansChains := func(h *fakeHost) func(context.Context, core.Env) error {
		return func(context.Context, core.Env) error {
			deTestHold(h.t, h, deTestSavePlain, deTestSavePlain)
			return nil
		}
	}

	t.Run("cleaned chains come back with a ufw reload", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newFakeHost(t)
		deTestHold(t, h, deTestSaveDeny, deTestSavePlain)
		d := h.deps()
		e := diTestForward(t, h, d, chainsOp("absent", cleansChains(h)))
		h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { deTestHold(t, h, deTestSaveDeny, deTestSavePlain); return 0 }
		if err := diTestUndo(h, d, e); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !slices.Contains(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/ufw reload") {
			t.Errorf("calls %v lack the reload", h.calls)
		}
	})
	t.Run("no reload while UFW is inactive", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newFakeHost(t)
		deTestHold(t, h, deTestSaveDeny, deTestSavePlain)
		d := h.deps()
		e := diTestForward(t, h, d, chainsOp("absent", cleansChains(h)))
		s := h.state()
		s.Enabled = false
		h.setState(s)
		h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { deTestHold(t, h, deTestSaveDeny, deTestSavePlain); return 0 }
		if err := diTestUndo(h, d, e); err == nil {
			t.Error("the undo succeeded with the chains still absent")
		}
		if slices.Contains(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/ufw reload") {
			t.Errorf("calls %v hold a reload on an inactive UFW", h.calls)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a failing reload fails the undo", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newFakeHost(t)
		deTestHold(t, h, deTestSaveDeny, deTestSavePlain)
		d := h.deps()
		e := diTestForward(t, h, d, chainsOp("absent", cleansChains(h)))
		h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 1 }
		if err := diTestUndo(h, d, e); err == nil {
			t.Error("the undo succeeded after a failed reload")
		}
	})
	t.Run("loaded chains are cleaned under the change id", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newFakeHost(t)
		deTestHold(t, h, deTestSavePlain, deTestSavePlain)
		d := h.deps()
		e := diTestForward(t, h, d, chainsOp("loaded", loadsChains(h)))
		var owners []string
		d.cleanChains = func(ctx context.Context, env core.Env, owner string) error {
			owners = append(owners, owner)
			return cleansChains(h)(ctx, env)
		}
		if err := diTestUndo(h, d, e); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !slices.Equal(owners, []string{"c1"}) {
			t.Errorf("cleanup owners = %v, want [c1]", owners)
		}
		if slices.Contains(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/ufw reload") {
			t.Errorf("calls %v hold a reload", h.calls)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a missing cleanup is an error", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newFakeHost(t)
		deTestHold(t, h, deTestSavePlain, deTestSavePlain)
		d := h.deps()
		e := diTestForward(t, h, d, chainsOp("loaded", loadsChains(h)))
		err := diTestUndo(h, d, e)
		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "cleanChains") {
			t.Errorf("undo with no cleanChains = %v, want an error naming cleanChains", err)
		}
		if obs := obTestObserve(t, h, core.EffectModify, "firewall.chains:docker"); string(obs.Current.State) != `"loaded"` {
			t.Errorf("chains = %s after the refused undo, want them loaded still", obs.Current.State)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a failing cleanup fails the undo", func(t *testing.T) {
		h := newFakeHost(t)
		deTestHold(t, h, deTestSavePlain, deTestSavePlain)
		d := h.deps()
		e := diTestForward(t, h, d, chainsOp("loaded", loadsChains(h)))
		d.cleanChains = func(context.Context, core.Env, string) error { return boom }
		if err := diTestUndo(h, d, e); !errors.Is(err, boom) {
			t.Errorf("undo = %v, want the cleanup's error", err)
		}
	})
}

				t.Error("the undo succeeded")
			}
			if c := diTestConfig(t, h); !c.Enabled {
				t.Error("the flag changed")
			}
			if got := deTestRules(t, h); !slices.Equal(got, []dockerfw.ContainerRule{deTestAllow()}) {
				t.Errorf("rows = %+v", got)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

```go
// dsnRules returns three rows in id order: an allow from any source on a
// binding of every host address, an allow from a range on one host address,

func dsnRules() []dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	web := dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}
	return []dockerfw.ContainerRule{

	}
}
```

```tsx
import { screen, within } from "@testing-library/react"
import userEvent from "@testing-library/user-event"
import { expect, test, vi } from "vitest"
import { axe } from "vitest-axe"
import { renderWithProviders, stubFetch, type FetchCall, type StubHandler } from "@/test/utils"
import { DockerPanel } from "./docker-panel"
import { fwDocker } from "./fixtures"
import type { DockerStatus } from "./types"

vi.mock("./docker-sources", () => ({
  DockerSources: ({ hostId, docker }: { hostId: string; docker: { settings: { privateSources: string[] } } }) => (
    <div data-testid="docker-sources">{`${hostId}: ${docker.settings.privateSources.join(", ")}`}</div>
  ),
}))

const DOCKER = "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/resources/firewall/docker"

// dpDocker is a supported Docker host with the integration off; every field
// a test reads is set here, so the tests do not depend on the fixture's.
function dpDocker(over: Partial<DockerStatus> = {}): DockerStatus {
  return fwDocker({
    available: true,
    version: "29.9.1",
    driver: "iptables",
    dockerVariant: "nft",
    ufwVariant: "nft",
    rawProtection: true,
    supported: true,
    unsupported: [],
    enabled: false,
    health: "off",
    issues: [],
    foreignRules: [],
    manualRoutes: [],
    networks: [
      { name: "bridge", id: "b1", bridge: "docker0", subnets: ["172.17.0.0/16"], protected: true },
      { name: "public", id: "n2", bridge: "dppublic", subnets: ["203.0.113.0/24"], protected: false, reason: "custom bridge name with a non-private subnet" },
    ],
    settings: { privateSources: ["10.0.0.0/8", "100.64.0.0/10"], forwardExemptions: [] },
    ...over,
  })
}

function dpRender(docker: DockerStatus, routes: Record<string, StubHandler> = {}): { calls: FetchCall[]; container: HTMLElement } {
  const plan = (call: FetchCall) => {
    const action = call.path.split("/")[6] ?? ""
    return { body: { planId: "p1", hostId: "h1", action, version: 1, inputHash: "h", diff: [{ op: "~", text: action }], guards: [], expiresAt: "2026-10-24T09:00:00Z", confirmation: null } }
  }
  const calls = stubFetch({
    [DOCKER]: { body: docker },
    "GET /api/v1/hosts/h1/modules/firewall/availability": { body: { module: "firewall", available: true, reason: null, actions: [] } },
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.docker.enable/v1/plan": plan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.docker.disable/v1/plan": plan,
    "POST /api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.docker.repair/v1/plan": plan,
    ...routes,
  })
  const { container } = renderWithProviders(<DockerPanel hostId="h1" />)
  return { calls, container }
}

async function dpPlanned(calls: FetchCall[], title: string): Promise<{ path: string; body: unknown }> {
  const dialog = await screen.findByRole("dialog", { name: title })
  await within(dialog).findByLabelText("Planned changes")
  const call = calls.find((c) => c.path.endsWith("/plan"))
  return { path: call?.path ?? "", body: call?.body }
}

test("an off, supported integration shows what was detected and plans docker.enable", async () => {
  const { calls } = dpRender(dpDocker())
  const detection = await screen.findByLabelText("Docker detection")
  const rows = Array.from(detection.querySelectorAll("dt")).map((dt) => [dt.textContent, dt.nextElementSibling?.textContent])
  expect(rows).toEqual([
    ["Docker", "29.9.1"],
    ["Firewall backend", "iptables"],
    ["Docker chains", "nft"],
    ["UFW chains", "nft"],
    ["Raw-table protection", "Loaded"],
    ["Supported", "Yes"],
  ])
  expect(screen.getByText("off").textContent).toBe("off")
  expect(screen.queryByRole("button", { name: "Disable integration" })).toBeNull()
  await userEvent.setup().click(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Enable integration" }))
  expect(await dpPlanned(calls, "Enable the Docker integration")).toEqual({ path: "/api/v1/hosts/h1/actions/firewall.docker.enable/v1/plan", body: { input: {} } })
})

  expect(reasons.map((li) => li.textContent)).toEqual(["Docker's chains are in the legacy variant and UFW's in nft", "Docker's raw protection is not loaded"])
  expect(screen.getByRole("button", { name: "Enable integration" }).hasAttribute("disabled")).toBe(true)
})
```
