The tests build the `prepared` change by hand, so they exercise `run` alone: the fake host is wave 1's `ruHost`, given the module's database (`dsDB`), the Docker block in both after files, and a loaded filter table that holds the block's chains until a restore program runs. The scripted `ufw reload` is wave 1's.

`internal/modules/firewall/run_docker_test.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"net/netip"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

const (
	druPlain4 = "*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n"
	druPlain6 = "*filter\n# after6\nCOMMIT\n"
	druBlock  = "# BEGIN DARKPANEL docker\n*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]\n" +
		"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n-A darkpanel-docker-deny -j DROP\nCOMMIT\n# END DARKPANEL docker\n"
	// druLoaded is a loaded filter table that holds the block's chains.
	druLoaded = "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:ufw-user-input - [0:0]\n" +
		":DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]\n" +
		"-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\n" +
		"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n-A darkpanel-docker-deny -j DROP\nCOMMIT\n"
	druForeignRule = "-A DOCKER-USER -s 192.0.2.0/24 -j DROP\n"
)

func druPtr[T any](v T) *T { return &v }

var (
	druOld = dockerfw.ContainerRule{ID: "01J00000000000000000000A01", Kind: dockerfw.Allow,
		Binding: dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}}
	druNew = dockerfw.ContainerRule{ID: "01J00000000000000000000A02", Kind: dockerfw.Deny, From: netip.MustParsePrefix("203.0.113.0/24"),
		Binding: dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}}
	druSources = dockerfw.Settings{PrivateSources: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("10.0.0.0/8")}}
)

// druHost is a fake host whose after files hold the Docker block and whose
// loaded filter table holds the block's chains; a restore program removes
// them. Its database is the module's, with the Docker tables.
func druHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, fw, core.Env, model.Rule) {
	t.Helper()
	h, f, _ := ruHost(t)
	h.db = dsDB(t)
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after.rules", []byte(druPlain4+druBlock))
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after6.rules", []byte(druPlain6+druBlock))
	h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, druLoaded), fhParse(t, druLoaded)
	h.onRun = func(h *fakeHost, cmd core.Cmd) core.CmdResult {
		if strings.HasSuffix(cmd.Path, "-restore") {
			h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, fhSave), fhParse(t, fhSave)
		}
		return core.CmdResult{}
	}
	env := h.env()
	env.ChangeID = ruChange
	var rule model.Rule
	for _, r := range model.Merge(h.config().Rules4, h.config().Rules6) {
		if r.Origin == model.OriginDarkpanel {
			rule = r
		}
	}
	return h, f, env, rule
}

// druResources lists the resources the journal holds, in order, one entry
// for each run of equal resources.
func druResources(h *fakeHost) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, e := range h.journal.effects {
		if len(out) == 0 || out[len(out)-1] != e.Resource {
			out = append(out, e.Resource)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func druIndex(calls []string, call string) int {
	return slices.IndexFunc(calls, func(c string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(c, call) })
}

func druLastIndex(calls []string, call string) int {
	for i := len(calls) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		if strings.HasPrefix(calls[i], call) {
			return i
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// TestDruRunOrder: a change that carries the Docker fields runs them in
// the order of spec 2.6: the logical rows and settings, the block files, the
// ufw commands, the cleanup of the loaded chains, then the transition.
func TestDruRunOrder(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, env, rule := druHost(t)
	if err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		if err := writeDockerConfig(ctx, tx, dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()}); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return insertContainerRule(ctx, tx, druOld, time.Now())
	}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	c := change{
		ops:     []ufwOp{deleteRuleOp(rule)},
		flag:    druPtr(false),
		sources: &druSources,
		rowsDel: []string{druOld.ID},
		rowsAdd: []dockerfw.ContainerRule{druNew},
		files:   map[string][]byte{"/etc/ufw/after.rules": []byte(druPlain4), "/etc/ufw/after6.rules": []byte(druPlain6)},
		cleanup: true,
		reload:  true,
	}
	p := prepared{cfg0: h.config(), cur: h.loaded, c: c, tg: target{cmds: [][]string{reloadArgs}}}
	h.calls = nil
	if err := f.run(ctx, env, p); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	want := []string{
		"firewall.setting:docker", "firewall.setting:sources", "firewall.container:" + druOld.ID, "firewall.container:" + druNew.ID,
		"firewall.file:/etc/ufw/after.rules", "firewall.file:/etc/ufw/after6.rules",
		"firewall.rule:" + rule.ID, "firewall.chains:docker", "firewall.state:enabled",
	}
	if got := druResources(h); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("effects\n%q\nwant\n%q", got, want)
	}
	for _, e := range h.journal.effects {
		if e.State == core.EffectIntended {
			t.Errorf("effect %d (%s) is still intended", e.Seq, e.Resource)
		}
	}
	cfg, err := readDockerConfig(ctx, h.db)
	if err != nil || cfg.Enabled || !reflect.DeepEqual(cfg.Settings.PrivateSources, druSources.PrivateSources) {
		t.Errorf("stored config %+v (%v), want the flag off and the new sources", cfg, err)
	}
	if rows, err := listContainerRules(ctx, h.db); err != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(rows, []dockerfw.ContainerRule{druNew}) {
		t.Errorf("stored rules %+v (%v), want only the new one", rows, err)
	}
	if left, err := pendingCleanups(ctx, h.db); err != nil || len(left) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("pending cleanups %v (%v), want none", left, err)
	}
	if got := string(h.config().Files["/etc/ufw/after.rules"].Data); got != druPlain4 {
		t.Errorf("after.rules is %q, want the file without the block", got)
	}
	file, del := druIndex(h.calls, "restore /etc/ufw/after.rules"), druIndex(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/ufw delete")
	clean, reload := druIndex(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore -n"), druLastIndex(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/ufw reload")
	if file < 0 || del <= file || clean <= del || reload <= clean {
		t.Errorf("calls %q: want the block file, the ufw rule delete, the chain cleanup and the reload in that order", h.calls)
	}
}

// TestDruRunFiles: a block file already as wanted is not
// rewritten; a missing row, and a file that is not a block file, stop the
// change before it writes.
func TestDruRunFiles(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name    string
		c       change
		wantErr string
		want    []string
	}{
		{
			name: "one file is as wanted",
			c: change{files: map[string][]byte{
				"/etc/ufw/after.rules": []byte(druPlain4 + druBlock), "/etc/ufw/after6.rules": []byte(druPlain6)}},
			want: []string{"firewall.file:/etc/ufw/after6.rules"},
		},
		{
			name:    "a row that does not exist",
			c:       change{rowsDel: []string{"01J00000000000000000000FFF"}, flag: druPtr(true)},
			wantErr: "01J00000000000000000000FFF",
			want:    []string{"firewall.setting:docker"},
		},
		{
			name:    "a file that is not a block file",
			c:       change{files: map[string][]byte{"/etc/ufw/user.rules": []byte("*filter\nCOMMIT\n")}},
			wantErr: "/etc/ufw/user.rules",
		},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, f, env, _ := druHost(t)
			h.calls = nil
			err := f.run(ctx, env, prepared{cfg0: h.config(), cur: h.loaded, c: c.c})
			if c.wantErr == "" && err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if c.wantErr != "" && (err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), c.wantErr)) {
				t.Fatalf("run = %v, want an error naming %s", err, c.wantErr)
			}
			if got := druResources(h); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.want) {
				t.Errorf("effects %q, want %q", got, c.want)
			}
			if c.name == "a file that is not a block file" && len(h.calls) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("calls %q, want none", h.calls)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDruCleanupRefused: a foreign rule in DOCKER-USER stops the
// change at the cleanup, before the chains are loaded and before UFW
// reloads.
func TestDruCleanupRefused(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, env, _ := druHost(t)
	h.loaded.V4 = fhParse(t, strings.Replace(druLoaded, "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n", "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n"+druForeignRule, 1))
	h.calls = nil
	c := change{
		files:   map[string][]byte{"/etc/ufw/after.rules": []byte(druPlain4), "/etc/ufw/after6.rules": []byte(druPlain6)},
		cleanup: true, reload: true,
	}
	err := f.run(ctx, env, prepared{cfg0: h.config(), cur: h.loaded, c: c, tg: target{cmds: [][]string{reloadArgs}}})
	if got := errcode.From(err).Code; got != errcode.FirewallDockerUserInUse || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "192.0.2.0/24") {
		t.Fatalf("run = %v, want firewall.docker_user_in_use naming the foreign rule", err)
	}
	for _, call := range h.calls {
		if strings.Contains(call, "-restore") || strings.HasSuffix(call, "ufw reload") {
			t.Errorf("call %q ran after the refusal", call)
		}
	}
	if slices.Contains(druResources(h), "firewall.state:enabled") {
		t.Errorf("effects %q hold the reload", druResources(h))
	}
}
```

Expected: FAIL. `TestDruRunOrder` reports the journal's effects as only `firewall.rule:<id>` and `firewall.state:enabled`, the stored configuration still enabled and the old row still stored; the three cases of `TestDruRunFiles` fail (no `firewall.file:` effect, no error for the missing row, no error for `/etc/ufw/user.rules`); `TestDruCleanupRefused` reports `run = <nil>`.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `fw.run` (`handler.go`) runs these steps in this order and stops at the first error: a restore's files (`writeRestored`, unchanged); `f.runLogical(ctx, env, p.c)`; `f.writeBlockFiles(ctx, env, p.c.files)`; the change's ufw commands (the existing loop over `p.c.ops` with `runUfw`); when `p.c.cleanup`, `f.cleanupChains(ctx, env, env.ChangeID, cleanupRefuse)`; the transition commands (the existing loop over `p.tg.cmds`); a restore's sysctl values (`restoreSysctl`, unchanged). Rewrite `run`'s doc comment to list this order. A change with none of the Docker fields runs exactly as before.
2. `runLogical` (`run_docker.go`) runs the logical effects through `runDockerEffect`, each one effect: the flag when `c.flag` is not nil (`flagOp(*c.flag)`); the settings when `c.sources` is not nil (`sourcesOp(*c.sources)`); then each id of `c.rowsDel`, in order, then each rule of `c.rowsAdd`, in order. A row delete first reads the stored row with `containerRule(ctx, env.DB, id)`: a read error is returned wrapped, and an id with no row is the error `firewall: container rule <id> does not exist`; the effect is `rowDeleteOp(row)`. An insert is `rowCreateOp(rule)`.
3. `writeBlockFiles` (`run_docker.go`) first refuses, before it writes anything, a path that is not `/etc/ufw/after.rules` or `/etc/ufw/after6.rules`, with the error `firewall: a change writes <path>, which is not a block file`. Then, for the paths in sorted order, it re-reads the configured state with `f.d.readConfig(f.d.root)` (as `writeRestored` does, so a later file sees the earlier write), takes the live entry of the path, replaces its `Data` and sets `Present`, and skips the path when `sameFile(live, want)`; otherwise it writes it with `writeFileEffect`. A path with no live entry gets mode `0o640` and owner root. Only the data changes for a path that exists, so its mode and owner are kept.
4. Do not change `prepare`, `predictTarget`, the plan, `Verify` or any wave 1 test. No new comment names a task or the spec.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

The host is wave 1's `unSetup` with `/usr/sbin/iptables` installed, the Docker block in both after files and the block's chains loaded; a restore program empties the loaded chains.

`internal/modules/firewall/uninstall_docker_test.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

const (
	dunBlock = "# BEGIN DARKPANEL docker\n*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]\n" +
		"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n-A darkpanel-docker-deny -j DROP\nCOMMIT\n# END DARKPANEL docker\n"
	dunOwned = "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:ufw-user-input - [0:0]\n" +
		":DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]\n" +
		"-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\n" +
		"-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n-A darkpanel-docker-deny -j DROP\nCOMMIT\n"
	dunForeignOnly = "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n" +
		"-A DOCKER-USER -s 192.0.2.0/24 -j DROP\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\nCOMMIT\n"
	dunForeign = "-A DOCKER-USER -s 192.0.2.0/24 -j DROP\n"
	dunCleanup = "-X darkpanel-docker-deny"
)

// dunHost is unSetup's host with iptables installed, the Docker block in
// both after files and the block's chains loaded; a restore program removes
// them.
func dunHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, module, core.Env, *bytes.Buffer) {
	t.Helper()
	h, m, env, log := unSetup(t)
	h.writeFile("/usr/sbin/iptables", []byte("#!/bin/sh\n"))
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after.rules", []byte("*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n"+dunBlock))
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after6.rules", []byte("*filter\n# after6\nCOMMIT\n"+dunBlock))
	h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, dunOwned), fhParse(t, dunOwned)
	h.onRun = func(h *fakeHost, cmd core.Cmd) core.CmdResult {
		if strings.HasSuffix(cmd.Path, "-restore") {
			h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, fhSave), fhParse(t, fhSave)
		}
		return core.CmdResult{}
	}
	return h, m, env, log
}

// dunCleaned fails the test unless the cleanup ran: the block is out of
// both files, the chains were flushed and deleted, and none is loaded.
func dunCleaned(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost) {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := h.config()
	for _, p := range []string{"/etc/ufw/after.rules", "/etc/ufw/after6.rules"} {
		if strings.Contains(string(cfg.Files[p].Data), "DARKPANEL docker") {
			t.Errorf("%s still holds the block", p)
		}
	}
	if in := string(h.stdin["/usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore"]); !strings.Contains(in, dunCleanup) {
		t.Errorf("iptables-nft-restore input %q, want the owned chains deleted (%s)", in, dunCleanup)
	}
	for _, tables := range [][]netfilter.Table{h.loaded.V4.Tables, h.loaded.V6.Tables} {
		for _, tb := range tables {
			if tb.Chain("darkpanel-docker-deny") != nil {
				t.Errorf("table %s still holds the chain darkpanel-docker-deny", tb.Name)
			}
		}
	}
}

// TestDunRunsCleanup: the owned-chain cleanup runs for every
// value of rules, after the rules work, and on a host without UFW.
func TestDunRunsCleanup(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name       string
		rules      string
		noUFW      bool
		wantDelete bool
	}{
		{name: "keep", rules: "keep"},
		{name: "remove", rules: "remove", wantDelete: true},
		{name: "baseline without a baseline snapshot", rules: "baseline"},
		{name: "remove without UFW", rules: "remove", noUFW: true},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, m, env, _ := dunHost(t)
			if c.noUFW {
				s := h.state()
				s.Enabled = false
				h.setState(s)
				pfRemove(t, h.root, ufwPath)
			}
			if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": c.rules}); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			deleted := slices.ContainsFunc(unRan(h, 0), func(v string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(v, "delete ") })
			if deleted != c.wantDelete {
				t.Errorf("ufw ran %q, want a rule delete: %v", unRan(h, 0), c.wantDelete)
			}
			if c.wantDelete {
				del := slices.IndexFunc(h.calls, func(v string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(v, "run /usr/sbin/ufw delete ") })
				clean := slices.IndexFunc(h.calls, func(v string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(v, "run /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore -n") })
				if del < 0 || clean < del {
					t.Errorf("calls %q, want the rules deleted before the cleanup loads", h.calls)
				}
			}
			dunCleaned(t, h)
		})
	}
}

// TestDunNeedsDarkpanelState: foreign DOCKER-USER rules
// alone are no reason to run the cleanup, which would refuse them; the block
// in a file or a loaded owned chain is.
func TestDunNeedsDarkpanelState(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, m, env, _ := dunHost(t)
	own4, own6 := h.config().Files["/etc/ufw/after.rules"], h.config().Files["/etc/ufw/after6.rules"]
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after.rules", []byte("*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n"))
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after6.rules", []byte("*filter\n# after6\nCOMMIT\n"))
	h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, dunForeignOnly), fhParse(t, fhSave)
	n := len(h.calls)
	if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "keep"}); err != nil || len(h.calls) != n {
		t.Errorf("uninstall = %v and ran %q, want nothing", err, h.calls[n:])
	}

	h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, dunOwned), fhParse(t, dunOwned)
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after.rules", own4.Data)
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after6.rules", own6.Data)
	if err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "keep"}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	dunCleaned(t, h)
}

// TestDunCleanupRefused: a foreign rule in DOCKER-USER refuses
// the cleanup, which fails the uninstall after the rules were deleted.
func TestDunCleanupRefused(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, m, env, _ := dunHost(t)
	h.loaded.V4 = fhParse(t, strings.Replace(dunOwned, "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n", "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n"+dunForeign, 1))
	err := m.Uninstall(ctx, env, false, map[string]string{"rules": "remove"})
	if errcode.From(err).Code != errcode.FirewallDockerUserInUse || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "192.0.2.0/24") {
		t.Fatalf("uninstall = %v, want firewall.docker_user_in_use naming the foreign rule", err)
	}
	if !slices.Contains(unRan(h, 0), "delete allow in proto tcp from any to any port 22") {
		t.Errorf("ufw ran %q, want the Darkpanel rule deleted before the refusal", unRan(h, 0))
	}
}

// TestDunFinishesInterrupted: an intent that an earlier
// change left is repeated, and cleared, by the next uninstall.
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

1. `module.Uninstall` keeps its option check first (an unknown value is the same error, before anything runs). It then finds out whether UFW is installed with `m.f.regular(ufwPath)`: `missingFile` means no UFW (remembered as `hasUFW` false, not returned), any other error is returned as before. It then runs three steps, attempting each whatever the earlier ones returned: `m.f.finishCleanups(ctx, env)`; `m.f.uninstallRules(ctx, env, v, hasUFW)`; `m.f.uninstallDocker(ctx, env, hasUFW)`. It returns `errors.Join` of their three errors. Update the doc comment: spec 2.9 runs the cleanup in every case, `keepData` still changes nothing, and a second uninstall succeeds again.
2. `uninstallRules` holds what `Uninstall` did after the option check, unchanged in behaviour: `keep` returns nil; without UFW it logs the existing message (`firewall: UFW is not installed; the uninstall leaves the firewall as it is`) and returns nil; `baseline` calls `restoreBaseline`; `remove` calls `removeRules`. Do not change `restoreBaseline` or `removeRules`.
3. `uninstallDocker` calls `dockerLeft`; an error from it is returned as `firewall: uninstall: <error>`; when it reports nothing left, it returns nil; otherwise it returns `f.cleanupChains(ctx, env, "uninstall", cleanupRefuse)`. The cleanup runs after the rules work, so a refusal (a foreign `DOCKER-USER` rule, `firewall.docker_user_in_use`) fails the uninstall only after the rules were deleted, and the operator removes the rule and runs the uninstall again.
4. `dockerLeft` reports whether the Docker integration left anything on the host, so that foreign `DOCKER-USER` rules alone never make the cleanup refuse an uninstall of a host that never enabled the integration. It is true when the marked block is in `/etc/ufw/after.rules` or `/etc/ufw/after6.rules` (read from `f.d.readConfig(f.d.root)`; `dockerfw.BlockOf` returning an error counts as a block, so the cleanup reports it), or when a chain whose name starts `darkpanel-` or `dp-b-` is loaded in either family of `f.d.readLoaded`. A configuration that cannot be read is an error only when UFW is installed; without UFW the files count as holding no block. The loaded state is read only when `/usr/sbin/iptables` is a regular file (`f.regular`; `missingFile` means nothing is loaded); a failure to read the loaded state is returned as `read the loaded state: <error>`.
5. Do not add a parameter to `cleanupChains` and do not call `ufw` from the new code. A reload after the cleanup is `cleanupChains`'s decision.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

The fake host is wave 1's `newFakeHost` with the Docker block in both after files (or without it) and `DOCKER-USER` loaded as the block makes it. `ufw reload` refills `DOCKER-USER` from the block when the files hold it, which flushes foreign rules as UFW does. A restore program loads the `-A DOCKER-USER` lines of its input. The comparison is the real `loaded.Compare` against a scripted prediction, so the tests also prove that a foreign rule is not counted as a difference. `DOCKER-USER` is served through `deps.readLoaded` from the fake host's `loaded` field, which is where `keepForeign` and `finishForeign` read it.

`internal/modules/firewall/docker_revert_test.go`:

```go
package firewall

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"reflect"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/loaded"
)

const (
	kfwForeign = "-A DOCKER-USER -s 192.0.2.0/24 -j DROP"
	kfwReturn  = "-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN"
	kfwPlain4  = "*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n"
	kfwPlain6  = "*filter\n# after6\nCOMMIT\n"
)

// kfwBlockLines are the DOCKER-USER lines of the block the fake host holds.
var kfwBlockLines = []string{
	"-A DOCKER-USER -i docker0 -j RETURN",
	"-A DOCKER-USER -m conntrack --ctstate DNAT -j darkpanel-docker-deny",
	kfwReturn,
}

func kfwBlockText() string {
	return "# BEGIN DARKPANEL docker\n*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]\n" +
		strings.Join(kfwBlockLines, "\n") + "\n-A darkpanel-docker-deny -j DROP\nCOMMIT\n# END DARKPANEL docker\n"
}

// kfwSave is a loaded filter table whose DOCKER-USER holds rules and which,
// when owned, holds the block's other chain.
func kfwSave(rules []string, owned bool) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:ufw-user-input - [0:0]\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n")
	if owned {
		b.WriteString(":darkpanel-docker-deny - [0:0]\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\n")
	for _, r := range rules {
		b.WriteString(r + "\n")
	}
	if owned {
		b.WriteString("-A darkpanel-docker-deny -j DROP\n")
	}
	b.WriteString("COMMIT\n")
	return b.String()
}

// kfwSet makes the fake host's loaded state hold rules in DOCKER-USER in
// both families.
func kfwSet(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, rules []string, owned bool) {
	t.Helper()
	h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, kfwSave(rules, owned)), fhParse(t, kfwSave(rules, owned))
}

// kfwChain lists the IPv4 DOCKER-USER rules the fake host has loaded.
func kfwChain(h *fakeHost) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, tb := range h.loaded.V4.Tables {
		if c := tb.Chain("DOCKER-USER"); c != nil {
			for _, r := range c.Rules {
				out = append(out, r.Text)
			}
		}
	}
	return out
}

// kfwWith inserts rule into rules at index at.
func kfwWith(rules []string, at int, rule string) []string {
	return slices.Insert(slices.Clone(rules), at, rule)
}

// kfwHost is a fake host whose UFW is active with the Docker block in both
// after files (or without it) and DOCKER-USER loaded as the block makes it.
// "ufw reload" refills DOCKER-USER from the block when the files hold it,
// and a restore program loads the DOCKER-USER lines of its input; the real
// comparison checks every restore against what the host predicts.
func kfwHost(t *testing.T, block bool) (*fakeHost, deps) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	kfwFiles(h, block)
	if block {
		kfwSet(t, h, kfwBlockLines, true)
	} else {
		kfwSet(t, h, []string{kfwReturn}, false)
	}
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int {
		if strings.Contains(string(h.config().Files["/etc/ufw/after.rules"].Data), "DARKPANEL docker") {
			kfwSet(t, h, kfwBlockLines, true)
		}
		return 0
	}
	h.onRun = func(h *fakeHost, cmd core.Cmd) core.CmdResult {
		if !strings.HasSuffix(cmd.Path, "-restore") {
			return core.CmdResult{}
		}
		var rules []string
		for _, l := range strings.Split(string(cmd.Stdin), "\n") {
			if strings.HasPrefix(l, "-A DOCKER-USER ") {
				rules = append(rules, l)
			}
		}
		owned := h.loaded.V4.Tables[0].Chain("darkpanel-docker-deny") != nil
		kfwSet(t, h, rules, owned)
		return core.CmdResult{}
	}
	d := h.deps()
	d.compare = loaded.Compare
	kfwPredict(t, h, block)
	return h, d
}

func kfwFiles(h *fakeHost, block bool) {
	a4, a6 := kfwPlain4, kfwPlain6
	if block {
		a4, a6 = a4+kfwBlockText(), a6+kfwBlockText()
	}
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after.rules", []byte(a4))
	h.writeFile("/etc/ufw/after6.rules", []byte(a6))
}

// kfwPredict sets the loaded state a restore of a snapshot with or without
// the block is predicted to give.
func kfwPredict(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, block bool) {
	t.Helper()
	rules, owned := []string{kfwReturn}, false
	if block {
		rules, owned = kfwBlockLines, true
	}
	h.predicted = &fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(t, kfwSave(rules, owned)), V6: fhParse(t, kfwSave(rules, owned))}
}

// kfwSnapshot captures the host as it is.
func kfwSnapshot(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, d deps) snapshot {
	t.Helper()
	env := h.env()
	env.ChangeID = ""
	raw, err := capture(context.Background(), env, d, nil, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	snap, err := getSnapshot(context.Background(), h.db, string(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return snap
}

func kfwInput(h *fakeHost, program string) []string {
	in := strings.TrimSpace(string(h.stdin["/usr/sbin/"+program+"-nft-restore"]))
	if in == "" {
		return nil
	}
	return strings.Split(in, "\n")
}

func kfwInputOf(rules ...string) []string {
	return append(append([]string{"*filter", ":DOCKER-USER - [0:0]"}, rules...), "COMMIT")
}

// TestKfwRestore: a whole restore reloads
// DOCKER-USER with the block's lines and the foreign rules that were loaded,
// before or after them, and a foreign rule between the block's lines goes
// before the first and is reported. A restore to a state without the block
// leaves the cleanup of the loaded chains to the module's cleanup, which
// keeps foreign rules itself. Nothing is reloaded when no foreign rule is
// loaded, and the verification does not count a foreign rule as a
// difference.
func TestKfwRestore(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name      string
		snapBlock bool
		nowBlock  bool
		now       []string // DOCKER-USER now
		wantInput []string // the IPv4 reload of DOCKER-USER; nil for none
		wantChain []string // DOCKER-USER afterwards
		wantOrder []string
		wantClean bool
	}{
		{
			name: "a foreign rule after the block's lines", snapBlock: true, nowBlock: true,
			now:       kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 3, kfwForeign),
			wantInput: kfwInputOf(append(slices.Clone(kfwBlockLines), kfwForeign)...),
			wantChain: append(slices.Clone(kfwBlockLines), kfwForeign),
		},
		{
			name: "a foreign rule before the block's lines", snapBlock: true, nowBlock: true,
			now:       kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 0, kfwForeign),
			wantInput: kfwInputOf(append([]string{kfwForeign}, kfwBlockLines...)...),
			wantChain: append([]string{kfwForeign}, kfwBlockLines...),
		},
		{
			name: "a foreign rule between the block's lines", snapBlock: true, nowBlock: true,
			now:       kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 1, kfwForeign),
			wantInput: kfwInputOf(append([]string{kfwForeign}, kfwBlockLines...)...),
			wantChain: append([]string{kfwForeign}, kfwBlockLines...),
			wantOrder: kfwOrder(kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 1, kfwForeign)),
		},
		{
			name: "no foreign rule", snapBlock: true, nowBlock: true,
			now: kfwBlockLines, wantChain: kfwBlockLines,
		},
		{
			name: "the snapshot has no block and the chains are loaded", snapBlock: false, nowBlock: true,
			now:       kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 3, kfwForeign),
			wantChain: []string{kfwForeign, kfwReturn}, wantClean: true,
		},
		{
			name: "the snapshot has no block and none is loaded", snapBlock: false, nowBlock: false,
			now: []string{kfwForeign, kfwReturn}, wantChain: []string{kfwForeign, kfwReturn},
		},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, d := kfwHost(t, c.snapBlock)
			snap := kfwSnapshot(t, h, d)
			kfwFiles(h, c.nowBlock)
			kfwSet(t, h, c.now, c.nowBlock)
			rvTestManualEdit(h)
			var cleaned []string
			d.cleanChains = func(_ context.Context, _ core.Env, owner string) error {
				cleaned = append(cleaned, owner)
				h.calls = append(h.calls, "clean "+owner)
				kfwSet(t, h, []string{kfwForeign, kfwReturn}, false)
				return nil
			}
			h.calls, h.stdin = nil, map[string][]byte{}

			rep, err := restore(ctx, h.env(), d, snap)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if got := kfwInput(h, "iptables"); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.wantInput) {
				t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER reload input %q, want %q", got, c.wantInput)
			}
			if got := kfwChain(h); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.wantChain) {
				t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER holds %q, want %q", got, c.wantChain)
			}
			if !slices.Equal(rep.Interleaved, c.wantOrder) {
				t.Errorf("interleaved order %q, want %q", rep.Interleaved, c.wantOrder)
			}
			if c.wantClean != (len(cleaned) == 1) || (c.wantClean && cleaned[0] != "c1") {
				t.Errorf("cleanups %q, want one for change c1: %v", cleaned, c.wantClean)
			}
			if c.wantClean && kfwIndex(h.calls, "clean c1") > kfwIndex(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/ufw reload") {
				t.Errorf("calls %q, want the cleanup before the transition", h.calls)
			}
			if _, ok, err := foreignOf(ctx, h.db, "restore:"+snap.ID); err != nil || ok {
				t.Errorf("a foreign record is left (%v, %v)", ok, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// kfwOrder is the original order a report gives when both families hold
// rules: the IPv4 rules, then the IPv6 rules, each behind its family.
func kfwOrder(rules []string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, fam := range []string{"v4", "v6"} {
		for _, r := range rules {
			out = append(out, fam+" "+r)
		}
	}
	return out
}

func kfwIndex(calls []string, call string) int {
	return slices.IndexFunc(calls, func(c string) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(c, call) })
}

// kfwRevertHost is a fake host on which change c1 set the outgoing default
// to DROP (effect 1) with the Docker block in the files, as its snapshot
// holds them; the post-apply hashes are recorded.
func kfwRevertHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, deps, snapshot) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, d := kfwHost(t, true)
	env := h.env()
	raw, err := capture(ctx, env, d, &core.GuardContext{Complete: true}, false)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := attach(ctx, env); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h.ufw["default deny outgoing"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Output = "DROP"; return 0 }
	h.ufw["default allow outgoing"] = func(s *fhState) int { s.Output = "ACCEPT"; return 0 }
	op, err := defaultOp("outgoing", "DROP")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := runUfw(ctx, env, d, op); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := recordPostHashes(ctx, env, d, string(raw)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	snap, err := getSnapshot(ctx, h.db, string(raw))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	h.calls, h.stdin = nil, map[string][]byte{}
	return h, d, snap
}

// TestKfwRevert: a revert never refuses a foreign
// DOCKER-USER rule. A whole restore and the inverses of a change that
// someone edited around both leave the rule loaded after the block's
// lines; a foreign rule between the block's lines ends the revert with an
// error that gives the original order.
func TestKfwRevert(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	t.Run("whole restore", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, d, snap := kfwRevertHost(t)
		kfwSet(t, h, kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 3, kfwForeign), true)
		out, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), d, []byte(snap.ID))
		if err != nil || len(out.Effects) != 1 || out.Effects[0].State != core.EffectUndone {
			t.Fatalf("revert = %+v, %v, want effect 1 undone", out, err)
		}
		if got, want := kfwChain(h), append(slices.Clone(kfwBlockLines), kfwForeign); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER holds %q, want %q", got, want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("inverses", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, d, _ := kfwRevertHost(t)
		kfwSet(t, h, kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 3, kfwForeign), true)
		rvTestManualEdit(h)
		out, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), d, []byte(kfwSnapshotID(t, h)))
		if err != nil || len(out.Effects) != 1 || out.Effects[0].State != core.EffectUndone {
			t.Fatalf("revert = %+v, %v, want effect 1 undone", out, err)
		}
		if !slices.Contains(unRan(h, 0), "default allow outgoing") {
			t.Fatalf("ufw ran %q, want the inverses, not a whole restore", unRan(h, 0))
		}
		if got, want := kfwChain(h), append(slices.Clone(kfwBlockLines), kfwForeign); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER holds %q, want %q", got, want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("an interrupted restore, finished", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, d, snap := kfwRevertHost(t)
		if err := beginRestoreRecord(ctx, h.db, snap.ID, restoreRecord{Transition: fwstate.TransReload}, time.Now()); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		kfwSet(t, h, kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 1, kfwForeign), true)
		if _, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), d, []byte(snap.ID)); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "original order") {
			t.Fatalf("revert = %v, want an error that lists the original order", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("interleaved", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, d, snap := kfwRevertHost(t)
		kfwSet(t, h, kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 1, kfwForeign), true)
		_, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), d, []byte(snap.ID))
		if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "original order") ||
			strings.Index(err.Error(), kfwBlockLines[0]) > strings.Index(err.Error(), kfwForeign) ||
			strings.Index(err.Error(), kfwForeign) > strings.Index(err.Error(), kfwBlockLines[1]) {
			t.Fatalf("revert = %v, want an error that lists the original order", err)
		}
		if got, want := kfwChain(h), append([]string{kfwForeign}, kfwBlockLines...); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER holds %q, want the foreign rule before the block's lines: %q", got, want)
		}
		if s, err := getSnapshot(ctx, h.db, snap.ID); err != nil || !s.Pinned {
			t.Errorf("snapshot pinned = %v (%v), want it pinned for the repair", s.Pinned, err)
		}
	})
}

func kfwSnapshotID(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost) string {
	t.Helper()
	id, err := snapshotOfChange(context.Background(), h.db, "c1")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return id
}

// TestKfwReloadsRecorded: a record that a cut-off run left
// (the foreign rules before the transition flushed DOCKER-USER) is loaded
// again before the retry writes anything.
func TestKfwReloadsRecorded(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, d, snap := kfwRevertHost(t)
	rec := foreignRecord{
		Layouts: map[fwstate.Family]dockerfw.Layout{fwstate.V4: {After: []string{kfwForeign}}},
		Block:   map[fwstate.Family][]string{fwstate.V4: kfwBlockLines},
	}
	if err := putForeign(ctx, h.db, "restore:"+snap.ID, rec, time.Now()); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if _, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), d, []byte(snap.ID)); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	load, file := kfwIndex(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/iptables-nft-restore -n"), kfwIndex(h.calls, "restore /etc/")
	if load < 0 || file < 0 || load > file {
		t.Errorf("calls %q, want the recorded reload before the first file is written", h.calls)
	}
	if got, want := kfwChain(h), append(slices.Clone(kfwBlockLines), kfwForeign); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER holds %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
	if _, ok, err := foreignOf(ctx, h.db, "restore:"+snap.ID); err != nil || ok {
		t.Errorf("the record is left (%v, %v)", ok, err)
	}
}

// TestKfwEmergencyOrder: the connectivity
// exception's record gives the original order of a foreign rule that sat
// between the block's lines.
func TestKfwEmergencyOrder(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, d, snap := kfwRevertHost(t)
	s := h.state()
	s.Output = "ACCEPT"
	h.setState(s)
	h.guardOK, h.guardDetail = false, "the guard fails"
	kfwSet(t, h, kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 1, kfwForeign), true)
	out, err := revert(ctx, h.env(), d, []byte(snap.ID))
	if err != nil || !out.Override {
		t.Fatalf("revert = %+v, %v, want the override", out, err)
	}
	var detail overrideDetail
	if err := json.Unmarshal(out.Detail, &detail); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := kfwOrder(kfwWith(kfwBlockLines, 1, kfwForeign)); !slices.Equal(detail.InterleavedForeign, want) {
		t.Errorf("interleaved order %q, want %q", detail.InterleavedForeign, want)
	}
	if got, want := kfwChain(h), append([]string{kfwForeign}, kfwBlockLines...); !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("DOCKER-USER holds %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"encoding/hex"
	"fmt"
	"reflect"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/oklog/ulid/v2"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
)

// droULID is the n-th 26-character ULID of these tests.
func droULID(n int) string { return fmt.Sprintf("01J%023d", n) }

// droSeq returns a newID function that hands out droULID(first), then the
// next numbers.
func droSeq(first int) func() string {
	n := first - 1
	return func() string {
		n++
		return droULID(n)
	}
}

// droRouteTuple is the tuple line UFW writes in user.rules for a route rule
// out on docker0 to 172.17.0.2 port 80, tagged id with label; an empty from
// is any source.
func droRouteTuple(action, from, id, label string) string {
	if from == "" {
		from = "0.0.0.0/0"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("### tuple ### route:%s tcp 80 172.17.0.2 any %s out_docker0 comment=%s",
		action, from, hex.EncodeToString([]byte(model.Tag(id, label))))
}

// droConfig is a configuration whose user.rules holds the given tuple
// lines.
func droConfig(t *testing.T, v4 ...string) fwstate.Config {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := fwstate.Config{IPv6: true, DefaultInput: "DROP"}
	for _, line := range v4 {
		tp, err := model.ParseTuple(line, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		cfg.Rules4 = append(cfg.Rules4, tp)
	}
	return cfg
}

// droRoute is the rule Realize wants for a route allow or deny out on
// docker0 to 172.17.0.2 port 80, labelled for container rule row: no id.
func droRoute(action model.Action, from, row string) model.Rule {
	return model.Rule{
		Action: action, Direction: model.DirRoute, Proto: model.ProtoTCP, From: from, To: "172.17.0.2", ToPort: "80",
		OutIface: "docker0", Family: model.FamilyV4, Log: model.LogOff, Comment: dockerfw.LabelPrefix + row,
		Origin: model.OriginDarkpanel,
	}
}

// droWithID is r as containerRuleOps must add it: with its new id.
func droWithID(r model.Rule, id string) model.Rule {
	r.ID = id
	return r
}

// TestDroNewULID: newULID mints a fresh valid ULID on every call, carrying
// the time of the env's clock.
func TestDroNewULID(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	newID := newULID(env)
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for range 5 {
		id := newID()
		parsed, err := ulid.ParseStrict(id)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("newID() = %q: %v", id, err)
		}
		if got, want := parsed.Time(), ulid.Timestamp(env.Clock.Now()); got != want {
			t.Errorf("ULID %s carries time %d, want the clock's %d", id, got, want)
		}
		if seen[id] {
			t.Errorf("ULID %s was minted twice", id)
		}
		seen[id] = true
	}
}

// TestDroContainerRuleOps: dockerfw.RuleOps' operations become ufw
// operations that a change can journal: a delete is wave 1's delete of the
// current rule with that id, an add that appends is wave 1's add, and an
// add at a position is the same effect through "ufw insert".
func TestDroContainerRuleOps(t *testing.T) {
	const (
		row1, row2, row3 = "01J00000000000000000000R01", "01J00000000000000000000R02", "01J00000000000000000000R03"
		tag1, tag2       = "01J00000000000000000000T01", "01J00000000000000000000T02"
	)
	manual := fhRule3000v4
	allow1 := droRouteTuple("allow", "", tag1, dockerfw.LabelPrefix+row1)
	deny2 := droRouteTuple("deny", "203.0.113.0/24", tag2, dockerfw.LabelPrefix+row2)
	cfg := droConfig(t, manual, allow1, deny2)
	current := model.Merge(cfg.Rules4, cfg.Rules6)
	if len(current) != 3 || current[1].ID != tag1 || current[2].ID != tag2 {
		t.Fatalf("the fixture's rules are %+v, want the manual rule and the two tagged ones", current)
	}
	wantDelete := func(r model.Rule) ufwOp {
		return ufwOp{Kind: core.EffectDelete, Resource: ruleResource(r.ID), Args: model.DeleteArgs(r)}
	}
	wantAdd := func(r model.Rule) ufwOp {
		return ufwOp{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: ruleResource(r.ID), Args: model.AddArgs(r)}
	}
	wantInsert := func(pos int, r model.Rule) ufwOp {
		return ufwOp{Kind: core.EffectCreate, Resource: ruleResource(r.ID), Args: model.InsertArgs(pos, r)}
	}
	kept := []model.Rule{droRoute(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, row1), droRoute(model.ActionDeny, "203.0.113.0/24", row2)}
	fresh := droRoute(model.ActionAllow, "198.51.100.0/24", row3)

	tests := []struct {
		name    string
		cfg     fwstate.Config
		desired []model.Rule
		want    []ufwOp
	}{
		{"rules the host holds already need no operation", cfg, kept, nil},
		{"nothing desired deletes every container rule and keeps the manual one", cfg, nil,
			[]ufwOp{wantDelete(current[1]), wantDelete(current[2])}},
		{"a missing rule at the end is added", droConfig(t, manual), kept[:1],
			[]ufwOp{wantAdd(droWithID(kept[0], droULID(500)))}},
		{"a missing rule before a kept one is inserted at its position", droConfig(t, manual, allow1),
			[]model.Rule{fresh, kept[0]},
			[]ufwOp{wantInsert(2, droWithID(fresh, droULID(500)))}},
		{"a changed rule is deleted and added again", droConfig(t, allow1), []model.Rule{fresh},
			[]ufwOp{wantDelete(current[1]), wantAdd(droWithID(fresh, droULID(500)))}},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := containerRuleOps(tt.cfg, tt.desired, droSeq(500))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if len(got) == 0 && len(tt.want) == 0 {
				return
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, tt.want) {
				t.Errorf("operations\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got, tt.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDroContainerRuleOpsError: a failure of dockerfw.RuleOps, here an id
// that is not a ULID, is returned as a firewall error and no operation
// comes with it.
func TestDroContainerRuleOpsError(t *testing.T) {
	ops, err := containerRuleOps(droConfig(t, fhRule3000v4), []model.Rule{droRoute(model.ActionAllow, model.Any, droULID(1))},
		func() string { return "not-a-ulid" })
	if err == nil || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "firewall:") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "dockerfw:") {
		t.Errorf("containerRuleOps = %v, want a firewall error that wraps the dockerfw one", err)
	}
	if len(ops) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("an error came with operations %+v", ops)
	}
}
```

```go
const (
	denAfter4 = "/etc/ufw/after.rules"
	denAfter6 = "/etc/ufw/after6.rules"
	denRow1   = "01J00000000000000000000R01"
	denTag1   = "01J00000000000000000000T01"
)

var denULIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`)

// denRouteTuple is the tuple line UFW writes in user.rules for a route rule
// out on docker0 to 172.17.0.2 port 80, tagged id with label; an empty from
// is any source.
func denRouteTuple(action, from, id, label string) string {
	if from == "" {
		from = "0.0.0.0/0"
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("### tuple ### route:%s tcp 80 172.17.0.2 any %s out_docker0 comment=%s",
		action, from, hex.EncodeToString([]byte(model.Tag(id, label))))
}

// denConfig is a configuration whose user.rules holds the given tuple
// lines.
func denConfig(t *testing.T, v4 ...string) fwstate.Config {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := fwstate.Config{IPv6: true, DefaultInput: "DROP"}
	for _, line := range v4 {
		tp, err := model.ParseTuple(line, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		cfg.Rules4 = append(cfg.Rules4, tp)
	}
	return cfg
}

// denBlock is a block as an after file holds it between its markers.
var denBlock = []byte("*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n")

// denAfterFile is an after file's own lines, with the Docker block when
// block is true.
func denAfterFile(t *testing.T, block bool) []byte {
	t.Helper()
	own := []byte("*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n")
	if !block {
		return own
	}
	out, err := dockerfw.WithBlock(own, denBlock)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return out
}

// denHasBlock reports whether an after file holds the marked block.
func denHasBlock(t *testing.T, data []byte) bool {
	t.Helper()
	_, ok, err := dockerfw.BlockOf(data)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return ok
}

// denFileConfig is a configuration with DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY DROP, the
// given user.rules tuples and both after files, each with a block when its
// flag is set.
func denFileConfig(t *testing.T, block4, block6 bool, v4 ...string) fwstate.Config {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := denConfig(t, v4...)
	cfg.Files = map[string]core.RestoreEntry{
		denAfter4: {Path: denAfter4, Present: true, Mode: 0o640, Data: denAfterFile(t, block4)},
		denAfter6: {Path: denAfter6, Present: true, Mode: 0o640, Data: denAfterFile(t, block6)},
	}
	return cfg
}

// denFacts is one running container, web, publishing 8080 to its port 80 on
// every IPv4 address, on the default bridge.
func denFacts() dockerfw.Facts {
	return dockerfw.Facts{
		Containers: []dockerfw.Container{{
			ID: "id-web", Name: "web",
			Ports:     []dockerfw.Published{{HostAddr: netip.MustParseAddr("0.0.0.0"), HostPort: 8080, ContainerPort: 80, Proto: "tcp"}},
			Endpoints: []dockerfw.Endpoint{{Network: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0", Addr4: netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.2")}},
		}},
		Networks: []dockerfw.Network{{ID: "id-bridge", Name: "bridge", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0",
			Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.17.0.0/16")}}},
	}
}

// denWebAllow is the allowance of web's published port 8080.
func denWebAllow() dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	return dockerfw.ContainerRule{ID: denRow1, Kind: dockerfw.Allow,
		Binding: dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}}
}

// denState is a supported Docker 29.9.1 with the integration off, the
// default settings, the facts of denFacts and the allowance of web:8080 as
// its only stored row; edit changes it before the block is realized.
func denState(edit func(*dockerState)) dockerState {
	st := dockerState{
		available: true,
		det: dockerfw.Detection{Version: "29.9.1", Driver: "iptables", DockerVariant: "nft", UFWVariant: "nft",
			RawProtection: true},
		facts: denFacts(),
		cfg:   dockerConfig{Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()},
		rows:  []dockerfw.ContainerRule{denWebAllow()},
	}
	if edit != nil {
		edit(&st)
	}
	st.realized = dockerfw.Realize(st.rows, st.facts, st.cfg.Settings)
	return st
}

// denLoaded is a loaded state whose nat tables hold the given save text of
// each family ("" for no table).
func denLoaded(t *testing.T, nat4, nat6 string) fwstate.Loaded {
	t.Helper()
	parse := func(text string) *netfilter.Ruleset {
		if text == "" {
			return fhParse(t, fhSave)
		}
		return fhParse(t, fhSave+text)
	}
	return fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: parse(nat4), V6: parse(nat6)}
}

const (
	denNatDocker = "*nat\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:DOCKER - [0:0]\n-A PREROUTING -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -j DOCKER\n" +
		"-A DOCKER ! -i docker0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 8080 -j DNAT --to-destination 172.17.0.2:80\nCOMMIT\n"
	denForward4 = "-A PREROUTING -d 192.0.2.10/32 -i eth0 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 80 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.5:8080"
	denForward6 = "-A PREROUTING -d 2001:db8::10/128 -p tcp -m tcp --dport 443 -j DNAT --to-destination [fd00::5]:8443"
)

// denNat is a nat table with Docker's chain and the given extra rule lines
// of PREROUTING.
func denNat(rules ...string) string {
	return "*nat\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:DOCKER - [0:0]\n-A PREROUTING -m addrtype --dst-type LOCAL -j DOCKER\n" +
		strings.Join(append(rules, ""), "\n") + "COMMIT\n"
}

// denLabels lists the label of each ufw operation's rule tag, sorted.
func denLabels(t *testing.T, ops []ufwOp) []string {
	t.Helper()
	var out []string
	for _, op := range ops {
		n := len(op.Args)
		if n < 2 || op.Args[n-2] != "comment" {
			t.Fatalf("operation %q does not end with a comment", op.Args)
		}
		id, label, ok := model.ParseTag(op.Args[n-1])
		if !ok || !denULIDRe.MatchString(id) {
			t.Fatalf("operation %q carries the tag %q, want darkpanel:<ULID> and a label", op.Args, op.Args[n-1])
		}
		out = append(out, label)
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return out
}

// denTokens reports whether args holds the tokens in order.
func denTokens(args []string, tokens ...string) bool {
	i := 0
	for _, a := range args {
		if i < len(tokens) && a == tokens[i] {
			i++
		}
	}
	return i == len(tokens)
}

func denEmpty(c change) bool {
	return c.flag == nil && c.sources == nil && c.enable == nil && c.restore == nil && !c.repair && !c.cleanup && !c.reload &&
		len(c.ops) == 0 && len(c.files) == 0 && len(c.rowsAdd) == 0 && len(c.rowsDel) == 0
}

func denSameFiles(a, b map[string][]byte) bool { return maps.EqualFunc(a, b, bytes.Equal) }

// TestDenEnableChange: enabling stores the flag, writes the block into both
// after files with the stored rows realized in the same change, reloads UFW,
// and refuses every condition spec 2.6 and the integration invariant name.
func TestDenEnableChange(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	exemption := dockerfw.Exemption{InInterface: "eth0", OrigDestination: netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.10"), OrigPort: 80,
		Destination: netip.MustParseAddr("10.9.0.5"), Proto: "tcp", Port: 8080}
	inDocker := dockerfw.Exemption{OrigDestination: netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.11"), OrigPort: 80,
		Destination: netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.9"), Proto: "tcp", Port: 80}
	withExemptions := func(ex ...dockerfw.Exemption) func(*dockerState) {
		return func(s *dockerState) { s.cfg.Settings.ForwardExemptions = ex }
	}
	tests := []struct {
		name string
		edit func(*dockerState)
		cur  fwstate.Loaded
		cfg  func(*fwstate.Config)
		// refused says the change is refused with firewall.unsupported_integration;
		// detail is what its detail must hold.
		refused bool
		detail  string
	}{
		{name: "a supported host", cur: denLoaded(t, denNatDocker, "")},
		{name: "a host with no nat table", cur: denLoaded(t, "", "")},
		{name: "a forward Docker made is not a foreign one", cur: denLoaded(t, denNat(), "")},
		{name: "a foreign forward its exemption covers", edit: withExemptions(exemption), cur: denLoaded(t, denNat(denForward4), "")},
		{name: "Docker cannot be reached", edit: func(s *dockerState) {
			s.available, s.reason, s.det, s.facts = false, "the Docker daemon is not reachable", dockerfw.Detection{}, dockerfw.Facts{}
		}, cur: denLoaded(t, "", ""), refused: true, detail: "the Docker daemon is not reachable"},
		{name: "an old Docker", edit: func(s *dockerState) { s.det.Version = "27.5.1" }, cur: denLoaded(t, "", ""),
			refused: true, detail: "Docker 27.5.1 is older than 28.0"},
		{name: "raw protection missing", edit: func(s *dockerState) { s.det.RawProtection = false }, cur: denLoaded(t, "", ""),
			refused: true, detail: "raw-table protection"},
		{name: "an open incoming policy", cur: denLoaded(t, "", ""), cfg: func(c *fwstate.Config) { c.DefaultInput = "ACCEPT" },
			refused: true},
		{name: "an exemption into a Docker network", edit: withExemptions(inDocker), cur: denLoaded(t, "", ""),
			refused: true, detail: "exemption 0: destination 172.17.0.9 lies in Docker network bridge (172.17.0.0/16)"},
		{name: "a foreign IPv4 forward without an exemption", cur: denLoaded(t, denNat(denForward4), ""),
			refused: true, detail: denForward4},
		{name: "a foreign IPv6 forward without an exemption", cur: denLoaded(t, "", denNat(denForward6)),
			refused: true, detail: denForward6},
		{name: "an exemption that covers another forward", edit: withExemptions(exemption),
			cur: denLoaded(t, denNat(denForward4), denNat(denForward6)), refused: true, detail: denForward6},
	}
	for _, tt := range tests {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			st := denState(tt.edit)
			cfg := denFileConfig(t, false, false, fhRule3000v4)
			if tt.cfg != nil {
				tt.cfg(&cfg)
			}
			c, err := dockerEnableChange(env, cfg, tt.cur, st)
			if tt.refused {
				if e := errcode.From(err); err == nil || e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, tt.detail) {
					t.Fatalf("dockerEnableChange = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration naming %q", err, tt.detail)
				}
				if !denEmpty(c) {
					t.Errorf("a refusal came with the change %+v", c)
				}
				return
			}
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if c.flag == nil || !*c.flag || !c.reload || c.cleanup || c.sources != nil || c.enable != nil ||
				len(c.rowsAdd) != 0 || len(c.rowsDel) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("change %+v, want only the flag on, the block files, the rule operations and a reload", c)
			}
			want, err := blockFiles(cfg, st, true)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !denSameFiles(c.files, want) || len(c.files) != 2 {
				t.Errorf("files %v, want what blockFiles writes for both after files", slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(c.files)))
			}
			for _, p := range []string{denAfter4, denAfter6} {
				if !denHasBlock(t, c.files[p]) {
					t.Errorf("%s has no block", p)
				}
			}
			if len(st.realized.Rules) != 1 || len(c.ops) != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("%d realized rules and %d operations, want one of each", len(st.realized.Rules), len(c.ops))
			}
			op := c.ops[0]
			if op.Kind != core.EffectCreate || !denTokens(op.Args, "route", "allow", "docker0", "172.17.0.2", "80") {
				t.Errorf("operation %+v, want the route allow to 172.17.0.2 port 80 out on docker0", op)
			}
			if got, want := denLabels(t, c.ops), []string{dockerfw.LabelPrefix + denRow1}; !slices.Equal(got, want) {
				t.Errorf("operation labels %q, want %q", got, want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDenEnableForeignForwards: the refusal for uncovered foreign DNAT rules
// names every uncovered rule of both families with the exemption proposed
// for it as JSON, or says that none can name it, and leaves out the rules
// an exemption covers.
func TestDenEnableForeignForwards(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	const (
		noAddress = "-A PREROUTING -p tcp -m tcp --dport 2222 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.7:22"
		covered   = "-A PREROUTING -d 192.0.2.11/32 -p udp -m udp --dport 53 -j DNAT --to-destination 10.9.0.8:5353"
	)
	cur := denLoaded(t, denNat(denForward4, noAddress, covered), denNat(denForward6))
	coveredEx := dockerfw.Exemption{OrigDestination: netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.11"), OrigPort: 53,
		Destination: netip.MustParseAddr("10.9.0.8"), Proto: "udp", Port: 5353}
	st := denState(func(s *dockerState) { s.cfg.Settings.ForwardExemptions = []dockerfw.Exemption{coveredEx} })
	_, err := dockerEnableChange(env, denFileConfig(t, false, false), cur, st)
	e := errcode.From(err)
	if err == nil || e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration {
		t.Fatalf("dockerEnableChange = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration", err)
	}
	propose := func(line string, fam fwstate.Family) string {
		t.Helper()
		table := cur.V4.Table("nat")
		if fam == fwstate.V6 {
			table = cur.V6.Table("nat")
		}
		for _, r := range dockerfw.ForeignDNAT(table) {
			if r.Text != line {
				continue
			}
			ex, ok := dockerfw.Propose(r, fam)
			if !ok {
				t.Fatalf("no exemption can name %s", line)
			}
			b, err := json.Marshal(ex)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			return string(b)
		}
		t.Fatalf("%s is not a foreign DNAT rule of the fixture", line)
		return ""
	}
	for _, want := range []string{
		denForward4, propose(denForward4, fwstate.V4),
		denForward6, propose(denForward6, fwstate.V6),
		noAddress, "no exemption can name it",
		"forwardExemptions",
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(e.Detail, want) {
			t.Errorf("detail lacks %q:\n%s", want, e.Detail)
		}
	}
	if strings.Contains(e.Detail, covered) {
		t.Errorf("detail names the rule an exemption covers:\n%s", e.Detail)
	}
}

// TestDenEnableAlreadyOn: enabling an enabled integration is a no-op even
// when Docker has become unavailable.
func TestDenEnableAlreadyOn(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	st := denState(func(s *dockerState) {
		s.cfg.Enabled, s.available, s.reason, s.facts = true, false, "the Docker daemon is not reachable", dockerfw.Facts{}
	})
	c, err := dockerEnableChange(env, denFileConfig(t, true, true), denLoaded(t, "", ""), st)
	if err != nil || !denEmpty(c) {
		t.Errorf("dockerEnableChange = %+v, %v; want no change and no error", c, err)
	}
}

// TestDenDisableChange: disabling stores the flag off, writes both after
// files without the block, deletes every tagged container rule, keeps the
// stored rows and the settings, and asks for the owned-chain cleanup; it
// works without Docker and is a no-op when the integration is off.
func TestDenDisableChange(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	tagged := denRouteTuple("allow", "", denTag1, dockerfw.LabelPrefix+denRow1)
	cfg := denFileConfig(t, true, true, fhRule3000v4, tagged)
	current := model.Merge(cfg.Rules4, cfg.Rules6)
	on := func(s *dockerState) { s.cfg.Enabled = true }
	gone := func(s *dockerState) {
		on(s)
		s.available, s.reason, s.det, s.facts = false, "the Docker daemon is not reachable", dockerfw.Detection{}, dockerfw.Facts{}
	}
	for name, edit := range map[string]func(*dockerState){"Docker running": on, "Docker unavailable": gone} {
		t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
			st := denState(edit)
			c, err := dockerDisableChange(env, cfg, st)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if c.flag == nil || *c.flag || !c.cleanup || c.reload || c.sources != nil || c.enable != nil ||
				len(c.rowsAdd) != 0 || len(c.rowsDel) != 0 {
				t.Errorf("change %+v, want only the flag off, the files, the rule deletes and the cleanup", c)
			}
			want, err := blockFiles(cfg, st, false)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !denSameFiles(c.files, want) || len(c.files) != 2 {
				t.Errorf("files %v, want what blockFiles writes without the block", slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(c.files)))
			}
			for _, p := range []string{denAfter4, denAfter6} {
				if denHasBlock(t, c.files[p]) {
					t.Errorf("%s still has the block", p)
				}
			}
			wantOps := []ufwOp{{Kind: core.EffectDelete, Resource: ruleResource(denTag1), Args: model.DeleteArgs(current[1])}}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(c.ops, wantOps) {
				t.Errorf("operations %+v, want the delete of the tagged rule only, not the manual one: %+v", c.ops, wantOps)
			}
		})
	}
	t.Run("already off", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := dockerDisableChange(env, cfg, denState(nil))
		if err != nil || !denEmpty(c) {
			t.Errorf("dockerDisableChange = %+v, %v; want no change and no error", c, err)
		}
	})
}

// denHost is a fake host with a Docker daemon whose UFW reloads and holds
// the Docker block and a tagged container rule when asked.
func denHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, fw, *fakeDocker) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	d := newFakeDocker()
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	f, _ := newFW(h)
	f.d = fdDeps(h, d)
	return h, f, d
}

// denSeed stores the Docker configuration of the fake host's database.
func denSeed(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, enabled bool) {
	t.Helper()
	ctx := context.Background()
	err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		return writeDockerConfig(ctx, tx, dockerConfig{Enabled: enabled, Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()})
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}

// denDockerLines are the Docker lines of a plan's diff.
func denDockerLines(out core.PlanOutcome) []core.DiffLine {
	var lines []core.DiffLine
	for _, l := range out.Diff {
		for _, p := range []string{"docker integration", "after.rules:", "after6.rules:", "Docker chains", "container rule"} {
			if strings.HasPrefix(l.Text, p) {
				lines = append(lines, l)
			}
		}
	}
	return lines
}

// denSupported makes the fake host a supported one: Docker's chains and raw
// protection in the nft variant UFW uses, DOCKER-USER holding only -j
// RETURN, and the legacy variant unreadable.
func denSupported(h *fakeHost) {
	const filter = "*filter\n:INPUT DROP [0:0]\n:FORWARD DROP [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n:DOCKER-FORWARD - [0:0]\n" +
		":ufw-user-input - [0:0]\n-A INPUT -j ufw-user-input\n-A FORWARD -j DOCKER-USER\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n" +
		"-A ufw-user-input -p tcp -m tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT\nCOMMIT\n"
	const raw = "*raw\n:PREROUTING ACCEPT [0:0]\n:OUTPUT ACCEPT [0:0]\nCOMMIT\n"
	h.loaded = fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: fhParse(h.t, filter), V6: fhParse(h.t, filter)}
	h.onReadVariant = func(f fwstate.Family, variant string, tables []string) (*netfilter.Ruleset, error) {
		switch {
		case f != fwstate.V4 || variant != "nft":
			return nil, nil
		case slices.Equal(tables, []string{"raw"}):
			return fhParse(h.t, raw), nil
		}
		return fhParse(h.t, filter), nil
	}
}

// TestDenEnablePlan: the plan of firewall.docker.enable on a supported host
// shows the flag and the block written into both after files; on an
// unsupported or unreachable Docker it is refused; when the integration is
// on already it shows nothing.
func TestDenEnablePlan(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	raw := json.RawMessage(`{}`)

	t.Run("supported", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, f, _ := denHost(t)
		denSupported(h)
		out, err := f.dockerEnable().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), raw)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		want := []core.DiffLine{
			{Op: "-", Text: "docker integration off"},
			{Op: "+", Text: "docker integration on"},
			{Op: "+", Text: "after.rules: Docker block written"},
			{Op: "+", Text: "after6.rules: Docker block written"},
		}
		if got := denDockerLines(out); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
			t.Errorf("Docker lines\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got, want)
		}
		if len(out.Guards) != 1 || out.Guards[0].ID != guard.GuardID || !out.Guards[0].OK {
			t.Errorf("guards %+v, want the lockout guard passing", out.Guards)
		}
	})
	t.Run("an old Docker", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, f, d := denHost(t)
		denSupported(h)
		d.info.ServerVersion = "27.5.1"
		_, err := f.dockerEnable().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), raw)
		if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "Docker 27.5.1 is older than 28.0") {
			t.Errorf("plan = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration naming the version", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("Docker is not running", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, f, d := denHost(t)
		denSupported(h)
		d.err = fmt.Errorf("dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)
		_, err := f.dockerEnable().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), raw)
		if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "not reachable") {
			t.Errorf("plan = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration saying Docker is not reachable", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("already enabled", func(t *testing.T) {
		h, f, d := denHost(t)
		denSupported(h)
		denSeed(t, h, true)
		d.err = fmt.Errorf("dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)
		out, err := f.dockerEnable().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), raw)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if got := denDockerLines(out); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("Docker lines %+v, want none", got)
		}
	})
}

// TestDenDisablePlan: the plan of firewall.docker.disable shows the flag off,
// the block removed from the file that has it, and the chains removed, with
// Docker unreachable too; on a host where the integration is off it shows
// nothing.
func TestDenDisablePlan(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	raw := json.RawMessage(`{}`)
	h, f, d := denHost(t)
	denSupported(h)
	denSeed(t, h, true)
	tagged := denRouteTuple("allow", "", denTag1, dockerfw.LabelPrefix+denRow1)
	s := h.state()
	s.Rules4 = append(s.Rules4, tagged)
	h.setState(s)
	h.writeFile(denAfter4, denAfterFile(t, true))
	rule := model.Merge(h.config().Rules4, nil)[2]
	h.ufw[strings.Join(model.DeleteArgs(rule), " ")] = func(s *fhState) int {
		s.Rules4 = slices.DeleteFunc(s.Rules4, func(l string) bool { return l == tagged })
		return 0
	}
	d.err = fmt.Errorf("dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)

	out, err := f.dockerDisable().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), raw)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	want := []core.DiffLine{
		{Op: "-", Text: "docker integration on"},
		{Op: "+", Text: "docker integration off"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "after.rules: Docker block removed"},
		{Op: "-", Text: "Docker chains removed"},
	}
	if got := denDockerLines(out); !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("Docker lines\n%+v\nwant\n%+v", got, want)
	}

	denSeed(t, h, false)
	out, err = f.dockerDisable().Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), raw)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got := denDockerLines(out); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("Docker lines %+v with the integration off, want none", got)
	}
}

// TestDenVerify: verify of enable and disable compares the stored flag and
// the after files with what the action set, before the comparison with the
// prediction.
func TestDenVerify(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, _ := denHost(t)
	verify := func(def core.ActionDef) error {
		return def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(`{}`), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	}
	mismatch := func(name string, err error) {
		t.Helper()
		if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "after the change") {
			t.Errorf("%s verify = %v, want the action's own prediction mismatch", name, err)
		}
	}
	h.writeFile(denAfter4, denAfterFile(t, false))
	h.writeFile(denAfter6, denAfterFile(t, false))
	if err := verify(f.dockerDisable()); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("disable verify with the flag off and no block = %v, want nil", err)
	}
	mismatch("enable with the flag off", verify(f.dockerEnable()))

	denSeed(t, h, true)
	mismatch("enable without the block", verify(f.dockerEnable()))
	mismatch("disable with the flag on", verify(f.dockerDisable()))
	h.writeFile(denAfter4, denAfterFile(t, true))
	mismatch("enable with the block in one file only", verify(f.dockerEnable()))
	h.writeFile(denAfter6, denAfterFile(t, true))
	if err := verify(f.dockerEnable()); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("enable verify with the flag and both blocks = %v, want nil", err)
	}

	denSeed(t, h, false)
	mismatch("disable with the blocks still in the files", verify(f.dockerDisable()))
}

// TestDenActionDefinitions: both actions are the revertible, agent-side,
// firewall-locked mutations of every firewall change, with the lockout
// guard and their empty guarded input.
func TestDenActionDefinitions(t *testing.T) {
	_, f, _ := denHost(t)
	for name, def := range map[string]core.ActionDef{
		"firewall.docker.enable": f.dockerEnable(), "firewall.docker.disable": f.dockerDisable(),
	} {
		s := def.Spec
		if s.Name != name || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != core.ClassRevertible || s.Side != core.SideAgent ||
			!slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, []string{"firewall"}) || s.RepairedBy != "firewall.state.repair" ||
			len(s.Guards) != 1 || s.Guards[0].ID != guard.GuardID || !s.Guards[0].Overridable {
			t.Errorf("%s spec %+v", name, s)
		}
		if err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(`{}`)); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s rejects an empty input: %v", name, err)
		}
		if err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(`{"manual":true}`)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s accepts a manual flag it has no use for", name)
		}
	}
}
```

**Implementer:** dforge:impl-opus-high
**Evaluation:** files 1 - spec 2 - coupling 2 - risk 2 = 7

The four actions are one operation list over the stored rows (spec 2.6, container policy): `allow`, `deny` and `remove` are the single-element lists, `containers.apply` takes the list itself. One builder, `containerChange`, validates the list against the stored rows in order, then realizes the resulting rows when the integration flag is on (Contracts "Integration on and off": the desired container rules are `st.realized.Rules` of the changed rows when the flag is on, nil when it is off). Decisions this task fixes: an allowance or deny equal to a stored row (binding, kind, source; not its id) changes nothing; a deny needs an allow row on the same binding at that point of the list; removing an allowance leaves the binding's denies stored (they realize nothing without an allowance, as Contracts "dockerfw realization" says, and `firewall.docker` lists them); with the integration on, an unreachable Docker is refused because the realization would otherwise close every published port.
