```go
package firewall

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"regexp"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/guard"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/model"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

const (
	ctrAfter4 = "/etc/ufw/after.rules"
	ctrAfter6 = "/etc/ufw/after6.rules"
	ctrRow1   = "01J00000000000000000000R01"
	ctrRow2   = "01J00000000000000000000R02"
	ctrRow9   = "01J00000000000000000000R09"
	ctrTag1   = "01J00000000000000000000T01"
)

var ctrULIDRe = regexp.MustCompile(`^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`)

// ctrBinding is web's published port 8080 on every host address.
func ctrBinding() dockerfw.Binding {
	return dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}
}

func ctrAllowRow(id string, b dockerfw.Binding) dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	return dockerfw.ContainerRule{ID: id, Binding: b, Kind: dockerfw.Allow}
}

// ctrFacts is one running container, web, publishing 8080 to its port 80
// on every IPv4 address, on the default bridge.
func ctrFacts() dockerfw.Facts {
	return dockerfw.Facts{
		Containers: []dockerfw.Container{{
			ID: "id-web", Name: "web",
			Ports:     []dockerfw.Published{{HostAddr: netip.MustParseAddr("0.0.0.0"), HostPort: 8080, ContainerPort: 80, Proto: "tcp"}},
			Endpoints: []dockerfw.Endpoint{{Network: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0", Addr4: netip.MustParseAddr("172.17.0.2")}},
		}},
		Networks: []dockerfw.Network{{ID: "id-bridge", Name: "bridge", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0",
			Subnets: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("172.17.0.0/16")}}},
	}
}

// ctrState is a Docker 29.9.1 that answers, with the integration off, the
// default settings, no facts and no stored row; edit changes it before the
// block is realized.
func ctrState(edit func(*dockerState)) dockerState {
	st := dockerState{
		available: true,
		det: dockerfw.Detection{Version: "29.9.1", Driver: "iptables", DockerVariant: "nft", UFWVariant: "nft",
			RawProtection: true},
		cfg: dockerConfig{Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()},
	}
	if edit != nil {
		edit(&st)
	}
	st.realized = dockerfw.Realize(st.rows, st.facts, st.cfg.Settings)
	return st
}

// ctrFiles is a configuration with both after files, each carrying the
// block of blocks, and the given user.rules tuples.
func ctrFiles(t *testing.T, blocks map[string][]byte, v4 ...string) fwstate.Config {
	t.Helper()
	cfg := fwstate.Config{IPv6: true, DefaultInput: "DROP", Files: map[string]core.RestoreEntry{}}
	for _, p := range []string{ctrAfter4, ctrAfter6} {
		data := []byte("*filter\n# after\nCOMMIT\n")
		if b, ok := blocks[p]; ok {
			var err error
			if data, err = dockerfw.WithBlock(data, b); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
		}
		cfg.Files[p] = core.RestoreEntry{Path: p, Present: true, Mode: 0o640, Data: data}
	}
	for _, line := range v4 {
		tp, err := model.ParseTuple(line, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		cfg.Rules4 = append(cfg.Rules4, tp)
	}
	return cfg
}

// ctrTuple is the tuple UFW writes for a route allow out on docker0 to
// 172.17.0.2 port 80, tagged id with label.
func ctrTuple(id, label string) string {
	return "### tuple ### route:allow tcp 80 172.17.0.2 any 0.0.0.0/0 out_docker0 comment=" +
		hex.EncodeToString([]byte(model.Tag(id, label)))
}

func ctrTokens(args []string, tokens ...string) bool {
	i := 0
	for _, a := range args {
		if i < len(tokens) && a == tokens[i] {
			i++
		}
	}
	return i == len(tokens)
}

func ctrEmpty(c change) bool {
	return c.flag == nil && c.sources == nil && c.enable == nil && c.restore == nil && !c.repair && !c.cleanup && !c.reload &&
		len(c.ops) == 0 && len(c.files) == 0 && len(c.rowsAdd) == 0 && len(c.rowsDel) == 0
}

// ctrPath is the first field path of an invalid-input refusal.
func ctrPath(t *testing.T, err error) string {
	t.Helper()
	e := errcode.From(err)
	if err == nil || e.Code != errcode.InvalidInput || len(e.Fields) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want an invalid input with a field", err)
	}
	return e.Fields[0].Path
}

func ctrOp(op string, b dockerfw.Binding, from string) ContainerOp {
	o := ContainerOp{Op: op, Binding: &b}
	if from != "" {
		o.From = netip.MustParsePrefix(from)
	}
	return o
}

// TestCtrChangeSingle: with the integration off, each action changes the
// stored rows only: an allowance or deny is one new row with a fresh ULID,
// a removal deletes the row; a rule that is stored already changes nothing;
// every invalid request is refused at the field that is wrong.
func TestCtrChangeSingle(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	cfg := ctrFiles(t, nil)
	b := ctrBinding()
	other := dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "db", HostPort: 5432, Proto: "tcp"}
	st := ctrState(func(s *dockerState) {
		s.rows = []dockerfw.ContainerRule{ctrAllowRow(ctrRow1, b), ctrAllowRow(ctrRow9, other)}
	})
	add := func(t *testing.T, st dockerState, op ContainerOp) dockerfw.ContainerRule {
		t.Helper()
		c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, []ContainerOp{op}, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if c.flag != nil || len(c.ops) != 0 || len(c.files) != 0 || c.reload || c.cleanup || len(c.rowsDel) != 0 || len(c.rowsAdd) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("change %+v, want one new row and nothing else", c)
		}
		if !ctrULIDRe.MatchString(c.rowsAdd[0].ID) {
			t.Errorf("row id %q is not a ULID", c.rowsAdd[0].ID)
		}
		return c.rowsAdd[0]
	}

	t.Run("an allowance for every source", func(t *testing.T) {
		r := add(t, ctrState(nil), ctrOp("allow", b, ""))
		if r.Kind != dockerfw.Allow || r.Binding != b || r.From.IsValid() {
			t.Errorf("row %+v, want an allowance of %+v for any source", r, b)
		}
	})
	t.Run("an allowance for a range", func(t *testing.T) {
		r := add(t, ctrState(nil), ctrOp("allow", b, "198.51.100.0/24"))
		if r.Kind != dockerfw.Allow || r.From != netip.MustParsePrefix("198.51.100.0/24") {
			t.Errorf("row %+v, want an allowance from 198.51.100.0/24", r)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a deny on an allowed binding", func(t *testing.T) {
		r := add(t, st, ctrOp("deny", b, "203.0.113.0/24"))
		if r.Kind != dockerfw.Deny || r.Binding != b || r.From != netip.MustParsePrefix("203.0.113.0/24") {
			t.Errorf("row %+v, want a deny of 203.0.113.0/24 on %+v", r, b)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a removal", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, []ContainerOp{{Op: "remove", ID: ctrRow9}}, false)
		if err != nil || !slices.Equal(c.rowsDel, []string{ctrRow9}) || len(c.rowsAdd) != 0 || len(c.ops) != 0 || len(c.files) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, %v; want only the deletion of %s", c, err, ctrRow9)
		}
	})
	t.Run("a rule that is stored already", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, []ContainerOp{ctrOp("allow", b, "")}, false)
		if err != nil || !ctrEmpty(c) {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, %v; want no change", c, err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("an empty batch", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, nil, true)
		if err != nil || !ctrEmpty(c) {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, %v; want no change", c, err)
		}
	})

	refused := []struct {
		name string
		op   ContainerOp
		path string
	}{
		{"a deny on a binding nobody allows", ctrOp("deny", dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8081, Proto: "tcp"}, "203.0.113.0/24"), "/binding"},
		{"a deny that could never match", ctrOp("deny", b, "10.1.0.0/16"), "/from"},
		{"a deny without a source", ctrOp("deny", b, ""), "/from"},
		{"a selector that is no name", ctrOp("allow", dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "-web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}, ""), "/binding/selector"},
		{"a protocol that is neither", ctrOp("allow", dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "icmp"}, ""), "/binding/proto"},
		{"no binding", ContainerOp{Op: "allow"}, "/binding"},
		{"a removal of no row", ContainerOp{Op: "remove", ID: ctrRow2}, "/id"},
		{"a removal without an id", ContainerOp{Op: "remove"}, "/id"},
		{"an operation that is none", ctrOp("toggle", b, ""), "/op"},
	}
	for _, tt := range refused {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, []ContainerOp{tt.op}, false)
			if got := ctrPath(t, err); got != tt.path {
				t.Errorf("refused at %s, want %s", got, tt.path)
			}
			if !ctrEmpty(c) {
				t.Errorf("a refusal came with the change %+v", c)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestCtrChangeBatch: a batch applies its operations in order to the stored
// rows, so a deny may follow the allowance it needs, and a refusal names the
// operation by its index.
func TestCtrChangeBatch(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	cfg := ctrFiles(t, nil)
	b := ctrBinding()
	other := dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "db", HostPort: 5432, Proto: "tcp"}
	st := ctrState(func(s *dockerState) { s.rows = []dockerfw.ContainerRule{ctrAllowRow(ctrRow9, other)} })

	c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, []ContainerOp{
		ctrOp("allow", b, ""), ctrOp("deny", b, "203.0.113.0/24"), {Op: "remove", ID: ctrRow9},
	}, true)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(c.rowsAdd) != 2 || c.rowsAdd[0].Kind != dockerfw.Allow || c.rowsAdd[1].Kind != dockerfw.Deny ||
		c.rowsAdd[0].ID == c.rowsAdd[1].ID || !slices.Equal(c.rowsDel, []string{ctrRow9}) {
		t.Errorf("change %+v, want the allowance and the deny added in order and %s deleted", c, ctrRow9)
	}

	refused := []struct {
		name string
		ops  []ContainerOp
		path string
	}{
		{"a deny that could never match", []ContainerOp{ctrOp("allow", b, ""), ctrOp("deny", b, "10.1.0.0/16")}, "/ops/1/from"},
		{"a deny before its allowance", []ContainerOp{ctrOp("deny", b, "203.0.113.0/24"), ctrOp("allow", b, "")}, "/ops/0/binding"},
		{"a removal twice", []ContainerOp{{Op: "remove", ID: ctrRow9}, {Op: "remove", ID: ctrRow9}}, "/ops/1/id"},
		{"a removal of no row", []ContainerOp{ctrOp("allow", b, ""), {Op: "remove", ID: ctrRow2}}, "/ops/1/id"},
		{"no binding", []ContainerOp{ctrOp("allow", b, ""), ctrOp("allow", b, "198.51.100.0/24"), {Op: "deny"}}, "/ops/2/binding"},
		{"an operation that is none", []ContainerOp{{Op: "toggle"}}, "/ops/0/op"},
	}
	for _, tt := range refused {
		t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, tt.ops, true)
			if got := ctrPath(t, err); got != tt.path {
				t.Errorf("refused at %s, want %s", got, tt.path)
			}
			if !ctrEmpty(c) {
				t.Errorf("a refusal came with the change %+v", c)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestCtrChangeIntegrationOn: with the integration on, the rows' realization
// follows in the same change: the block files of both families, a reload
// and the tagged UFW rules the new rows need; a change that leaves the
// realization as it is writes nothing, and the integration needs Docker to
// be reachable.
func TestCtrChangeIntegrationOn(t *testing.T) {
	env := newFakeHost(t).env()
	b := ctrBinding()
	on := func(s *dockerState) { s.cfg.Enabled, s.facts = true, ctrFacts() }

	t.Run("an allowance is realized", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := ctrState(on)
		cfg := ctrFiles(t, nil)
		c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, []ContainerOp{ctrOp("allow", b, "")}, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if len(c.rowsAdd) != 1 || c.flag != nil || !c.reload || c.cleanup || len(c.rowsDel) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("change %+v, want the new row, the block files and a reload", c)
		}
		for _, p := range []string{ctrAfter4, ctrAfter6} {
			if _, ok, err := dockerfw.BlockOf(c.files[p]); err != nil || !ok {
				t.Fatalf("%s: block %v, %v", p, ok, err)
			}
		}
		if !bytes.Contains(c.files[ctrAfter4], []byte(b.Chain())) {
			t.Errorf("after.rules lacks the binding chain %s:\n%s", b.Chain(), c.files[ctrAfter4])
		}
		if len(c.ops) != 1 || c.ops[0].Kind != core.EffectCreate ||
			!ctrTokens(c.ops[0].Args, "route", "allow", "docker0", "172.17.0.2", "80", "comment") {
			t.Fatalf("operations %+v, want the route allow to 172.17.0.2 port 80 out on docker0", c.ops)
		}
		args := c.ops[0].Args
		id, label, ok := model.ParseTag(args[len(args)-1])
		if !ok || !ctrULIDRe.MatchString(id) || label != dockerfw.LabelPrefix+c.rowsAdd[0].ID {
			t.Errorf("rule tag %q, want darkpanel:<ULID> labelled for the new row %s", args[len(args)-1], c.rowsAdd[0].ID)
		}
	})

	t.Run("a removal takes the realization away", func(t *testing.T) {
		before := ctrState(func(s *dockerState) {
			on(s)
			s.rows = []dockerfw.ContainerRule{ctrAllowRow(ctrRow1, b)}
		})
		cfg := ctrFiles(t, nil)
		files, err := blockFiles(cfg, before, true)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		cfg = ctrFiles(t, nil, ctrTuple(ctrTag1, dockerfw.LabelPrefix+ctrRow1))
		for p, data := range files {
			cfg.Files[p] = core.RestoreEntry{Path: p, Present: true, Mode: 0o640, Data: data}
		}
		c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, before, []ContainerOp{{Op: "remove", ID: ctrRow1}}, false)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		current := model.Merge(cfg.Rules4, cfg.Rules6)
		wantOps := []ufwOp{{Kind: core.EffectDelete, Resource: ruleResource(ctrTag1), Args: model.DeleteArgs(current[0])}}
		if !slices.Equal(c.rowsDel, []string{ctrRow1}) || !c.reload || len(c.ops) != 1 || c.ops[0].Resource != wantOps[0].Resource ||
			!slices.Equal(c.ops[0].Args, wantOps[0].Args) || c.ops[0].Kind != core.EffectDelete {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, want the row deleted, its UFW rule deleted and the block rewritten", c)
		}
		if bytes.Contains(c.files[ctrAfter4], []byte(b.Chain())) {
			t.Errorf("after.rules still has the binding chain %s", b.Chain())
		}
	})

	t.Run("nothing changes when the realization already holds", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := ctrState(func(s *dockerState) {
			on(s)
			s.rows = []dockerfw.ContainerRule{ctrAllowRow(ctrRow1, b)}
		})
		files, err := blockFiles(ctrFiles(t, nil), st, true)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		cfg := ctrFiles(t, nil, ctrTuple(ctrTag1, dockerfw.LabelPrefix+ctrRow1))
		for p, data := range files {
			cfg.Files[p] = core.RestoreEntry{Path: p, Present: true, Mode: 0o640, Data: data}
		}
		c, err := containerChange(env, cfg, st, nil, true)
		if err != nil || !ctrEmpty(c) {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, %v; want no change", c, err)
		}
	})

	t.Run("a change that restores a lost realization is made", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := ctrState(func(s *dockerState) {
			on(s)
			s.rows = []dockerfw.ContainerRule{ctrAllowRow(ctrRow1, b)}
		})
		c, err := containerChange(env, ctrFiles(t, nil), st, nil, true)
		if err != nil || len(c.files) != 2 || !c.reload || len(c.ops) != 1 || len(c.rowsAdd) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, %v; want the block and the rule written with no row change", c, err)
		}
	})

	t.Run("an unreachable Docker is refused", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := ctrState(func(s *dockerState) {
			s.cfg.Enabled, s.available, s.reason = true, false, "the Docker daemon is not reachable"
		})
		c, err := containerChange(env, ctrFiles(t, nil), st, []ContainerOp{ctrOp("allow", b, "")}, false)
		if e := errcode.From(err); err == nil || e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "not reachable") {
			t.Errorf("containerChange = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration saying Docker is not reachable", err)
		}
		if !ctrEmpty(c) {
			t.Errorf("a refusal came with the change %+v", c)
		}
	})

	t.Run("an unreachable Docker does not matter while the integration is off", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := ctrState(func(s *dockerState) { s.available, s.reason = false, "the Docker daemon is not reachable" })
		c, err := containerChange(env, ctrFiles(t, nil), st, []ContainerOp{ctrOp("allow", b, "")}, false)
		if err != nil || len(c.rowsAdd) != 1 || len(c.files) != 0 || len(c.ops) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, %v; want the row alone", c, err)
		}
	})
}

// ctrHost is a fake host with a Docker daemon that answers and no
// container, and the firewall over both.
func ctrHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, fw, *fakeDocker) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	d := newFakeDocker()
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	f, _ := newFW(h)
	f.d = fdDeps(h, d)
	return h, f, d
}

func ctrRows(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost) []dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := listContainerRules(context.Background(), h.db)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return rows
}

// ctrFind returns the stored row of the kind and binding with the source.
func ctrFind(t *testing.T, h *fakeHost, kind dockerfw.Kind, selector, from string) dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	t.Helper()
	for _, r := range ctrRows(t, h) {
		if r.Kind == kind && r.Binding.Selector == selector && (r.From.String() == from || (from == "" && !r.From.IsValid())) {
			return r
		}
	}
	t.Fatalf("no stored %s row of %s from %q in %+v", kind, selector, from, ctrRows(t, h))
	return dockerfw.ContainerRule{}
}

// ctrLines are the container rule lines of a plan's diff.
func ctrLines(out core.PlanOutcome) []string {
	var lines []string
	for _, l := range out.Diff {
		if strings.HasPrefix(l.Text, "container rule") {
			lines = append(lines, l.Op+" "+l.Text)
		}
	}
	return lines
}

// ctrCreated counts the journaled creations of container rows made.
func ctrCreated(h *fakeHost) int {
	n := 0
	for _, e := range h.journal.effects {
		if e.Kind == core.EffectCreate && e.State == core.EffectMade && strings.HasPrefix(e.Resource, "firewall.container:") {
			n++
		}
	}
	return n
}

// TestCtrActions: the four actions through the engine's pipeline with the
// integration off: each plan lists its rule lines, each apply stores or
// deletes the rows as journaled effects without any ufw command, and verify
// finds them.
func TestCtrActions(t *testing.T) {
	h, f, _ := ctrHost(t)
	web := `{"selector":"web","hostPort":8080,"proto":"tcp"}`
	shop := `{"selector":"shop/api","hostAddr":"192.0.2.1","hostPort":9090,"proto":"tcp"}`
	step := func(def core.ActionDef, raw string, wantLines ...string) {
		t.Helper()
		out, ran := acRun(t, h, def, raw)
		if got := ctrLines(out); !slices.Equal(got, wantLines) {
			t.Errorf("%s %s: lines %q, want %q", def.Spec.Name, raw, got, wantLines)
		}
		if len(ran) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("%s ran ufw %q, want no command", def.Spec.Name, ran)
		}
	}

	step(f.containerAllow(), `{"binding":`+web+`}`, "+ container rule + web all:8080/tcp allow any")
	allow := ctrFind(t, h, dockerfw.Allow, "web", "")
	if allow.Binding != ctrBinding() || ctrCreated(h) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("row %+v with %d creations journaled, want the allowance and one creation", allow, ctrCreated(h))
	}
	var created *core.Effect
	for i, e := range h.journal.effects {
		if e.Resource == "firewall.container:"+allow.ID {
			created = &h.journal.effects[i]
		}
	}
	if created == nil || created.Kind != core.EffectCreate || created.State != core.EffectMade || !created.Local || !created.InverseLocal {
		t.Errorf("effect %+v, want the made, local creation of firewall.container:%s", created, allow.ID)
	}

	step(f.containerAllow(), `{"binding":`+web+`}`)
	if n := len(ctrRows(t, h)); n != 1 || ctrCreated(h) != 1 {
		t.Errorf("%d rows and %d creations after the same allowance again, want one and one", n, ctrCreated(h))
	}

	step(f.containerDeny(), `{"binding":`+web+`,"from":"203.0.113.0/24"}`, "+ container rule + web all:8080/tcp deny 203.0.113.0/24")
	deny := ctrFind(t, h, dockerfw.Deny, "web", "203.0.113.0/24")

	step(f.containersApply(), `{"ops":[{"op":"allow","binding":`+shop+`,"from":"198.51.100.0/24"},{"op":"remove","id":"`+deny.ID+`"}]}`,
		"+ container rule + shop/api 192.0.2.1:9090/tcp allow 198.51.100.0/24",
		"- container rule - web all:8080/tcp deny 203.0.113.0/24")
	shopRow := ctrFind(t, h, dockerfw.Allow, "shop/api", "198.51.100.0/24")
	if rows := ctrRows(t, h); len(rows) != 2 || shopRow.Binding.HostAddr != netip.MustParseAddr("192.0.2.1") {
		t.Errorf("rows %+v, want web's allowance and the shop/api allowance", rows)
	}

	step(f.containersApply(), `{"ops":[]}`)
	step(f.containerRemove(), `{"id":"`+shopRow.ID+`"}`, "- container rule - shop/api 192.0.2.1:9090/tcp allow 198.51.100.0/24")
	if rows := ctrRows(t, h); len(rows) != 1 || rows[0].ID != allow.ID {
		t.Errorf("rows %+v, want web's allowance only", rows)
	}
}

// TestCtrPlanRefusals: the plan refuses what the builder refuses, at the
// same fields, and an integration that is on needs a reachable Docker.
func TestCtrPlanRefusals(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, d := ctrHost(t)
	web := `{"selector":"web","hostPort":8080,"proto":"tcp"}`
	plan := func(def core.ActionDef, raw string) error {
		_, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(raw))
		return err
	}
	if got := ctrPath(t, plan(f.containerDeny(), `{"binding":`+web+`,"from":"203.0.113.0/24"}`)); got != "/binding" {
		t.Errorf("deny without an allowance refused at %s, want /binding", got)
	}
	if got := ctrPath(t, plan(f.containerRemove(), `{"id":"`+ctrRow2+`"}`)); got != "/id" {
		t.Errorf("removal of no row refused at %s, want /id", got)
	}
	if got := ctrPath(t, plan(f.containersApply(), `{"ops":[{"op":"allow","binding":`+web+`},{"op":"deny","binding":`+web+`,"from":"10.1.0.0/16"}]}`)); got != "/ops/1/from" {
		t.Errorf("batch refused at %s, want /ops/1/from", got)
	}

	err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		return writeDockerConfig(ctx, tx, dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()})
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	d.err = fmt.Errorf("dial unix /var/run/docker.sock: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)
	if e := errcode.From(plan(f.containerAllow(), `{"binding":`+web+`}`)); e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration {
		t.Errorf("allow with the integration on and Docker down = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration", e)
	}
}

// TestCtrVerify: verify finds the stored rows the action stored or removed
// and refuses when they are not as it left them, before it compares the
// loaded state.
func TestCtrVerify(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f, _ := ctrHost(t)
	web := `{"selector":"web","hostPort":8080,"proto":"tcp"}`
	allowRaw := `{"binding":` + web + `}`
	verify := func(def core.ActionDef, raw string) error {
		return def.Handler.Verify(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(raw), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	}
	wantMismatch := func(name string, err error) {
		t.Helper()
		if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.FirewallPredictionMismatch || !strings.Contains(e.Detail, "after the change") {
			t.Errorf("%s verify = %v, want the action's own prediction mismatch", name, err)
		}
	}
	wantMismatch("allow with no stored row", verify(f.containerAllow(), allowRaw))

	acRun(t, h, f.containerAllow(), allowRaw)
	allow := ctrFind(t, h, dockerfw.Allow, "web", "")
	if err := verify(f.containerAllow(), allowRaw); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("allow verify with the row stored = %v, want nil", err)
	}
	wantMismatch("remove of a stored row", verify(f.containerRemove(), `{"id":"`+allow.ID+`"}`))
	wantMismatch("deny with no stored row", verify(f.containerDeny(), `{"binding":`+web+`,"from":"203.0.113.0/24"}`))
	wantMismatch("apply whose removal left the row", verify(f.containersApply(), `{"ops":[{"op":"remove","id":"`+allow.ID+`"}]}`))
	if err := verify(f.containersApply(), `{"ops":[{"op":"allow","binding":`+web+`}]}`); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("apply verify with its allowance stored = %v, want nil", err)
	}

	err := h.db.Write(ctx, func(tx *sql.Tx) error { return deleteContainerRule(ctx, tx, allow.ID) })
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := verify(f.containerRemove(), `{"id":"`+allow.ID+`"}`); err != nil {
		t.Errorf("remove verify with the row gone = %v, want nil", err)
	}
	wantMismatch("allow after the row went", verify(f.containerAllow(), allowRaw))
}

// TestCtrActionDefinitions: the four actions are the revertible, agent-side,
// firewall-locked mutations of every firewall change with the lockout guard;
// their schemas take a binding, and a deny needs its source.
func TestCtrActionDefinitions(t *testing.T) {
	_, f, _ := ctrHost(t)
	defs := map[string]core.ActionDef{
		"firewall.container.allow": f.containerAllow(), "firewall.container.deny": f.containerDeny(),
		"firewall.container.remove": f.containerRemove(), "firewall.containers.apply": f.containersApply(),
	}
	for name, def := range defs {
		s := def.Spec
		if s.Name != name || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != core.ClassRevertible || s.Side != core.SideAgent ||
			!slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, []string{"firewall"}) || s.RepairedBy != "firewall.state.repair" ||
			len(s.Guards) != 1 || s.Guards[0].ID != guard.GuardID || !s.Guards[0].Overridable {
			t.Errorf("%s spec %+v", name, s)
		}
	}
	web := `{"selector":"web","hostPort":8080,"proto":"tcp"}`
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name string
		raw  string
		ok   bool
	}{
		{"firewall.container.allow", `{"binding":` + web + `}`, true},
		{"firewall.container.allow", `{"binding":` + web + `,"from":"198.51.100.0/24"}`, true},
		{"firewall.container.allow", `{"binding":` + web + `,"from":"198.51.100.0"}`, false},
		{"firewall.container.allow", `{}`, false},
		{"firewall.container.deny", `{"binding":` + web + `,"from":"203.0.113.0/24"}`, true},
		{"firewall.container.deny", `{"binding":` + web + `}`, false},
		{"firewall.container.remove", `{"id":"` + ctrRow1 + `"}`, true},
		{"firewall.container.remove", `{}`, false},
		{"firewall.containers.apply", `{"ops":[]}`, true},
		{"firewall.containers.apply", `{"ops":[{"op":"remove","id":"` + ctrRow1 + `"},{"op":"allow","binding":` + web + `}]}`, true},
		{"firewall.containers.apply", `{"ops":[{"op":"toggle"}]}`, false},
		{"firewall.containers.apply", `{"ops":[{"op":"allow","binding":` + web + `,"manual":true}]}`, false},
	} {
		err := schema.NewValidator().ValidateInput(defs[c.name], json.RawMessage(c.raw))
		if (err == nil) != c.ok {
			t.Errorf("%s input %s: error %v, want ok=%v", c.name, c.raw, err, c.ok)
		}
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run the tests to verify they fail**

Run: `mkdir -p /root/.cache/w2-tmp/43 && TMPDIR=/root/.cache/w2-tmp/43 GOTOOLCHAIN=local timeout 300 go test -count=1 -run 'TestCtr' ./internal/modules/firewall/`
Expected: FAIL to build with errors naming only identifiers this task adds: `undefined: ContainerOp` (first), `containerChange`, and `f.containerAllow`, `f.containerDeny`, `f.containerRemove`, `f.containersApply undefined`. An error that names anything else (`dockerfw`, `dockerState`, `blockFiles`, `fdDeps`, `listContainerRules`, `writeDockerConfig`, `newULID`) means a task this one depends on is missing from the base: stop and report it.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

Create `actions_container.go` with a doc comment on every exported identifier.

1. Input types, exactly as Contracts "Shapes the web and the schemas read" give them (`ContainerAllowInput`, `ContainerDenyInput`, `ContainerRemoveInput`, `ContainerOp`, `ContainersApplyInput`), each embedding `core.Guarded` where the Contract does. Add `jsonschema` tags only: `ContainerOp.Op` carries `jsonschema:"enum=allow,enum=deny,enum=remove"`, and every field gets a `jsonschema_description`. `ContainerOp.Binding` stays a pointer with `omitempty` and `From` keeps `omitzero`, so a remove needs no binding and an allow needs no source; `ContainerDenyInput.From` has no `omitzero`, so the schema requires it. No `manual` field exists on any of them.
2. `containerChange(env core.Env, cfg fwstate.Config, st dockerState, ops []ContainerOp, batch bool) (change, error)`. `batch` says the field paths of a refusal are `/ops/<i>/…` (the zero-based index of the operation) instead of `/…`. Every refusal returns the zero `change`.
   1. When `st.cfg.Enabled && !st.available`: `errcode.New(errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration, ...)` with detail `container rules cannot change while the integration is on and Docker is unavailable: ` and `st.reason`.
   2. Work on a copy of `st.rows`, with `newID := newULID(env)`, and process the operations in order:
      - `allow` and `deny`: a nil `Binding` is `request.invalid_input` at `<path>/binding`. Build `dockerfw.ContainerRule{ID: newID(), Binding: *op.Binding, Kind: Allow or Deny, From: op.From}`. Run `Binding.Validate()` and return its error through `fieldErrors(err, <path>/binding)`; then run `rule.Validate(st.cfg.Settings)` and return its error through `fieldErrors(err, <path>)` (its pointers already start with `/binding`, `/kind` or `/from`). A rule equal to a row of the working copy in binding, kind and source is skipped without error. A deny for which the working copy holds no `Allow` row of the same binding is `request.invalid_input` at `<path>/binding`, message `a deny narrows an allowance, and this binding has none`. Otherwise the rule is appended to the copy and to `rowsAdd`.
      - `remove`: an empty `ID`, or one no row of the working copy has, is `request.invalid_input` at `<path>/id`, message `no container rule has this id`. Otherwise the row leaves the copy and its id joins `rowsDel`.
      - any other `Op`: `request.invalid_input` at `<path>/op`.
      Build these errors as `*errcode.Error{Code: errcode.InvalidInput, Detail: <message>, Fields: []errcode.FieldError{{Path: …, Message: <message>}}}`.
   3. `c := change{rowsAdd: …, rowsDel: …}`. With the integration off (`!st.cfg.Enabled`) the desired rules are nil and nothing is realized. With it on, set `st.rows` to the working copy and `st.realized` to `dockerfw.Realize(copy, st.facts, st.cfg.Settings)`, take `blockFiles(cfg, st, true)` and put into `c.files` only the paths whose bytes differ from `cfg.Files[path].Data` (a map stays nil when none differs); `c.reload` is true exactly when `c.files` is not empty; the desired rules are `st.realized.Rules`. Finally `c.ops` is `containerRuleOps(cfg, desired, newID)`; its error is returned. The result is the empty change when nothing differs, so a `containers.apply` with no operations re-realizes the stored rows and writes nothing when the host already holds the realization.
3. `containerRowsCheck(ctx, env, ops []ContainerOp) error` is the verify check. It reads `listContainerRules(ctx, env.DB)` (a read error is `firewall: verify: %w`) and compares the stored rows with the list: for each `remove` operation, a row with its id is still stored: `mismatch("container rule %s is still stored after the change", id)`; for each `allow` or `deny` operation after the last `remove` of the list (every one when the list has no remove), no stored row has its binding, kind and source: `mismatch("no %s rule of %s:%d/%s is stored after the change", op, selector, hostPort, proto)`. Operations before a later remove are skipped, because a later removal may take a row an earlier equal operation skipped or stored.
4. // dshSettings differ from the defaults, so a block rendered from them
```go
// shows where it came from; dshPrivateLine is the line Render writes into
// after.rules for them.
var (
	dshSettings    = dockerfw.Settings{PrivateSources: []netip.Prefix{netip.MustParsePrefix("198.51.100.0/24")}}
	dshInput       = dockerfw.BlockInput{Settings: dshSettings}
	dshFiles       = []string{"/etc/ufw/after.rules", "/etc/ufw/after6.rules"}
	dshPrivateLine = "-A DOCKER-USER -s 198.51.100.0/24 -j RETURN"

// dshHost is acHost with the integration flag set to flag, the settings
// of dshSettings and a Docker daemon that cannot be reached, so the block
// holds no binding.
func dshHost(t *testing.T, enabled, flag bool) (*fakeHost, fw) {
	t.Helper()
	h, f := acHost(t, enabled)
	d := newFakeDocker()
	d.err = dockerapi.ErrUnavailable
	f.d = fdDeps(h, d)
	err := h.db.Write(context.Background(), func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
		return writeDockerConfig(context.Background(), tx, dockerConfig{Enabled: flag, Settings: dshSettings})
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return h, f
}

// dshConfig reads the configuration of a host whose UFW is enabled or not
// and whose after files hold the block of dshInput or not.
func dshConfig(t *testing.T, enabled, block bool) fwstate.Config {
	t.Helper()
	h, _ := acHost(t, enabled)
	if block {
		for p, fam := range map[string]fwstate.Family{"/etc/ufw/after.rules": fwstate.V4, "/etc/ufw/after6.rules": fwstate.V6} {
			data, err := dockerfw.WithBlock(h.config().Files[p].Data, dockerfw.Render(dshInput, fam))
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			h.writeFile(p, data)
		}

}

// TestDshIntegrationChange: with the flag on, enabling a stopped UFW
// writes the block into both after files, and disabling an active UFW
// writes them without it and asks for the owned-chain cleanup; a change
// that leaves UFW as it is writes no file.
func TestDshIntegrationChange(t *testing.T) {
	st := dockerState{cfg: dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dshSettings}, realized: dockerfw.Realized{Block: dshInput}}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name                    string
		enable, ufwOn, hasBlock bool
		files                   []string
		block, cleanup          bool
	}{
		{"enable writes the block into both files", true, false, false, dshFiles, true, false},
		{"enable of an active UFW writes nothing", true, true, false, nil, false, false},
		{"disable removes the block and cleans up", false, true, true, dshFiles, false, true},
		{"disable cleans up although the files hold no block", false, true, false, nil, false, true},
		{"disable of a stopped UFW does nothing", false, false, false, nil, false, false},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := integrationChange(c.enable, dshConfig(t, c.ufwOn, c.hasBlock), st)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if got.enable == nil || *got.enable != c.enable {
				t.Errorf("enable = %v, want %v", got.enable, c.enable)
			}
			if keys := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(got.files)); !slices.Equal(keys, c.files) {
				t.Fatalf("files %q, want %q", keys, c.files)
			}
			for p, data := range got.files {
				_, ok, err := dockerfw.BlockOf(data)
				if err != nil || ok != c.block {
					t.Errorf("%s: block present %v (%v), want %v", p, ok, err, c.block)
				}
				if !strings.Contains(string(data), "# after") {
					t.Errorf("%s lost the file's own lines:\n%s", p, data)
				}
				if has := strings.Contains(string(data), dshPrivateLine); has != (c.block && p == "/etc/ufw/after.rules") {
					t.Errorf("%s holds the IPv4 private source line: %v", p, has)
				}
			}
			if got.cleanup != c.cleanup {
				t.Errorf("cleanup = %v, want %v", got.cleanup, c.cleanup)
			}
			if got.flag != nil || got.sources != nil || got.rowsAdd != nil || got.rowsDel != nil || got.reload {
				t.Errorf("change %+v touches the logical state or reloads", got)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDshEnableWritesBlock: firewall.state.enable with the flag on writes
// the block through the journal before it starts UFW; with the flag off
// it leaves the after files alone.
func TestDshEnableWritesBlock(t *testing.T) {
	h, f := dshHost(t, false, true)
	_, ran := acRun(t, h, f.stateEnable(), `{}`)
	if !slices.Equal(ran, []string{"--force enable"}) {
		t.Errorf("ufw ran %q, want the start only", ran)
	}
	start := slices.Index(h.calls, "run /usr/sbin/ufw --force enable")
	for _, p := range dshFiles {
		if i := slices.Index(h.calls, "restore "+p); i < 0 || start < 0 || i > start {
			t.Errorf("%s written at call %d, UFW started at call %d, want the write first", p, i, start)
		}
		if !slices.Contains(hkEffects(h), "firewall.file:"+p+" made") {
			t.Errorf("effects %v, want the write of %s journaled", hkEffects(h), p)
		}
		data := h.config().Files[p].Data
		if _, ok, err := dockerfw.BlockOf(data); err != nil || !ok {
			t.Errorf("%s holds no block (%v):\n%s", p, err, data)
		}
	}
	if !strings.Contains(string(h.config().Files[dshFiles[0]].Data), dshPrivateLine) {
		t.Error("the block does not carry the stored private sources")
	}

	h, f = dshHost(t, false, false)
	acRun(t, h, f.stateEnable(), `{}`)
	for _, c := range h.calls {
		if strings.HasPrefix(c, "restore ") {
			t.Errorf("flag off: %q, want no file written", c)
		}
	}
}

// TestDshRefusesOpenIncoming: with the flag on, enabling UFW and setting
// the default policies refuse a resulting incoming policy of ACCEPT
// (firewall.unsupported_integration), also when the policy is already
// ACCEPT and the request leaves it; disabling UFW and the flag off are not
// refused.
func TestDshRefusesOpenIncoming(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name          string
		enabled, flag bool
		input         string
		action        string
		raw           string
		refused       bool
	}{
		{"enable, flag on, incoming ACCEPT", false, true, "ACCEPT", "enable", `{}`, true},
		{"enable, flag off, incoming ACCEPT", false, false, "ACCEPT", "enable", `{}`, false},
		{"enable, flag on, incoming DROP", false, true, "DROP", "enable", `{}`, false},
		{"disable, flag on, incoming ACCEPT", true, true, "ACCEPT", "disable", `{}`, false},
		{"defaults to ACCEPT, flag on", true, true, "DROP", "defaults", `{"incoming":"ACCEPT"}`, true},
		{"defaults to ACCEPT, flag off", true, false, "DROP", "defaults", `{"incoming":"ACCEPT"}`, false},
		{"defaults to REJECT, flag on", true, true, "DROP", "defaults", `{"incoming":"REJECT"}`, false},
		{"defaults leave an ACCEPT incoming, flag on", true, true, "ACCEPT", "defaults", `{"outgoing":"DROP"}`, true},
		{"defaults replace an ACCEPT incoming, flag on", true, true, "ACCEPT", "defaults", `{"incoming":"DROP"}`, false},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, f := dshHost(t, c.enabled, c.flag)
			s := h.state()
			s.Input = c.input
			h.setState(s)
			def := f.stateEnable()
			switch c.action {
			case "disable":
				def = f.stateDisable()
			case "defaults":
				def = f.defaultsSet()
			}
			_, err := def.Handler.Plan(ctx, h.env(), json.RawMessage(c.raw))
			if !c.refused {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("plan = %v, want it planned", err)
				}
				return
			}
			if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration {
				t.Fatalf("plan = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration", err)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

All changes are in `internal/modules/firewall/actions_state.go`.

1. `stateAction` (shared by `stateEnable` and `stateDisable`): its `build` closure now returns `f.stateChange(ctx, env, enable, cfg, cur)` from the `buildFunc`, using the closure's `ctx` and `env`. Nothing else in `stateAction` changes, and neither does `StateInput`.
2. `func (f fw) stateChange(ctx, env, enable, cfg, cur) (change, error)`, with a doc comment: it reads `readDockerConfig(ctx, env.DB)`, returning its error unchanged.
   - Flag off: return `change{enable: &enable}`, exactly what wave 1 returned. It makes no other read, so wave 1's tests, whose `deps` have no Docker client, never reach the daemon.
   - Flag on and `enable`: first `refuseOpenIncoming(true, cfg)`, returned unchanged (the incoming policy is an invariant while the flag is on, spec 2.6); then `f.dockerState(ctx, env, cur)`, whose error is returned unchanged.
   - Flag on and not `enable`: use a zero `dockerState`. Removing the block needs no facts, and turning UFW off must not depend on the daemon answering. A comment says so.
   - Then return `integrationChange(enable, cfg, st)`.
3. `func integrationChange(enable bool, cfg fwstate.Config, st dockerState) (change, error)`, pure, with a doc comment. It returns a change whose `enable` points at `enable`. When `enable == cfg.Enabled` it stops there: starting an active UFW and stopping a stopped one change nothing, and rewriting the block of an active UFW is `firewall.docker.repair`'s job (a comment gives that reason). Otherwise it calls `blockFiles(cfg, st, enable)` (the files with the realized block when enabling, without it when disabling), returning its error unchanged, and puts into `files` only the paths whose bytes differ from `cfg.Files[path].Data`; `files` stays nil when none differs. It sets `cleanup` to `!enable`: stopping UFW with the flag on runs the owned-chain cleanup, which also writes the files without the block when they still hold one. It sets no other field: `flag`, `sources`, `rowsAdd`, `rowsDel` and `reload` stay zero, because `state.disable` leaves the flag set (spec 2.6) and neither action changes a row or a setting.
4. `defaultsSet`'s `build`: after the existing "set at least one default policy" refusal and before the loop that builds the ops, read `readDockerConfig(ctx, env.DB)` (its `buildFunc` and the closure already have `ctx` and `env`; the closure parameters that were `_` become named), copy `cfg` into `final` with `DefaultInput` replaced by `in.Incoming` when that is set, and return `refuseOpenIncoming(flag, final)`'s error unchanged. A request that leaves an incoming policy of ACCEPT in place is refused too while the flag is on, because the refusal is about the resulting policy; a request that replaces ACCEPT with DROP or REJECT passes.
5. Do not refuse `firewall.state.disable` for an incoming policy of ACCEPT: it is the way out. Do not touch `firewall.logging.set`.

```go
func TestDsrWithDockerRestore(t *testing.T) {
	a, b := dsrRule(dsrRuleA, "web"), dsrRule(dsrRuleB, "db")
	on := dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dsrCustom}

		{"turning it on restores flag, settings and rows", dockerRestoreSide{off, nil}, dockerRestoreSide{on, []dockerfw.ContainerRule{a, b}},
			&yes, &dsrCustom, []string{dsrRuleA, dsrRuleB}, nil, false},
		{"equal states change nothing", dockerRestoreSide{on, []dockerfw.ContainerRule{a}}, dockerRestoreSide{on, []dockerfw.ContainerRule{a}},

		{"settings alone", dockerRestoreSide{off, nil}, dockerRestoreSide{offCustom, nil},
			nil, &dsrCustom, nil, nil, false},
		{"rows alone with the integration off", dockerRestoreSide{off, []dockerfw.ContainerRule{a}}, dockerRestoreSide{off, nil},
			nil, nil, nil, []string{dsrRuleA}, false},
	} {

			snap := &snapshot{ID: "s1"}
			got := withDockerRestore(change{restore: snap, repair: true}, c.now, c.want)
			if got.restore != snap || !got.repair {
				t.Errorf("restore %p repair %v, want the change's own fields kept", got.restore, got.repair)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.flag, c.flag) {
				t.Errorf("flag %v, want %v", got.flag, c.flag)
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got.sources, c.sources) {
				t.Errorf("sources %v, want %v", got.sources, c.sources)
			}
			if !slices.Equal(dsrIDs(got.rowsAdd), c.add) || !slices.Equal(got.rowsDel, c.del) {
				t.Errorf("rows add %q delete %q, want add %q delete %q", dsrIDs(got.rowsAdd), got.rowsDel, c.add, c.del)
			}
			if got.cleanup != c.cleanup || got.files != nil || got.reload {
				t.Errorf("cleanup %v files %v reload %v, want cleanup %v and no files or reload", got.cleanup, got.files, got.reload, c.cleanup)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDsrReadSide: the stored flag, settings and rows, rows in id order.
func TestDsrReadSide(t *testing.T) {
	h, _ := dsrHost(t)
	got, err := readDockerRestoreSide(context.Background(), h.db)
	if err != nil || got.cfg.Enabled || !reflect.DeepEqual(got.cfg.Settings, dockerfw.DefaultSettings()) || len(got.rows) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a host without the integration reads %+v (%v), want it off with the defaults and no rows", got, err)
	}
	dsrSet(t, h, dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dsrCustom}, dsrRule(dsrRuleB, "db"), dsrRule(dsrRuleA, "web"))
	got, err = readDockerRestoreSide(context.Background(), h.db)
	if err != nil || !got.cfg.Enabled || !reflect.DeepEqual(got.cfg.Settings, dsrCustom) || !slices.Equal(dsrIDs(got.rows), []string{dsrRuleA, dsrRuleB}) {
		t.Errorf("read %+v (%v), want the stored state with the rows in id order", got, err)
	}
}

// TestDsrRestorePlan: restoring a snapshot taken without the integration
// on a host that has it on plans turning it off, removing its rows and
// removing its chains.
func TestDsrRestorePlan(t *testing.T) {
	h, f := dsrHost(t)
	id := snCapture(t, h, f)
	dsrSet(t, h, dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dsrCustom}, dsrRule(dsrRuleA, "web"))
	h.loaded.V4, h.loaded.V6 = fhParse(t, dsrLoaded), fhParse(t, dsrLoaded)
	plan, err := f.snapshotRestore().Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(), json.RawMessage(`{"id":"`+id+`"}`))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	diff := strings.Join(acDiff(plan), "\n")
	for _, want := range []string{"docker integration off", "web all:8080/tcp allow any", "Docker chains removed"} {
		if !strings.Contains(diff, want) {
			t.Errorf("diff\n%s\nwant a line with %q", diff, want)
		}
	}
}

// TestDsrRestoreAppliesState: restoring a snapshot taken with the
// integration on brings back its settings and rows through the journal and
// leaves the flag alone.
func TestDsrRestoreAppliesState(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := context.Background()
	h, f := dsrHost(t)
	dsrSet(t, h, dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dsrCustom}, dsrRule(dsrRuleA, "web"))
	id := snCapture(t, h, f)
	dsrSet(t, h, dockerConfig{Enabled: true, Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()}, dsrRule(dsrRuleA, "web"), dsrRule(dsrRuleB, "db"))

	_, ran := acRun(t, h, f.snapshotRestore(), `{"id":"`+id+`"}`)
	if !slices.Equal(ran, []string{"reload"}) {
		t.Errorf("ufw ran %q, want the reload", ran)
	}
	rows, err := listContainerRules(ctx, h.db)
	if err != nil || !slices.Equal(dsrIDs(rows), []string{dsrRuleA}) {
		t.Errorf("rows %q (%v), want only %s", dsrIDs(rows), err, dsrRuleA)
	}
	cfg, err := readDockerConfig(ctx, h.db)
	if err != nil || !cfg.Enabled || !reflect.DeepEqual(cfg.Settings, dsrCustom) {
		t.Errorf("config %+v (%v), want the integration on with the snapshot's settings", cfg, err)
	}
	effects := hkEffects(h)
	for _, want := range []string{"firewall.container:" + dsrRuleB + " made", "firewall.setting:sources made"} {
		if !slices.Contains(effects, want) {
			t.Errorf("effects %q, want %q", effects, want)
		}
	}
	if slices.Contains(effects, "firewall.setting:docker made") {
		t.Errorf("effects %q, want the flag left alone", effects)
	}
}

// TestDsrRestoreRefusesOpenIncoming: a restore whose configured incoming
// policy is ACCEPT is refused when the integration is on afterwards, which
// is the snapshot's flag, and not when it is off afterwards.
func TestDsrRestoreRefusesOpenIncoming(t *testing.T) {
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name              string
		snapFlag, nowFlag bool
		refused           bool
	}{
		{"snapshot with the integration on", true, true, true},
		{"snapshot with the integration off", false, false, false},
		{"integration on now, off in the snapshot", false, true, false},
	} {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			h, f := dsrHost(t)
			s := h.state()
			s.Input = "ACCEPT"
			h.setState(s)
			dsrSet(t, h, dockerConfig{Enabled: c.snapFlag, Settings: dsrCustom})
			id := snCapture(t, h, f)
			s.Input = "DROP"
			h.setState(s)
			dsrSet(t, h, dockerConfig{Enabled: c.nowFlag, Settings: dsrCustom})
			_, err := f.snapshotRestore().Handler.Plan(context.Background(), h.env(), json.RawMessage(`{"id":"`+id+`"}`))
			if !c.refused {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("plan = %v, want it planned", err)
				}
				return
			}
			if e := errcode.From(err); e.Code != errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration {
				t.Fatalf("plan = %v, want firewall.unsupported_integration", err)
			}
		})
	}
}
```

1. Create `docker_restore_change.go` (a doc comment on each declaration; imports `internal/core`, `internal/core/store`, `internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw`):
   - `dockerRestoreSide` is the Docker integration's logical state on one side of a restore: `cfg dockerConfig` then `rows []dockerfw.ContainerRule`, in that order.
   - `readDockerRestoreSide(ctx, db)` reads `readDockerConfig` and `listContainerRules` and returns them as a side; an error is returned as `firewall: read the Docker state: %w`.
   - `snapshotDockerSide(s)` is the state a snapshot records: `Enabled` from `s.State.Docker`, `Settings` from `*s.State.DockerSettings`, or `dockerfw.DefaultSettings()` when that pointer is nil, and `rows` from `s.State.ContainerRules`. Read these three fields of `snapshotState` directly; they are Task 28's, and Task 30 reads them the same way.
   - `withDockerRestore(c, now, want)` returns `c` with its Docker fields set for a restore from `now` to `want`, and every other field of `c` (`restore`, `repair`, `ops`, ...) as it was: `flag` points at `want.cfg.Enabled` when it differs from `now.cfg.Enabled`; `sources` points at a copy of `want.cfg.Settings` when `PrivateSources` or `ForwardExemptions` differ (compare each with `slices.Equal`; both element types are comparable, so a nil list and an empty one are equal); `rowsAdd` holds, in `want.rows` order, the rows of `want` whose id `now` lacks; `rowsDel` holds, in `now.rows` order, the ids of the rows of `now` that `want` lacks (rows are told apart by id alone: a row is never edited); `cleanup` is true exactly when `now.cfg.Enabled` is true and `want.cfg.Enabled` is false. It sets neither `files` nor `reload`: the snapshot's own files already carry or lack the block, and a restore of an active UFW reloads anyway. A comment gives the reason for the cleanup condition: with the flag off no integration chain is loaded, and a cleanup would refuse a host whose `DOCKER-USER` holds the operator's own rules.
   - `(f fw) dockerRestoreChange(ctx, env, c, s)`: `want := snapshotDockerSide(s)`; `final, err := f.snapshotConfig(s)`; `refuseOpenIncoming(want.cfg.Enabled, final)` (the invariant is about the integration after the restore, which is the snapshot's flag); `now, err := readDockerRestoreSide(ctx, env.DB)`; return `withDockerRestore(c, now, want)`. Errors are returned unchanged.
2. `actions_snapshot.go`, `snapshotRestore`'s `build`: after `loadSnapshot`, return `f.dockerRestoreChange(ctx, env, change{restore: &s}, s)` in place of `change{restore: &s}, nil`. The `check`, `keep` and the input do not change.

```go
package firewall

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"maps"
	"net/netip"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/netfilter"
)

const (
	dreAfter4 = "/etc/ufw/after.rules"
	dreAfter6 = "/etc/ufw/after6.rules"
	dreAllow1 = "01J00000000000000000000001"
)

func dreAddr(s string) netip.Addr     { return netip.MustParseAddr(s) }
func drePrefix(s string) netip.Prefix { return netip.MustParsePrefix(s) }

// dreFacts is one running container, web, that publishes host port 8080 to
// its port 80 on the default bridge.
func dreFacts() dockerfw.Facts {
	return dockerfw.Facts{
		Containers: []dockerfw.Container{{
			ID: "id-web", Name: "web",
			Ports:     []dockerfw.Published{{HostAddr: dreAddr("0.0.0.0"), HostPort: 8080, ContainerPort: 80, Proto: "tcp"}},
			Endpoints: []dockerfw.Endpoint{{Network: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0", Addr4: dreAddr("172.17.0.2")}},
		}},
		Networks: []dockerfw.Network{{
			ID: "id-bridge", Name: "bridge", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0",
			Subnets: []netip.Prefix{drePrefix("172.17.0.0/16")},
		}},
	}
}

// dreRows is an allowance of web's binding 8080/tcp.
func dreRows() []dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	b := dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}
	return []dockerfw.ContainerRule{{ID: dreAllow1, Binding: b, Kind: dockerfw.Allow}}
}

// dreState is the Docker state of a supported daemon whose integration flag
// is enabled, holding rows and settings s, realized against dreFacts.
func dreState(enabled bool, rows []dockerfw.ContainerRule, s dockerfw.Settings) dockerState {
	facts := dreFacts()
	return dockerState{
		available: true,
		det:       dockerfw.Detection{Version: "29.9.1", Driver: "iptables", DockerVariant: "nft", UFWVariant: "nft", RawProtection: true},
		facts:     facts,
		cfg:       dockerConfig{Enabled: enabled, Settings: s},
		rows:      rows,
		realized:  dockerfw.Realize(rows, facts, s),
	}
}

// dreIDs mints distinct rule ids.
func dreIDs() func() string {
	n := 0
	return func() string {
		n++
		return fmt.Sprintf("01J%023d", n)
	}
}

// dreRefused fails the test unless err is an *errcode.Error with code.
func dreRefused(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code) *errcode.Error {
	t.Helper()
	var e *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &e) || e.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want code %s", err, code)
	}
	return e
}

// dreHost is a fake host whose Docker daemon cannot be reached and whose
// ufw reloads, with the firewall over it.
func dreHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, fw) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	d := newFakeDocker()
	d.err = fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	f, _ := newFW(h)
	f.d = fdDeps(h, d)
	return h, f
}

// TestDreRepairChange: the repair rewrites the block into both files,
// realizes the stored rows and reloads, as a repair of UFW's loaded state;
// only discardForeign together with manual lets it discard foreign rules.
func TestDreRepairChange(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := newFakeHost(t).config()
	settings := dockerfw.DefaultSettings()
	supported := dreState(true, nil, settings)
	withRows := dreState(true, dreRows(), settings)
	off := dreState(false, nil, settings)
	gone := supported
	gone.available, gone.reason = false, "the Docker daemon is not running"
	nftables := supported
	nftables.det.Driver = "nftables"

	refusals := []struct {
		name string
		in   DockerRepairInput
		st   dockerState
		code errcode.Code
		want string
	}{
		{"discard without manual", DockerRepairInput{DiscardForeign: true}, supported, errcode.FirewallManualRequired, "manual: true"},
		{"integration off", DockerRepairInput{}, off, errcode.InvalidInput, "off"},
		{"daemon unavailable", DockerRepairInput{}, gone, errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration, "not running"},
		{"unsupported driver", DockerRepairInput{}, nftables, errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration, ""},
	}
	for _, tc := range refusals {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, err := dockerRepairChange(cfg, tc.in, tc.st, dreIDs())
			if e := dreRefused(t, err, tc.code); !strings.Contains(e.Detail, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("detail %q, want it to contain %q", e.Detail, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}

	t.Run("rewrites the block and reloads", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := dockerRepairChange(cfg, DockerRepairInput{}, supported, dreIDs())
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if !c.repair || !c.reload || c.discardForeign || c.flag != nil || c.sources != nil || len(c.ops) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, want a repair that reloads and changes no flag, setting, rule or foreign rule", c)
		}
		for _, p := range []string{dreAfter4, dreAfter6} {
			if _, ok, err := dockerfw.BlockOf(c.files[p]); err != nil || !ok {
				t.Errorf("%s holds no marked block (ok %v, err %v)", p, ok, err)
			}
		}
	})
	t.Run("realizes the stored rows", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := dockerRepairChange(cfg, DockerRepairInput{}, withRows, dreIDs())
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if len(c.ops) != 1 || c.ops[0].Kind != core.EffectCreate {
			t.Errorf("ops %+v, want the one route allow for web's address", c.ops)
		}
		if want := ":" + dreRows()[0].Binding.Chain() + " - [0:0]"; !strings.Contains(string(c.files[dreAfter4]), want) {
			t.Errorf("after.rules lacks the binding chain declaration %q", want)
		}
	})
	t.Run("manual alone discards nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := dockerRepairChange(cfg, DockerRepairInput{Manual: true}, supported, dreIDs())
		if err != nil || c.discardForeign {
			t.Errorf("discardForeign %v, err %v; want false, nil", c.discardForeign, err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("discard with manual", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := dockerRepairChange(cfg, DockerRepairInput{DiscardForeign: true, Manual: true}, supported, dreIDs())
		if err != nil || !c.discardForeign || !c.repair {
			t.Errorf("discardForeign %v repair %v, err %v; want true, true, nil", c.discardForeign, c.repair, err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("an open incoming policy is not refused", func(t *testing.T) {
		open := cfg
		open.DefaultInput = "ACCEPT"
		if _, err := dockerRepairChange(open, DockerRepairInput{}, supported, dreIDs()); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("repair refused an ACCEPT incoming policy, which it cannot change: %v", err)
		}
	})
}

// TestDreRepairDiscards: a repair that discards foreign rules lists each one
// in the plan, the rules DOCKER-USER holds beyond the block's own, per
// family and in chain order; any other repair lists none.
func TestDreRepairDiscards(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := newFakeHost(t).config()
	block := dockerfw.Render(dockerfw.BlockInput{Settings: dockerfw.DefaultSettings()}, fwstate.V4)
	spliced, err := dockerfw.WithBlock(cfg.Files[dreAfter4].Data, block)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	withBlock := cfg
	withBlock.Files = maps.Clone(cfg.Files)
	e := withBlock.Files[dreAfter4]
	e.Data = spliced
	withBlock.Files[dreAfter4] = e

	loaded := func(text string) fwstate.Loaded {
		rs, err := netfilter.ParseRestore(strings.NewReader(text))
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return fwstate.Loaded{Variant: "nft", V4: rs}
	}
	blockPlus := func(foreign ...string) fwstate.Loaded {
		extra := ""
		for _, l := range foreign {
			extra += l + "\n"
		}
		return loaded(strings.Replace(string(block), "COMMIT\n", extra+"COMMIT\n", 1))
	}
	const drop1, drop2 = "-A DOCKER-USER -s 203.0.113.0/24 -j DROP", "-A DOCKER-USER -i eth9 -j ACCEPT"
	line := func(text string) core.DiffLine {
		return core.DiffLine{Op: "-", Text: "foreign DOCKER-USER rule (v4): " + text}
	}
	both := DockerRepairInput{DiscardForeign: true, Manual: true}

	cases := []struct {
		name string
		in   DockerRepairInput
		cfg  fwstate.Config
		cur  fwstate.Loaded
		want []core.DiffLine
	}{
		{"one rule beside the block", both, withBlock, blockPlus(drop1), []core.DiffLine{line(drop1)}},
		{"two rules in chain order", both, withBlock, blockPlus(drop1, drop2), []core.DiffLine{line(drop1), line(drop2)}},
		{"only the block", both, withBlock, blockPlus(), nil},
		{"no block in the file: every rule but Docker's RETURN", both, cfg,
			loaded("*filter\n:DOCKER-USER - [0:0]\n-A DOCKER-USER -j RETURN\n" + drop1 + "\nCOMMIT\n"),
			[]core.DiffLine{line(drop1)}},
		{"a repair without discardForeign lists none", DockerRepairInput{Manual: true}, withBlock, blockPlus(drop1), nil},
		{"discardForeign without manual lists none", DockerRepairInput{DiscardForeign: true}, withBlock, blockPlus(drop1), nil},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			got, err := repairDiscards(tc.in, tc.cfg, tc.cur)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if !slices.Equal(got, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("lines %v, want %v", got, tc.want)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDreRepairOffRefusedByPlan: planning the repair while the integration is
// off is refused before anything is computed.
func TestDreRepairOffRefusedByPlan(t *testing.T) {
	h, f := dreHost(t)
	_, err := f.dockerRepair().Handler.Plan(t.Context(), h.env(), json.RawMessage(`{}`))
	dreRefused(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput)
}

// TestDreActionSpec: the action is a revertible agent action under the
// firewall lock, repaired by firewall.state.repair, and its input schema
// takes the documented fields only.
func TestDreActionSpec(t *testing.T) {
	def := fw{}.dockerRepair()
	s := def.Spec
	if s.Name != "firewall.docker.repair" || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != core.ClassRevertible || s.Side != core.SideAgent ||
		!slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, []string{"firewall"}) || s.RepairedBy != "firewall.state.repair" {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v, want a version 1 revertible agent action under the firewall lock repaired by firewall.state.repair", s)
	}
	v := schema.NewValidator()
	for _, raw := range []string{`{}`, `{"discardForeign":true,"manual":true}`} {
		if err := v.ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("input %s refused: %v", raw, err)
		}
	}
	for _, raw := range []string{`{"discardForeign":"yes"}`, `{"discard":true}`} {
		if err := v.ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("input %s accepted", raw)
		}
	}
}
```

```go
package firewall

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/netip"
	"slices"
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/errcode"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/core/schema"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/dockerfw"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/modules/firewall/fwstate"
	"github.com/darkraise/darkpanel/internal/platform/dockerapi"
)

const (
	dsoAfter4 = "/etc/ufw/after.rules"
	dsoAfter6 = "/etc/ufw/after6.rules"
	dsoAllow1 = "01J00000000000000000000001"
	dsoDeny2  = "01J00000000000000000000002"
)

func dsoAddr(s string) netip.Addr     { return netip.MustParseAddr(s) }
func dsoPrefix(s string) netip.Prefix { return netip.MustParsePrefix(s) }

// dsoFacts is one running container, web, that publishes host port 8080 to
// its port 80 on the default bridge.
func dsoFacts() dockerfw.Facts {
	return dockerfw.Facts{
		Containers: []dockerfw.Container{{
			ID: "id-web", Name: "web",
			Ports:     []dockerfw.Published{{HostAddr: dsoAddr("0.0.0.0"), HostPort: 8080, ContainerPort: 80, Proto: "tcp"}},
			Endpoints: []dockerfw.Endpoint{{Network: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0", Addr4: dsoAddr("172.17.0.2")}},
		}},
		Networks: []dockerfw.Network{{
			ID: "id-bridge", Name: "bridge", Driver: "bridge", Bridge: "docker0",
			Subnets: []netip.Prefix{dsoPrefix("172.17.0.0/16")},
		}},
	}
}

// dsoRows is an allowance of web's binding 8080/tcp and, when deny is set,
// a deny of 203.0.113.0/24 on it.
func dsoRows(deny bool) []dockerfw.ContainerRule {
	b := dockerfw.Binding{Selector: "web", HostPort: 8080, Proto: "tcp"}
	rows := []dockerfw.ContainerRule{{ID: dsoAllow1, Binding: b, Kind: dockerfw.Allow}}
	if deny {
		rows = append(rows, dockerfw.ContainerRule{ID: dsoDeny2, Binding: b, Kind: dockerfw.Deny, From: dsoPrefix("203.0.113.0/24")})
	}
	return rows
}

// dsoState is the Docker state of a supported daemon whose integration flag
// is enabled, holding rows and settings s, realized against dsoFacts.
func dsoState(enabled bool, rows []dockerfw.ContainerRule, s dockerfw.Settings) dockerState {
	facts := dsoFacts()
	return dockerState{
		available: true,
		det:       dockerfw.Detection{Version: "29.9.1", Driver: "iptables", DockerVariant: "nft", UFWVariant: "nft", RawProtection: true},
		facts:     facts,
		cfg:       dockerConfig{Enabled: enabled, Settings: s},
		rows:      rows,
		realized:  dockerfw.Realize(rows, facts, s),
	}
}

// dsoIDs mints distinct rule ids.
func dsoIDs() func() string {
	n := 0
	return func() string {
		n++
		return fmt.Sprintf("01J%023d", n)
	}
}

// dsoRefused fails the test unless err is an *errcode.Error with code.
func dsoRefused(t *testing.T, err error, code errcode.Code) *errcode.Error {
	t.Helper()
	var e *errcode.Error
	if !errors.As(err, &e) || e.Code != code {
		t.Fatalf("error %v, want code %s", err, code)
	}
	return e
}

// dsoEmpty reports whether c asks for nothing.
func dsoEmpty(c change) bool {
	return c.sources == nil && c.flag == nil && c.files == nil && !c.reload && !c.cleanup && !c.repair && !c.discardForeign &&
		len(c.ops) == 0 && len(c.rowsAdd) == 0 && len(c.rowsDel) == 0
}

// dsoHost is a fake host whose Docker daemon cannot be reached and whose
// ufw reloads, with the firewall over it.
func dsoHost(t *testing.T) (*fakeHost, fw) {
	t.Helper()
	h := newFakeHost(t)
	d := newFakeDocker()
	d.err = fmt.Errorf("dockerapi: %w", dockerapi.ErrUnavailable)
	h.ufw["reload"] = func(*fhState) int { return 0 }
	f, _ := newFW(h)
	f.d = fdDeps(h, d)
	return h, f
}

func dsoSources(ranges ...string) *[]netip.Prefix {
	out := make([]netip.Prefix, len(ranges))
	for i, r := range ranges {
		out[i] = dsoPrefix(r)
	}
	return &out
}

func dsoExemptions(e ...dockerfw.Exemption) *[]dockerfw.Exemption { return &e }

// dsoForward is a foreign port forward: connections to 192.0.2.10:8443 that
// the host's own rule sends to dest:443.
func dsoForward(dest string) dockerfw.Exemption {
	return dockerfw.Exemption{OrigDestination: dsoAddr("192.0.2.10"), OrigPort: 8443, Destination: dsoAddr(dest), Proto: "tcp", Port: 443}
}

// TestDsoSourcesChange: the new lists are validated against the settings'
// rules, the Docker networks and the stored container rules; with the
// integration off they are only stored, and with it on the block is
// rewritten and UFW reloaded.
func TestDsoSourcesChange(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := newFakeHost(t).config()
	settings := dockerfw.DefaultSettings()
	off := dsoState(false, nil, settings)
	on := dsoState(true, nil, settings)
	denied := dsoState(false, dsoRows(true), settings)
	gone := on
	gone.available, gone.reason = false, "the Docker daemon is not running"
	nftables := on
	nftables.det.Driver = "nftables"
	open := cfg
	open.DefaultInput = "ACCEPT"
	extra := append(slices.Clone(settings.PrivateSources), dsoPrefix("203.0.113.0/24"))
	var tooMany []string
	for i := range 33 {
		tooMany = append(tooMany, fmt.Sprintf("10.%d.0.0/16", i))
	}

	refusals := []struct {
		name string
		cfg  fwstate.Config
		in   DockerSourcesInput
		st   dockerState
		code errcode.Code
		path string
		want string
	}{
		{"no list", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{}, off, errcode.InvalidInput, "/privateSources", ""},
		{"a range shorter than /8", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: dsoSources("0.0.0.0/0")}, off, errcode.InvalidInput, "/privateSources/0", ""},
		{"a range that is not masked", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: dsoSources("10.1.2.3/8")}, off, errcode.InvalidInput, "/privateSources/0", ""},
		{"more than 32 ranges", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: dsoSources(tooMany...)}, off, errcode.InvalidInput, "", ""},
		{"an exemption with an unknown protocol", cfg,
			DockerSourcesInput{ForwardExemptions: dsoExemptions(dockerfw.Exemption{OrigDestination: dsoAddr("192.0.2.10"), Destination: dsoAddr("10.9.0.5"), Proto: "icmp"})},
			off, errcode.InvalidInput, "/forwardExemptions/0/proto", ""},
		{"an exemption into a Docker network", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{ForwardExemptions: dsoExemptions(dsoForward("172.17.0.2"))},
			off, errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration, "", "bridge"},
		{"a deny that a new range would shadow", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &extra},
			denied, errcode.InvalidInput, "/privateSources", dsoDeny2},
		{"integration on with an open incoming policy", open, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &extra},
			on, errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration, "", ""},
		{"integration on without a daemon", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &extra},
			gone, errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration, "", "not running"},
		{"integration on with an unsupported driver", cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &extra},
			nftables, errcode.FirewallUnsupportedIntegration, "", ""},
	}
	for _, tc := range refusals {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			_, err := dockerSourcesChange(tc.cfg, tc.in, tc.st, dsoIDs())
			e := dsoRefused(t, err, tc.code)
			if !strings.Contains(e.Detail, tc.want) {
				t.Errorf("detail %q, want it to contain %q", e.Detail, tc.want)
			}
			if tc.path != "" && (len(e.Fields) == 0 || e.Fields[0].Path != tc.path) {
				t.Errorf("fields %+v, want the first at %s", e.Fields, tc.path)
			}
		})
	}

	t.Run("the stored lists change nothing", func(t *testing.T) {
		same := settings.PrivateSources
		c, err := dockerSourcesChange(cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &same, ForwardExemptions: dsoExemptions()}, on, dsoIDs())
		if err != nil || !dsoEmpty(c) {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, err %v; want an empty change", c, err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("integration off: stored, nothing written", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := dockerSourcesChange(cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &extra}, off, dsoIDs())
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if c.sources == nil || !slices.Equal(c.sources.PrivateSources, extra) || len(c.sources.ForwardExemptions) != 0 {
			t.Errorf("sources %+v, want the new ranges and no exemptions", c.sources)
		}
		if c.files != nil || c.reload || len(c.ops) != 0 || c.flag != nil || c.repair {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, want only the stored settings", c)
		}
	})
	t.Run("integration off: a missing daemon and an open policy do not matter", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := off
		st.available = false
		if _, err := dockerSourcesChange(open, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &extra}, st, dsoIDs()); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("refused: %v", err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("one list keeps the other", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := dsoState(false, nil, dockerfw.Settings{PrivateSources: extra})
		c, err := dockerSourcesChange(cfg, DockerSourcesInput{ForwardExemptions: dsoExemptions(dsoForward("10.9.0.5"))}, st, dsoIDs())
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if c.sources == nil || !slices.Equal(c.sources.PrivateSources, extra) || len(c.sources.ForwardExemptions) != 1 {
			t.Errorf("sources %+v, want the stored ranges and the one new exemption", c.sources)
		}
	})
	t.Run("integration on: the block is rewritten and UFW reloaded", func(t *testing.T) {
		c, err := dockerSourcesChange(cfg, DockerSourcesInput{
			PrivateSources: &extra, ForwardExemptions: dsoExemptions(dsoForward("10.9.0.5")),
		}, on, dsoIDs())
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if c.sources == nil || !slices.Equal(c.sources.PrivateSources, extra) || !c.reload || c.flag != nil || c.repair {
			t.Errorf("change %+v, want the new settings and a reload", c)
		}
		after4, after6 := string(c.files[dsoAfter4]), string(c.files[dsoAfter6])
		for _, want := range []string{
			"-A DOCKER-USER -s 203.0.113.0/24 -j RETURN",
			"-A DOCKER-USER -m conntrack --ctstate DNAT --ctorigdst 192.0.2.10 --ctorigdstport 8443 -p tcp -d 10.9.0.5 --dport 443 -j RETURN",
		} {
			if !strings.Contains(after4, want) {
				t.Errorf("after.rules lacks %q", want)
			}
		}
		if strings.Contains(after6, "203.0.113.0/24") || strings.Contains(after6, "10.9.0.5") {
			t.Errorf("after6.rules holds IPv4 entries:\n%s", after6)
		}
		if _, ok, err := dockerfw.BlockOf(c.files[dsoAfter6]); err != nil || !ok {
			t.Errorf("after6.rules holds no marked block (ok %v, err %v)", ok, err)
		}
	})
	t.Run("integration on: the stored rows are realized with it", func(t *testing.T) {
		st := dsoState(true, dsoRows(false), settings)
		c, err := dockerSourcesChange(cfg, DockerSourcesInput{PrivateSources: &extra}, st, dsoIDs())
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if len(c.ops) != 1 || c.ops[0].Kind != core.EffectCreate {
			t.Errorf("ops %+v, want the one route allow for web's address", c.ops)
		}
	})
}

// TestDsoSourcesSetApplied: with the integration off the action runs
// through the engine's steps, stores the lists as one journaled setting
// effect and runs no ufw command; the same input again changes nothing.
func TestDsoSourcesSetApplied(t *testing.T) {
	h, f := dsoHost(t)
	def := f.dockerSourcesSet()
	out, ran := acRun(t, h, def, `{"privateSources":["10.0.0.0/8","203.0.113.0/24"]}`)
	if len(ran) != 0 {
		t.Errorf("ufw ran %q, want nothing while the integration is off", ran)
	}
	if !slices.ContainsFunc(out.Diff, func(l core.DiffLine) bool { return strings.HasPrefix(l.Text, "private sources:") }) {
		t.Errorf("plan lines %q, want one that starts with \"private sources:\"", acDiff(out))
	}
	got, err := readDockerConfig(t.Context(), h.db)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if want := []netip.Prefix{dsoPrefix("10.0.0.0/8"), dsoPrefix("203.0.113.0/24")}; !slices.Equal(got.Settings.PrivateSources, want) ||
		len(got.Settings.ForwardExemptions) != 0 || got.Enabled {
		t.Errorf("stored config %+v, want the two ranges, no exemptions and the flag off", got)
	}
	var made []string
	for _, e := range h.journal.effects {
		if e.State == core.EffectMade {
			made = append(made, e.Resource)
		}
	}
	if want := []string{"firewall.setting:sources"}; !slices.Equal(made, want) {
		t.Errorf("effects made %q, want %q", made, want)
	}

	again, _ := acRun(t, h, def, `{"privateSources":["10.0.0.0/8","203.0.113.0/24"]}`)
	if len(again.Diff) != 0 || len(h.journal.effects) != len(made) {
		t.Errorf("the same lists again: plan %q, %d effects; want no plan line and no new effect", acDiff(again), len(h.journal.effects))
	}
}

// TestDsoSourcesSetPlanRefused: an input that names neither list is refused
// when planned.
func TestDsoSourcesSetPlanRefused(t *testing.T) {
	h, f := dsoHost(t)
	_, err := f.dockerSourcesSet().Handler.Plan(t.Context(), h.env(), []byte(`{}`))
	e := dsoRefused(t, err, errcode.InvalidInput)
	if len(e.Fields) == 0 || e.Fields[0].Path != "/privateSources" {
		t.Errorf("fields %+v, want the first at /privateSources", e.Fields)
	}
}

// TestDsoActionSpec: the action is a revertible agent action under the
// firewall lock, repaired by firewall.state.repair, and its input schema
// takes the documented fields only.
func TestDsoActionSpec(t *testing.T) {
	def := fw{}.dockerSourcesSet()
	s := def.Spec
	if s.Name != "firewall.docker.set-sources" || s.Version != 1 || s.Class != core.ClassRevertible || s.Side != core.SideAgent ||
		!slices.Equal(s.LockKeys, []string{"firewall"}) || s.RepairedBy != "firewall.state.repair" {
		t.Errorf("spec %+v, want a version 1 revertible agent action under the firewall lock repaired by firewall.state.repair", s)
	}
	v := schema.NewValidator()
	for _, raw := range []string{
		`{"privateSources":["10.0.0.0/8","fc00::/7"]}`, `{"privateSources":[]}`,
		`{"forwardExemptions":[{"origDestination":"192.0.2.10","destination":"10.9.0.5","proto":"tcp","port":80}]}`,
	} {
		if err := v.ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(raw)); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("input %s refused: %v", raw, err)
		}
	}
	for _, raw := range []string{
		`{"privateSources":"10.0.0.0/8"}`, `{"privateSources":["not-a-prefix"]}`,
		`{"forwardExemptions":[{"origDestination":"192.0.2.10"}]}`,
	} {
		if err := v.ValidateInput(def, json.RawMessage(raw)); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("input %s accepted", raw)
		}
	}
}
```
