- [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

The scenarios run only in `.github/workflows/harness.yml` (gate 7); on a developer machine they are checked by `go vet` and `golangci-lint` and by the unit tests above. Everything below is in package `harness` under the build tag `harness`, with doc comments on every declaration as the neighbouring `m3_firewall_*` files have. The Docker host of every scenario is the fleet's agent VM (`f.agent`, host id `f.agentID`); the scanner is `f.scanner`. Error strings are lower case like the `m3x` helpers'.

**A. The mirror types** (`m3_docker_lifecycle_test.go`). They mirror the JSON of Contracts "Shapes the web and the schemas read" with plain strings in place of `netip` types, so the harness stays a black-box API client, and they carry exactly these JSON names (`TestM3xDockStatusJSON` pins them):

| Type | Fields (Go name: JSON name) |
|---|---|
| `m3dDockExemption` (comparable) | `InInterface: inInterface,omitempty` (string), `OrigDestination: origDestination` (string), `OrigPort: origPort,omitempty` (uint16), `Destination: destination` (string), `Proto: proto` (string), `Port: port,omitempty` (uint16) |
| `m3dDockIssue` | `Level: level`, `Reason: reason` |
| `m3dDockNetwork` | `Name: name`, `ID: id`, `Bridge: bridge`, `Subnets: subnets` ([]string), `Protected: protected` (bool), `Reason: reason,omitempty` |
| `m3dDockBinding` | `Selector: selector`, `HostAddr: hostAddr,omitempty` (string), `HostPort: hostPort` (uint16), `Proto: proto` |
| `m3dDockRule` | `ID: id`, `Binding: binding` (`m3dDockBinding`), `Kind: kind`, `From: from,omitempty` (string) |
| `m3dDockBindingView` | `Binding: binding`, `ID: id`, `Containers: containers` ([]string), `ContainerPort: containerPort` (uint16), `Allowed: allowed`, `Denied: denied`, `Proxied: proxied,omitempty`, `PrivateReach: privateReach,omitempty` (all []string) |
| `m3dDockStatus` | `Available: available`, `Reason: reason,omitempty`, `Version: version,omitempty`, `Driver: driver,omitempty`, `DockerVariant: dockerVariant,omitempty`, `UFWVariant: ufwVariant,omitempty`, `RawProtection: rawProtection`, `Supported: supported`, `Unsupported: unsupported,omitempty` ([]string), `Enabled: enabled`, `Health: health`, `Issues: issues,omitempty` ([]m3dDockIssue), `ForeignRules: foreignRules,omitempty` ([]string), `ForeignForwards: foreignForwards,omitempty` ([]m3dDockExemption), `ManualRoutes: manualRoutes,omitempty` ([]string), `Networks: networks` ([]m3dDockNetwork), `Settings: settings` (an anonymous struct with `PrivateSources: privateSources` []string and `ForwardExemptions: forwardExemptions` []m3dDockExemption), `Rules: rules` ([]m3dDockRule), `Bindings: bindings` ([]m3dDockBindingView) |

**B. The pure helpers** (`m3_docker_lifecycle_test.go`), each exactly as the unit tests above require:

1. `m3dxDockDetected(st m3dDockStatus) error` accepts the status of a host where Docker is installed and the integration has never been enabled. It returns an error, in this order of checks, when: `Available` is false (the text contains `unavailable: ` and `Reason`); `Supported` is false (the text contains every entry of `Unsupported`); the integer before the first dot of `Version` is under 28 (the text contains `Version`); `Driver` is not `iptables` (names the driver); `RawProtection` is false (the text contains `raw`); `DockerVariant` is empty, `both`, or differs from `UFWVariant` (the text names both variants and contains the word `variant`); `Enabled` is true or `Health` is not `off` (the text contains `enabled`); no network is named `bridge` with `Bridge` `docker0` (the text contains `bridge`).
2. `m3dxDockHealth(want string) func(m3dDockStatus) error` returns a check that accepts a status with `Enabled` true and `Health` equal to `want`; the error names the health and prints `Issues` with `%+v`.
3. `m3dxDockChains(save string) []string` returns, in order, the names of the chains an `iptables-save` text declares (lines `:<name> <policy> [<counters>]`) whose name starts with `darkpanel-` or `dp-b-`.
4. `m3dxDockRulesOf(save, chain string) []string` returns the text after `-A <chain> ` of every rule line of exactly that chain, in order (a chain whose name is a prefix of another's must not collect the other's rules: match the prefix `-A <chain> ` with its trailing space).
5. `m3dxDockCleaned(save string, foreign []string, wantReturn bool) error` is what the cleanup leaves: it fails when `m3dxDockChains` is not empty (naming the chains), when the `DOCKER-USER` rules other than `-j RETURN` are not equal to `foreign` (naming both lists), when `DOCKER-USER` holds more than one `-j RETURN`, and, only when `wantReturn` is true, when it does not hold exactly one (the text contains `-j RETURN`).
6. `m3dxDockBlockLoaded(save string) error` accepts a save with the chains `darkpanel-docker-bindings` and `darkpanel-docker-deny` declared (the error names the missing chain), a `DOCKER-USER` rule whose tokens include `DNAT` and whose text ends `-j darkpanel-docker-bindings` (the error contains `DNAT`), and a `darkpanel-docker-deny` chain whose last rule is `-j DROP` (the error contains `DROP`).
7. `m3dxDockExemptionLine(save string, e m3dDockExemption) error` accepts a save whose `DOCKER-USER` holds a rule that ends ` -j RETURN`, has `--ctstate DNAT` and has, as the token after each option, `--ctorigdst` equal to `e.OrigDestination`, `--ctorigdstport` equal to `e.OrigPort` (absent when 0), `-d` equal to `e.Destination`, `-p` equal to `e.Proto`, `--dport` equal to `e.Port` (absent when 0) and `-i` equal to `e.InInterface` (absent when empty). A trailing `/32` or `/128` on the address options is ignored, because `iptables-save` prints a host address either way. The error names the exemption and lists `DOCKER-USER`'s rules.
8. `m3dxDockRefusal(err error, code string, want ...string) error` returns nil only when `err` is (or wraps) an `*APIError` whose `Code` equals `code` (any code when `code` is empty) and whose `Detail` contains every `want`. A nil `err` is an error ("the request succeeded; want a refusal"), as is an error that is not an `*APIError`.
9. `m3dxDockInSubnet(subnet string) (string, error)` returns the second host address of a CIDR (its masked network address advanced twice, `172.17.0.0/16` gives `172.17.0.2`, `fd00:3d::/64` gives `fd00:3d::2`); it is an error for text that is not a prefix and for a prefix too small to hold it (IPv4 /31 and /32, IPv6 /127 and /128).
10. `m3dxDockRoutes(rules []model.Rule) []string` returns one string for every rule whose `Direction` is `model.DirRoute`, built from `ID`, `Origin`, `Action`, `Proto`, `From`, `FromPort`, `To`, `ToPort`, `InIface`, `OutIface`, `Family` and `Comment` (so a changed tag or a lost rule changes the result), sorted, independent of the order of `rules`.

**C. The helpers that talk to the fleet** (`m3_docker_lifecycle_test.go`):

1. `(a *API) m3dDockRead` reads the resource `firewall.docker` of `host` into an `m3dDockStatus` with `a.Resource`.
2. `(a *API) m3dDockConfirm` posts to `/api/v1/changes/<url-escaped id>/confirm` through `a.do` exactly as `m3Revert` posts to `.../revert`, and returns the `Change`.
3. `m3dDockWait` polls `m3dDockRead` of the agent with `eventually` until `check` accepts, as `m3WaitStatus` does for `firewall.status`, calls `t.Fatalf` naming the host and the last error on timeout, and returns the accepted status.
4. `m3dDockApply` plans and applies the revertible action with `f.api.m3Apply(ctx, f.agentID, action, input, 300)`, requires the change to be pending (`m3RequirePending`), confirms it with `m3dDockConfirm`, requires the answer's `State` to be `core.StateConfirmed`, and returns it. A failing guard or a refusal fails the test.
5. `m3dDockRefused` plans `action` with `input` on the agent through `f.api.m3Plan`, passes the error to `m3dxDockRefusal` with `code` and `want`, and calls `t.Fatalf` with the action's name when that returns an error.
6. `m3dDockEnable` waits (one minute) until the agent's status passes a check that `Available` and `Supported` are true and `Enabled` is false; registers, before it applies anything, a `t.Cleanup` that reads the status and, when `Enabled`, applies `firewall.docker.disable` with `m3Apply` (timeout 300) and confirms it, logging with `t.Logf` and never failing (a foreign rule may make the disable refuse; the scenario that added the rule removes it in a cleanup registered later, which runs first); then `m3dDockApply(ctx, t, f, "firewall.docker.enable", map[string]any{})`, then `m3dDockWait` for two minutes with `m3dxDockHealth("ok")`.
7. `m3dDockSave` returns `sudo iptables-save -t filter` for family `"v4"` and `sudo ip6tables-save -t filter` for `"v6"`, run on `v` with `m3Run`. The default `iptables` of a target is Docker's variant (Docker runs the `iptables` on its own `PATH`).
8. `m3dDockRemove` runs `sudo docker rm -f <names>` on `v`, ignoring the error (it is for `t.Cleanup`).
9. `m3dDockReach` runs `timeout 5 bash -c '</dev/tcp/<host>/<port>'` on `v` and returns its error; `host` is always one of the fleet's address constants or a literal of this task, never input.

**D. `m3_docker_test.go`.** `const m3dDockDeadline = 60 * time.Minute`. `TestM3Docker` skips with the message `no -os, -m2 or -m3 given: the VM tests run in .github/workflows/harness.yml` when `*osFlag == "" || *m2Flag == "" || !*m3Flag` (it shares TestM3Firewall's `-m3` flag; the workflow selects it with `-run`), runs under `context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), m3dDockDeadline)`, calls `bootFleet` and `serveReleases` (the release server on the scanner is also the outbound target of Task 53), and runs the same `steps` table as `TestM3Firewall` (name, gate, run; a failing gate step stops the run). Steps in this order, gate steps first:

| Name | Gate | Function |
|---|---|---|
| `install` | yes | `scenarioInstall(ctx, t, f)` |
| `firewall-ready` | yes | `m3Ready(ctx, t, f)` |
| `docker-detected` | yes | `m3dDockDetect` |
| `refuse-foreign-docker-user` | no | `m3dDockRefuseUser` |
| `foreign-after-enable` | no | `m3dDockForeignAfterEnable` |
| `foreign-forward` | no | `m3dDockForeignForward` |
| `refuse-exemption-overlap` | no | `m3dDockExemptionOverlap` |
| `refuse-open-incoming` | no | `m3dDockOpenIncoming` |
| `disable-cleanup` | no | `m3dDockDisableCleanup` |
| `routes-survive` | no | `m3dDockRoutesSurvive` |
| `foreign-in-confirmation-window` | no | `m3dDockForeignWindow` |
| `foreign-in-interrupted-cleanup` | no | `m3dDockForeignCleanup` |
| `refuse-ipv6no-docker-rules` | no | `m3dDockIPv6NoRules` |

Every scenario function has the signature `func(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet)`. Tasks 53 and 54 append their steps after the last row. Every scenario that enables the integration does it with `m3dDockEnable`, so the cleanup disables it again and each step starts on a host with the integration off; a scenario that adds a rule, namespace, container or file registers its undo with `t.Cleanup` before it creates the thing, and the undos ignore errors.

**E. The scenarios** (`m3_docker_lifecycle_test.go`). The foreign `DOCKER-USER` rules are plain `iptables` insertions on the agent VM; Docker's own `DOCKER-USER` holds one `-j RETURN`, so `-I DOCKER-USER 1` puts a foreign rule before everything else.

1. `m3dDockDetect` (spec 2.6 Detection, R43). `m3dDockWait` (one minute) with `m3dxDockDetected`; then `m3dxDockCleaned(m3dDockSave(v4), nil, false)` and the same for `v6`, which fail if the host starts with a Darkpanel chain loaded or a foreign rule in `DOCKER-USER`.
2. `m3dDockRefuseUser` (adoption). Foreign rule text `-s 192.0.2.77/32 -j DROP`: register a cleanup that runs `sudo iptables -D DOCKER-USER <text>`, then run `sudo iptables -I DOCKER-USER 1 <text>` and wait until the status' `ForeignRules` has an entry containing `192.0.2.77`. `m3dDockRefused(…, "firewall.docker.enable", map[string]any{}, "firewall.docker_user_in_use", "192.0.2.77")`. Delete the rule, wait until `ForeignRules` is empty, then plan `firewall.docker.enable` with `f.api.m3Plan`: it must succeed, its `m3DiffText()` must contain `docker integration on` and `after.rules: Docker block written`, and its `firewall.lockout` guard must be present and OK. Nothing is applied.
3. `m3dDockForeignAfterEnable` (spec 2.6 adoption, R44, R47). `m3dDockEnable`. Foreign rule `-s 192.0.2.78/32 -j DROP` inserted at position 1 (cleanup deletes it). Wait until the status passes `m3dxDockHealth("broken")` and `ForeignRules` names `192.0.2.78`. `m3dDockRefused` with code `firewall.docker_user_in_use` naming `192.0.2.78` for `firewall.rule.add` (`m3PortRule(8101)`), for `firewall.docker.set-sources` with input `{"forwardExemptions": []}` and for `firewall.docker.repair` with `{}`. `m3dDockRefused` with an empty code and no `want` for `firewall.docker.repair` with `{"discardForeign": true}` (it needs `manual: true`; the spec names no code for this refusal). Plan `firewall.docker.repair` with `{"discardForeign": true, "manual": true}` through `m3Plan`: it must succeed and its diff text must contain `192.0.2.78`. `m3dDockApply` that input, `m3dDockWait` for `m3dxDockHealth("ok")`, and require `m3dxDockRulesOf(m3dDockSave(v4), "DOCKER-USER")` not to contain the rule text.
4. `m3dDockForeignForward` (spec 2.6 non-Docker forwarding). The agent VM gets a network namespace that stands in for a non-Docker forward target. Register one cleanup per command, then run: `sudo ip netns add m3dfwd`; `sudo ip link add m3dfv0 type veth peer name m3dfv1 netns m3dfwd`; `sudo ip addr add 192.0.2.49/30 dev m3dfv0`; `sudo ip link set m3dfv0 up`; `sudo ip -n m3dfwd addr add 192.0.2.50/30 dev m3dfv1`; `sudo ip -n m3dfwd link set m3dfv1 up`; `sudo ip -n m3dfwd link set lo up`; `sudo ip -n m3dfwd route add default via 192.0.2.49`; `sudo systemd-run --unit=m3d-fwd --collect ip netns exec m3dfwd /usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 9100 --bind 192.0.2.50` (the cleanup stops the unit); the foreign DNAT rule `sudo iptables -t nat -I PREROUTING -d 198.18.0.11 -p tcp --dport 9100 -j DNAT --to-destination 192.0.2.50:9100` (use `agentIPv4` for the address); and the manual route rule `sudo ufw route allow proto tcp to 192.0.2.50 port 9100` (the cleanup runs `sudo ufw route delete allow proto tcp to 192.0.2.50 port 9100`). Then, in this order:
   a. Require `sudo sysctl -n net.ipv4.ip_forward` to print `1` (Docker sets it) and, with `eventually` for 30 seconds, `m3dDockReach(ctx, f.scanner, agentIPv4, 9100)` to succeed: the forward works before the integration.
   b. `m3dDockWait` until `ForeignForwards` equals exactly `[]m3dDockExemption{{OrigDestination: agentIPv4, OrigPort: 9100, Destination: "192.0.2.50", Proto: "tcp", Port: 9100}}` (call this value `want`; compare with `slices.Equal`).
   c. `m3dDockRefused(…, "firewall.docker.enable", map[string]any{}, "", "192.0.2.50")`: spec 2.6 names no code for this refusal, so only that it is a refusal naming the destination is asserted.
   d. Register a cleanup that applies `firewall.docker.set-sources` with `{"forwardExemptions": []}` (log, never fail); `m3dDockApply` `firewall.docker.set-sources` with `{"forwardExemptions": [want]}`; `m3dDockWait` until `Settings.ForwardExemptions` equals `[want]` and `ForeignForwards` is empty.
   e. `m3dDockEnable`; require `m3dxDockBlockLoaded(m3dDockSave(v4))` and `m3dxDockExemptionLine(save, want)`; and, with `eventually` for 30 seconds, `m3dDockReach(ctx, f.scanner, agentIPv4, 9100)` to succeed again: the forward works after the exemption.
5. `m3dDockExemptionOverlap` (spec 2.6, an exemption overlapping a Docker subnet). `m3dDockEnable`. Read the status, take the first subnet of the network named `bridge`, and compute an address in it with `m3dxDockInSubnet`. `m3dDockRefused(…, "firewall.docker.set-sources", map[string]any{"forwardExemptions": []m3dDockExemption{{OrigDestination: agentIPv4, OrigPort: 9102, Destination: <that address>, Proto: "tcp", Port: 9102}}}, "firewall.unsupported_integration", "bridge")`.
6. `m3dDockOpenIncoming` (spec 2.6 proxied families, the incoming-policy invariant). Read `DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY` with `sudo sed -n 's/^DEFAULT_INPUT_POLICY=//p' /etc/default/ufw` and require the trimmed output to equal `"DROP"` with its double quotes (the four images' default); register a cleanup that runs `sudo ufw default deny incoming`. With the integration off, `m3dDockApply` `firewall.defaults.set` with `{"incoming": "ACCEPT"}`, then `m3dDockRefused(…, "firewall.docker.enable", map[string]any{}, "firewall.unsupported_integration")`, then `m3dDockApply` `{"incoming": "DROP"}`. Then `m3dDockEnable` and `m3dDockRefused(…, "firewall.defaults.set", map[string]any{"incoming": "ACCEPT"}, "firewall.unsupported_integration")`.
7. `m3dDockDisableCleanup` (cleanup of loaded chains). `m3dDockEnable`; require `m3dxDockBlockLoaded` on both families. `m3dDockApply` `firewall.docker.disable` with `{}`; `m3dDockWait` until `Enabled` is false and `Health` is `off`; require `m3dxDockCleaned(save, nil, true)` for both families, and no block in the files: `sudo grep -l 'BEGIN DARKPANEL docker' /etc/ufw/after.rules /etc/ufw/after6.rules` run with `|| true` prints nothing. Then enable again with `m3dDockEnable`, `m3dDockApply` `firewall.state.disable` with `{}`: `m3dxDockCleaned` holds on both families, the status' `Enabled` is still true (the flag persists, spec 2.6) and `sudo ufw status` starts with `Status: inactive`; `m3dDockApply` `firewall.state.enable` with `{}`: `m3dDockWait` for `m3dxDockHealth("ok")` and `m3dxDockBlockLoaded` on both families.
8. `m3dDockRoutesSurvive` (tagged and manual route rules). `m3dDockEnable`. `m3dRunTCP(ctx, t, f.agent, "m3d-rt", "bridge", "18101:14000")` with `m3dWaitRunning`, and `t.Cleanup(func() { m3dDockRemove(ctx, f.agent, "m3d-rt") })` registered before it. `m3dDockApply` `firewall.container.allow` with `{"binding": m3dDockBinding{Selector: "m3d-rt", HostPort: 18101, Proto: "tcp"}}` (a zero `HostAddr` is omitted from the JSON). Register the cleanup `sudo ufw route delete allow proto tcp from 192.0.2.0/24 to any port 9099`, then run `sudo ufw route allow proto tcp from 192.0.2.0/24 to any port 9099`. Read `firewall.status` (`m3WaitStatus` with `m3Healthy`): `before := m3dxDockRoutes(st.Rules)` must have exactly two entries, one that contains ` darkpanel ` and `ctr ` and one that contains ` manual `. - [ ] **Step 3: Implement**

The scenarios run only in `.github/workflows/harness.yml` (gate 7). Everything is in package `harness` under the build tag `harness`, with doc comments, error strings in lower case. Host of every scenario: the agent VM (`f.agent`, `f.agentID`), scanned from `f.scanner`. Constants: `m3dTrafficIface = "dpinet"` (the internet link's interface name on both VMs) and `m3dTrafficSrcB = "198.18.1.30"` (a second scanner source address inside the lab's 198.18.0.0/15 link; the first is `scannerIPv4`). Port numbers 18201–18209 are this task's alone.

**A. The pure helpers** (`m3_docker_traffic_test.go`), exactly as the unit tests above require:

1. `m3dxTrafficExpect(states []PortState, proto string, port uint16, want string) error` looks up the entry for `proto` and `port` in a scan; `want` is `open`, `closed`, `filtered` or `notopen` (`closed` or `filtered`); another `want` is an error naming it (`harness: unknown expectation "<want>"`); a missing entry is an error saying `<proto>/<port> is not in the scan`; a mismatch says `<proto>/<port> is <state>, want <want>`.
2. `m3dxTrafficExpectAll(states []PortState, want map[uint16]string) error` applies `m3dxTrafficExpect` with proto `tcp` to every entry in ascending port order and returns one error joining every message with `"; "`, nil when all match.
3. `m3dxTrafficLeaks(log string, unallowed []uint16, minAttempts int) error` reads the probe log (one line per attempt: `<port> ok` or `<port> fail`; blank lines are skipped; any other line is an error containing `malformed`). For each port of `unallowed`, in order: an `ok` line is an error naming the port and counting `ok` lines against attempts; fewer than `minAttempts` lines is an error naming the port and saying `<n> attempts` (a port never probed counts 0, so a probe that never ran cannot pass as one that saw nothing). The parameter is not named `min`, which the linter rejects as a redefined built-in.
4. `m3dxTrafficConnect(pid int, addr string, port uint16) (string, error)` returns `sudo nsenter -t <pid> -n -- timeout 5 bash -c '</dev/tcp/<addr>/<port>'` with `addr` re-printed by `netip.Addr.String`; it is an error for `pid <= 0`, `port == 0`, an address that `netip.ParseAddr` rejects or one with a zone, which keeps shell metacharacters out of the command.
5. `m3dxTrafficRuleID(st m3dDockStatus, selector string, port uint16, kind, from string) (string, error)` returns the `ID` of the rule in `st.Rules` whose binding has that selector and host port and whose `Kind` and `From` equal `kind` and `from` (`from` is `""` for any source); otherwise an error printing the rules.

**B. The helpers that talk to the fleet:**

1. `m3dTrafficWant(ctx, t, f, o ScanOpts, want map[uint16]string)` sets `o.Ports` to the keys of `want` in ascending order, `o.Target` to `agentIPv4` for `o.Family == "-4"` and `agentIPv6` for `"-6"` when empty, and `o.Iface` to `m3dTrafficIface` when `o.Source` is valid; then, with `eventually` for 90 seconds, runs `m3dScan(ctx, t, f.scanner, o)` and `m3dxTrafficExpectAll` until the result matches, and fails the test with the last mismatch otherwise. A scan whose first result already matches returns at once.
2. `m3dTrafficPublish(ctx, t, f, name, network string, publish ...string)` registers `t.Cleanup(func() { m3dDockRemove(ctx, f.agent, name) })`, calls `m3dRunTCP(ctx, t, f.agent, name, network, publish...)` and `m3dWaitRunning`.
3. `m3dTrafficNetwork(ctx, t, f, name string, opts ...string)` registers the cleanup `sudo docker network rm <name>` (it runs after the containers' removals, which are registered later), then `m3dDocker(ctx, t, f.agent, "network", "create", opts..., name)`.
4. `m3dTrafficAllow(ctx, t, f, selector string, port uint16, from string)` and `m3dTrafficDeny(…)` call `m3dDockApply` with `firewall.container.allow` or `firewall.container.deny` and the input `{"binding": m3dDockBinding{Selector: selector, HostPort: port, Proto: "tcp"}, "from": from}`, leaving `from` out of the map when it is empty. `m3dTrafficRemove(ctx, t, f, selector string, port uint16, kind, from string)` reads `m3dDockRead`, finds the rule's id with `m3dxTrafficRuleID` and applies `firewall.container.remove` with `{"id": id}`.
5. `m3dTrafficAddr(ctx, t, f, container, network, field string) string` runs `m3dDocker(ctx, t, f.agent, "inspect", "-f", "{{.NetworkSettings.Networks.<network>.<field>}}", container)` (`field` is `IPAddress` or `GlobalIPv6Address`) and returns the trimmed output; `m3dTrafficPID(ctx, t, f, container string) int` does the same with `{{.State.Pid}}` and `strconv.Atoi`.
6. `m3dTrafficProbe(ctx, t, f, unit, host string, ports ...uint16) (stop func() string)` starts a transient unit on the scanner with `sudo systemd-run --unit=<unit> --collect /usr/bin/python3 -c <m3Quote(script)> /var/tmp/<unit>.log <host> <ports…>` after removing any old log. The script (a package constant `m3dTrafficProbeScript`) takes the log path, the host and the ports from `sys.argv[1:]`, uses `AF_INET6` when the host contains `:` and `AF_INET` otherwise, and loops forever: for each port it opens a TCP connection with a 0.4 second timeout, appends `<port> ok` (connected) or `<port> fail` (any `OSError`) to the log and flushes it, then sleeps 0.1 seconds after each round. `stop` runs `sudo systemctl stop <unit>`, returns the log read with `sudo cat`, and is also registered with `t.Cleanup`; calling it twice is harmless.

**C. `m3_docker_test.go`.** Append these rows to `TestM3Docker`'s step table, none a gate, in this order: `traffic-unallowed-closed` → `m3dTrafficUnallowed`, `traffic-new-network` → `m3dTrafficNewNetwork`, `traffic-container-to-container` → `m3dTrafficContainers`, `traffic-disjoint-bindings` → `m3dTrafficDisjoint`, `traffic-deny-keeps-allow` → `m3dTrafficDenyKeeps`, `traffic-proxied-ipv6` → `m3dTrafficProxied`, `traffic-recreate-under-scan` → `m3dTrafficRecreate`. Each function has the signature `func(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet)` and starts with `m3dDockEnable(ctx, t, f)`; its containers and networks are removed by the cleanups of `m3dTrafficPublish` and `m3dTrafficNetwork`. Published ports are `m3dRunTCP` containers (the pinned Pebble image, container port 14000).

**D. The scenarios** (`m3_docker_traffic_test.go`). "Default source" is a `ScanOpts` without `Source`; "source B" is `Source: netip.MustParseAddr(m3dTrafficSrcB)` after `m3dAddSource(ctx, t, f.scanner, netip.MustParsePrefix(m3dTrafficSrcB+"/32"), m3dTrafficIface)`.

1. `m3dTrafficUnallowed` (published ports unreachable unless a binding is allowed, R45). Publish `m3d-t1` on the `bridge` network with `18201:14000`. `m3dTrafficWant` with `ScanOpts{Family: "-4"}` and `{18201: "filtered"}` (the block drops it; Docker's own accept for the published port would otherwise make it `open`). `m3dTrafficAllow(…, "m3d-t1", 18201, "")`; `m3dTrafficWant` `{18201: "open"}`; the status' binding view for `m3d-t1` port 18201 has `Allowed` equal to `["any"]`. `m3dTrafficRemove(…, "m3d-t1", 18201, "allow", "")`; `m3dTrafficWant` `{18201: "filtered"}`.
2. `m3dTrafficNewNetwork` (a new Docker network protected at creation). `m3dTrafficNetwork(…, "m3dn1", "-o", "com.docker.network.bridge.name=m3dcust")`; publish `m3d-n1` on `m3dn1` with `18202:14000`. Straight after `m3dWaitRunning`, with no retry, `m3dScan` with `ScanOpts{Family: "-4", Ports: []uint16{18202}, Target: agentIPv4}` and `m3dxTrafficExpectAll(states, {18202: "filtered"})` must hold: the DNAT gate protects a bridge no reconcile has seen. Then `m3dTrafficAllow(…, "m3d-n1", 18202, "")` and `m3dTrafficWant` `{18202: "open"}`, which shows the port was filtered by the block and not because the container was not listening.
3. `m3dTrafficContainers` (R46: container-to-container and outbound traffic keep working). `m3dTrafficNetwork(…, "m3dpub", "--subnet", "203.0.113.0/24", "--ipv6", "--subnet", "2001:db8:dd:1::/64")` (a public IPv4 and a global IPv6 network); publish `m3d-c1` and `m3d-c2` on it without ports. Read each container's `IPAddress` and `GlobalIPv6Address` on `m3dpub` with `m3dTrafficAddr` and require them inside the two subnets (`netip.Prefix.Contains`). For both directions (`m3d-c2` to `m3d-c1` and back) and both families, run `m3dxTrafficConnect(m3dTrafficPID(source), target address, 14000)` on `f.agent` with `eventually` for 30 seconds (Pebble needs a moment to listen): a container opens a TCP connection to the other over the bridge. Finally the outbound flow: the same with `m3d-c2`'s namespace to `scannerIPv4` port 8000, the release server `serveReleases` started on the scanner.
4. `m3dTrafficDisjoint` (two bindings to one container port with disjoint allowed sources). Add source B. Publish `m3d-d1` on `bridge` with `18203:14000` and `18204:14000`. One `m3dDockApply` of `firewall.containers.apply` with `{"ops": [{"op": "allow", "binding": <selector m3d-d1, port 18203, tcp>, "from": "198.18.0.20/32"}, {"op": "allow", "binding": <selector m3d-d1, port 18204, tcp>, "from": "198.18.1.30/32"}]}` (use `scannerIPv4+"/32"` for the first source). `m3dTrafficWant` from the default source with `{18203: "open", 18204: "filtered"}` and from source B with `{18203: "filtered", 18204: "open"}`: each binding refuses the other's source though both route to container port 14000.
5. `m3dTrafficDenyKeeps` (an explicit deny on one binding does not remove another binding's allowance). Add source B. Publish `m3d-k1` with `18205:14000` and `18206:14000`; `m3dTrafficAllow` both ports from any source; `m3dTrafficDeny(…, "m3d-k1", 18206, scannerIPv4+"/32")`. Default source: `{18205: "open", 18206: "filtered"}` (the denied source still reaches the other binding of the same container port). Source B: `{18205: "open", 18206: "open"}` (the deny names only the first source).
6. `m3dTrafficProxied` (an unallowed IPv6 binding proxied to an IPv4-only container is closed). Publish `m3d-p1` on `bridge` with `18207:14000`; the default bridge has no IPv6, so `docker-proxy` serves the IPv6 side. `m3dTrafficWant` with `ScanOpts{Family: "-4"}` and `ScanOpts{Family: "-6"}`, each `{18207: "notopen"}`. `m3dTrafficAllow(…, "m3d-p1", 18207, "")`; both families `{18207: "open"}` (the IPv6 side through the tagged `allow in` rule); the binding view for `m3d-p1` port 18207 has a non-empty `Proxied`. `m3dTrafficRemove` the allowance; both families `{18207: "notopen"}` again.
7. `m3dTrafficRecreate` (containers recreated under continuous scanning, including across an agent restart, never expose an unallowed binding). Publish `m3d-r1` (`18208:14000`) and `m3d-r2` (`18209:14000`) on `bridge`; `m3dTrafficAllow(…, "m3d-r1", 18208, "")`; `m3dTrafficWant` `{18208: "open"}` and `{18209: "notopen"}`. Start the probes `stop4 := m3dTrafficProbe(ctx, t, f, "m3d-probe4", agentIPv4, 18209)` and `stop6 := m3dTrafficProbe(ctx, t, f, "m3d-probe6", agentIPv6, 18209)`. Three times: remove and publish again `m3d-r2` and then `m3d-r1` under the same names and ports (`m3dDockRemove`, then `m3dTrafficPublish`), then `m3dTrafficWant` `{18208: "open"}` with the probes still running (the reconcile task re-applies the allowance to the new address). Then restart the agent with `sudo systemctl restart ` plus `update.AgentUnit` through `m3Run`, recreate `m3d-r2` and `m3d-r1` once more at once, `waitHosts(ctx, t, f, 3*time.Minute, hostsAt(versionN, f.agentID))`, and `m3dTrafficWant` `{18208: "open"}` (the first pass at agent start reconciles) and `{18209: "notopen"}`. Last, `m3dxTrafficLeaks(stop4(), []uint16{18209}, 20)` and `m3dxTrafficLeaks(stop6(), []uint16{18209}, 20)` must both be nil; a failure prints the log.

```go
//go:build harness

package harness

import (
	"net/netip"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

// m3dxExpoDoc is the JSON of firewall.exposure (Contracts: ExposureView)
// with a partial row that splits by source port.
const m3dxExpoDoc = `{"rows":[
{"proto":"tcp","addr":"0.0.0.0","port":18302,"family":"v4","container":{"name":"m3d-x2","binding":{"selector":"m3d-x2","hostPort":18302,"proto":"tcp"},"containerPort":14000,"proxied":false},
 "classes":[
  {"class":"internet","verdict":"partial","allowed":[{"sources":["198.18.0.20/32"],"ifaces":["dpinet"],"decidedBy":"binding dp-b-0123456789ab"}]},
  {"class":"private","range":"10.0.0.0/8","verdict":"open","decidedBy":"DOCKER-USER -s 10.0.0.0/8"},
  {"class":"tailnet","verdict":"closed","note":"host firewall; tailnet policy not evaluated"},
  {"class":"localhost","verdict":"open"}]},
{"proto":"tcp","addr":"0.0.0.0","port":18311,"family":"v4","process":"python3",
 "classes":[{"class":"internet","verdict":"partial","allowed":[{"sources":["any"],"srcPorts":["5300-5399"],"decidedBy":"ufw-user-input #12"}]}]}],
"notes":["Docker is unavailable"]}`

func TestM3xExpoDecode(t *testing.T) {
	v, err := m3dExpoDecode([]byte(m3dxExpoDoc))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(v.Rows) != 2 || len(v.Notes) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("rows %d, notes %q", len(v.Rows), v.Notes)
	}
	r := v.Rows[0]
	if r.Proto != "tcp" || r.Addr != "0.0.0.0" || r.Port != 18302 || r.Family != "v4" || r.Container == nil || r.Container.Name != "m3d-x2" {
		t.Errorf("row %+v", r)
	}
	c, ok := r.m3dExpoClassOf("internet", "")
	if !ok || c.Verdict != "partial" || len(c.Allowed) != 1 || c.Allowed[0].Sources[0] != "198.18.0.20/32" || c.Allowed[0].Ifaces[0] != "dpinet" {
		t.Errorf("internet class %+v, %v", c, ok)
	}
	if c, ok := r.m3dExpoClassOf("private", "10.0.0.0/8"); !ok || c.Verdict != "open" {
		t.Errorf("private class of 10.0.0.0/8: %+v, %v", c, ok)
	}
	if _, ok := r.m3dExpoClassOf("private", "192.168.0.0/16"); ok {
		t.Error("a private class of a range the row does not list was found")
	}
	if _, ok := r.m3dExpoClassOf("nonesuch", ""); ok {
		t.Error("an unknown class was found")
	}
	if _, err := m3dExpoDecode([]byte(`{"rows":[{"proto":"tcp"}]`)); err == nil {
		t.Error("truncated JSON decoded")
	}
}

func TestM3xExpoExpect(t *testing.T) {
	in, out := netip.MustParseAddr("198.18.0.20"), netip.MustParseAddr("198.18.1.30")
	partial := m3dExpoClass{Class: "internet", Verdict: "partial", Allowed: []m3dExpoAllowed{
		{Sources: []string{"198.18.0.20/32"}, Ifaces: []string{"dpinet"}},
		{Sources: []string{"198.18.1.1-198.18.1.9", "203.0.113.7"}},
	}}
	bySrcPort := m3dExpoClass{Class: "internet", Verdict: "partial", Allowed: []m3dExpoAllowed{{Sources: []string{"any"}, SrcPorts: []string{"5300-5399", "7000"}}}}
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		name    string
		c       m3dExpoClass
		src     netip.Addr
		srcPort uint16
		iface   string
		want    string // "" for an error
	}{
		{"open", m3dExpoClass{Verdict: "open"}, out, 0, "dpinet", "open"},
		{"closed", m3dExpoClass{Verdict: "closed"}, out, 0, "dpinet", "closed"},
		{"filtered", m3dExpoClass{Verdict: "filtered"}, out, 0, "dpinet", "filtered"},
		{"partial, inside by prefix", partial, in, 0, "dpinet", "open"},
		{"partial, outside", partial, out, 0, "dpinet", "notopen"},
		{"partial, inside by range", partial, netip.MustParseAddr("198.18.1.5"), 0, "dpinet", "open"},
		{"partial, range end", partial, netip.MustParseAddr("198.18.1.9"), 0, "dpinet", "open"},
		{"partial, past the range", partial, netip.MustParseAddr("198.18.1.10"), 0, "dpinet", "notopen"},
		{"partial, inside by address", partial, netip.MustParseAddr("203.0.113.7"), 0, "dpinet", "open"},
		{"partial, wrong interface", partial, in, 0, "dppriv", "notopen"},
		{"source port inside", bySrcPort, in, 5350, "dpinet", "open"},
		{"source port single", bySrcPort, in, 7000, "dpinet", "open"},
		{"source port outside", bySrcPort, in, 5400, "dpinet", "notopen"},
		{"source port unknown", bySrcPort, in, 0, "dpinet", ""},
		{"unknown verdict", m3dExpoClass{Verdict: "unknown", Note: "too many partitions"}, in, 0, "dpinet", ""},
		{"unreadable source", m3dExpoClass{Verdict: "partial", Allowed: []m3dExpoAllowed{{Sources: []string{"lan"}}}}, in, 0, "dpinet", ""},
	} {
		got, err := m3dxExpoExpect(tc.c, tc.src, tc.srcPort, tc.iface)
		if tc.want == "" {
			if err == nil {
				t.Errorf("%s: %q, want an error", tc.name, got)
			}
			continue
		}
		if err != nil || got != tc.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: %q, %v, want %q", tc.name, got, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestM3xExpoSourcePorts(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		in       []string
		inside   uint16
		outside  uint16
		wantFail bool
	}{
		{[]string{"5300-5399"}, 5300, 40001, false},
		{[]string{"5300:5399", "7000"}, 5300, 40001, false},
		{[]string{"53"}, 53, 40001, false},
		{[]string{"40001-40010"}, 40001, 40011, false},
		{[]string{"1-65535"}, 0, 0, true},
		{[]string{"x"}, 0, 0, true},
		{[]string{"9-5"}, 0, 0, true},
		{nil, 0, 0, true},
	} {
		inside, outside, err := m3dxExpoSourcePorts(tc.in)
		switch {
		case tc.wantFail && err == nil:
			t.Errorf("%q = %d, %d, want an error", tc.in, inside, outside)
		case !tc.wantFail && (err != nil || inside != tc.inside || outside != tc.outside):
			t.Errorf("%q = %d, %d, %v, want %d, %d", tc.in, inside, outside, err, tc.inside, tc.outside)
		}
	}
}

func TestM3xExpoCompare(t *testing.T) {
	for _, tc := range []struct {
		expect, proto, state string
		ok                   bool
	}{
		{"open", "tcp", "open", true},
		{"open", "tcp", "filtered", false},
		{"closed", "tcp", "closed", true},
		{"closed", "tcp", "filtered", false},
		{"filtered", "tcp", "filtered", true},
		{"filtered", "tcp", "closed", false},
		{"notopen", "tcp", "closed", true},
		{"notopen", "tcp", "filtered", true},
		{"notopen", "tcp", "open", false},
		{"open", "udp", "open", true},
		{"open", "udp", "open|filtered", true},
		{"open", "udp", "closed", false},
		{"closed", "udp", "closed", true},
		{"closed", "udp", "open|filtered", true},
		{"closed", "udp", "open", false},
		{"filtered", "udp", "open", false},
		{"notopen", "udp", "open|filtered", true},
		{"notopen", "udp", "open", false},
	} {
		err := m3dxExpoCompare(tc.expect, PortState{Port: 18304, Proto: tc.proto, State: tc.state}, tc.proto)
		if (err == nil) != tc.ok {
			t.Errorf("m3dxExpoCompare(%s, %s %s) = %v, want ok=%t", tc.expect, tc.proto, tc.state, err, tc.ok)
		}
	}
	if err := m3dxExpoCompare("open", PortState{Port: 1, Proto: "udp", State: "open"}, "tcp"); err == nil {
		t.Error("a UDP result was compared as TCP")
	}
}

const m3dxExpoWorkflowDoc = `jobs:
  build:
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - run: go test -tags harness ./test/harness/...
  vm:
    timeout-minutes: 280
    steps:
      - name: Run the harness
        run: >-
          go test -tags harness -timeout 100m -v ./test/harness/
      - name: Run the M3 firewall harness
        run: >-
          go test -tags harness -timeout 70m -v -run '^TestM3Firewall$' ./test/harness/
          -args -os ${{ matrix.os }} -m3
      - name: Run the M3 Docker harness
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: >-
          go test -tags harness -timeout 70m -v -run '^TestM3Docker$' ./test/harness/
          -args -os ${{ matrix.os }} -m3
          -workdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/harness-m3d"
      - if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/harness/**/*.log
            ${{ runner.temp }}/harness-m3d/**/*.log
`

func TestM3xExpoWorkflow(t *testing.T) {
	if err := m3dxExpoWorkflow(m3dxExpoWorkflowDoc, 60*time.Minute); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a complete workflow: %v", err)
	}
	for name, tc := range map[string]struct{ from, to, want string }{
		"no Docker step":         {"Run the M3 Docker harness", "Run another harness", "Run the M3 Docker harness"},
		"wrong test":             {"'^TestM3Docker$'", "'^TestM3Firewall$'", "TestM3Docker"},
		"no -m3":                 {"-args -os ${{ matrix.os }} -m3\n          -workdir", "-args -os ${{ matrix.os }}\n          -workdir", "-m3"},
		"timeout under deadline": {"-timeout 70m -v -run '^TestM3Docker$'", "-timeout 65m -v -run '^TestM3Docker$'", "deadline"},
		"job limit too small":    {"timeout-minutes: 280", "timeout-minutes: 200", "timeout-minutes"},
		"no logs":                {"${{ runner.temp }}/harness-m3d/**/*.log", "", "harness-m3d"},
	} {
		if !strings.Contains(m3dxExpoWorkflowDoc, tc.from) {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the fixture lacks %q", name, tc.from)
		}
		if err := m3dxExpoWorkflow(strings.Replace(m3dxExpoWorkflowDoc, tc.from, tc.to, 1), 60*time.Minute); err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), tc.want) {
			t.Errorf("%s: %v, want an error naming %q", name, err, tc.want)
		}
	}
}

func TestM3xExpoVerdicts(t *testing.T) {
	row := func(proto, addr, family string, port uint16, internet string) m3dExpoRow {
		return m3dExpoRow{Proto: proto, Addr: addr, Port: port, Family: family, Classes: []m3dExpoClass{{Class: "internet", Verdict: internet}, {Class: "localhost", Verdict: "open"}}}
	}
	rows := []m3dExpoRow{
		row("tcp", "0.0.0.0", "v4", 18301, "open"),
		row("tcp", "::", "v6", 18301, "filtered"),
		row("udp", "0.0.0.0", "v4", 18304, "open"),
		row("tcp", "198.18.0.11", "v4", 18301, "open"), // the same port on another address
	}
	if err := m3dxExpoVerdicts(rows, map[string]string{"tcp/v4/18301": "open", "tcp/v6/18301": "filtered", "udp/v4/18304": "open"}); err != nil {

	}
	err := m3dxExpoVerdicts(rows, map[string]string{"tcp/v4/18301": "filtered", "tcp/v6/18301": "filtered", "tcp/v4/18399": "open"})
	if err == nil || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "tcp/v4/18301") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "tcp/v4/18399") || strings.Contains(err.Error(), "tcp/v6/18301") {
		t.Errorf("a wrong and a missing row: %v, want an error naming exactly those two", err)

	if err := m3dxExpoVerdicts(mixed, map[string]string{"tcp/v4/18301": "open"}); err == nil {

}
```

**B. The pure helpers** (same file), exactly as the unit tests require:

1. `m3dExpoDecode(raw []byte) (m3dExpoView, error)` unmarshals the resource's JSON; the error text starts `harness: firewall.exposure:`.
2. `(r m3dExpoRow) m3dExpoClassOf(class, rng string) (m3dExpoClass, bool)` returns the class with that `Class` and `Range` (`""` for the internet, tailnet and localhost classes, the CIDR for a `private` one).
3. `(c m3dExpoClass) m3dExpoBySourcePort() bool` is true when any `Allowed` group has `SrcPorts`.
4. `m3dxExpoExpect(c m3dExpoClass, src netip.Addr, srcPort uint16, iface string) (string, error)` is the scan result the view promises for one probe: `open`, `closed` and `filtered` verdicts return themselves; `partial` returns `open` when some `Allowed` group holds the probe and `notopen` otherwise; any other verdict (`unknown`, with its `Note`) is an error. A group holds the probe when `src` is in one of its `Sources`, `iface` is in `Ifaces` (or `Ifaces` is empty) and `srcPort` is in one of its `SrcPorts` intervals (or `SrcPorts` is empty); a group with `SrcPorts` and `srcPort == 0` is an error (the verdict needs a source port nobody gave). A source entry is `any`, a CIDR, an address or a range `<from>-<to>` (spaces around the dash allowed); anything else is an error naming the entry. A source port entry is `<n>`, `<from>-<to>` or `<from>:<to>`, ports 1–65535 and `from <= to`; anything else is an error. The groups are read as the conjunction of their three lists.
5. `m3dxExpoSourcePorts(srcPorts []string) (inside, outside uint16, err error)` parses the intervals the same way: `inside` is the first interval's first port, `outside` is the lowest port from 40001 up to 65535 that no interval covers, then 1024 and 1025; an empty list, an unparsable entry or intervals that cover all of those is an error.
6. `m3dxExpoCompare(expect string, got PortState, proto string) error` compares a scan result with an expectation (`open`, `closed`, `filtered` or `notopen`). A `got.Proto` that differs from `proto` is an error. TCP is exact: `got.State` equals `expect`, and `notopen` accepts `closed` and `filtered`. UDP follows spec 2.7: `open` accepts every state but `closed`; every other expectation accepts every state but `open` (`open|filtered` is no answer). The error reads `<proto>/<port> is <state>, want <expect>`.
7. `m3dxExpoTarget(addr, family, inet4, inet6 string) (string, bool)` returns the address the scanner can probe for a row: `inet4` for family `v4` when `addr` is `0.0.0.0` or `inet4`, `inet6` for family `v6` when `addr` is `::` or `inet6` (compare with `netip.Addr`, so spelling does not matter), and `"", false` for anything else (loopback, the private link, a Docker bridge address, another family spelling).
8. `m3dxExpoVerdicts(rows []m3dExpoRow, want map[string]string) error` checks the internet class of the rows: the key is `<proto>/<family>/<port>`; the error lists, in key order and joined with `"; "`, every key with no row (`<key> has no row`), every key whose verdict differs (`<key> is <verdict>, want <want>`), and every key whose rows (one per address) hold different verdicts.
9. `m3dxExpoWorkflow(yml string, deadline time.Duration) error` checks the text of `harness.yml`: a step whose `name:` is `Run the M3 Docker harness` (steps are split at lines starting with six spaces and `- `) contains `-run '^TestM3Docker$'`, ` -m3`, `-os ${{ matrix.os }}` and `-workdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/harness-m3d"`; its `-timeout <n>m` is at least `deadline` plus 10 minutes; the file mentions `harness-m3d/**/*.log` (the failure artifact); and the `vm` job's own `timeout-minutes` (the first one after the line `  vm:`) is at least the sum of every `-timeout <n>m` in that job plus 30 minutes of setup. Every error names what is missing (`TestM3Docker`, `-m3`, `deadline`, `timeout-minutes`, `harness-m3d`, the step's name).

**C. The workflow** (`.github/workflows/harness.yml`, a configuration value). In the `vm` job replace the comment and limit

```yaml
    # 120 minutes for the M1 and M2 run, 80 more for the M3 firewall run.
    timeout-minutes: 200
```

with

```yaml
    # 120 minutes for the M1 and M2 run, 80 more for the M3 firewall run and
    # 80 more for the M3 Docker run.
    timeout-minutes: 280
```

(the job's steps now hold `-timeout` 100m, 70m and 70m, 240 minutes, and 30 more cover the KVM, QEMU and download setup), insert this step directly after `Run the M3 firewall harness` and before the `if: failure()` upload step:

```yaml
      # TestM3Docker boots a fleet of its own, as TestM3Firewall does. Its own
      # deadline is 60 minutes, and the extra 10 leave its VM cleanups time to
      # finish.
      - name: Run the M3 Docker harness
        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
        run: >-
          go test -tags harness -timeout 70m -v -run '^TestM3Docker$' ./test/harness/
          -args -os ${{ matrix.os }} -m3
          -bin "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/bin/darkpanel-linux-amd64"
          -m2 "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/bin/harness"
          -commit "$GITHUB_SHA"
          -workdir "$RUNNER_TEMP/harness-m3d"
          -cache "$HOME/.cache/darkpanel-harness"
```

and add the line `            ${{ runner.temp }}/harness-m3d/**/*.log` after the `harness-m3` line of the failure artifact's `path:`. Change nothing else in the file.

**D. `m3_docker_test.go`.** Append these rows, none a gate, after Task 53's: `exposure-equals-scan` → `m3dExpoScan`, `exposure-source-port` → `m3dExpoSourcePort`, `exposure-private-class` → `m3dExpoPrivateClass`. Signature `func(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, f *fleet)`.

**E. The helpers that talk to the fleet** (`m3_docker_exposure_test.go`):

1. `m3dExpoRead(ctx, t, f) ([]byte, m3dExpoView)` reads `firewall.exposure` of the agent into a `json.RawMessage` with `f.api.Resource`, decodes it with `m3dExpoDecode` and fails the test on an error.
2. `m3dExpoPublishUDP(ctx, t, f, name string, publish ...string)` registers the cleanup `m3dDockRemove(ctx, f.agent, name)`, then `m3dRunUDP(ctx, t, f.agent, name, "bridge", publish...)` and `m3dWaitRunning`. `m3dExpoAllowUDP(ctx, t, f, selector string, port uint16)` applies `firewall.container.allow` through `m3dDockApply` with the binding `{Selector: selector, HostPort: port, Proto: "udp"}` and no `from`.
3. `m3dExpoCheck(ctx, t, f, raw []byte, view m3dExpoView)` is spec 2.7's harness check over every row of `view`, described in scenario 1 below.

**F. The scenarios** (`m3_docker_exposure_test.go`):

1. `m3dExpoScan` (R48, R49: exposure equals the scan, including a partial rule and IPv6 published to an IPv4-only bridge). `m3dDockEnable`; add both second sources; `m3dTrafficNetwork(…, "m3dxn", "--ipv6", "--subnet", "fd00:3d:2::/64")`. Containers (all with `m3dTrafficPublish` unless UDP), then their policy:

   | Container | Network | Publish | Policy |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `m3d-x1` | `bridge` | `18301:14000` | `m3dTrafficAllow` from any |
   | `m3d-x2` | `m3dxn` | `18302:14000` | `m3dTrafficAllow` from `scannerIPv4+"/32"`, and from `scannerIPv6+"/128"` |
   | `m3d-x3` | `bridge` | `18303:14000` | none |
   | `m3d-x4` | `bridge` | UDP `18304:8053/udp` (`m3dExpoPublishUDP`) | `m3dExpoAllowUDP` |
   | `m3d-x5` | `bridge` | UDP `18305:8053/udp` | none |
   | `m3d-x6` | `bridge` | `18306:14000` | none |
   | `m3d-x7` | `bridge` | `18307:14000` | `m3dTrafficAllow` from any |

   With `eventually` for two minutes, read the view (`m3dExpoRead`) until `m3dxExpoVerdicts(view.Rows, want)` is nil for `want` = `tcp/v4/18301` open, `tcp/v6/18301` open, `tcp/v4/18302` partial, `tcp/v6/18302` partial, `tcp/v4/18303` filtered, `tcp/v6/18303` filtered, `udp/v4/18304` open, `udp/v4/18305` filtered, `tcp/v4/18306` filtered, `tcp/v6/18306` filtered, `tcp/v4/18307` open, `tcp/v6/18307` open (the IPv6 rows of the default-bridge containers are `docker-proxy`'s, governed by UFW's INPUT rules; `m3d-x2`, on an IPv6 network, is DNATed and partial for both families). The test fails with the last error otherwise. Then `m3dExpoCheck`, which does, for the final view:
   - `view.Notes` must be empty (`t.Errorf` otherwise).
   - Decode `raw` with Task 9's `m3dxRows`. For each family (`v4` with flag `-4`, `v6` with `-6`) and protocol (`tcp`, `udp`): the rows of that family and protocol whose `m3dxExpoTarget(row.Addr, row.Family, agentIPv4, agentIPv6)` is true give the target (`agentIPv4` or `agentIPv6`) and the port list (ascending, no duplicates); skip the pair when the list is empty. One `m3dScan(ctx, t, f.scanner, ScanOpts{Family: flag, UDP: proto == "udp", Ports: ports, Target: target})` from the default source. `m3dxMismatch(plain, scanned, proto)` for `plain` = those rows whose `Verdict` is neither `partial` nor `unknown`; each returned line is a `t.Errorf`.
   - For every scannable TCP row of `view` whose internet class is `partial` and for which `m3dExpoBySourcePort()` is false, and for every source of its family (IPv4: `scannerIPv4` and `m3dTrafficSrcB`; IPv6: `scannerIPv6` and `m3dExpoSrcB6`): `expect, err := m3dxExpoExpect(class, src, 0, m3dTrafficIface)` (an error is a `t.Errorf`); one `m3dScan` of the row's port with `ScanOpts{Family: flag, Ports: []uint16{row.Port}, Target: target}` plus `Source: src` and `Iface: m3dTrafficIface` when `src` is a second source; `m3dxExpoCompare(expect, scanned[0], "tcp")`. For the rows of port 18302 the sources must split: at least one expectation `open` and one `notopen` per family, or the scenario fails (a partial row scanned from one side proves nothing).
   - A scannable row whose internet verdict is `unknown` fails the test when its port is 18301–18399 and is logged with `t.Logf` otherwise; a row skipped by `m3dxExpoTarget` is not scanned (a loopback or private-link listener cannot be probed from the internet link).
2. `m3dExpoSourcePort` (a rule restricted by source port, scanned from inside and outside its range). Run a listener on the agent: `sudo systemd-run --unit=m3d-sp --collect /usr/bin/python3 -m http.server 18311 --bind 0.0.0.0` (cleanup `sudo systemctl stop m3d-sp`), and the manual rule `sudo ufw allow proto tcp from any port 5300:5399 to any port 18311` (cleanup `sudo ufw delete allow proto tcp from any port 5300:5399 to any port 18311`); `m3WaitStatus` with `m3Healthy`. With `eventually` for a minute, read the view until the row `tcp`/`v4`/18311 has an internet class that is `partial` and `m3dExpoBySourcePort()`. Collect every `SrcPorts` entry of its groups into one list and take `inside, outside` from `m3dxExpoSourcePorts`. For each of `inside` and `outside`: `expect` from `m3dxExpoExpect(class, netip.MustParseAddr(scannerIPv4), port, m3dTrafficIface)`, which must be `open` for `inside` and `notopen` for `outside`; then `m3dScan` with `ScanOpts{Family: "-4", Ports: []uint16{18311}, SourcePort: port, Target: agentIPv4}` and `m3dxExpoCompare(expect, scanned[0], "tcp")`.
3. `m3dExpoPrivateClass` (a source in a configured `privateSources` range is the `private` class and reaches a published port). `m3dDockEnable`; add source B (`m3dTrafficSrcB`); `m3dTrafficPublish(…, "m3d-q1", "bridge", "18321:14000")` with no policy. Read `orig := st.Settings.PrivateSources` from `m3dDockRead`; the row `tcp`/`v4`/18321 must have an internet class `filtered` and no class `private` with range `198.18.1.0/24`. Register a cleanup that applies `firewall.docker.set-sources` with `{"privateSources": orig}` (logging, never failing), then `m3dDockApply` `firewall.docker.set-sources` with `{"privateSources": orig + ["198.18.1.0/24"]}`. With `eventually` for a minute, read the view until that row has a `private` class with range `198.18.1.0/24` and verdict `open` while its internet class is still `filtered`. `m3dScan` of port 18321 (`Family: "-4"`, `Target: agentIPv4`) from the default source must give `filtered` and from source B (`Source`, `Iface: m3dTrafficIface`) `open`, both through `m3dxExpoCompare`. The binding view of `m3d-q1` port 18321 in `m3dDockRead` must hold `198.18.1.0/24` in `PrivateReach`.

Order of work: the pure helpers, the mirror types and `m3dxExpoWorkflow` first (they turn every unit test green but `TestM3xExpoWorkflowFile`), then the workflow edit of C (which turns it green), then the helpers and scenarios.
